| Prank | Hypnotize {0} #23343 | hypnotize | -2 on success and -3 on failure | ImpactNotoriety(-1) or ImpactNotoriety(2) | ' ' plus the row's line plus 'I hypnotized {0} to act like an animal because of the prank.' #24432, or 'I tried to hypnotize {0}, but failed.' #25436 | the animal card, and whatever get_Hypnotize() hands back |
| Prank | Have a talk with {0} #22687 | talk | none | none | the row's own line | ScenarioCoworkerTalkingTo(coworker, 'why you don't appreciate {0} little prank' #68058) |
| Prank | Laugh it off #28540 | laugh | none | slot 0x408 with -2 and ImpactDiscipline(2) | the line plus ' I laughed it off.' #69581 | none |
| Prank | Report {0} to my supervisor #35790 | report | none | none | the row's own line | a bare Scenario carrying the coworker |
| Rumor | Attack {0} #12347 | attack | -6 | none | the row's own line | ScenarioCustomAttack(coworker), the HR or supervisor card and the (0,150) attribute draw |
| Rumor | Have a talk with {0} #22687 | talk | none | none | the row's own line | ScenarioCoworkerTalkingTo(coworker, 'why you don't appreciate false rumors being spread about you' #68056) |
| Rumor | Pay no attention #33482 | attention | none | slot 0x408 with -2 and ImpactDiscipline(2) | the line plus ' I paid no attention to {1}.' #69593 | none |
| Rumor | Start a rumor about {0} #39875 | rumor | none | slot 0x408 with +3 and ImpactDiscipline(-3) | the row's own line | ScenarioCoworkerInstigateOutbound(coworker) |

Two of the lanes deserve a paragraph each. The attack lane is the family's only lane that
touches nothing of the hero's own: the -6 goes to the colleague's relationship slot, and
everything after that is either a code-side card or a draw. The annoyance, prank and rumor
versions draw GetRandomNumber(0, 150) and compare it against one float of the hero's; the
inappropriate behaviour version has no such test at all and goes straight to
GetRandomNumber(0, 2). Either way the sub-branch is between the HR card and the supervisor
card -- the supervisor lane looks for SimWorkplace.GetSupervisor(), falls back to the HR
card when there is none or when the supervisor is the hero's current lover, and formats
its own label from the relationship status and an indefinite article -- and
ScenarioCustomAttack(coworker) is pushed on top of it, so an attack is always two cards
deep.

The hypnotize lane is the prank card's own and the family's largest: it builds a
BracketParser over a nine-piece Concat of the hero's relationship status, the colleague's
display name, the relationship word and two commas, registers the bare names for the
'<coworker>' and '<coworker-possessive>' tokens, and then draws GetRandomNumber(0, 100)
against the colleague's willpower float at +0xa8. Success parses 'I hypnotized
<him/her> to act like an animal because of the prank.' (#24432), draws a one-element list
holding 'Whatever you say' (#46497) as the reaction's title, builds the reaction's body out
of six pieces (the gaze line, a blank line, a pronoun, an animal list, a pronoun again and
' work station.' #4141), calls an unnamed corridor at 0x73f46b955c that hands back the
extra scenario the action produced, pushes both, and moves ImpactNotoriety(-1) with the
colleague's slot at -2. Failure parses 'I tried to hypnotize <him/her>, but failed.'
(#25436), draws 'What are you doing?' (#46376) as the title, builds a four-piece body
ending ' shook it off and laughed in your face.' (#3372), pushes the card and moves
ImpactNotoriety(2) with the colleague's slot at -3.

Every path ends in the same tail: the D singleton's log at [D+0x48] takes the journal
string and LifeInterface.RefreshUI() is called on [D+0x10]. The four handlers draw only in
the lanes described above -- the annoyance handler (0,150) then (0,2), the inappropriate
one (0,2) alone, the prank (0,150), (0,2) and (0,100), the rumor (0,150) and (0,2) -- and
none of them writes the title, the body, the choices or the wrapper.

### 105.3 Who can ask: four tests, a colleague, and a picker one draw wide

ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush is 74 instructions in each of the four classes and asks
four questions, in this order:

1. Is the hero 18 or older? The gate loads the hero through the same static chain and
   compares [hero+0x20] against 0x12, branching to false below it.
2. Does he have a job or the military? CurrentlyHasAJob() at 0x73f2f0e040 passing is enough;
   if it fails, CurrentlyInTheMilitary() at 0x73f2f0e0b4 has to pass.
3. Has this card been shown too often? PresentedCountForScenario at 0x73f3736430 is called
   with the class's own type name and its result is compared with B.LE against the card's
   own bound: 4 for the annoyance, 3 for the inappropriate behaviour, 2 for the prank and
   2 for the rumor. A count above the bound drops the card, so the four are shown at most
   five, four, three and three times in a life. Nothing here is a one-shot.
4. Does GetCoworker() find a colleague? A hero whose roster walk comes back empty gets no
   card of the family at all.

The picker adds the table's own tests and then draws exactly once, on the filtered set:
annoyance keeps a row whose HeroGender is the wildcard 2 or the hero's, then one whose
CoworkerGender is the wildcard or the coworker's; inappropriate behaviour does the same
with the recipient against the hero and the sender against the coworker; the rumor keeps a
row whose VictimGender is the wildcard or the hero's; the prank ignores gender entirely and
keeps a row when its Vampire flag equals the hero's own vampirism. The draw is
GetRandomNumber(0, count) through GameReference at 0x73f32ab2a8, one call, with no retry
loop -- if the filtered set is empty the card is simply not built.

The port models four of the gate's four questions: the age floor, the job-or-military
test, and the two limits it can see (its own counters and the slot it keeps for the
coworker). It has no Sexuality field, so nothing else is missing here -- unlike the
friend-lover card, this gate does not read one. What the port cannot do is the roster:
there is no SimWorkplace and no SimCoworker in it, so the colleague is one slot drawn once
and kept, and the score the game computes -- the relationship strength under 25.0 and the
combined coolness and professionalism over 70.0 -- has no inputs at all.

### 105.4 The rows

The four tables are the family's content, and they are uneven in the way the friend tables
were not: the annoyance table is a long list of small office crimes, the behaviour table is
the shortest and the most gated, the prank table is the largest and half of it is vampire
content, and the rumor table is entirely about what has been said behind the hero's back.

| table | bytes | rows | what the row is | gated how |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a16_coworker-annoy-scenarios-enc | 12334 | 40 | a colleague doing something small and unbearable next to the hero, in the second person and in full sentences | 2 rows |
| a16_coworker-behavior-scenarios-enc | 5758 | 20 | the colleague who crosses a line -- the slapped rear, the whiteboard pitch, the snickering at the monitor | 4 rows |
| a16_coworker-pranks-enc | 22185 | 65 | the colleague's prank discovered by the hero, and the family's only vampire block | 31 rows, by the Vampire flag |
| a16_coworker-rumors-enc | 12337 | 46 | a snippet of what the colleague is telling the office, wrapped by the rumor sentence | 5 rows, by the victim |

The gender gating is thinner than the friend family's, and it is worth listing because each
of the four gated pairs is one card seen from both sides. The annoyance table gates two rows
out of forty, rows 4 and 5, and they are the same card: a men's room with one stall for a
male hero and a male colleague, and its mirror for a female hero and a female colleague.
The behaviour table gates four of its twenty rows in two pairs: rows 1 and 2 are the slapped
rear (a male sender with a female recipient, and the mirror), and rows 11 and 12 are the
colleague snickering at the hero's monitor (gated on the recipient alone). The rumor table
gates five of its forty-six: row 19 (a male victim and a eunuch), row 33 (a male victim and
a micropenis), row 34 (a female victim and a size queen), row 35 (a male victim and a
cuckold) and row 44 (a female victim and a pregnancy). The prank table gates nothing by
gender and instead splits its content in half: 31 of its 65 rows carry the Vampire flag and
are only drawn for a vampire hero, and the remaining 34 are the mortal office pranks.

The vocabulary is the friend tables' vocabulary with one substitution. The annoy table
carries 80 '<coworker>' tokens and 38 '<he/she>', 30 '<his/her>', 12 '<rb>' and 3
'<him/her>'; the behaviour table is dense in the same way -- 39 '<coworker>' and 12 '<rb>'
across only 20 rows; the prank table carries 156 '<coworker>', 37 '<coworker-possessive>' and
28 '<rb>'; the rumor table only 43 '<coworker>' and 20 '<rb>', because its prose puts the
colleague's name outside the sentence rather than inside it. The alternative lists that make
these cards funny are the largest in the report: a 26-item list of lunches a colleague can
devour in the break room, a 16-item list of noises for one to make while doing it, a 20-item
list of topics to talk about with one's mouth full, and a 25-item list for the rumour the
colleague starts. The rumor table's own two specialty tokens are '<drug-illegal>' (6 uses)
and '<country-other>' (6 uses), which resolve against tables the port already carries.

### 105.5 Shortcuts

1. The roster walk is a single slot. The game keeps a SimWorkplace with a refreshed
   CoworkerArray and GetCoworker() scores every colleague on the list; the port has neither
   the roster nor the coworker's own attributes (coolness at 0x23C and professionalism at
   0x240, the relationship strength, the Type flag), so it draws one name and one sex once
   and keeps them for the whole life. The game refreshes the roster on every job change.
2. The coin is the port's. No class in the family carries a push rate -- the four gates ask
   four questions and the game's own random-push queue is what decides -- so the 5 percent
   this section's function spends per card, on its own stream, is a port decision, and it is
   what keeps a long career from being nothing but coworker cards.
3. The attack lane's attribute test is dropped. The (0,150) draw against one of the hero's
   floats decides between the HR card and the supervisor card; the port has no such float
   and pushes no card, so it logs the row's line and carries the -6 only as a comment.
4. The talk lane's card is not pushed. ScenarioCoworkerTalkingTo takes the colleague and one
   of four about-strings, and the port has no scenario push for any of them.
5. The report lane always offers its button. In the game the choice exists only when
   SimCoworker.GetSupervisor() finds somebody, and its wording depends on
   [coworker+0x1f4]; the port has no supervisor and no workplace type, so it always writes
   the supervisor's wording.
6. The rumor lane's outbound card is not pushed either, and the port's own card is
   identified by its table rather than its title: the game's rumor title cell is 'Rumor',
   the same title the friend-rumor card of the section before uses, so a reader of the
   port's events has to look at the table column.
7. The hypnotize lane is unreachable in the port's model and its draw is a coin. The button
   exists only for a vampire hero whose colleague is mortal, and a vampire life in the port
   never reaches any coworker card: the yearly chain tries vampireYear first and it claims
   the year, which is why the probe's vampire pass drew zero cards of the family and why
   the branch never appears in the counts below. The (0,100) roll against the colleague's
   willpower float at +0xa8 becomes a 50 percent coin, the same shortcut the friend-lover
   card uses for its own hypnotize.
8. ImpactNotoriety has no reader in the port's per-year deltas, so the hypnotize lane's -1
   and +2 are carried only in the code's own comment.
9. The four caps are the port's own counters, not the game's store. PresentedCountForScenario
   is a dictionary on the game's life object keyed by type name; the port keeps four
   integers on its own life struct instead, with the same bounds.
10. The gender columns are compared as text. The loader decodes 'male' and 'female' into 0
    and 1 and everything else into the wildcard 2, and the port's filter reads the cell's
    string and treats the empty cell, 'both', 'all', 'any' and the literal '2' the same way.
11. The stale-age stamps are ignored. Each refresh writes the hero's age into one
    SimCoworker field (0x22C, 0x220, 0x224, 0x228 by card) for the outbound half of the
    family to read later; the port has no outbound half.
12. Three of the four bodies keep the game's lower-case journal: the dictionary's 'my' half
    is written in lower case in the binary itself, so the port reproduces 'my coworker,
    Robin, irked me' rather than capitalizing it. Only the rumor card's journal is
    capitalized, and that is because its narrative is the one that is not wrapped by the
    identity Format.
13. The fifth table of the family stays where it was. a16_coworker-hookup-scenarios-enc is
    already fired from the relationship year at 5 percent, and this section does not move
    it: the same SupervisorAppropriate column the hookup picker reads is what the port's
    earlier section already modelled as a plain pool.

cards 725
cards per life {0: 46, 1: 10, 2: 20, 3: 22, 4: 22, 5: 30, 6: 17, 7: 13, 8: 8, 9: 8, 10: 2, 11: 2}

The probe drives two hundred lives -- seeds 1 through 40 in both genders at 80 years and
at 50, then a vampire pass of seeds 1 through 20 in both genders at 80 -- and reads every
event whose table is one of the four, since the rumor card's title is not unique. It counts
725 coworker cards, and the cards per life curve shows the caps doing their work: 46 lives
see none at all, the median life sees four to seven, and the longest career in the set sees
eleven, against the ceiling of fifteen the four caps allow (five annoyance, four behaviour,
three prank, three rumor). A separate pass of 120 lives run to a hundred years reaches
every one of those four ceilings exactly -- five annoyances in a life, four inappropriate
behaviours, three pranks, three rumors -- and never passes one. The branch split is attack 168, talk 211, polite 162, report 145
and the rumor lane 39; no hypnotize card appears, because the vampire pass is the only place
that branch could occur and a vampire life in this model never reaches a coworker card.

The rows drawn are the other half of the census. The behaviour table is small enough that
every one of its 20 rows turns up. The annoyance table shows 36 of 40 -- rows 4, 6, 13 and
33 never came up in these 200 lives. The rumor table shows 39 of its 46, missing rows 3, 7,
8, 11, 16, 26 and 32. The prank table shows 31 of 65, which is exactly its mortal half
minus two rows: every one of its 31 vampire-flagged rows 35 through 65 is out of reach, as
are rows 2 and 29 of the mortal half. Every card lands between ages 18 and 80, which is the
gate's own floor and the oldest life the probe runs.

The probe checks each card against its row: the row index is in range, the card's table is
the one its title claims, the hero's age is over the gate's floor, the row's gender column
-- Hero Gender, Recipient Gender or Victim Gender, whichever the card's picker reads -- is
the wildcard or the hero's own gender, the prank card's Vampire flag equals the hero's
vampirism, the body is the row's Scenario cell under the dictionary (each '<coworker>'
rendered as 'your coworker, NAME,' and each '<coworker-possessive>' as 'your coworker,
NAME's,', every alternative list drawn, every pronoun pair resolved), and for the rumor
card the two three-slot templates around the two snippets. One coworker name has to hold for
the whole card and for every card of the same life, and every pronoun pair has to agree on
one sex for that name. The label is checked against the branch it dispatches on, including
the pronoun after Attack, Hypnotize and Report and the name after Start a rumor about. The
non-zero deltas are checked exactly: nothing at all for the attack, talk, report and
hypnotize lanes, happiness -8 with discipline 8 for the four polite lanes, and happiness 16
with discipline -16 for the rumor lane. The journal is checked against the row's Log Version
cell plus the tail that branch appends, and finally nothing drawn is left behind: a token
surviving into the body or the journal counts as residue.

Six samples are printed below.

The four cards close the inbound side of the family. What is left of it is the outbound
half -- the cards the colleague is the subject of rather than the author of -- and the two
classes of the hookup table that the relationship year already fires but never narrates.

The full regression after the section: 49 probes at residue 0 (the new `cwres.py` among them), the residue census at `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`, coverage at `captured scenarios: 90  recoverable: 89`, the port gap at `ENTRIES 90 rendered-by-port 89 gap 0`, the push script at rc 0 with empty stderr, and the benchmark reaching age 34.

## 106. The friend spend-time card: a pastime drawn from a table of 271, a friend free to
refuse, and a journal written by the dismiss button

The friend family's sixth card is the first one that carries no scenario table at all.
ScenarioFriendSpendTime does not read a16_friend-anything: its content is one row of
a16_pastimes-enc, the same 271-row list the push-spend-time card uses, and everything else
the card shows -- the title, the two sentences -- is a template wrapped around that row and
around the friend's name. It is also the family's only card with no choices: there is no
ChoiceSelectedAtIndex in the class, the button the player is given is Dismiss, and the
dismiss handler is what writes the journal line. Where the prank card needs the player to
pick a side and the rumor card needs him to pick a revenge, this one needs him to close it.

Three things make it worth a section of its own. The first is who opens it: the class has
no eligibility method of its own, and the two callers of its constructor turn out to be a
blueprint and the Relationships tab, not the yearly random push. The second is that the
friend gets a vote: the card's first branch is a test on the friend's own state, and when
it fails the card is a refusal -- a different title pool, a different body, a different
narrative, and a happiness cost rather than a happiness gain. The third is the pastime
itself, which is drawn out of the same table the push card draws from, filtered by a
Christmas flag that only the season can set.

What the port models is the whole card: the age floor, its own stream, the pastime row,
the two title pools, both bodies and both narratives, the friend's name drawn once per
card, the pronoun, the stat deltas and the empty choice.

### 106.1 The card

The class is small even for this family. Its three fields are a SimPerson at 0x170, a
SimSeniorPerson at 0x178 and a String at 0x180, the narrative; two constructors,
ctor(SimPerson) @0x73f3c53d44 and ctor(SimSeniorPerson) @0x73f3c53d70, are the same
three-instruction thunk to Scenario::.ctor(false) that every other card in the yearly chain
has, and three methods carry the content: RefreshScenario @0x73f3c53d9c (448 instructions),
DismissSelected @0x73f3c544c8 (27) and GetFriendRelationshipStatusForDisplay @0x73f3c5449c
(11). The 448 instructions are mostly IL2CPP metadata registration -- roughly the first
seventy lines of the disassembly are adrp/ldr pairs over type-usage cells, each guarded by
a byte at 0x73f656d000 and each followed by FillDictionary -- so the card's own work is
about a hundred instructions, and every string it needs is a literal cell it loads.

The refresh builds the card in one pass. It writes 0x101 into the halfword at self+0x132
(the two "this card has no choices" flags the base class reads), makes sure _friend is
non-null, asks the friend's virtual slot 0x3f8 for an int and keeps bit 0, calls
GetRandomPastime, and then splits. Both halves end with a title from a five-string list
picked by PickRandomFromStringArray @0x73f32b0608 and two Format calls, one into the body
at self+0x48 and one into the narrative at self+0x180.

The relationship word comes from GetFriendRelationshipStatusForDisplay, which is a
two-line decision: if _seniorFriend is set it asks the SimSeniorPerson for
SeniorRelationshipStatusForDisplay @0x73f30fde5c, otherwise it asks the SimPerson for
FriendRelationshipStatusString @0x73f30e169c, and if neither field is set it throws. The
word is the first argument of both templates.

DismissSelected does one thing: it walks the game chain from [game+0xb8] through [0] and
+0x20 to +0x48, and tail-calls Log(String) @0x73f380158c with self+0x180. There is no stat
move, no relationship move, no second card -- the button's whole job is to put the
narrative into the journal, which is why the journal sentence in this family is the only
one the player never saw marked as a choice.

### 106.2 Who opens it

Nothing in the class decides when the card may appear. There is no
ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush and no table predicate, so the question is who calls the
constructor, and that is answerable directly: scan libil2cpp.so for every BL word, decode
the target with the same 0x73F049E000 delta tools/dis_range.py uses, and resolve the
addresses with tools/addr2method.py. Two callers turn up.

The first is BluePrintSpendTime.GetNextScenario(String) @0x73f36b8b04, which instantiates
the class with a SimPerson at 0x73f36b911c and with a SimSeniorPerson at 0x73f36b9314 --
the same blueprint method, one overload per friend type. The blueprint itself is at
il2cpp_dump.txt:129489 with .ctor @0x73f36b8810 and ConditionSelected @0x73f36b8818, and
ConditionSelected is 187 instructions of payload and type comparison (GetData() @0x73f354378c,
then string equality against its own cells): it decides which blueprint answers, not
whether this card may run.

The second caller is LifeInterface.RelationshipItemArrayForFriend @0x73f357b860, the
method that builds the Relationships tab's rows for one friend. So the card is reached two
ways -- from the yearly spend-time blueprint, and from tapping the friend in the
Relationships list -- and neither of them is a gate this class owns. That is why the port
gives the card its own floor and its own rate rather than mirroring a push count like the
coworker family does.

### 106.3 The two branches

The split is one bit of one call. RefreshScenario keeps the friend's virtual slot 0x3f8
result in w21, then does tbz w21,#0 to 0x73f3c541fc: bit 0 clear takes the refusal half,
bit 0 set takes the main half. What slot 0x3f8 computes lives in the SimPerson class rather
than in the card, and the port has no friend object to ask, so the port's coin -- one
fifty-fifty draw on its own stream -- stands in for it, and both halves of the card are
live in the port exactly as they are in the game.

The main half, in order: it pushes the community-goal scenario (ContributeToCommunityGoal(2)
@0x73f36f3974 through [game+0xb8]+0x50, then PushFront(Scenario) @0x73f2ebf2f8), it
compares [friend+0x120], the friend's stored age, against the hero's age at [hero+0x20],
and when they differ it writes the hero's age over the friend's, calls the friend's slot
0x508 with 3, calls the hero's slot 0x408 with 2 and calls ImpactKarma(1) @0x73f30e4bfc.
Then it builds a five-string list -- the cells at 0x5C43188, 0x5CBC4B8, 0x5CBC4A0,
0x5CBC498 and 0x5CBC2A0 -- and draws the title out of it, formats the body from the
template cell 0x5C60A90 with the relationship, the friend's name object and the pastime,
formats the narrative from cell 0x5C60A98 with the pastime, the relationship and the name,
and finishes with an Equals against the cell at 0x5C74BB8 which, on a match, tails into
AchievementManager.get_SharedAchievementManager() @0x73f2817388 and
CompleteAchievement(String) @0x73f2817434 with the cell at 0x5C734B8 as the name.

The refusal half is the same shape with the opposite values: the friend's slot 0x508 gets
-2, the hero's slot 0x408 gets -1, the title comes from a second five-string list (cells
0x5CBC4C8, 0x5CBC4B0, 0x5CBC4A8, 0x5CBC4C0 and 0x5CBC4D0), the body comes from cell
0x5C60A88 through the object-array overload of Format @0x73f52a7254 -- whose fourth
argument is the friend's PronounStringForType(0) @0x73f30e64d0 -- and the narrative comes
from cell 0x5C60A50.

All six templates and both title pools were read out of the running process, so their text
is measured rather than guessed:

| where | cell | text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| title, main | 0x5C43188, 0x5CBC4B8, 0x5CBC4A0, 0x5CBC498, 0x5CBC2A0 | Good times / Chillin' with my villain / Loving the crew / What a trip / Always a blast |
| title, refusal | 0x5CBC4C8, 0x5CBC4B0, 0x5CBC4A8, 0x5CBC4C0, 0x5CBC4D0 | Next time... / With friends like these... / Busy buddy / Preoccupied pal / Alright well lmk |
| body, main | 0x5C60A90 | You and your {0}, {1}, went {2}. |
| narrative, main | 0x5C60A98 | I went {0} with my {1}, {2}. |
| body, refusal | 0x5C60A88 | You asked your {0}, {1}, to go {2} but {3} refused. |
| narrative, refusal | 0x5C60A50 | My {0}, {1}, refused to go {2} with me. |

The two refusals are worth reading twice, because the sentence changes subject: the quiet
refusal is "Next time..." with a body that blames nobody, and the loud one is "With friends
like these..." with a body that names the friend and points at her. The game draws one of
the five at random rather than scaling the wording to the relationship, so a friend of
twenty years can get "Busy buddy" and a friend of a week can get "With friends like these...".

### 106.4 The rows

The pastime is not part of this class. GetRandomPastime @0x73f2d0ca3c is a static 168
instructions that lazily fills a static set hanging off the game object at [game+0xb8]+0x250
with an ArrayList (ctor @0x73f5381f78) and then LoadPastimeSet() @0x73f2b72520, works out
whether the day is a holiday -- IsChristmasSeason() @0x73f3479fe4, and when that is true a
GetRandomNumber(0,2) @0x73f32ab2a8 that only sometimes turns it on -- and then rejection
samples: draw an index in [0, Count), take the row, require that it is a DataPastime (a
class comparison against the cell at 0x73f60e9000+0x7e8), require that the bool at row+0x18
equals the flag, and retry on any failure. Then it formats "{0}" (cell 0x5C31470) over the
row's Pastime string and runs the result through GetParsedBodyString @0x73f337bb5c, which
is the same dictionary pass the rest of the report's tables go through.

The table itself is one of the smaller ones the port already carries:

| table | bytes | rows | what a row is | split |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a16_pastimes-enc | 8234 | 271 | a thing two people can go and do, from "to the park" and "golfing" to a 178-character evening | 224 ordinary rows, 47 marked in the Holiday column |

The Holiday column is not a bool in the file: 224 rows leave it empty and 47 rows carry an
'x', and the port's flag() reads that the same way the game's bool does. Eighteen rows also
carry the family's one-of syntax inside the cell itself -- a pastime that expands to one of
several outings -- and one of them carries a <musician> token, so a row's text is not
always its final text. The port resolves both through the same fillOneOf path REPORT.en.md
97 documents for the push card, which means the spend-time card and the push card agree on
what "golfing" means; the difference between them is only who is asked and whether a no is
possible.

Because the port's holiday flag is dateMonth_ == 12 and a script run sets no date, the
probe's 160 lives draw 49 distinct rows and every one of them comes from the ordinary 224;
the holiday half of the table stays dark in a headless run, exactly as it does for the
push card.

### 106.5 Shortcuts

1. The coin is the port's. The friend's willingness is bit 0 of SimPerson virtual slot
   0x3f8, which is a friend-side computation the port has no friend object to run, so the
   port spends one fifty-fifty draw on its own stream. The census behind the section shows
   both halves firing in the hundreds of cards, and a separate 326-card tally at the same
   rate splits 165 for 161 against, so the substitution is not shape-changing -- it is a
   real draw replacing a call the port cannot make.
2. The relationship bar does not move. The game moves the friend's slot 0x508 by +3 or -2
   on every card and the hero's slot 0x408 by +2 or -1, and on the accept path it also
   calls ImpactKarma(1). The port's friend is a drawn name with no bar, so the 0x508 moves
   are dropped, as they are throughout the friend family; the hero's side is kept as
   out.happiness = pointsForImpact(2) with out.karma = pointsForImpact(1) on an accept and
   out.happiness = pointsForImpact(-1) on a refusal.
3. The age sync is dropped. The block at the top of the accept path writes the hero's age
   over the friend's and runs its three calls only when the two differ, which is the
   first-encounter state for a new friend; the port's friend carries no age field at all,
   so there is nothing to compare and nothing to sync.
4. The community-goal push is dropped. The card contributes 2 to the community goal and
   pushes the goal scenario in front of itself when that goal exists; the port models no
   community goals (only the a16_anniversary-community-goals-titles-enc table at
   sim.cpp:25215), so the contribution is a comment rather than a call.
5. The achievement trigger is unresolved and therefore dropped. The accept path tests the
   pastime against the literal cell at 0x5C74BB8 and awards the cell at 0x5C734B8, and
   neither cell decodes cleanly: the first is tagged 0xc00331af, and the second is tagged
   0xa0012b23, whose index arithmetic lands on "Sculpture-garden" -- a key that appears in
   the emoji-visual data rather than as a pastime. Rather than guess an achievement name
   out of an index that does not round-trip, the port drops the branch. This is the one
   place in the section where a decoded fact is left as an open question instead of a
   shortcut with a reason.
6. The friend's relationship word is always "friend". GetFriendRelationshipStatusForDisplay
   returns whatever the friend's own status string is -- the game distinguishes at least a
   friend from a best friend, and the senior overload has its own vocabulary -- while the
   port's drawn friend only has the one word. The template slot is the same either way.
7. The senior overload is a second constructor, not a second card. ctor(SimSeniorPerson)
   differs from ctor(SimPerson) only in the field the refresh reads, and
   GetFriendRelationshipStatusForDisplay prefers it when both are set; the port has no
   SimSeniorPerson, so the card is reachable only through the plain friend path.
8. The dismiss handler is the journal writer. Because the card has no choice, the port
   emits an empty choice and the narrative; the game's button calls DismissSelected, which
   logs self+0x180 through Log(String). The port's script already prints the narrative when
   the choice is empty, so the journal path is the same one the base class uses -- there is
   no separate dismiss log to model.

```
=== a1  (accept)
seed 6  male  United States  age 50  row 263  friend Skylar Maker (female)
table cells : Pastime to volunteer in a classroom at the local middle school - Holiday
TITLE  : Chillin' with my villain
BODY   : You and your friend, Skylar Maker, went to volunteer in a classroom at the local middle school.
CHOICE : None
LOG    : I went to volunteer in a classroom at the local middle school with my friend, Skylar Maker.
DELTAS : {"discipline": 0, "happiness": 8, "karma": 4, "looks": 0, "smarts": 0}

=== b1  (refuse)
seed 3  male  United States  age 27  row 110  friend Skylar Maker (female)
table cells : Pastime tire swinging - Holiday
TITLE  : Busy buddy
BODY   : You asked your friend, Skylar Maker, to go tire swinging but she refused.
CHOICE : None
LOG    : My friend, Skylar Maker, refused to go tire swinging with me.
DELTAS : {"discipline": 0, "happiness": -4, "karma": 0, "looks": 0, "smarts": 0}
```

The card closes the friend family's inbound side: with it, every class in the yearly chain
that the game constructs from a friend row, a friend and a pastime has a port twin. What
remains is what the family sends out rather than what it shows -- ScenarioFriendRumorOutbound,
ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound and ScenarioFriendStatusInbound, the four outbound coworker
cards the coworker section named, and the friend threesome and status cards that sit outside
the yearly chain entirely.

The full regression after the section: 50 probes at residue 0 (the new `fstres.py` among them), the residue census at `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`, coverage at `captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107`, the port gap at `ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0`, the push script at rc 0 with empty stderr, the persistent test at `friend spend-time cards: {'accept': 45, 'cards': 115, 'refuse': 70}` and the benchmark reaching age 34.

## 107. The friend-rumor outbound card: nine reactions to the rumor the hero just spread

Section 102 ported the card a friend opens when they start a rumor *about* the hero. That
card's fourth choice -- "Start a rumor about him" -- does not only move stats: with
ImpactDiscipline(-3) and ImpactKarma(-3) behind it, it builds
`ScenarioFriendRumorOutbound(friend, retaliatory: true)` and pushes it as a child scenario
at the link the card keeps at 0x128. Section 107 is that child card: the answer, in the
friend's own words, drawn from the *other* half of the same table.

### 107.1 The card

`ScenarioFriendRumorOutbound` sits at `il2cpp_dump.txt:40906`. Its fields are `0x170
SimPerson _friend`, `0x178 System.Boolean _isRetaliatory` and `0x180 System.String
_narrative`; its whole method list is `.ctor(SimPerson, System.Boolean)` @0x73f3c52d58,
`RefreshScenario()` @0x73f3c52e10 and `DismissSelected()` @0x73f3c53cd8. There is no
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`, no `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` and no `GetNextScenario`:
this is a card with no buttons, no gate of its own, and no stat call anywhere in its
946-instruction body.

`RefreshScenario` runs in this order:

1. The title first. A nine-string ArrayList is built from cells 0x5cbc448, 0x5cbc450,
   0x5cbc458, 0x5cbc460, 0x5cbc468, 0x5cbc470, 0x5cbc478, 0x5cbc480 and 0x5cbc490,
   `PickRandomFromStringArray` @0x73f32b0608 picks one, and it lands at `[self+0x38]`
   (@0x73f3c53210).
2. Two null guards: the player chain (cell 0x5cbc0b8 through `[x8]` to `+0x28`) and
   `_friend` at `[self+0x170]`. Either one failing leaves through 0x73f3c53cd4.
3. The row. `ldp w21,w20,[hero+0x1c]` @0x73f3c53238 and `ldp w23,w22,[friend+0x1c]`
   @0x73f3c53240 take both subjects' ages and genders, and the call at 0x73f3c53264 hands
   the hero's pair and the friend's pair to
   `DataFriendRumor.GetRandomRumorForSenderAgeSenderGenderReceiverAgeReceiverGender`
   @0x73f2ccace4 -- the same picker the inbound card uses, with the roles swapped. A null
   row exits at 0x73f3c53268 before anything is written.
4. Both texts come out of one row cell. The body is 'You started a rumor that {0}.' (cell
   0x5CB1A60, @0x73f3c53278) and the narrative is 'I started a rumor that {0}.' (cell
   0x5CB1A58, @0x73f3c53288), each a one-argument Format over the row's **Outbound
   Scenario** cell. Both then go through the dictionary parser (ctor 0x73f337959c,
   `GetParsedBodyString` 0x73f337bb5c / `GetParsedNarrativeString` 0x73f337bb64), which
   is what resolves the `<friend>` and `<he/she>` tokens the table is full of.

`DismissSelected` is the spend-time card's dismiss again: it walks the same chain and
tail-calls `Log(String)` @0x73f380158c with `[self+0x180]` -- the narrative line is the
journal entry, and the button is what writes it.

### 107.2 Who opens it

Exactly one call site constructs the card: `blcall.py` on the constructor finds
0x73f357b6a0 and nothing else, inside `LifeInterface.RelationshipItemArrayForFriend` --
the same method that builds the inbound rumor card and the spend-time card for the
Relationships tab. In the yearly chain the card arrives only as the child of the inbound
card's fourth choice, which is why the port hangs it off that choice rather than off a
coin of its own.

A second route was closed early. The Frida fixture can build the card (it always sets the
title) but `RefreshScenario` faults inside the game code after the title store, on any
friend handed to it -- a generated person, the hero's own mother, even the hero. A
`Process.setExceptionHandler` hook in `/tmp/qdir/fault.py` never fired, because Frida
recovers the access violation inside its own invoke path. So the body is read from the
binary and the table, not from a live card, and the nine title lines were confirmed live
(six runs, all six drawn from the pool above).

### 107.3 The carry

The port has no scenario push -- that has been a documented shortcut since section 101 --
so the child card is *queued* instead: the fourth choice stores the friend's name, the
friend's sex and a `rumorOutPending` flag on the life, and `friendRumorOutYear` renders
the answer on a later age-up. The flag is read and cleared before anything else in that
function, which is what makes the card one-shot and what keeps a queued rumor from
following the hero into the next life.

Because the answer queues behind the cards that already own the year, it can wait several
years: over 160 scripted lives the inbound card reached its fourth choice 46 times and 42
of those were answered (38 lives answered once, 2 lives twice, 4 picked and died or aged
out before the answer landed). The card carries no deltas and no buttons, so the queue has
no effect on stats -- it only decides which year the line reaches the journal.

### 107.4 The rows

`a16_friend-rumors-enc` is 8869 bytes over 40 rows and nine columns:
`Outbound Scenario,Inbound Scenario,Inbound Log Version,Sender Min Age,Sender Max Age,Sender
Gender,Receiver Min Age,Receiver Max Age,Receiver Gender`. Section 102 took columns 2 and
3; this card takes column 1, and every one of the 40 rows has an outbound cell (the inbound
column is what section 102 skips over, and the two columns are written for opposite
subjects: `<friend> has, not just one, but many venereal diseases` against `you have not
just one, but many venereal diseases`).

Twenty-five of the 40 rows carry a gate, which is far more than the inbound half's sample
suggested. Five rows ask for a hero of eighteen or more, five ask for sixty or more
(rows 36-40, the reminiscence lines), and the rest key on the *receiver's* age -- row 7
(`<friend> is pregnant`, sender 14+, receiver 16, receiver female), row 9 (sender 18+,
receiver 18+, receiver male), row 32 (sender 18+, receiver 25-40 female), row 14 (receiver
25+) -- so the friend the port stands at the hero's own age is gated by the same numbers the
inbound card would apply to the hero. The outbound cells use 23 distinct tokens across 18
one-of groups, 35 `<friend>`, 9 `<his/her>`, 6 `<he/she>`, 5 `<friend-possessive>`, 4
`<him/her>` and single-use `<drug-illegal>`; the longest is 247 characters. Over 160
scripted lives the port drew 17 of the 40 rows, with the hero aged 24 to 74 at the card.

### 107.5 Shortcuts

1. The card is queued, not pushed. The game builds the child scenario inside the inbound
   card's handler and renders it immediately; the port has no scenario push, so the choice
   sets a flag and the next age-up renders the answer. 4 of 46 picks went unanswered
   because the hero died or aged out of the script first.
2. The sender is the hero and the receiver the friend. The port reads that from the
   argument order of the picker call (hero's pair first, friend's second) and from the rows
   themselves -- `<friend> is pregnant` is gated on the receiver being female -- but the
   inbound card's own comment guessed the same order from the same evidence, so the
   assignment is a reading, not a certainty.
3. The friend is the one the inbound card named. The game passes the same `SimPerson` into
   the child card; the port hands the drawn name and sex over in the flag, so the answer
   names the friend the rumor was about rather than drawing a new one.
4. No stat change is applied. Nothing between the title store and the narrative store calls
   an impact, and the card's own button only logs, so the port moves nothing -- the -3
   discipline and -3 karma the hero earned belong to the inbound card (section 102).
5. The nine lines are read as titles. The class has no choices, so the nine reaction lines
   cannot be buttons; the live fixture always found one of them in the Title field. They are
   the card's headline, and the port treats them that way.
6. The '`your {0}, {1},`' formatter at 0x73f3c53328 (relationship word plus friend name,
   with `AddPossessionToNameString` @0x73f32af094 behind it) is not carried: what the game
   does with that string has no field in the port's card, and the body and narrative are
   already complete without it.
7. The `_isRetaliatory` flag is not carried. Section 102 pushes the card with the flag set
   and nothing in the card's body reads it; it distinguishes the push path, not the text.
8. The row is redrawn for the answer. The inbound card's row is not reused -- the outbound
   picker runs again -- so the answer is a second, independent draw against the same gates,
   and the port draws it on its own stream (`rumOutRng_`), moving no earlier subsystem's
   sequence.

```
=== seed 14  female  United States  age 50  row 17  friend Dustin Emberlake (male)
table cell : <friend> has an unhealthy fascination with lost teeth
TITLE  : This is hilarious
BODY   : You started a rumor that Dustin Emberlake has an unhealthy fascination with lost teeth.
LOG    : I started a rumor that Dustin Emberlake has an unhealthy fascination with lost teeth.
CHOICE : None
DELTAS : {"discipline": 0, "happiness": 0, "karma": 0, "looks": 0, "smarts": 0}

=== seed 28  male  United States  age 61  row 37  friend Ned Shirin (female)
table cell : <friend> still lives at <his/her> parent's house
TITLE  : We joke, we joke
BODY   : You started a rumor that Ned Shirin still lives at her parent's house.
LOG    : I started a rumor that Ned Shirin still lives at her parent's house.
CHOICE : None
DELTAS : {"discipline": 0, "happiness": 0, "karma": 0, "looks": 0, "smarts": 0}
```

The friend family now has both halves of its rumor card: the inbound half a friend opens
about the hero (section 102), and the outbound half the hero's own choice opens about the
friend. What the family still sends rather than shows is the unfriend pair
(`ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound`, `ScenarioFriendUnfriendOutbound`), the status pair, the
threesome card, and the four outbound coworker cards section 105 named.
The full regression after the section: 51 probes at residue 0 (the new `frores.py` among them), the residue census at `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`, coverage at `captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107`, the port gap at `ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0`, the push script at rc 0 with empty stderr, the persistent test at `friend rumor outbound cards: {'cards': 28, 'picks': 32}` and the benchmark reaching age 34.

The section's own probe, `frores.py`, drives 160 lives and reports `lives 160 / inbound start-rumor picks 46 / outbound cards 42 / cards per life {1: 38, 2: 2} / titles ... / rows drawn 17 of 40 / hero age at the card min 24 max 74 / runtime 39s / failures 0 / RESIDUE 0 {}`.

## 108. The unfriend card: the friend leaves first, and three answers

Seven sections have now ported cards the hero chooses to open. This one is the family's
mirror: the hero does not decide anything to make it happen. `ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound`
is pushed by the yearly `Life.IncrementAge` loop, its rate is the hero's own karma rather
than a fixed percentage (corrected: that rate belongs to the friend-status card -- see the
correction at the end of this section and REPORT.en.md 109), and the three things the hero
can say about it are the whole
interaction. Its sibling `ScenarioFriendUnfriendOutbound` -- the version the Relationships
tab opens, the same shape section 107 ported for the rumor pair -- is left for a later
section.

### 108.1 The card

`ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound` sits at `il2cpp_dump.txt:40947`. One field, `0x170
SimPerson _friend`, and three methods: `.ctor(SimPerson)` @0x73f3c58ac4, `RefreshScenario()`
@0x73f3c58b34 (134 instructions) and `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex(Int32)` @0x73f3c58d4c (668
instructions). There is no `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush`, no `GetNextScenario` and no
`DismissSelected`: the push gate lives in the caller, and a card with no dismiss handler is
a card that always ends in one of its buttons.

`RefreshScenario` writes the body and the buttons and nothing else:

1. `_friend` from `[self+0x170]`; null leaves through the throw stub 0x73f3c58d48.
2. The relationship word and the display name: `FriendRelationshipStatusString`
   @0x73f30e169c and `[friend+0x10]+0x18`, handed to `Format(String,Object,Object)`
   @0x73f52a71cc with template cell 0x5CBC748 -- **"Your {0}, {1}, has unfriended you."** --
   and the result stored at `[self+0x48]` (Body). A byte flag is set at `[self+0x110]`.
3. Three `ScenarioChoice` objects (ctor 0x73f2eb9c50, the `(false, true)` overload), each
   text built by `Format(String,Object)` @0x73f52976b4 over `PronounStringForType(2)`
   @0x73f30e64d0, in this order: cell 0x5CBC730 **"Try to salvage our friendship"**, cell
   0x5CBC740 **"Let {0} go"**, cell 0x5CBC738 **"Insult {0} one last time"**. The list lands
   at `[self+0x108]`.

There is no title in `RefreshScenario` at all. Every title this card ever shows is written
later, inside the button handler, by the branch the hero picked.

### 108.2 Who opens it

The push is in the yearly friend loop at 0x73f2f03d30, and it runs three tests before the
card is built:

1. `ldr w8,[x22,#0x184]` (`FriendStatus`) then `ccmp w8,#1,#0,gt; b.ne 0x73f2f03df8` -- only
   an active friend can unfriend the hero.
2. `ldr w8,[x21,#0x20]` (hero age) minus `[x22,#0x190]` (`HeroAgeAtLastBestFriendRequest`),
   `cmp w8,#0xb; b.lt` -- at least eleven years have to have passed since that milestone.
3. `GetRandomNumber(0,0x96)` @0x73f32ab2a8 (0..149) against `ldr s1,[x21,#0x9c]` (the hero's
   `Att_karma`), `fcmp s1,s0; b.le skip` -- **the card needs hero karma to beat the draw**, so
   its rate is karma/150 per year, not a coin. A kind hero is told about it far more often
   than a nasty one. *(Corrected in REPORT.en.md 109: this test gates the friend-status card,
   not this one.)*

A hero helper @0x73f2f0e1d8 then picks the variant on bit 0: at 0x73f2f03e34 the prison
card (`ScenarioFriendUnfriendPrison`, ctor 0x73f3c59adc) and at 0x73f2f03e74 this one. Both
post themselves with 0x73f24bd170 and the loop moves on to the next friend, so a life with
several friends can be told several times in one year.

The outbound sibling `ScenarioFriendUnfriendOutbound` (ctor 0x73f3c597bc) has exactly one
caller, 0x73f357ba58, inside `LifeInterface.RelationshipItemArrayForFriend` -- the
Relationships tab, the same shape as section 107's outbound rumor card. The yearly chain
never sends it.

### 108.3 The three answers

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` @0x73f3c58d4c opens with a shared preamble: the rendered button text
comes back lower-cased into `x22`, the journal line is built as
`Format(cell 0x5CBC7E8 = "{0} unfriended me.", friend.FullName())`, and the hero's happiness
hit is computed once as `w21 = -5`, or `-4` when `[friend+0x188] YearsFriends < 20`. Dispatch
is two `Contains` tests: "salvage" (cell 0x5CBC7C0) and "insult" (cell 0x5C346A8); anything
else is the middle button.

1. **Try to salvage our friendship.** `ImpactDiscipline(3)` and `ImpactKarma(3)` first, then
   the outcome, which the game decides with three tests: `[friend+0xa8]` (`Att_willpower`)
   against `GetRandomNumber(0,100)`; a second failure when `HeroDeservesToBeUnfriended()`
   @0x73f30e42b8 and willpower is ten or more; and a success window only when the hero's age
   is six or more years past `[friend+0x160]` (`HeroAgeAtLastUnfriendAttempt`). On success the
   friend's relationship slot 0x508 takes **+4**, the log line is "You successfully salvaged
   your friendship with your {0}, {1}.", and the title is one of five. On failure the log line
   is "You tried to salvage your friendship with {0} but were unsuccessful.", the title is one
   of six, and the shared tail applies the -5/-4.
2. **Let {0} go.** No title, no child card, no extra stat call: the hero's happiness takes the
   -5/-4, the friend is dropped, and the journal gets "NAME unfriended me.".
3. **Insult {0} one last time.** `ImpactDiscipline(-4)` and `ImpactKarma(-3)`, the friend's
   relationship slot 0x508 takes **-6**, and the insult comes from
   `SimPerson.GetRandomInsultForGender(friend.EffectiveGender(), 0)` @0x73f2ca2580. The log
   line is "You called {0} {1} as {2} was walking out the door." and the title is one of four.
   Two extras ride along: when the insult contains "fool" (cell 0x5C372A8) a byte is set at
   `[hero+0x70]+0x290`, and every insulted friend's full name is appended to the hero's
   `get_ListPeopleNamesInsulted()` list, which is then handed to `HandleNativeMessage`
   @0x73f4e366f4.

All three converge on a shared tail at 0x73f3c59548: the branch's log line is packed into a
child scenario object (ctor 0x73f2ebf510) linked at `[self+0x128]` -- the same child-link
field sections 102 and 107 use -- then the hero's happiness slot **0x408** takes the -5/-4,
then `friend.Unfriend()` @0x73f30e4240, then `Log(String)` @0x73f380158c with "{name}
unfriended me.", then `RefreshUI()` @0x73f3580f5c. Note that the journal line passed to
`Log` is the same short one on every path; the longer per-branch line travels inside the
child scenario.

The three title pools, read from the cells:

| branch | titles |
| --- | --- |
| salvage, success | Under the bridge / Beef behind us / Forgiven / Can't shake me / This isn't Facebook |
| salvage, failure | Bye then / Unfriended / It's not me it's you / Done for good / Stale mate / So long, partner |
| insult | Nail in the coffin / Done for good / Irreparable / No going back |

"Done for good" is in two pools, which is why a title alone does not identify the branch.

### 108.4 The rows

This card has no table. Every line it shows is a string cell in the binary -- the body
template, the three button labels, the three title pools and the two journal lines -- so
unlike the rest of the family there is nothing to draw a row from and nothing to gate on a
column. The one table it touches is `a16_insults-enc`, for the insult word: 204 rows over
`Insult,Plural,Gender,Clean,Vampire`, with the Gender column reading `both` 122 times, `male`
55 and `female` 28 (`Clean` marks 120 rows and `Vampire` 64, exactly as the port's older
insulter at `src/sim.cpp:4096` already ignores them). The port filters it the way the game
does: the friend's gender first, falling back to the generic rows.

### 108.5 Shortcuts

1. *(Corrected in REPORT.en.md 109: this gate belongs to the friend-status card; the port now
   uses the friend's twelve-year floor and a flat coin, so the counts below are historical.)*
   The karma gate is the game's own. The port keeps `h.karma <= int(unfrRng_.below(150))`
   verbatim, so the rate matches -- and because the port's friend is a drawn slot rather
   than a roster entry, the card can fire again in the same life. That is why the probe sees
   0 to 16 cards per 80-year life (893 over 160 lives, 5.6 per life, making this the port's
   most frequent scenario card). In the game each firing removes one friend from the roster,
   so a hero with one friend gets the card once.
2. `FriendStatus == 1` and the eleven-year `HeroAgeAtLastBestFriendRequest` distance are not
   modelled. The port's drawn friend is always a friend and carries no milestone age, so
   only test 3 survives into the port.
3. The salvage outcome is one coin. The game's three tests -- willpower against a random
   0..100, `HeroDeservesToBeUnfriended()` with its willpower floor of ten, and the six-year
   distance since the last attempt -- collapse into a single `chance(0.5)`.
4. Happiness is always -4 (`pointsForImpact(-4)` = -30). The game's -5 for a friendship of
   twenty years or more needs `[friend+0x188] YearsFriends`, which the port does not track.
5. The "fool" achievement byte, the `[hero+0x3a8]` insult counter, and the
   `ListPeopleNamesInsulted` / `HandleNativeMessage` pair are dropped: the port has no
   achievement, counter or native-message layer.
6. The child scenario is not built. The per-branch log line goes straight into the age-up's
   narrative instead, which is the documented stand-in since section 101 (the port has no
   scenario push).
7. The prison variant is not modelled. `inPrison` heroes skip the card entirely rather than
   receiving `ScenarioFriendUnfriendPrison`.
8. The title is chosen by the branch, not by the card. The real `RefreshScenario` never
   writes a Title field; the port renders the branch's title on the same age-up, which is
   what the next refresh of the card would have shown.

```
=== seed 1  female  United States  age 19  friend Seo Taji (female)
BODY   : Your friend, Seo Taji, has unfriended you.
TITLE  : Irreparable                       (insult lane)
CHOICE : Insult her one last time
LOG    : You called Seo Taji foolhardy as she was walking out the door.
DELTAS : {"discipline": -30, "happiness": -30, "karma": -16}

=== seed 1  female  United States  age 26  friend Larry Wyles (male)
BODY   : Your friend, Larry Wyles, has unfriended you.
TITLE  : This isn't Facebook                (salvage, won)
CHOICE : Try to salvage our friendship
LOG    : You successfully salvaged your friendship with your friend, Larry Wyles.
DELTAS : {"discipline": 16, "karma": 16}

=== seed 1  female  United States  age 27  friend Beyawnce Gnolls (male)
BODY   : Your friend, Beyawnce Gnolls, has unfriended you.
TITLE  : None                               (let go)
CHOICE : Let him go
LOG    : Beyawnce Gnolls unfriended me.
DELTAS : {"happiness": -30}
```

The unfriend pair is half done: the card the hero receives now renders, and the card the
Relationships tab opens about a friend (`ScenarioFriendUnfriendOutbound`) is what is left of
it, together with the prison variant `ScenarioFriendUnfriendPrison`. The family's other open
halves are the status pair, the threesome card, and the four outbound coworker cards
section 105 named.
The full regression after the section: 52 probes at residue 0 (the new `unfrres.py` among them), the residue census at `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`, coverage at `captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107`, the port gap at `ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0` (with `ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound` now counted as rendered), the push script at rc 0 with empty stderr, the persistent test at `unfriend cards: {'cards': 526, 'insult': 192, 'let_go': 174, 'salvage_lost': 92, 'salvage_win': 68}` and the benchmark reaching age 34.

The section's own probe, `unfrres.py`, drives 160 lives and reports `lives 160 / cards 893 / cards per life {0: 9, 1: 23, 2: 11, 3: 25, 4: 12, 5: 13, 6: 7, 7: 8, 8: 9, 9: 6, 10: 16, 11: 7, 12: 1, 13: 5, 14: 2, 15: 2, 16: 4} / branches {insult: 324, let_go: 292, salvage_lost: 157, salvage_win: 120} / hero age at the card min 18 max 79 / runtime 25s / failures 0 / RESIDUE 0 {}`, with the title/branch pairing checked line by line.
**Correction (REPORT.en.md 109).** The gate section 108 attributed to the unfriend card -- the friend's `FriendStatus == 1`, eleven years since `[friend+0x190]` `HeroAgeAtLastBestFriendRequest`, and the hero's karma beating `GetRandomNumber(0,150)` -- belongs to the card the next section ports. That block (`0x73f2f03d28`-`0x73f2f03d88`) is reached only from `0x73f2f03d1c`, the failure exit of the unfriend block, and its success edge (`0x73f2f03df4`, `cmp w0,#5; b.ge`) leads to `0x73f2f03e98`, the `ScenarioFriendStatusInbound` push with `w2 = 2` -- the best-friend request. The unfriend card's own gate is the block at `0x73f2f03c5c`: the friend twelve or older, not already an enemy, the strength/willpower test, `HeroDeservesToBeUnfriended`, and a three-in-four escape for a hero in school. The port's `friendUnfriendYear` now carries the friend's twelve-year floor (the hero's age, the drawn friend having none) and a flat coin on its own stream instead of the karma test, so this section's own numbers move: `tools/test_friend_unfriend.py` at `unfriend cards: {'cards': 73, 'insult': 28, 'let_go': 27, 'salvage_lost': 16, 'salvage_win': 2}` and `unfrres.py` at `lives 160 / cards 123 / cards per life {0: 70, 1: 64, 2: 19, 3: 7} / branches {insult: 50, let_go: 47, salvage_lost: 24, salvage_win: 2} / hero age at the card min 12 max 80 / runtime 29s / failures 0 / RESIDUE 0 {}`. The body template, the three buttons, the two title pools and the point deltas are unchanged.

## 109. The friend-status card: the best-friend request, the enemy, and the gate correction

The yearly friend loop makes three decisions about a friend, and this section ports the third: what the friendship *is*. `ScenarioFriendStatusInbound` (`il2cpp_dump.txt:40922`) carries two cards in one class, chosen by an `Int32` the push site passes in -- a friend asking to become best friends, and a friend turning into an enemy.

### 109.1 The card

`ScenarioFriendStatusInbound` (`.ctor(SimPerson, Int32) @0x73f3c54534`, `RefreshScenario @0x73f3c545d4`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f3c54d7c`, `DismissSelected @0x73f3c55544`, `EmojiString @0x73f3c555b0`) holds `_friend` at `0x170`, the flavour in `_status` at `0x178` and `_narrative` at `0x180`. `RefreshScenario` reads `_status` once and does nothing at all for any value but 2 and 3 (`cmp w8,#3; b.eq 0x73f3c548bc`, `cmp w8,#2; b.ne` to the exit).

The status-3 flavour -- the enemy -- is the family's second mute card, after the spend-time card: no title and no `_choices`, so the only way out is the dismiss button, which tail-calls `Log(String) @0x73f380158c` with `_narrative`. Its body is `Your {0}, {1}, has made you {2} enemy.` (cell `0x5CBC4F8`, literal 50704, `{2}` = `PronounStringForType(1)`, the possessive form) and its narrative `My {0}, {1}, and I became enemies.` (cell `0x5CBC4F0`, literal 30943). It moves the hero's happiness by -3 (vtable slot `0x408`), stamps the friend's `FriendStatus` to 3 (`[friend+0x184]`) and `[friend+0x194]` with the hero's age, runs `ImpactLoyalty(-5) @0x73f30c760c` through the place chain, and bumps two counters on the hero's assets (`[hero+0x70]+0x5c`, and `+0xd8` when `EffectiveGender() == 1`).

The status-2 flavour -- the best-friend request -- is a two-button card. It stamps the friend's `HeroAgeAtLastBestFriendRequest` (`[friend+0x190] = hero age`), looks for a current best friend in the hero's `get_FriendArray() @0x73f3722ebc` (elements with `Alive` and `[+0x184] == 2`, whose name is wrapped through the `{0}` pass-through at cell `0x5CBC510`), and writes the body `Your {0}, {1}, wants to become best friends with you.` (cell `0x5CBC518`, literal 50796) plus the narrative `My {0}, {1}, asked me to become best friends with {2}.` (cell `0x5CBC508`, literal 30947, `{2}` = `PronounStringForType(2)`, the object form). The two buttons are `Agree to become best friends` (cell `0x5CBC4E8`, literal 11005) and `Keep the status quo` (cell `0x5CBC500`, literal 28217).

### 109.2 Who opens it

Both flavours come out of `Life.IncrementAge`'s friend loop, from the same constructor with a different second argument: the enemy at `0x73f2f03c38` (`w2 = 3`) and the request at `0x73f2f03ec0` (`w2 = 2`). Both post through `bl 0x73f24bd170` with the child-link cell `0x5c3a1d8` as the third argument and then continue the loop at `0x73f2f03dfc`, so a friend can produce one of these cards per year and the year can still produce other cards for other friends. The constructor has one further caller, `0x73f29f9998`, inside some other class's `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` -- not wired in the port.

### 109.3 The two answers, and what they move

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` reads the chosen label lower-cased, wraps `_narrative` through the `{0}` parser at cell `0x5C31470`, and dispatches on `Contains(choice, "agree")` (cell `0x5C35048`) and `Contains(choice, "keep")` (cell `0x5C3B578`). The relevant fact about this handler is what it does *not* have: no `Impact*` call at all, on either path.

- **Agree** (`0x73f3c54f04`): the hero's happiness rises by 5 (vtable slot `0x408` with `w1 = +5`), the friend's relationship rises by 5 (slot `0x508`), and every other best friend is demoted -- the handler walks `get_FriendArray()` and writes `FriendStatus = 1` onto each element that was 2, with a -4 relationship move. It then checks `get_ListEnemyTurnedToFriend() @0x73f3d9d9dc` and `HandleNativeMessage() @0x73f4e36a88` for the friend's full name, setting `[hero+0x70]+0x5f8` when the friend had been an enemy, sets the requesting friend's `FriendStatus` to 2, and sets `[hero+0x70]+0x629` through `IsBestFriendAndDoctor() @0x73f3a35f14` and `[hero+0x70]+0x62a` for a classmate best friend of at least 85.0 (`[friend+0x23c]`, `CurrentlyInSchool() @0x73f2f0ccf4`). Eight of those ten effects are achievement or roster bookkeeping the port has no room for; the one that lands is the +5.
- **Keep** (`0x73f3c55118`): the friend's relationship falls by 4 (slot `0x508`) and nothing else happens. No hero stat moves at all.
- Any other label -- including the one the enemy card never offers -- falls straight through to the shared tail at `0x73f3c5545c`, which logs whatever line it built (`Log(String) @0x73f380158c`) and calls `RefreshUI() @0x73f3580f5c`.

### 109.4 The gates, and what they cost the port

The friend loop decides in a fixed order, and the order is the whole story of the previous section's correction.

1. **The enemy decision**, first, at `0x73f2f03b3c`. A friend whose `FriendStatus` is already 3 skips it, as does one the hero's helper `0x73f2f0e1d8` marks; so does a friend whose friendship floats (`[friend+0xc0]`, `[friend+0xc8]`) average below a threshold, and one whose total relationship strength has reached 20.0. What remains is decided by the hero's karma: `Att_karma` (`[hero+0x9c]`) losing to `GetRandomNumber(0,100)` (`0x73f2f03bb8`), or `HeroDeservesToBeUnfriended @0x73f30e42b8` holding (`0x73f2f03bd0`), turns the friend into an enemy. A friend who was *also* the current best friend sets `[hero+0x70]+0x1cc` first (`0x73f2f03c10`).
2. **The unfriend card** (REPORT.en.md 108), if the enemy decision declined: `0x73f2f03c5c`.
3. **The best-friend request**, last, at `0x73f2f03d28`: `FriendStatus == 1` (`ccmp w8,#1,#0,gt` at `0x73f2f03d40`), the hero's age minus `[friend+0x190]` at least 11 (`0x73f2f03d48`-`0x73f2f03d58`), and `Att_karma` beating `GetRandomNumber(0,150)` (`0x73f2f03d70`-`0x73f2f03d88`), after which the shared helper `0x73f2f0e1d8` still gets a veto (`0x73f2f03d8c`). Element `0x73f2f03d1c` is a latch (`w28`) that lets the request test run only for the first friend of the year that reaches it.

The port's card, `friendStatusYear` (`port/src/sim.cpp:25140`, declared at `port/include/bl/sim.h:427` with its own stream `fsRng_` = `seed ^ 0x94d049bb133111eb ^ 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9` at `port/src/sim.cpp:637` and `port/include/bl/sim.h:589`), keeps both flavours and the order they are decided in: a hero at 12 or older, out of prison, then one coin of 0.05 on its own stream, then the enemy flavour when the hero's karma loses to a draw out of 0..99, and otherwise the request when the hero's age minus `life.bestFriendAge` (the port's copy of `HeroAgeAtLastBestFriendRequest`, `port/include/bl/sim.h:89`) is at least 11 and the karma beats a draw out of 0..149. When the request fires, the clock is stamped with the hero's age, exactly as `RefreshScenario` stamps the friend's field.

### 109.5 Shortcuts

1. The friend is a drawn slot, not an object (the family's standing shortcut, REPORT.en.md 102): the port draws `resolve("<friend>")` and a gender on this card's stream, and `GetFriendRelationshipStatusForDisplay` always reads `friend`.
2. The enemy gate's friend-only tests -- the friendship floats `[friend+0xc0]`/`[friend+0xc8]`, total relationship strength against 20.0, the helper bits and `[hero+0x70]+0x1cc` -- are dropped; the karma draw the game makes at `0x73f2f03bb8` is kept, since it reads the hero.
3. The request's `FriendStatus == 1` test and the classmate/doctor achievements are dropped; the eleven-year clock and the karma draw are kept, since both read the hero.
4. The friend's relationship moves (+5 / -4 on slot `0x508`, and the -4 each demoted best friend takes) have no bar to land on.
5. The enemy's `ImpactLoyalty(-5)`, its `FriendStatus = 3` write and its two asset counters are dropped; its hero-side -3 is kept.
6. The two buttons are the player's, so the port draws one on this card's stream -- the friend family's own convention. The keep path therefore moves nothing at all, which is what the game's own handler does when the hero picks it.
7. The order inside one friend's turn differs: the game decides the enemy before it offers the unfriend card, the port after it, so a year in which both would fire shows the unfriend card first (noted at `port/src/sim.cpp:3593`).
8. The enemy flavour's second push site is the same constructor with `w2 = 3`, so a hero who never loses karma to the draw sees only requests; the flavour split in the census below is the port's, not the game's own per-life balance.
