## 110. The prison unfriend card: the same friend, from behind bars

The unfriend family has three members and section 108 ported one of them. This is the
second: the flavour the yearly push picks when the hero is in prison. It shares the push
block with the inbound card, so it is not a second roll -- it is the same roll with a
different card.

### 110.1 The card

`ScenarioFriendUnfriendPrison` (il2cpp_dump.txt:40958) carries the same two fields as its
sibling -- `_friend` at `0x170` (`SimPerson`) and `_narrative` at `0x178`
(`System.String`) -- and three methods: `.ctor(SimPerson) @0x73f3c59adc`, `RefreshScenario`
`@0x73f3c59b08` (158 instructions) and `DismissSelected @0x73f3c59d80` (27). It has no
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`: there is nothing to choose.

`RefreshScenario` stamps the usual card flags, then:

- draws the headline from five literals appended to the shared list and picked by
  `PickRandomFromStringArray @0x73f32b0608` into `[self+0x38]` -- 'Petty prison pal'
  (cell `0x5CBC828`), 'Limited options here' (`0x5CBC838`), 'Squad: -1' (`0x5CBC810`),
  'Lonely behind bars' (`0x5CBC820`) and 'See you later...' (`0x5CBC818`);
- stores the body `Format(cell 0x5CBC830 = "Your {0}, {1}, has unfriended you.",
  FriendRelationshipStatusString(), friend.Name)` at `[self+0x48]` -- byte for byte the
  inbound card's sentence;
- stores the journal line `Format(cell 0x5CBC7E8 = "{0} unfriended me.",
  friend.Name.FullName())` at `[self+0x178]`;
- moves the hero's happiness by `-4`, or `-5` once `[friend+0x188]` `YearsFriends` reaches
  20 (`mov w9,#-5; cmp w10,#0x14; cinc w1,w9,lt` against the hero's slot `0x408`);
- tail-calls `SimPerson.Unfriend() @0x73f30e4240`.

`DismissSelected` is the family's usual one-liner: `Log([self+0x178]) @0x73f380158c`. The
card binds no table row.

### 110.2 Who opens it

The prison card's constructor has exactly one caller in the whole binary: `0x73f2f03e34`,
inside `Life.IncrementAge`'s friend loop -- the same block that builds
`ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound` at `0x73f2f03e74`. One test picks between them, at
`0x73f2f03e08`:

```
bl 0x73f2f0e1d8                     ; SimHero.CurrentlyInPrison()
tbz w0, #0, #0x73f2f03e58
0x73f2f03e34  ScenarioFriendUnfriendPrison        ; the hero is in prison
0x73f2f03e74  ScenarioFriendUnfriendInbound       ; the hero is not
```

Sections 108 and 110 are therefore one push, not two. Everything section 108 documented
about that block -- the friend's twelve-year floor, the strength-versus-willpower test,
`HeroDeservesToBeUnfriended`, the three-in-four escape for a hero in school -- gates this
card too, at the same rate. Before this section the port refused the card outright for a
hero in prison (`h.inPrison` sat in `friendUnfriendYear`'s gate), which is why it could
not appear at all; the gate now runs and the branch answers it.

### 110.3 The rate, and what it costs

There is no table behind the card, so the headline is the whole draw. Because the roll is
shared with the inbound card, a hero in prison simply gets the muted version of it: the
same gate, the same `unfrRng_.chance(0.05)`, one headline from the five, and no buttons.
Over seeds 1..40 x both genders x an 80-year and a 50-year run the port renders 12 prison
cards against 87 unfriend cards -- 0 to 2 per life, hero ages 30 to 75 -- because the card
only exists in the years the hero spends in prison.

### 110.4 Shortcuts

1. The hero's own `h.inPrison` stands in for `SimHero.CurrentlyInPrison()`; the port's
   drawn friend has no status of its own.
2. The step from `-4` to `-5` at `YearsFriends >= 20` is not modelled -- the drawn friend
   carries no `[friend+0x188]` -- so the card always uses the `-4` impact,
   `pointsForImpact(-4)` = `-30`.
3. `SimPerson.Unfriend()` has no analogue: the port's friend is a drawn slot that survives
   every card (the family's standing shortcut), so the same name can be unfriended twice.
4. The card binds no row and draws no dictionary token, so there is nothing to resolve and
   nothing to leak; the body is the inbound card's own sentence with the same drawn name.
5. The headline is drawn on the unfriend stream (`unfrRng_`), so no earlier subsystem's
   sequence moves for a given seed.

A prison card, as the port renders it:

```
AGE    : 30
TITLE  : Petty prison pal
BODY   : Your friend, Ray Lee Carter, has unfriended you.
LOG    : Ray Lee Carter unfriended me.
CHOICE : (none)
DELTAS : {"happiness": -30}

AGE    : 69
TITLE  : Lonely behind bars
BODY   : Your friend, Ram Smith, has unfriended you.
LOG    : Ram Smith unfriended me.
CHOICE : (none)
DELTAS : {"happiness": -30}
```

The card is small and the section is short on purpose: it is the second half of a push
section 108 already ported, and the port answers it in the same method. The family's third
member, `ScenarioFriendUnfriendOutbound` (`@0x73f3c597bc`), the hero's own unfriend opened
from the Relationships tab, stays unwired.

Verification for the section: the port's own test `tools/test_friend_unfriend.py`, extended
with the prison flavour, reads `unfriend cards: {'cards': 87, 'insult': 35, 'let_go': 30,
'prison': 8, 'salvage_lost': 12, 'salvage_win': 2}`; the new probe `/tmp/qdir/fuprres.py`
renders 12 prison cards over 160 lives and reports `failures 0` with `RESIDUE 0 {}`.
The full regression after the section: 54 probes with the new `fuprres.py` at
`rc=0 residue=0 fails=0 events=12`, the residue census at
`distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`, coverage at
`captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107`, the port gap at
`ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0`, the push script at rc 0 with empty stderr, and
the benchmark reaching age 34. That pass also caught one stale probe: `/tmp/qdir/unfrres.py`
matched the unfriend card by its body sentence, and this section's prison card wears the same
sentence with no buttons, so the probe crashed on the empty choice. It now skips buttonless
cards (they belong to this section) and reports `failures 0` again; the corrected probe count
for the family is in section 111.
## 111. The unfriend outbound card: the hero's own half of the ending

Section 108 ported the unfriend push and section 110 its prison flavour, and both are cards
the friend deals the hero. The family's third member runs the other way:
`ScenarioFriendUnfriendOutbound` (`il2cpp_dump.txt:40952`) is what the hero sees after ending
the friendship, and it is the last member of the unfriend set. It has no yearly push at all,
which is why this section is as much about *when* the card can happen as about what it says.

### 111.1 The card

Fields `_friend` at `+0x170` (`SimPerson`) and `_narrative` at `+0x178` (`System.String`).
`.ctor(SimPerson)` `@0x73f3c597bc` (11 instructions) calls `Scenario::.ctor(Boolean)` with
`false` `@0x73f2eb9db8` and stores the friend; `RefreshScenario` `@0x73f3c597e8` is 162
instructions; `DismissSelected` `@0x73f3c59a70` is 27 and tail-calls `Log(String)`
`@0x73f380158c` with `[self+0x178]`. There is no `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`: the card is
dismiss-only, and the dismiss is what writes the journal line.

`RefreshScenario` appends five literals to a fresh `ArrayList` through vtable slot `0x308` in
this order:

| cell | text |
| --- | --- |
| `0x5C32938` | `Begone` |
| `0x5CBC800` (idx 43134) | `They're too toxic` |
| `0x5C30980` (idx 13651) | `Blocked` |
| `0x5CBC808` (idx 46249) | `Weeding 'em out` |
| `0x5CA3AC8` (idx 28685) | `Left on read` |

`PickRandomFromStringArray` `@0x73f32b0608` picks one into `[self+0x38]` (Title). The body is
`Format(String,Object,Object)` `@0x73f52a71cc` with cell `0x5CBC7F8` (idx 48818)
`You have unfriended your {0}, {1}.`, argument 1 the friend's
`FriendRelationshipStatusString` `@0x73f30e169c` and argument 2 the friend's `Name`
(`[friend+0x10]+0x18`); it lands in `[self+0x48]`. The narrative is `Format(String,Object)`
`@0x73f52976b4` with cell `0x5CBC7F0` (idx 25538) `I unfriended {0}.` and the friend's name,
landing in `[self+0x178]`.

### 111.2 What it costs, and who opens it

After the two formats the method moves the hero's happiness slot `0x408` by `w1 = -1`, calls
`ImpactDiscipline(2)` `@0x73f30e4cdc`, and tail-branches to `SimPerson::Unfriend()`
`@0x73f30e4240`. Through `pointsForImpact` that is `-4` happiness and `+8` discipline -- the
mirror image of the inbound card, which costs happiness and pays karma.

A BL census over the constructor, `python3 /tmp/qdir/blcall.py 0x73f3c597bc`, finds exactly one
caller: `0x73f357ba58`, inside `LifeInterface.RelationshipItemArrayForFriend(SimPerson)`
`(+0x183c)`. That is the same method that builds this family's inbound card and the friend
spend-time card (section 106), i.e. the Relationships tab's friend list. The outbound card is
*never* pushed by the year loop; the hero only sees it after choosing to end the friendship,
and the game reaches it through the tab.

### 111.3 How the port reaches it

The port has no Relationships tab, so the ending queues its own follow-up. `Life` gained
`unfriendOutPending`, `unfriendOutFriend` and `unfriendOutFemale` (`include/bl/sim.h:93-95`),
and `friendUnfriendYear` sets all three in both of its ending branches -- the `Let {0} go`
branch at `src/sim.cpp:25084` and the `Insult {0} one last time` branch at `src/sim.cpp:25120`
-- so the follow-up carries the same drawn friend forward. `bool Sim::friendUnfriendOutYear`
(`src/sim.cpp:25162`) runs from `ageUp` immediately after `friendUnfriendYear`
(`src/sim.cpp:3598`), ahead of the friend-status card, and:

1. returns `false` unless the flag is set,
2. clears the flag in the same breath, so one ending produces exactly one card even when a
   louder card eats the next age-up,
3. keeps the family's floor (`h.age < 12`),
4. takes the friend from the queue and falls back to a fresh `resolve("<friend>")` when the
   queue is empty (a save loaded mid-life, or `forcedChoice` replays),
5. draws `kGone[unrOutRng_.below(5)]` for the title, writes the two templates, and sets
   `out.happiness = pointsForImpact(-1)` and `out.discipline = pointsForImpact(2)`.

The title is drawn on a new stream, `unrOutRng_ = seed ^ 0x1d8e4e27c47d124f ^ 0x6a09e667f3bcc909`
(`include/bl/sim.h:603`, initialized at `src/sim.cpp:638`), so no earlier subsystem's sequence
moves for a given seed.

### 111.4 Shortcuts

1. The real trigger is the Relationships tab (`@0x73f357ba58`), which the port does not have.
   The port queues the card from the inbound card's ending instead and renders it on a later
   age-up of the same life, keeping the friend's name and gender. The card itself, its pool,
   its templates and its cost are the game's.
2. `SimPerson::Unfriend()` is dropped: the port's friend is a drawn slot rather than a
   relationship object (the family's standing shortcut), so the same name can be unfriended
   again later in the same life.
3. The card binds no row and draws no dictionary token -- both templates are plain `Format`
   calls with the friend's name -- so there is no table gate to port and nothing to resolve.
4. The floor is the family's `12`, not a number the card itself carries: the real gate lives
   in the year loop that builds the inbound card, and the outbound card inherits it by being
   its follow-up.
5. The pool is five fixed literals with no gender or age variants, so the port keeps them as
   a static array rather than reading them through the metadata cells.

An outbound card, as the port renders it:

```
AGE    : 33
TITLE  : Begone
BODY   : You have unfriended your friend, Arianna Venti.
LOG    : I unfriended Arianna Venti.
CHOICE : (none)
DELTAS : {"discipline": 8, "happiness": -4}

AGE    : 75
TITLE  : Left on read
BODY   : You have unfriended your friend, Ronno Two.
LOG    : I unfriended Ronno Two.
CHOICE : (none)
DELTAS : {"discipline": 8, "happiness": -4}
```

The card is the last member of the unfriend set, and with it the family is closed on both
sides: the push the friend deals the hero (sections 108 and 110) and the ending the hero deals
the friend (this section).

Verification for the section: the port’s own test `tools/test_friend_unfriend.py`, extended
with the outbound flavour, reads `unfriend cards: {'cards': 93, 'insult': 38, 'let_go': 32,
'out': 69, 'prison': 8, 'salvage_lost': 13, 'salvage_win': 2}`; the new probe
`/tmp/qdir/fuoutres.py` renders 111 outbound cards over 160 lives (seeds 1..40, both genders,
80- and 50-year runs) and reports `titles {'Begone': 25, 'Blocked': 24, 'Left on read': 28,
"They’re too toxic": 24, "Weeding ’em out": 10}`, hero age at the card 14..78, `failures 0` and
`RESIDUE 0 {}`. The full regression after the section: 55 probes, every one at `rc=0` and
`residue=0`, with the three unfriend probes at `fuprres.py rc=0 residue=0 fails=0 events=12`,
`fuoutres.py rc=0 residue=0 fails=0 events=111` and the corrected
`unfrres.py rc=0 residue=0 fails=0 events=135`; the residue census at
`distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`, coverage at
`captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107`, the port gap at
`ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0`, the push script at rc 0 with empty stderr, and the
benchmark reaching age 34 unchanged (age 33 happiness delta 17, age 34 karma delta 30).

## 112. The friend weapon encounter: a friend walks in armed

The friend family so far has been a family of social cards. `ScenarioFriendWeaponEncounter`
(`il2cpp_dump.txt:40964-40972`) is its one escalation -- a friend comes into the home of the
hero holding a weapon -- and it is a doorway: whichever of the four replies the hero picks, the
friendship loses the same six points, and the assault family then opens with the weapon the
friend was carrying.

### 112.1 The card

Fields `_friend` at `+0x170` (`SimPerson`), `_weapon` at `+0x178` (`DataWeapon`) and
`_narrative` at `+0x180` (`System.String`). Methods: `.ctor()` `@0x73f3c59dec`, `GetFriend()`
`@0x73f3c59e90`, `RefreshScenario` `@0x73f3c5a1b4` (338 instructions),
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` `@0x73f3c5a6fc` (1187) and `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush`
`@0x73f3c5b988` (33). The last one asks four things: the hero is not null, `Age >= 18`
(`cmp w8,#0x12` / `b.lt`), `!SimHero::CurrentlyInPrison()` `@0x73f2f0e1d8`, and `GetFriend()`
is not null.

`RefreshScenario` builds the body from `DataHub.GetRandomCircumstanceAtHome()` `@0x73f2ce322c`
-- the ~45 `While ...` home phrases the port already carries as `kCircumstanceHomeScenes`
(`src/sim.cpp:1640`) -- and a drawn `DataWeapon` (`il2cpp_dump.txt:15595`: `Name` `+0x10`,
`Plural` `+0x18`, `Verb` `+0x20`, `DangerScore` `+0x28`, `FoundInPrison` `+0x2c`, `Medieval`
`+0x2d`). The table behind it is `gamedata_plain/a16_weapons-enc` -- 88 rows, exactly those
columns. The drawn weapon's own `DangerScore` picks between two templates:

| cell | idx | text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x5CBC860` | 70593 | `{0}, you notice out of the corner of your eye your {1}, {2}, sneaking up on you with {3}.` |
| `0x5CBC840` | 70594 | `{0}, you turn around to discover your {1}, {2}, standing there with {3}.` |

`{1}` is the relationship word of the friend, `{2}` its name, `{3}` the article form of the
weapon (`AddIndefiniteArticleToString` over `Name`), and the assembled body lands in
`[self+0x48]` through `Format(String,Object[])` `@0x73f52a7254`. The narrative in `[self+0x180]`
is a second pass, `Format(String,Object,Object,Object)` `@0x73f52a7210` with cell `0x5CBC858`
(idx 30976) `My {0}, {1}, entered my home with {2}.`. `RefreshScenario` never writes
`[self+0x38]`, so the card presents no title of its own: the headline the player sees is the
reply the branch picks.

The four buttons are appended through vtable slot `0x308` as `ScenarioChoice(String,Boolean,
Boolean)` `@0x73f2eb9c50`: `Reason with {0}` (`0x5CBC848`, the pronoun filled in by
`PronounStringForType(2)`), `Beg for forgiveness` (`0x5CBC850`), `Argue with {0}` (`0x5C386C8`)
and `Run for my life` (`0x5C3CE08`).

### 112.2 The four replies, dispatched by label

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` never reads a choice index. It lowercases the tapped label
(`[self+0x10]`) and `Contains`-tests one word per block: `reason` (`0x5C77FA0`, idx 64327),
`forgiveness` (`0x5CBC8F0`, idx 59224), `argue` (`0x5C346B8`, idx 54365) and `run`
(`0x5C3CEF8`). A label that matches none of the four falls into the `FillDictionary` throw
helper `@0x73f3c5b974`.

| button | happiness | ImpactDiscipline | reply pool | log line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Reason with {0}` | -3 | 2 | five lines, `0x5CBC8E0`..`0x5CBC890` | `0x5CBC8A8` (idx 47844) `You attemped to reason with {0}!` |
| `Beg for forgiveness` | -5 | -3 | five lines, `0x5CBC918`..`0x5CBC898` | `0x5CBC8F8` (idx 47884) `You begged {0} for forgiveness!` |
| `Argue with {0}` | -2 | -3 | four lines, `0x5CBC870`..`0x5CBC8B0` | `0x5CBC8E8` (idx 49902) `You {0} {1}!` |
| `Run for my life` | -4 | -3 | five + five lines, `0x5CAFC90`..`0x5CAFD00` and `0x5CAFD68`..`0x5CAFD20` | `0x5CAFCF0` (idx 49172) `You ran for your life and got away from {0}!` / `0x5CAFD08` (idx 49174) `You ran for your life but {0} caught you!` |

The replies, in the order of each pool. Reason: `Woah, take it easy`, `It's me remember?`,
`This isn't you`, `Whatcha got there...`, `*nervous chuckle*`. Forgiveness: `It's not worth it`,
`Think about your future`, `I'm on my knees`, `Spare me`, `Let's use our words`. Argue:
`Uncalled for`, `What's gotten into you`, `Put that away`, `Are you crazy?!`. The away pool of
the run arm: `Dodge, duck, dip, dive, & dodge`, `Too close for comfort`, `Wild goose chase`,
`No fight, just flight`, `Run. Don't stop. Go!`; the caught pool: `Back to the wall`,
`Out of options`, `Cat & mouse`, `Dead end`, `Nowhere to go`. Through `pointsForImpact` the four
pairs are -16/+8, -50/-16, -8/-16 and -30/-16. The `attemped` in the reason line is the spelling
of the game itself (idx 47844), not a transcription slip.

The argue line is the one line that is not a constant: `DataHub.GetRandomArguerAction`
`@0x73f2ca2120` supplies the verb, so `You {0} {1}!` reads `You scratched her!`, `You punched
him!` and so on, with the object pronoun in the second slot.

Every block then jumps to the same tail (`b 0x73f3c5b824`): `mov w1,#-6` into the relationship
slot of the friend at `+0x508` -- the friendship takes the same hit whatever the hero says --
then `ScenarioAttackInbound::.ctor(SimPerson,DataWeapon)` `@0x73f3cd79ec` pushed as a child at
`[self+0x128]`, then `Log(Fmt1)` `@0x73f380158c` and `RefreshUI()` `@0x73f3580f5c`. The weapon
the friend walked in with is the weapon the assault family then swings.

### 112.3 How the port reaches it

`bool Sim::friendWeaponYear` (`src/sim.cpp:25365`) runs as the last of the friend cards, wired
in `ageUp` right after `friendStatusYear` (`src/sim.cpp:3618`), and draws on its own stream
`fwRng_ = seed ^ 0x9fb21c651e98df25 ^ 0x6a09e667f3bcc909` (`include/bl/sim.h:603`, initialized
at `src/sim.cpp:638`), so no sequence of another subsystem moves for a given seed. In order:

1. `forcedChoice > 3` returns false, so the harness can only ask for one of the four buttons;
2. the three gates of the class itself: `h.age >= 18`, not in prison, a friend;
3. a flat `fwRng_.chance(0.05)` coin;
4. a weapon drawn uniformly over the `a16_weapons-enc` rows whose `Weapon` cell is non-empty
   and which are not flagged `Found in Prison` (the gate has already refused a hero in prison);
5. the body template from `wt.num(wrow, "Danger") <= 2.0`, with `{0}` from `circumstanceHome()`
   and `{3}` from `withArticle(weaponName, true) + weaponName`;
6. the reply: `forcedChoice` when the harness gave one, else `fwRng_.below(4)`;
7. the reply pool of that branch as the title, its button text, its `pointsForImpact` pair and
   its own log line as the narrative.

The argue arm takes its verb from the `Past Verb` column of `a16_custom-attack-actions-enc`
weighted by `Commonness Score` (`weightedPickOf`, `src/sim.cpp:25469-25478`); the run arm draws
`fwRng_.chance(0.5)` for the outcome and then one of its two five-line pools
(`src/sim.cpp:25479-25501`). The function ends with the shared tail left unmodelled
(`src/sim.cpp:25502-25507`).

template with a verb the argue arm drew; the last two are the `Danger <= 2` sneaking template
across the two run outcomes, one of each.

### 112.4 Shortcuts

1. `.ctor()` `@0x73f3c59dec` has no caller inside BitLife -- a generic factory instantiates the
   class -- so there is no push site to read and the port cannot derive the rate of this card
   the way sections 104-111 derive theirs. The flat 0.05 is the coin of the port; the
   instrumentation measured 22 cards in 414 age-ups while it was in place, and the 121 cards of
   the probe in 160 lives sit at the same scale.
2. `GetRandomArguerAction` (`@0x73f2ca2120`) is not pinned, so the port substitutes the
   `Past Verb` column of `a16_custom-attack-actions-enc` weighted by `Commonness Score`: the
   right kind of word, drawn from a substitute table.
3. The forgiveness block pushes a child `Scenario(String,String,Scenario)` `@0x73f2ebf510` whose
   labels are `Mercy! Mercy!` (`0x5CBC928`, idx 30003) and `Finally, some sense` (`0x5CBC910`,
   idx 20187); the port writes the reply and log line of the branch alone.
4. The shared tail is not modelled: the port has no friend object to move by -6 and no
   `ScenarioAttackInbound` to push, so the weapon encounter does not hand off to the assault
   family and the -6 is not charged. This is the mirror of the sections 108 and 110 shortcut,
   where the friend is a drawn slot and not an object.
5. The reason branch shows its reply through `BarGraph(String,Single)` `@0x73f2ec31f8` under the
   label `{0} Receptiveness` (`0x5C44C50`, idx 69689) -- a widget the port does not render -- so
   the reply becomes the headline of the card instead.
6. The narrative `My {0}, {1}, entered my home with {2}.` is not carried; the journal of the
   port keeps the log line of the branch, as it does for every card in this family.
7. The relationship word is always `friend`: `GetFriendRelationshipStatusForDisplay` reads the
   `FriendStatus` field of the friend, which the drawn slot of the port does not carry (the
   standing shortcut of the family, sections 105-111).
8. The gender of the friend is its own coin, independent of the name the `<friend>` pool drew
   (the pattern of the family, `src/sim.cpp:23846` and the six cards that follow it), so a
   female name can carry `him` in the log line.

The card closes the inbound side of the friend family: sections 108 and 110 dealt the end of
the friendship to the hero, 111 let the hero deal it out, and this is the member of the family
that hands off to another family entirely. It is also the first ported card to read
`gamedata_plain/a16_weapons-enc`, the table the assault family needs in full.

Verification for the section: the port’s own test `tools/test_friend_unfriend.py`, extended

'weapon_forgive': 15, 'weapon_reason': 13, 'weapon_run_away': 20, 'weapon_run_caught': 15}` --
the unfriend counts move against the section 111 run because the new card consumes draws from

{'Argue with her': 16, 'Argue with him': 18, 'Beg for forgiveness': 21, 'Reason with her': 9,
'Reason with him': 8, 'Run for my life': 49}`, cards per life `{0: 84, 1: 43, 2: 23, 3: 8,
4: 2}`, 34 distinct weapons with `horse whip` at 9, hero age at the card 18..78, `failures 0`
and `RESIDUE 0 {}`. The full regression after the section: 56 probes, every one at `rc=0` and
`residue=0` (the `idres.py` row prints its own summary format, `residue=? fails=- events=?`, in

## 113. The assault card: the friend who walked in armed comes back swinging

Section 112 ended on a shortcut. The friend weapon encounter's shared tail -- the block
every one of its four replies jumps into -- moves the friend's relationship slot by -6
and links a second scenario at [self+0x128]. That second scenario is
ScenarioAttackInbound (il2cpp_dump.txt:41670), and section 112 could only document the
link. This section ports it, in the one shape the encounter actually produces.

ScenarioAttackInbound is a large class with nine constructors -- one each for a
SimPerson plus an Int32 and some strings, a SimSecretAgent, a SimClassmate, a
SimSibling, a SimPrisoner, a SimPerson plus a DataWeapon, a DataHitman plus a
DataWeapon, a SimDealerStreetPerson, and a SimPerson plus a list of strings -- and their
cards are all titled, worded and priced differently. The one the friend weapon
encounter links is .ctor(SimPerson,DataWeapon) @0x73f3cd79ec, and that is the one this
section ports. The other eight keep their shortcut entries in 113.4.

### 113.1 The card

The class carries the attacker in every form it can take: _whoString 0x178 and
_whoStringNarrative 0x180 (the pre-built caller phrases), _attackerIsBully 0x188,
_attackerIsSibling 0x189 and _attackerIsPrisoner 0x18a (three flags), _weapon 0x190
(DataWeapon), _bully 0x198, _friend 0x1a0, _hitman 0x1a8, _attackerGender 0x1b0,
_person 0x1b8, _heroDeathOverride 0x1c0, _secretAgent 0x1c8 and _streetPerson 0x1d0.
The friend overload fills exactly five of them and then builds its own buttons:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| title [0x38] | Aggravated Assault (cell 0x5CBF4E0) |
| _person [0x1b8], _friend [0x1a0], the attacker slot [0x60] | the SimPerson it was handed |
| _attackerGender [0x1b0] | that person's own gender field |
| _weapon [0x190] | the DataWeapon it was handed |
| _whoString [0x178] | String.Format(Your {0}, {1},) over the relationship word and the name |
| _whoStringNarrative [0x180] | String.Format(My {0}, {1},) over the same two |
| [0x110] | 1 (the card is a charged scenario) |

The three buttons go in through the ScenarioChoice(String,Boolean,Boolean) constructor
@0x73f2eb9c50, appended to the list at [0x108]:

| label | cell |
|---|---|
| Run away from {0} | 0x5CBF4A0 (the object pronoun comes from PronounStringForType(person,2,null)) |
| Fight back | 0x5CBF4B8 |
| Call the police on {0} | 0x5CBF4B0 (same pronoun) |

The sentence itself is not built in the constructor; RefreshScenario @0x73f3cd80c8
composes it from the two who-strings, the weapon's own verb and its article form.
Two literal pairs are involved: cell 0x5C3CDC0 ('{0} {1} you{2}!') writes the card body
at [0x48] and the first-person twin cell 0x5C3CDA8 ('{0} {1} me{2}!') writes the
narrative at [0x170]; {0} is _whoString for the body and _whoStringNarrative for the
narrative, {1} is DataWeapon.Verb, and {2} is String.Format(cell 0x5C3CDB0, ' with {0}')
over DataWeapon::GetNameWithIndefiniteArticle() @0x73f2e61780. A weapon that carries no
verb falls back to the literal 'attacked' (cell 0x5C3CDC8). The card therefore reads
Your friend, Sabrina Stonemason, hit you with a prosthetic leg! on screen and
My friend, Sabrina Stonemason, hit me with a prosthetic leg! in the log.

### 113.2 The three replies, dispatched by their own label text

ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f3cd9470 opens by logging the narrative it was carrying
([self+0x170] through LifeLog::Log @0x73f380158c), then lowercases the chosen label
(System.String::ToLower @0x73f52aa938) and tests it with Contains @0x73f52aafdc against
one word per arm: 'run away' (cell 0x5CBF578), 'fight' (cell 0x5C3F728) and 'police'
(cell 0x5C3CED0). A fourth Contains site answers the prison guard word, which only the
prisoner constructor's cards can reach. Every arm ends by jumping to one shared tail
0x73f3cd9ac0, which loads the LifeLog singleton and tail-calls Log with whatever message
that arm left in x20 -- an arm that writes no message logs nothing at all.

| button | impact | log line |
|---|---|---|
| Run away from {0} | ImpactDiscipline(1), or ImpactDiscipline(-3) when _attackerIsBully | I ran away from {0}. (cell 0x5CBF580) |
| Fight back | ImpactDiscipline(4) | none -- the arm leaves the empty string in the log register |
| Call the police on {0} | ImpactKarma(-1) | three-way split on GetRandomNumber(0,10) |

The police arm rolls GameReference::GetRandomNumber(0,10) @0x73f32ab2a8 and then
branches twice: a roll of 2 or less takes the arrest line (cell 0x5CBF5D0, 'I called the
police on {0} and {1} was arrested.'), 3 through 7 takes the flight line (cell 0x5CBF568,
'I called the police on {0} but {1} fled before they arrived.'), and 8 or more takes the
warning line (cell 0x5CBF5B0, 'I called the police on {0}. The police warned me for
wasting their time.'). The three outcomes move nothing but that single karma point.
The fight arm instead builds a ScenarioCustomAttack over the friend
(.ctor(SimPerson) @0x73f3cda45c) and chains it at [self+0x128], so a fight leads
straight into the custom attack card. The run-away arm closes with an obituary colour
line rather than a life log line: 'Friends describe {0} as sometimes cowardly.'
(cell 0x5CBF5C0) through ObituaryGenerator::AddColorString @0x73f3803dc0.

### 113.3 How the port reaches it

The encounter that hands the assault its victim and its weapon is section 112's card, so
the queue lives on the Life: attackInPending, attackInFriend, attackInFemale,
attackInWeapon and attackInVerb (port/include/bl/sim.h:101-105). Section 112 used to end
by documenting the unmodelled child push; it now fills those five fields instead
(port/src/sim.cpp:25519-25523) and returns. The relationship move stays a shortcut
because the port's relationship model is a single value rather than the game's slot
array.

The card itself is Sim::attackInboundYear (port/src/sim.cpp:25554, declared at
port/include/bl/sim.h:465), called last in the friend family right after the encounter
(port/src/sim.cpp:3624), and it behaves like this:

1. It refuses anything that is not queued: if attackInPending is false, or a forced
   choice above 2 is asked for, the year belongs to another card and the function
   returns false without consuming the queue.
2. It clears the queue on entry, then re-reads the age gate the encounter imposed -- the
   hero must still be 18 or older -- so a queued assault cannot surface in a later
   childhood.
3. The friend, the gender, the weapon and the verb all come from the queue rather than
   from a fresh draw, which is what makes the card traceable to the encounter that
   armed it. The weapon's article form is rebuilt with withArticle(weaponName, true) +
   weaponName, the same helper pair section 112 uses.
4. The title is Aggravated Assault and the body is the second-person sentence over the
   friend, the verb and the weapon, exactly as RefreshScenario composes it.
5. The button is forced when the harness asks for one and otherwise drawn from the
   card's own stream aiRng_ (port/include/bl/sim.h:629, initialised at
   port/src/sim.cpp:640). The three arms write the label, the impact through
   pointsForImpact and the narrative: run away gives discipline +1 with the first-person
   line, fight back gives discipline +4 and no narrative (the fight arm's log line is the
   button itself, which is what the empty message in the game produces), and the police
   arm gives karma -1 and then rolls its own aiRng_.below(10) for the three outcomes.
   pointsForImpact (port/src/sim.cpp:3877) maps 1 to 4, 4 to 30 and -1 to -4.

### 113.4 Shortcuts

1. Only the ctor(SimPerson,DataWeapon) overload is ported. The eight others -- the
   sibling, bully, prisoner, secret agent, hitman, street person, string-list and
   person-plus-int attackers -- never appear, with their own attacker selection,
   wording and prices.
2. RefreshScenario's own attacker selection (the bully, sibling and prisoner flags, the
   Random.value draw that sends an unsupported card to the throw helper, and the
   secret-agent path behind [self+0x1c8]) is not modelled: the port only ever produces
   the card the encounter queues.
3. The weapon fallback is not modelled either. In the game a constructor that arrives
   without a weapon asks DataHub::GetRandomAssaultWeaponAndIsInPrison(
   SimHero::CurrentlyInPrison()) for one; the port always has the encounter's weapon.
4. The damage and the death test are dropped. The game rolls GetRandomNumber(0,0xc)
   when the weapon's DangerScore is 4 or above (GetRandomNumber(0,0x14) on the hitman
   path), compares it against the DangerScore, honours the Medieval flag at [weapon+0x2d]
   and lets _heroDeathOverride [self+0x1c0] suppress the whole test. The port's hero
   cannot be killed by this card, and the assault moves no health.
5. The miss phrasing and the assassination phrasing are unmodelled: cells 0x5CBF538 and
   0x5CBF508 ('... but missed!') and the four 'for trying to assassinate {3}' lines
   belong to sub-variants the friend overload never selects, so every ported card wears
   the plain '{0} {1} you{2}!' wording.
6. The fight arm's child card is documented rather than pushed: the game links a
   ScenarioCustomAttack over the friend at [self+0x128], and the port stops at the
   discipline price.
7. The prison guard arm, its ImpactKarma(-2) and its 'I snitched on {0} to the prison
   guards.' line stay out of the port, because only the prisoner constructor's cards can
   reach that Contains site.
8. The obituary colour lines ('Friends describe {0} as sometimes cowardly.' and
   'Friends say {0} was tramautized for life after once being attacked with {1}.') are
   not written to the port's obituary, and the -6 relationship move the encounter's tail
   performs is still not modelled.

A few cards from a seeded run:

```
seed 2 female age 52  Aggravated Assault
  Your friend, Sabrina Stonemason, hit you with a prosthetic leg!
  [Fight back]                 discipline +30
seed 2 female age 57  Aggravated Assault
  Your friend, Mary Overwood, shot you with a BB gun!
  [Call the police on him]     I called the police on him and he was arrested.
                               karma -4
seed 3 female age 71  Aggravated Assault
  Your friend, Hung Cook, blew up you with a homemade bomb!
  [Call the police on her]     I called the police on her but she fled before they
                               arrived.   karma -4
```

The card also shows the game's own grammar: a multi-word verb such as 'blew up' lands
between the attacker phrase and the object, so the sentence reads 'blew up you with a
homemade bomb'. The port keeps that wording rather than repairing it.

Verification for the section: tools/test_friend_unfriend.py covers the assault card as
well, so the family regression now drives 113's three buttons from the encounter the
previous section queues: the assault's friend must be one the same life already saw walk
in armed, the weapon and its verb are read back against a16_weapons-enc (an in-prison
row is never drawn and the article agrees with the vowel), and each branch asserts its
own label, narrative and deltas. It reports `unfriend cards: {'attack': 74,
'attack_fight': 28, 'attack_police': 23, 'attack_run': 23, 'cards': 94, 'insult': 40,
'let_go': 31, 'out': 67, 'prison': 6, 'salvage_lost': 15, 'salvage_win': 2, 'weapon':
80, 'weapon_argue': 20, 'weapon_forgive': 15, 'weapon_reason': 13, 'weapon_run_away':
20, 'weapon_run_caught': 12}` at rc=0. The section's own probe, /tmp/qdir/aires.py,
drives blsim over seeds 1..40 x both genders x an 80-year and a 50-year run (160 lives)
and found 108 assault cards, every single one carried from an encounter the same life had

40, 2: 31, 3: 2}`, `branches {'Call the': 31, 'Fight back': 42, 'Run away': 35}`, titles
all 'Aggravated Assault', 31 distinct weapons (horse whip 10, boomerang 8, prosthetic leg

## 114. The threesome: the friend who will not be left out

### 114.1 The card

ScenarioFriendThreesome (il2cpp_dump.txt:40936) is the friend family's one adult
card, and the only card in the family the game itself offers as a random push:
obs_corpus/scenario_registry.json lists it under `candidates` with a limit of
fourteen, the same list that carries FriendAdvice (70), FriendDrug (14) and
FriendWeaponEncounter (7). The outbound half of the family (the status card, the
unfriend outbound card) is absent from that list because the relationships UI
pushes it, not the scenario chain.

The card carries `_friend` at 0x170 and `_threesomeLover` at 0x178, wears the
title 'Threesome' (cell 0x5C5DBF8), and its constructor takes no argument:
`.ctor() @0x73f3c575c8` calls `GetFriend() @0x73f3c57630` and stores the result in
both `_friend` and the generic scenario person slot at [0x60]. GetFriend walks
`Life.FriendArray` @0x73f3722ebc and keeps a friend who
`LivesInSamePlaceAsHero` @0x73f30e6b28 and whose
`GetTotalHeroRelationshipStrength` @0x73f30d284c reaches 65.0f (the method's own
`mov w24,#0x42820000`).

`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f3c58a1c` asks, in its own order, for a
hero, an age of eighteen or more, `!SimHero::CurrentlyInPrison()` @0x73f2f0e1d8,
a Sexuality field at [hero+0x24] no greater than one, and a friend. There is no
repeat or cooldown test inside the class: the registry's own limit of fourteen is
what paces it.

`RefreshScenario @0x73f3c579e4` then generates the third person rather than
taking one: `PersonGenerator`
.GenerateLoverCandidateOfGenderAndSexualityAndOverrideAgeToAndOverrideBirthplaceToAndMustBeSingleAndCanBeCustom
@0x73f38101d8, handed the sex opposite the hero's own `EffectiveGender`
@0x73f30dbc30, the hero's sexuality, and `GetRandomNumber(0, 10)` @0x73f32ab2a8
as an age override off a floor of eighteen -- the friend-lover card's own reading
of the same generator (src/sim.cpp 24666). The result lands in `_threesomeLover`.

The body is assembled in two halves. The first names the hero's own partner: cell
0x5CBC6F8 'Even though you {0}, ' over one of three cells -- 0x5CBC6D8 'are married
to {0}', 0x5CBC6E8 'are engaged to {0}', 0x5CBC6E0 'have a {0}' -- picked by
`SimLover::RelationshipStatusString` @0x73f30d35a0 lowered with
`String::ToLower` @0x73f52aa938, whose {0} is `SimPersonName::FullName`
@0x73f2fc62bc. A single hero leaves that half empty and the sentence opens on the
template's own lower-case 'you', which `GameReference::CapitalizeFirstLetterOfSentenceString`
@0x73f32afedc then capitalizes. The second half is the template itself, cell
0x5CBC6F0 '{0}you and your {1}, {2}, have an opportunity to have a threesome with
{3} named {4}.' through `String::Format(String, Object[])` @0x73f52a7254, written
to [self+0x48]: {1} the word `FriendRelationshipStatusString` @0x73f30e169c
returns ('friend'), {2} the friend GetFriend picked, {3} `DataHub`
.GetGenericTermForPersonInPlace @0x73f2d0dd40 ->
`GetGenericTermForPersonOfGenderAndAge` @0x73f2d0df00 behind
`GameReference::AddIndefiniteArticleToString` @0x73f32aee9c, and {4} the third
person's own full name. A `ScenarioBarGraph` @0x73f2ec31f8 labelled '{0} Looks'
(cell 0x5CA29E0) goes to [self+0xb8], and the two buttons, 'No way!' (cell
0x5C4B360) and "I'm in" (cell 0x5CA8F70), are appended as
`ScenarioChoice(String, Boolean, Boolean)` @0x73f2eb9c50.

### 114.2 The two replies dispatched by their own label text

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f3c57fa4` first writes the card's first-person
narrative through `LifeLog::Log(System.String)` @0x73f380158c, then lowers the
selected label with `ToLower` @0x73f52aa938 and tests it with `Contains`
@0x73f52aafdc: "i'm in" (cell 0x5CBC298) first, 'no way' (cell 0x5CBC080)
second. A label that matches neither falls into the shared tail, which logs
whatever message the dispatch left in its register.

- **No way!** moves the friend's relationship slot, the vtable slot at 0x508,
  by -2 (`mov w1,#-2` then `blr x9`) and runs `ImpactDiscipline(3)`
  @0x73f30e4cdc on the hero, which is +16 attribute points through
  AttributeAdjustmentPointsForImpactScore. The journal sentence is cell 0x5CBC708
  'I turned down an opportunity to have a threesome with my {0}, {1}, and {2}.'
  through `String::Format(String, Object, Object, Object)` @0x73f52a7210.
- **I'm in** runs `ImpactKarma(-4)` @0x73f30e4bfc and then `ImpactDiscipline(-4)`,
  -30 points each. It then rolls `GetRandomNumber(0, 150)` and may push a child
  `ScenarioLoverArgues` @0x73f3da31b8 at [self+0x128] or, through
  `SimPregnancy`
  `.GetResultingPregnancyForMotherAndFatherAndTypeAndAssignToMother` @0x73f2fd4438,
  a `ScenarioPregnancy` -- the partner's own scene, drawn from the third person
  the card generated. It ends with two `ScenarioBarGraph` draws (labels 'Your
  Enjoyment' cell 0x5C34A68 and '{0} Enjoyment' cell 0x5C3DAE0), the child
  `Scenario` @0x73f2ebf510 titled 'Kinky' (cell 0x5CBC720) carrying cell 0x5CBC718
  'You and your {0}, {1}, had a threesome with {2}.', the obituary line 'Rumors
  suggest {0} was wild in bed.' (cell 0x5CBC700) through
  `ObituaryGenerator::AddColorString` @0x73f3803dc0, and the first-person
  narrative cell 0x5CBC710 'My {0}, {1}, and I had a threesome with {2}.'

### 114.3 How the port reaches it

`bool Sim::friendThreesomeYear(Life& life, AgeUp& out, int forcedChoice)`
(port/src/sim.cpp:25655) is the friend family's sixth card and the last one tried:

1. `if (forcedChoice > 1) return false;` -- the card owns two buttons, so a forced
   choice beyond them is not its turn. `out = AgeUp()` before any field is filled.
2. The class's gate, in the class's order: `h.age < 18 || h.inPrison` closes the
   card. The Sexuality test at [hero+0x24] has no counterpart in the port, exactly
   as on the friend-lover card, and is documented as a shortcut.
3. The push coin. The class carries no rate of its own -- the registry's candidate
   list is what pushes it, at most fourteen times in a life -- so the port draws
   `ftRng_.chance(0.05)` on the family's own stream, which moves no other
   subsystem's sequence for a given seed.
4. The friend: `resolve("<friend>")` for the name, a coin for the gender, and the
   relationship word 'friend', as the family's other cards do.
5. The third person: the sex opposite the hero's own, `18 + ftRng_.below(10)` for
   the age, and a name out of the port's name pools. The term is the bucket word
   for that age and gender -- 'little girl'/'little boy', 'girl'/'boy', 'young
   woman'/'young man', 'woman'/'man' -- with `withArticle` writing the article.
6. The hero's own partner, when the life has one: 'Even though you are married to
   <name>, ' / 'Even though you are engaged to <name>, ' / 'Even though you have a
   girlfriend, ', drawn from the hero's relationship fields.
7. The body (with the capitalize step the class applies to the assembled
   sentence), the title 'Threesome', and the two arms: 'No way!' with
   `pointsForImpact(3)` of discipline, "I'm in" with `pointsForImpact(-4)` of
   karma and of discipline, each arm writing its own journal sentence.

### 114.4 Shortcuts

1. The Sexuality test at [hero+0x24] is absent: the port's hero carries no
   sexuality field, and the friend-lover card already skips the same test
   (src/sim.cpp 24642).
2. The push rate is the port's own. The class has none; the game's registry limit
   of fourteen draws per life is what the 0.05 coin stands in for.
3. `GetFriend`'s two filters are absent: the port's friend slot has no place of
   residence and no 0-100 relationship score, so any drawn friend qualifies.
4. The third person is drawn from the port's own name pools at eighteen plus 0..9
   rather than through PersonGenerator, which also weighs birthplace, single
   status and custom-name flags.
5. The generic term is the age bucket's plain word. The game picks among bucket
   alternatives with `GetRandomNumber(0, 4)` ('dude', 'chick', 'young lady'), and
   the drawn age never leaves the 18-29 bucket in this port.
6. The partner half of the body reads the hero's own fields. `RelationshipStatusString`
   is asked for a full clause by the game and for a status word by the port, so the
   three cells are matched on the status the port stores ('married', 'dating').
7. The friend's relationship move of -2 (vtable slot 0x508) is not modelled: the
   port's friend relationship is a table, not a number.
8. The acceptance drops its children: no `ScenarioLoverArgues`, no
   `ScenarioPregnancy` from the 0-150 roll, no child 'Kinky' scenario, no bar
   graphs, and no obituary line. The stat move and the journal sentence are what
   the section keeps.
9. The card draws no bar graph at all, so the looks pairing the game shows beside
   the body is absent.

## 115. The paywall marker: the two captured entries the port does not render

Every captured card that carries content is now replayed. Two entries were still
counted as unrecovered, and this section closes them: they are not cards. Both are
`ScenarioMiniPaywall` objects, and both are empty.

### 115.1 What the captured objects carry

The class (il2cpp_dump.txt:56559) is the game's shop trigger. Its fields are the
offer, not a scene: `_gameData MiniGameDataMiniPaywall 0x170`, `_paywallType 0x178`,
`_origin 0x17c`, `_isFeatured 0x180`, `_purchaseFollowUpScenario 0x188`,
`webShopType 0x190` and `ThePregnancy 0x198`. Its methods are the two ctors
(`.ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)` @0x73f2ebd27c and
`.ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,Scenario,System.Boolean)` @0x73f2ebd2d0),
`RefreshScenario @0x73f2ebd32c`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f2ebe95c` and
`PurchaseWebShop @0x73f2ebf254`.

The two rows the capture saw carry nothing for a port to render:

```
age 17   cls ScenarioMiniPaywall   title null   body null   choices [""]
age 109  cls ScenarioMiniPaywall   title null   body null   choices []
```

The age-17 object ships a single button whose label is the empty string; the
age-109 object ships no button at all. Neither wears a title or a body, and no
`gamedata_plain` table backs them -- `ls gamedata_plain | grep -i paywall` is
empty, because the text of a shop offer lives in the game's own UI-side
`MiniGameData`, not in a scenario table.

### 115.2 Why the port leaves them out

A scenario row is rendered from its table: title, body, and the button labels a
choice handler dispatches on. These two objects have none of the three, so there
is no row to render and no branch to take -- the card is a marker the UI layer
consumes, and the port has no shop surface for it to open. Rendering an invented
paywall card would be less faithful than leaving the trigger alone.

### 115.3 What changed in tools/coverage.py

The tool counted such an entry as unrecovered, which made the headline read
`109 captured / 107 recoverable` and left the last two looking like port gaps.
It now classifies an entry as contentless when it has no title, no body and no
non-empty button label, and prints them as their own line:

```
captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107
contentless entries: 2 -- ScenarioMiniPaywall x2
```

The headline line is unchanged, so every earlier section's quoted count still
reads the same; the second line accounts for the difference. A choice label is
read from the `label`/`Label`/`text` key when a choice arrives as a dict and from
the bare string otherwise, because one of the two captured objects ships its
button as an empty string.

Verification for the section: tools/coverage.py now prints
`captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107` followed by
`contentless entries: 2 -- ScenarioMiniPaywall x2`, which closes the accounting --
109 captured = 107 replayed + 2 contentless, with no content-bearing entry left
unrecovered. /tmp/qdir/portgap.py still reads
`ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0`, because it walks the same push corpus
and the two paywall rows produce no push entry at all. The batch, the family
regression and the bench are untouched by the tool change: the changed file is
`tools/coverage.py` alone, and the probe suite reads the same push corpus it
already did.
## 116. The unprofessional supervisor: the workplace's second card, four answers to a boss who is also a colleague

The workplace family is the largest connected block of cards in the game, and the
coworker half of it is already replayed (section 105). The supervisor half is the
other half of the same roster: same office, same colleagues, a different subject.
`ScenarioSupervisorUnprofessional` (il2cpp_dump.txt:55202) is the only real class
behind the three registry rows `ScenarioSupervisorSeduce`, `ScenarioSupervisorSocialize`
and `ScenarioSupervisorUnprofessional` -- the registry lists the row names, the
assembly has one class -- and this section wires it.

### 116.1 The class and its gate

The class extends `Scenario` and carries two fields: `_supervisor SimCoworker 0x170`
and `_narrative 0x178`. Its methods are the two ctors (a bare `.ctor() @0x73f2e359f8`
and one that takes the supervisor), `RefreshScenario @0x73f2e34c00`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f2e35338` and
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f2e3583c`.

The gate is that eligibility method, and it is the strictest one in the family --
the card is about a boss, so the hero must actually have one:

- `SimHero::CurrentlyHasAJob() @0x73f2f0e040` or
  `SimHero::CurrentlyInTheMilitary() @0x73f2f0e0b4`;
- `SimOccupation::get_Workplace() @0x73f3008584` must be non-null, then
  `SimWorkplace::RefreshCoworkers() @0x73f2fe7178` and
  `SimWorkplace::GetSupervisor() @0x73f2fe8db8` must produce a supervisor;
- the supervisor's own slot 0x240 must read under 25.0 -- `fcmp s1,s0` followed by
  `b.pl @0x73f2e35938`, which skips the card when the bar has filled;
- `SimPerson::IsCurrentLover() @0x73f30e0f70` must be false, so a supervisor who is
  also the hero's lover cannot be the subject;
- the hero must be at least 18 (`cmp w9,#0x12`);
- `Life::PresentedCountForScenario(System.String) @0x73f3736430` must read under five
  (`cmp w0,#5; cset w8,lt @0x73f2e359dc`), the same five-card cap the coworker
  family carries.

### 116.2 The table, the tokens, the four buttons

`a16_supervisor-unprofessional-scenarios-enc` holds 55 rows over five columns:
`Scenario`, `Log Version`, `Report For`, `Hero Gender` and `Supervisor Gender`. The
two gender columns are the interesting part, because all four cards the class can
draw are filtered twice. Their values are '', 'both', 'male' and 'female' -- the
hero column reads '' in 30 rows, 'both' in 21, 'female' in 3 and 'male' in 1, and
the supervisor column '' in 23, 'both' in 21, 'male' in 7 and 'female' in 4. The
DataHub picker behind the draw,
`GetRandomSupervisorUnprofessionalScenarioForHeroGenderAndSupervisorGender @0x73f2cc6f14`,
tests both columns before its single draw; the loader decodes male as 0, female as
1 and anything else as 2, the wildcard -- the same reading section 105 documents.

The text carries the same two-entry dictionary the coworker cards use.
`<supervisor>` (#9749) and `<supervisor-possessive>` (#9748) are expanded by
RefreshScenario against its own literals: #68432 `your supervisor, {0},` for the
body and #62730 `my supervisor, {0},` for the journal, with the name in the single
slot. The trailing comma is the game's own, which is why a Scenario cell that
already writes its own punctuation after the token renders both: row 14 reads
`...it's just you and <supervisor>. <He/She> smiles...` in the table and renders
`...just you and your supervisor, Jam Roll,. She smiles...` in the game, and row 2
(`with <supervisor>, you distinctly smell...`) renders a doubled comma the same way.
The port keeps the literal exactly as decoded rather than repairing the table.

The buttons come from RefreshScenario in a fixed order: `Attack {0}` (#12347),
`Have a talk with {0}` (#22687), `It doesn't bother me` (#27502) and the report
button -- `Report {0} to HR` (#35787), or `Report {0} misconduct` (#35788) when the
supervisor's own 0x1f4 field reads 1 (`cmp w8,#1; csel x21,x9,x10,eq`).
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f2e35338` then lowers the chosen label and tests it with
`String.Contains` in a fixed order -- attack #54542, report #64521, talk #66580 and
doesn't #57652 -- so a label matching none of the four changes nothing at all.

### 116.3 The four lanes

Each button is a different tail of the same method, and only one of them touches
the hero's stats.

- **Attack** @0x73f2e354ec moves the supervisor's own slot 0x508 by -6
  (`mov w1,#-6`), draws `GetRandomNumber(0,150)`, and pushes two follow-up cards --
  `ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineHR` (`.ctor(String,Int32) @0x73f2e2734c`) and
  `ScenarioCustomAttack` (`.ctor(SimCoworker,Boolean) @0x73f3cdaed0`) -- both linked
  at `[self+0x128]`, then adds an obituary colour line
  (`Friends say the most pleasure {0} ever derived from life was from assaulting {1} {2}.`
  #20716).
- **Report to HR** @0x73f2e35664 pushes and links a bare `Scenario`
  (`.ctor(Boolean) @0x73f2eb9db8`) carrying a string. No hero stat moves.
- **Have a talk** @0x73f2e356b8 pushes `ScenarioCoworkerTalkingTo`
  (`.ctor(SimCoworker,String) @0x73f2e2cd34`) with a reason the class builds by
  Format against the talk literal (`why you don't appreciate {0} behavior` #68057).
  No hero stat moves.
- **It doesn't bother me** @0x73f2e35744 is the only lane that moves the hero: his
  own slot 0x408 with -1 (`mov w1,#-1; blr [x8+0x408]`) and
  `SimPerson::ImpactDiscipline(int) @0x73f30e4cdc` with 2, and the journal gains
  `{0} I didn't let it bother me.` (#69558) after the row's own line.

### 116.4 How the port reaches it

`Sim::supervisorYear(Life&, AgeUp&, int forcedChoice)` sits at port/src/sim.cpp:26027
and is declared at port/include/bl/sim.h:477 next to `coworkerYear`. The wire is one
call at port/src/sim.cpp:3593, right after the coworker card's own call, so the two
share the workplace moment and keep their order. The card is built the way section
105 builds its four: a table pick, the two-token substitution, the shared bracket
drawer for `<A/B>` alternatives and for the pronoun tokens, `out.title = "Unprofessional
Boss"` (#45024) and `out.cta = "What will you do?"` (#46439).

Two details are the port's own reading of the class rather than a copy of it. The
first is the random stream: the class carries no push rate of its own (the game's
random-push queue decides), so the card draws its coin from a stream of its own,
`supRng_`, seeded `seed ^ 0x2545f4914f6cdd1dULL ^ 0x6a09e667f3bcc909ULL`. Section 105's
coworker stream and every other family's sequence are therefore untouched, which
matters because the supervisor name is resolved through the shared
`resolve("<supervisor>")` path. The second is the capitalization: a third of the
table's Scenario cells open in lower case, and the game capitalizes the assembled
sentence (`GameReference::CapitalizeFirstLetterOfSentenceString @0x73f32afedc`), so
the port uppercases the first character of the body after substitution.

The name and sex are drawn once per life and kept (`supName`, `supFemale` in
port/include/bl/game.h:751), so every supervisor card in a life names the same
person, the way the game's workplace does. `"supervisor"` was added to the kPeople
array at port/src/sim.cpp:1513ff so that `resolve("<supervisor>")` returns a name.

Four cards, one per lane, as the port draws them:

```
age 26  row 19  Attack him
  Your supervisor, Maylor Shift, made a big mistake on his project but then
  told the big boss it was your fault.
  journal: my supervisor, Maylor Shift, made a big mistake on his project and
  blamed it on me.

age 35  row 45  Report her to HR
  Your supervisor, April Levine, just asked the entire staff why we can't all
  be more like her.
  journal: my supervisor, April Levine, asked the entire staff why we can't be
  more like her.

age 68  row 14  Have a talk with him
  When you arrive at the office party, you quickly realize it's just you and
  your supervisor, Maylor Shift,. He smiles and asks if you want to "play
  doctor" with him.
  journal: my supervisor, Maylor Shift, asked if I wanted to "play doctor"
  with him.

age 28  row 48  It doesn't bother me
  Your supervisor, Maylor Shift, just told a co-worker that being her boss
  makes him feel like he owns her.
  journal: my supervisor, Maylor Shift, told a coworker that being her boss
  makes him feel like he owns her. I didn't let it bother me.
  deltas: happiness -4  discipline +8
```

The row 14 card is the table's own punctuation and the row 48 card is a table
whose Supervisor Gender column reads 'male' over text that assumes a male
supervisor either way; both render the way the game renders them.

### 116.5 Shortcuts

- The port keeps no supervisor record. The gate's slot 0x240 test, the attack
  lane's 0x508 move, the 0x1f4 field that chooses between the two report wordings,
  and the two pushed follow-up cards are all read from the class but not modelled:
  the port draws the card from the hero's own coworker slot. The report button
  therefore always wears the HR wording.
- The push rate (0.05) is the port's own, since the game decides by queue.
- `out.happiness` and `out.discipline` are `pointsForImpact(-1)` and
  `pointsForImpact(2)`, the same conversion every other card in the port uses for a
  raw impact and discipline move.

### 116.6 Verification

`tools/test_coworker.py` grew a supervisor block inside its per-run event loop (cap
five, title, both gender columns, a capitalized body, no unresolved tokens, the name
matching between body and journal, the pronoun matching the gendered rows, the
deltas, and the ignore sentence), plus a final set assertion that every family table
was seen. It reads:

```
coworker cards by table: {'a16_coworker-annoy-scenarios-enc': 138,
  'a16_coworker-behavior-scenarios-enc': 114, 'a16_coworker-pranks-enc': 112,
  'a16_coworker-rumors-enc': 95,
  'a16_supervisor-unprofessional-scenarios-enc': 116}
supervisors seen: 41
```

The probe /tmp/qdir/supres.py replays 80 lives (seeds 1..40 x both genders, 80
years each) and checks every supervisor card against the table row it came from,
including the strictest check available: a Scenario cell with no bracket
alternatives must render exactly, once the two tokens are substituted and the
sentence capitalized. It reads:

The 39 of 55 rows is the two gender columns doing their work: the hero and

## 117. The team building invitation: the workplace's third card, and the one that spends a year of goodwill

ScenarioSupervisorTeamBuilding is the third class this workplace block pushes and
the plainest of the three: no table row, no tokens, no pronoun machinery -- one
sentence the class composes out of four objects, and two buttons.

### 117.1 The class and its gate

il2cpp_dump.txt:55195 declares

    class ScenarioSupervisorTeamBuilding : Scenario

with two fields, `0x170 System.String _activity` and `0x178 SimCoworker _supervisor`,
and four methods: `.ctor() @0x73f2e34388`, `RefreshScenario @0x73f2e343e4`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f2e34720` and `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush
@0x73f2e34ad4`.

The gate is one conjunction:

- `SimHero::CurrentlyHasAJob() @0x73f2f0e040`, with the military fallback the 116
  gate builds as well;
- the hero's own age field compared with `0x14` (`cmp w10, #0x14` / `cset w10, gt`),
  so a hero under 21 never sees the card even holding a job;
- `SimOccupation::get_Workplace() @0x73f3008584` non-null and of the workplace type
  (cell 0x5c38458);
- `SimWorkplace::GetSupervisor() @0x73f2fe8db8` non-null;
- the workplace's own byte at 0x38 still zero. Both lanes set it to one
  (`strb w9, [workplace, #0x38]`), so the game shows this card once per workplace.

No `Life::PresentedCountForScenario` call appears anywhere in the class, unlike the
five-showing cap of 116: only the workplace flag stops the pattern repeating.

### 117.2 The sentence and the two buttons

`.ctor()` stores the literal `Team Building` (#41065, cell 0x5c610f0) into the base
scenario's title slot and calls `Scenario::.ctor(bool)` with false, so the card
carries no CTA and no follow-up. `RefreshScenario` resolves the supervisor, draws
the activity from `DataHub::GetRandomPastime() @0x73f2d0ca3c` -- the same hub behind
the part-time, celebrity and gross-taste pools, called with a null method info
(`mov x0, xzr`) -- and formats four objects through cell 0x5c610f8:

    {0}, your {1} at {2}, is sponsoring a team building activity by taking the team {3}.

(#70597), the arguments being `SimPerson::NameStringAndIncludeFullName @0x73f30c999c`
on the supervisor, `SimPerson::RelationshipStatusStringAndCapitalize @0x73f30c9ad0`
on that same person, the workplace's own name (`[[workplace+0x28]+0x18]`, read
through the hero's 0x40 field) and `_activity`.

The activity is a row of `a16_pastimes-enc` (271 lines, `Pastime,Holiday`), not of
`a16_business-team-building-activities-enc`: the 50-line business table is the
strongest candidate obs_corpus/scen_source.json offers this class, and the class
never reads it. The candidate map is a hint, not evidence.

The buttons are cell 0x5c61100, `Sure, I'll go` (#40421), and cell 0x5c61108,
`No, that sounds lame` (#31864). `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` lowercases the chosen label
and tests it with `String.Contains` against cell 0x5c61118, `sure` (#66382): a
substring test, not an equality, so any label carrying the word takes the accept
lane.

### 117.3 The two lanes

The accept lane (`@0x73f2e349cc`) moves the hero's own happiness slot 0x408 by +1,
calls `SimPerson::ImpactDiscipline(3) @0x73f30e4cdc` and
`SimPerson::ImpactKarma(2) @0x73f30e4bfc`, moves the supervisor's slot 0x508 bar by
+3, calls `SimWorkplace::ImpactRelationshipWithAllCoworkers(+2) @0x73f2fe9714`, sets
the workplace flag, and writes cell 0x5c61120:

    I went {0} with my company on a team building exercise.

(#25798).

The refusal lane leaves the hero's happiness slot untouched, calls
`ImpactDiscipline(-3)` and `ImpactKarma(-2)`, moves the supervisor -3 and the
coworker relationships -2, sets the same flag, and writes cell 0x5c61110:

    I refused to go {0} with my company on a team building exercise.

(#24946).

Both lanes then compare `_activity` with `cliff diving` (cell 0x5c34bb8, #55815) and,
when it matches, hand the activity to `AchievementManager::CompleteAchievement
@0x73f2817434` through the singleton at `@0x73f2817388`: one of the 271 pastimes
doubles as an achievement, and the refusal earns it as readily as the acceptance.
Both end with `Log @0x73f380158c` and a tail `RefreshUI @0x73f3580f5c`.

The card is a one-year goodwill trade: the supervision that 116 answers with an
attack, a talk or a report is here answered with attendance, and refusing is the
only way an action in this family costs discipline.

### 117.4 How the port reaches it

`Sim::teamBuildingYear` sits at port/src/sim.cpp:26192, declared at
port/include/bl/sim.h:480 and wired at port/src/sim.cpp:3602 immediately after the
supervisor card's call, so the year is still offered to the other friend cards when
this one declines it. The card carries its own stream, `tbRng_` (port/include/bl/sim.h:624,
seeded `seed ^ 0x1f83d9abfb41bd6bULL ^ 0x94d049bb133111ebULL` at port/src/sim.cpp:635):

no earlier subsystem's sequence moves. Two hero slots hold its state
(port/include/bl/game.h:758-759): `tbSupName`, the name the card needs when 116 has
not drawn one yet (it never writes 116's own slot), and `tbDone`, the port's
stand-in for the workplace byte.

The port's year is the gate, a 0.05 coin, then the two lanes: age 21 and up,
employed or in the military, not yet shown this life. The push rate is the port's
own, since the game decides by its random-push queue. The activity comes from
`pickPastime` (port/src/sim.cpp:23598), which enforces the table's `Holiday` column
the way the friend and mob cards already do, and the sentence is assembled from the
name, the workplace and the pastime. Happiness, discipline and karma go through
`pointsForImpact` (port/src/sim.cpp:3905), the conversion every other card uses for
a raw impact: +1 / +3 / +2 for attendance, -3 / -2 for the refusal.

Four cards, as the port draws them:

```

  Jam Roll, your supervisor at the company, is sponsoring a team building

  journal: I refused to go to attend a juggling class with my company on a
```

The last is row 266's own inline list, `horseback riding <along the river/in the
country/in the desert/in the mountains/in the forest>`, resolved before the sentence

### 117.5 Shortcuts

- The workplace name in the {2} slot is `h.ofcCompany` (port/include/bl/game.h:120,
  set from `companyName()` / `businessName()` at port/src/sim.cpp:20084-20086 when
  the hero's job is an office job), with the token resolver's own `the company`
  fallback (port/src/sim.cpp:20113). Calling `companyName()` here would draw from the
  main `rng_` stream (port/src/sim.cpp:3017), which no card in this port does, so a
  hero who works anywhere else reads `at the company`. Every card in the verification
  probe took that fallback.
- The {1} slot is the port's literal word `supervisor`, where the class fills it from
  `SimPerson::RelationshipStatusStringAndCapitalize` on the drawn supervisor: the
  port's drawn people carry no relationship status. It is the word the game's own
  dictionary expands the `<supervisor>` token to (#68432, `your supervisor, {0},`,
  REPORT.en.md 116), which is why the sentence still reads the way the game's does.
- The supervisor's own relationship bar (slot 0x508),
  `ImpactRelationshipWithAllCoworkers` and the cliff-diving achievement are read from
  the class but not modelled: the port keeps no coworker relationships and no
  achievements (REPORT.en.md 105, 116).
- The workplace byte of the gate becomes `tbDone`, one card per life: in the game a
  hero who changes jobs would be invited again at the new workplace.
- The ten pastimes the card can name are whichever row the port's `pickPastime`
  returns, with the same `Holiday` filter the other pastime cards use; the game draws
  from the hub's own list.
- The 50/50 lane split is the port's, since the game hands the choice to the player.
