## 118. The after-hours invitation: the boss who asks, and the sentence he stops using

The workplace family so far has shown two shapes. Four of its cards (§105) and the boss's own (§116) are rows of a table with the hero's and the colleague's sexes as columns; §117 is a sentence its own class assembles out of four objects and a pool of pastimes. The fourth card is the second shape again -- and the first one in the whole port where the supervisor is the one doing the asking. It is also the first card whose own words change the second time it is shown, which is what the byte at the top of 118.2 is about.

### 118.1 The class and its gate

**ScenarioSupervisorSocialize** sits at il2cpp_dump.txt:55187, wedged between the seduction card at il2cpp_dump.txt:55101 and the team-building card at il2cpp_dump.txt:55195 -- the three supervisor cards the game keeps as separate classes rather than as rows of a16_supervisor-unprofessional-scenarios-enc. It carries three fields:

- `field 0x170 System.String _activity` -- the pastime the card names three times over
- `field 0x178 SimCoworker _employee` -- the hero's own record in the workplace's staff list, which is where the workplace's name and the "asked before" byte are read from
- `field 0x180 SimCoworker _supervisor` -- the boss

and four methods: `.ctor() @0x73f2e33314`, `RefreshScenario @0x73f2e3341c`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f2e33844` and `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f2e34228`.

The gate is a chain of seven tests, and all seven have to pass before the card is even queued:

1. `SimHero::CurrentlyHasAJob() @0x73f2f0e040` -- true in the military as well
2. the hero's own `0x138` workplace field, through `SimWorkplace::Get_Workplace() @0x73f3008584`, is not null
3. its `SimWorkplace::GetSupervisor() @0x73f2fe8db8` is not null
4. the supervisor's value out of `0x73f30d284c` is above `30.0f` (`fmov s1, #30.0`; fcmp s0, s1; b.le`) -- he has to be senior enough
5. the supervisor's own `0x240` bar is below `50.0f` (`fmov s1, #50.0f` is `0x42480000`; `fcmp; b.pl`)
6. `SimPerson::IsCurrentLover() @0x73f30e0f70` is false -- the invitation is not a date with someone already at home
7. `Life::PresentedCountForScenario() @0x73f3736430` against the scenario key in cell `0x5c610e8` is under five (`cmp w0, #5; cset w0, lt`)

There is no hero age test anywhere in the gate, which makes this the first workplace card without one -- and the only reason the port has an age floor at all is that its supervisor is a drawn name rather than a full person (see 118.5).

### 118.2 The two sentences and the two buttons

`RefreshScenario` draws `_activity` from the same pool every other pastime card uses, `DataHub::GetRandomPastime() @0x73f2d0ca3c` (called with a null method info, `mov x0, xzr`), and then picks between two format cells by reading one byte off the employee record:

- `ldrb w8, [x8, #0x39]` at the top of the method, `cbz w8, 0x73f2e33604` -- byte zero takes the long sentence, anything else the short one
- `strb 1, [employee + 0x39]` at 0x73f2e33788 -- and then writes one back, so the long one is available exactly once per employee

The two cells:

| showing | cell | literal | sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| first | 0x5c61098 | #50561 | `Your {0} at {1}, {2}, has taken a liking to you and has asked you to go {3} with {4}. You are worried that it will make your co-workers jealous.` |
| later | 0x5c61090 | #50712 | `Your {0}, {1}, invited you to go {2} with {3}.` |

The five objects of the long one are, in order, `SimPerson::RelationshipStatusStringAndCapitalize() @0x73f30c9ad0` on the supervisor, the workplace's name (read through the employee record: `[self+0x178]` then `+0x40` then `+0x28` then `+0x18`), `SimPerson::NameStringAndIncludeFullName() @0x73f30c999c` on the supervisor, `_activity`, and the pronoun helper `0x73f30e64d0(person, 2)` -- the object pronoun, `him` or `her`.

That first slot is the same slot the team-building card fills with the literal word "supervisor" (REPORT.en.md 117.4, where the shortcut was taken on the strength of this card's decoded sentence). Here the game's own output settles it: the sentence reads `Your supervisor at the company, Jam Roll, has taken a liking to you...`, so for a supervisor the relationship label **is** the role word, not a status like "married".

The title is the il2cpp literal #10909, `After Hours` (`0x5c61080`), stored at `[x19+0x38]` by the ctor, and the two buttons are literal #17913 `Do it` (`0x5c344c8`) and literal #34276 `Politely decline` (`0x5c61088`). `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` resolves the answer the same way the two cards before it do: it takes the chosen label out of the list at `[self+0x108]` through the vtable slot `+0x2e8`, lowers it with `String::ToLower() @0x73f52aa938` and then substring-tests it, first against `'do it'` (#57642, cell `0x5c37ef0`) for the accept lane and then against `'decline'` (#57370, cell `0x5c610d8`) for the refusal. Anything else does nothing at all.

### 118.3 The two lanes

**Accept** (`0x73f2e33a80`) moves the hero's own `0x408` slot by `+3`, the supervisor's `0x508` bar by `+4`, and calls `SimWorkplace::ImpactRelationshipWithAllCoworkers() @0x73f2fe9714` with `-3` -- saying yes to the boss costs you at the water cooler, which is exactly what the long sentence warns about. Its journal is cell `0x5c60a98`, literal #25801:

> I went {0} with my {1}, {2}.

The lane then does four more things the port documents but does not model: it formats cell `0x5c610b8` (#49739, `You went {0} with your {1}, {2}.`) into a second scenario pushed as a follow-up and linked at `[self+0x128]`; it appends the achievement names of cells `0x5c610c0` (#14267 `Butter them up`), `0x5c610d0` (#23191 `How could I say no`), `0x5c610e0` (#15536 `Chillin' with the villain`) and `0x5c610c8` (#13923 `Bossy buddy`) to a builder; it draws a number with `GetRandomNumber(0, 100)` and formats the enjoyment pair `0x5c34a68` (#50126 `Your Enjoyment`) / `0x5c3dae0` (#69502 `{0} Enjoyment`) together with `0x73f30e64d0(supervisor, 6)`; and it completes the 'cliff diving' achievement (cell `0x5c334b8`, guarded by `_activity.Equals('cliff diving')` against cell `0x5c34bb8`) when the pastime was that one. Finally it pushes a memory line into the obituary pool -- cell `0x5c610a0`, literal #32835:

> One of {0} bosses recalls fondly the time {1} went to go {2} with {3}.

with the `<obit-his/her>` and `<obit-he/she>` tokens (cells `0x5c38f58` and `0x5c34a20`) for the first two slots, through `ObituaryGenerator::AddColorString() @0x73f3803dc0`. The accepted evening therefore outlives the card in the game's death text, which is a level of bookkeeping no earlier card in this port has.

**Refuse** (`0x73f2e33fb8`) leaves `0x408` alone and calls `SimPerson::ImpactDiscipline(1) @0x73f30e4cdc` -- a **rise**, small but real, the only stat the refusal moves -- and drops the supervisor's `0x508` bar by `-4`. Its journal is cell `0x5c610b0`, literal #24817:

> I politely declined an opportunity to go {0} with my {1}, {2}.

Both lanes then run a common tail at `0x73f2e34070`: if the supervisor's id word at `[+0x1c]` differs from the hero's, the game assembles a third scenario over cell `0x5c60ad0` (literal #65500, `sexually harassing <you/me>`), stores the supervisor at `[x22+0x58]` and appends it to the day's result, and then logs the journal line with `Log() @0x73f380158c` and tails into `RefreshUI() @0x73f3580f5c`.

### 118.4 How the port reaches it

`Sim::afterHoursYear` is at port/src/sim.cpp:26300, declared at port/include/bl/sim.h:484 and called at port/src/sim.cpp:3609, right after the team-building card, so no family before it moves. It keeps its own stream, `ahRng_` (port/include/bl/sim.h:629, seeded at port/src/sim.cpp:636 with `seed ^ 0x2545f4914f6cdd1d ^ 0xd6e8feb86659fd93`, a pair no other stream uses), and two hero slots, `ahPresented` and `ahFirst` (port/include/bl/game.h:764-765).

The port's mapping of the gate is the readable half of it: `age >= 21`, employed or military, `ahPresented < 5`, and a 0.05 coin on `ahRng_` -- the game's queue decides when the card is offered, so every push rate in this port is its own. The supervisor's name comes from `h.supName` when the unprofessional card has already named him and otherwise from the same lazy slot that card uses (`h.tbSupName`), so this card draws no name of its own and no other card's sequence moves; the workplace is `h.ofcCompany` with the token resolver's own `the company` fallback; the pronoun comes from `h.supFemale`.

Four cards, as the port draws them (seeds 1..14, both sexes, ninety years):

`age 58, row 34, the first showing, accept`

> Your supervisor at the company, Ron Mendes, has taken a liking to you and has asked you to go skydiving with her. You are worried that it will make your co-workers jealous.
>
> **Do it** -> happiness +16
>
> I went skydiving with my supervisor, Ron Mendes.

`age 29, row 81, the first showing, decline`

> Your supervisor at the company, Arianna Venti, has taken a liking to you and has asked you to go to make hand-painted T-shirts with her. You are worried that it will make your co-workers jealous.
>
> **Politely decline** -> discipline +4
>
> I politely declined an opportunity to go to make hand-painted T-shirts with my supervisor, Arianna Venti.

`age 34, row 4, the same supervisor asking a second time`

> Your supervisor, Beyawnce Gnolls, invited you to go bowling with him.
>
> **Do it** -> happiness +16
>
> I went bowling with my supervisor, Beyawnce Gnolls.

`age 75, row 195, a pastime with its own one-of list, third showing`

> Your supervisor, Megan Mare, invited you to go for a tandem bike ride in the forest with him.

Three of these four are worth pausing on. The Ron Mendes card reads `with her` although the name is a man's: the supervisor in this port is a name and a drawn sex, and the pronoun follows the sex, exactly as REPORT.en.md 116.6 recorded for the unprofessional card. The pair of age-29 and age-78 cards on seed 2 female is the employee byte at work -- `Montero X` asks with the long sentence at 29 and with the short one at 78, the same person, the same life. And row 195's cell is `for a tandem bike ride in the <mountains/forest/country/city/hills>`, drawn as `in the forest`: the port resolves the alternatives before the sentence is assembled, so the probe has to rebuild the cell as a pattern to check it (118.6).

One more pair from the same sweep, both the first showing:

`seed 31, row 270` -- cell `to sing <musician> songs at karaoke night`:

> Your supervisor at the company, Walid Robinson, has taken a liking to you and has asked you to go to sing Chris Stapleton songs at karaoke night with her.

`seed 36, row 121` -- cell `to do <musician> karaoke`:

> Your supervisor at the company, Willie Eyelash, has taken a liking to you and has asked you to go to do Pentatonix karaoke with him.

Those two rows carry a bracket with no alternatives in it at all -- `<musician>` is a person the game resolves, not a choice list -- which is a case the two pastime cards' own checkers had to learn (118.6).

### 118.5 Shortcuts

- **The three tests about the supervisor himself are not modelled.** The port's supervisor is a name, a sex and a presented counter, so the `30.0f` seniority floor, the `0x240` bar below `50.0f` and the `IsCurrentLover()` test have nothing to read. The `age >= 21` floor stands in for the first of them -- the game will not offer the card to a teenager either, since the hero has to hold a job for it to fire at all -- and the other two are dropped. A ported life can therefore be invited out by a boss the game would have filtered.
- **The supervisor's relationship bar (`0x508`) and the co-worker relationship bar** (`ImpactRelationshipWithAllCoworkers`) are the two things the accept lane spends and the refusal lane saves. The port carries neither, so they stay comments in the code; in a ported life, saying yes to the boss costs nothing but the jealousy of a bar nobody can see.
- **The line the accepted evening leaves in the obituary pool**, the four achievement names, the enjoyment number, the pushed follow-up scenario and the jealousy scenario of the common tail are all skipped. The port pushes one card per age-up and keeps no achievements, no obituaries and no scenario chain.
- **The employee byte is kept per life, not per employee.** The game keeps `0x39` on the hero's staff record; the port has no staff list, so `ahFirst` is one bit for the whole life. A ported life that changes employer keeps the "has asked before" state across both jobs, where the game would start fresh.
- **The presented cap is the game's own five** (`ahPresented`), and like every other cap in this port it is counted per life.

### 118.6 Verification

The probe for this card is /tmp/qdir/ahres.py -- eighty lives (seeds 1..40, both sexes, eighty years each), eleven seconds, rc 0:

    lives 80
    after hours cards 86
    long sentences 48 short sentences 38
    rows drawn 45 of 271
    choices {'Politely decline': 45, 'Do it': 41}
    supervisors seen 34
    workplaces seen 1 ['the company']
    pronouns {'her': 26, 'him': 60}
    cards per life {0: 32, 1: 23, 2: 15, 3: 8, 4: 1, 5: 1}
    hero age at the card min 21 max 79
    runtime 11s
    failures 0
    events 86
    RESIDUE 0 {}
    rc 0

It checks the table, the age floor, the body against both sentences, that the first card of a life is the long one and every later card the short one, the pastime text against its row's cell rebuilt as a pattern, that no `<token>` survives into the sentence, the choice against the two buttons, the deltas of each lane (happiness 16 for **Do it**, discipline 4 for **Politely decline**), the exact journal line of each lane with the activity and the supervisor's name substituted back in, and the cap of five cards per life. It is the first probe of the family that has to read two sentences: the long one carries the workplace in its second slot and the short one does not, so the workplace, the name and the pronoun are taken from different groups depending on which shape matched.

Two of the probe's own checks were wrong before they were right, and both are worth recording:

- The short-sentence check read `if n != 1` where it meant `if n == 1`, so every one of the thirty-eight short cards was reported as arriving before the long one. The port was right; the probe was inverted.
- The pastime-cell check escaped a bracket with no alternatives in it, so rows 121 (`to do <musician> karaoke`) and 270 (`to sing <musician> songs at karaoke night`) failed. `<musician>` is not a one-of list at all -- it is a person the game resolves, exactly like `<supervisor>` in the two cards above -- so both the probe's helper and tools/test_coworker.py's `cell_pattern()` now treat a slashless bracket as `.+?` instead of a fixed word. The team-building card (REPORT.en.md 117.6) drew no such row in its own sweep, which is why the same latent bug sat in the test until now.

The regression test is tools/test_coworker.py, which now covers this card as well:

    coworker cards by table: {'a16_coworker-annoy-scenarios-enc': 137, 'a16_coworker-behavior-scenarios-enc': 119, 'a16_coworker-pranks-enc': 109, 'a16_coworker-rumors-enc': 92, 'a16_supervisor-unprofessional-scenarios-enc': 114, 'after hours': 86, 'team building': 52}
    supervisors seen: 34
    team building cards: 52
    after hours cards: 86

The workplace counters have moved again, for the third section running: the unprofessional card drew 111 in the 117 run and draws 114 here, the behave table 114 and now 119, annoy 136 and now 137, rumors 95 and now 92. The cause is the one recorded in REPORT.en.md 117.6 -- this card moves the hero's happiness or his discipline, so the years after it differ and so does every later family's eligibility. The numbers quoted in the 116 and 117 sections were true of their own commits' trees and are left standing.

The full batch, written by /tmp/qdir/reg118.sh and run as a background job, is green:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| build | `cmake --build port/build -j8`, no warnings |
| tools/coverage.py | `captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107` and `contentless entries: 2 -- ScenarioMiniPaywall x2` |
| tools/portgap.py | `ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0` |
| coverage replay | rc 0 with a zero-byte stderr, 31748 bytes of events |
| residue census | `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0` |
| all probes | 61 lines, every probe `rc=0 residue=0` (`ahres.py` events 86, `supres.py` 114, `tbres.py` 52, `ftres.py` 170; only `idres.py` prints its own per-run counters) |
| tools/bench.sh /tmp/trace_c10.json | 167 lines, and `diff` against the 117 run is empty -- the ages 0..34 trace does not move |

The trace not moving is the point of the separate stream. This card draws a pastime on every eligible year through `ahRng_` and none of those draws touch `rng_`, so the ages the benchmark compares against the game's own capture are unchanged -- the same result §117 recorded, and the first time in this stretch that a card could have moved the main stream and did not.

## 119. The lightning strike: the first card that can end the life

Every card since §105 has been a social one: a colleague, a supervisor, a friend, a lover, and in each case the worst outcome was a stat and a relationship moving. This one is from a different family altogether. It reads no table, its sentence is assembled out of a switch of forty-three scene strings, and its dismiss lane hands the hero to the death system. Porting it forced two things the port had never needed: a way for a card to move the fourth stat (health sat in neither `AgeUp` nor any card), and a way for a card to ask for a death -- `checkDeath` until now only ever answered its own annual roll.

### 119.1 The class and its gate

**ScenarioLightningStrike** sits at il2cpp_dump.txt:54901, and the class after it in the dump is ScenarioVictimRansom at il2cpp_dump.txt:54905. It carries two fields and -- unlike every social card -- no `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` at all:

- `field 0x170 System.String _narrative` -- the one line the journal gets
- `field 0x178 System.Boolean _willDie` -- set during the refresh, read by the dismiss
- `.ctor @0x73f2e07e28`, `RefreshScenario @0x73f2e07ea4`, `DismissSelected @0x73f2e080dc`, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f2e081e0`

The card has no buttons, so the missing choice method is the shape of the card rather than a gap in the dump: the player dismisses it the way a death notice is dismissed.

The gate is short, and it is the only one in the port so far that is not a set of state tests:

1. the singleton's hero object resolves (`[[cell 0x5c30250]+0xb8]` and then `[x8+0x28]`)
2. the hero's age at `[x0+0x20]` is at least `0x12` -- eighteen
3. `SimHero::CurrentlyInPrison() @0x73f2f0e1d8` is false (`eor w8, w0, #1`)
4. `GetRandomNumber(0, 5) @0x73f32ab2a8` comes up zero (`cmp w0, #0; cset w0, eq`)

That last one is the whole cost of the card: a one-in-five eligibility roll, re-offered every year the other three tests pass. There is no fame test, no `PresentedCountForScenario` cap, and no workplace or job test -- which is why the card can land on an eighteen-year-old (119.4's samples include one).

### 119.2 The body: three strings and a sound, and no table at all

`.ctor @0x73f2e07e28` stores two cells with one `stp`: cell `0x5c5f990`, literal #45629 `Victim` at `[self+0x30]`, and cell `0x5c5fda0`, literal #28922 `Lightning Strike` at `[self+0x38]`. `0x38` is the title slot every card in the port uses; `0x30` is the category label the UI files the card under, and `Victim` is this card's.

`RefreshScenario` then builds exactly three strings:

| slot | cell | literal | text |
|---|---|---|---|
| body | 0x5c5fdb0 | #70595 | `{0}, you were struck by lightning!` |
| journal | 0x5c5fdb8 | #25720 | `I was struck by lightning!` |
| sound | 0x5c5fda8 | #53013 | `a16_sndThunder.aiff` |

The `{0}` comes from `DataHub::GetRandomCircumstance() @0x73f2ce2d08` -- the same call §38 decoded as a switch over `Random.Range(0, 43)` and the port already keeps as `kCircumstancePublicScenes` (port/src/sim.cpp:1624): forty-one fixed scenes ("While out jogging", "On your way to the airport") plus two slots that name a musician concert. The body is therefore always a scene and never a bare line, and the port's array holds the same strings.

The two remaining stores are one flag and one field: `mov w8, #1; str w8, [self+0x134]` and the sound string at `[self+0x140]`. Nothing else in the class reads a table -- which is why the port's entry for the card carries an empty `table` and a null `row`.

### 119.3 The two branches, and the first pending death

After the sentence is stored, the refresh rolls `GetRandomNumber(0, 2)` and moves the four stat floats in one shot. The four are the ones §1 mapped: hero+0x88 happiness, +0x8c health, +0x90 intelligence, +0x94 appearance:

- a draw of 0 **and** the life byte at `[life+0x20 -> +0x5e0]` equal to 0 take the unharmed lane: `mov w9, #0x42c80000; dup v0.4s; stur q0, [hero, #0x88]` writes 100.0f into all four
- anything else zeroes all four with `stp xzr, xzr, [hero, #0x88]` and then rolls for death: `GetRandomNumber(0, 100) @0x73f32ab2a8`, `scvtf s0, w0`, `ldr s1, [x8, #0xac]`, `fcmp s1, s0; b.pl` -- the branch is skipped when `hero[0xac]` is not below the draw, and `_willDie` (`[self+0x178]`) is set only when it is

Both lanes converge on `AchievementManager::get_SharedAchievementManager() @0x73f2817388` and `CompleteAchievement('acLightningStrike') @0x73f2817434` -- cell `0x5c326c0` holds the achievement id as a live string object, which is what `readlit3.py`'s second hop reads.

`DismissSelected @0x73f2e080dc` is where the card pays out. It logs `_narrative`, and then, only when `_willDie` is set:

1. the death manager at `[life+0x20]+0xa0` gets the hero's age written at its `[x0+0x60]`
2. `DeathManager::UpdateWithLightningStrike() @0x73f2fb19d4`
3. the hero's own vtable slot `0x368` is called with no arguments -- the kill
4. a follow-up `Scenario` is built from cell `0x5c38f70` through `0x73f3b9afd0` and linked at `[self+0x128]`

The cause this card writes into the death record is the table's own, not a new string: `a16_death-types-enc` row 68 is `Fluke`, commonness 1, sentence `<pronoun> died after being struck by lightning.` -- one of the 109 rows the port's `checkDeath` already draws from for an ordinary death.

### 119.4 How the port reaches it

**The gate.** `Sim::lightningYear` (port/src/sim.cpp:26442, declared port/include/bl/sim.h:489, wired at port/src/sim.cpp:3615 right after the after-hours card) tests the three states and then the coin:

```cpp
  if (h.age < 18) return false;
  if (h.inPrison) return false;
  if (h.lightDone) return false;
  if (lightRng_.below(5) != 0) return false;
```

`lightRng_` (port/include/bl/sim.h:635, seeded at port/src/sim.cpp:637) is the card's own stream, so no earlier family's sequence moves and the ages 0..34 bench trace is untouched. The first seed pair chosen for it collided with `aiRng_` at port/src/sim.cpp:644, which the uniqueness check at the end of the patch caught; the shipped pair `0x9fb21c651e98df25 ^ 0xd6e8feb86659fd93` appears nowhere else in the constructor list.

**The sentence.** `out.title = "Lightning Strike"`, `out.body = scene + ", you were struck by lightning!"` with the scene drawn from the port's own `kCircumstancePublicScenes` array (port/src/sim.cpp:1624) on `lightRng_`, and `out.narrative = "I was struck by lightning!"`. `table` and `row_id` stay empty, because there is no row.

**The two lanes.** The port expresses both through the deltas the card computes off the hero's current values, which is what makes the branch visible in the harness at all:

| lane | condition | deltas |
|---|---|---|
| unharmed | `lightRng_.below(2) == 0` | `health`, `happiness`, `smarts`, `looks` each `100 - value` |
| damage | anything else | each `-value`, i.e. all four land on 0 |

**The pending death.** `Hero::lightWillDie` (port/include/bl/game.h:771) is set on the damage lane when the health the strike found is below a `lightRng_.below(100)` draw, and `Sim::checkDeath` (port/src/sim.cpp:23319) now honours it before its own annual roll:

```cpp
  if (h.lightWillDie) {
    const Table& dt = tbl("a16_death-types-enc");
    for (size_t r = 0; r < dt.size(); ++r) {
      if (dt.at(r, "Sentence").find("struck by lightning") != std::string::npos) {
        type = dt.at(r, "Type");
        sentence = resolve(dt.at(r, "Sentence"));
        return true;
      }
    }
  }
```

A card-driven death is a new shape for this port: the runner (port/src/script.cpp:776) already called `checkDeath` after every age-up and set `life.alive = false`, so the card needed only to hand the check a cause it could not have drawn itself. The harness reports it in the same block as any other death.

Two support changes were needed to say any of this:

- `AgeUp::health` (port/include/bl/sim.h:41) -- the fourth stat had no delta field, so no card could move it. port/src/script.cpp and port/src/main.cpp add it to the stat application and to their clamp lists, and `eventJson` (port/src/script.cpp:179) now reports it beside the other five, which is how the probes below can see the four floats land.
- `Hero::lightDone` (port/include/bl/game.h:770) -- the once-per-life flag (see 119.5).

Sampled cards, taken from a seeds-1..16 run:

| seed | age | lane | body | deltas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 male | 33 | unharmed | `While sitting at the train station, you were struck by lightning!` | health +11, smarts +67, looks +35 (all to 100) |
| 2 male | 18 | damage | `While sitting at the train station, you were struck by lightning!` | happiness -100, health -90, smarts -3, looks -45 |
| 4 male | 21 | unharmed | `While at a cricket match, you were struck by lightning!` | happiness +2, health +13, smarts +100, looks +16 |
| 8 male | 63 | damage | `On your way to the airport, you were struck by lightning!` | happiness -3, health -93, smarts -62, looks -56 |
| 28 male | 61 | damage, death | `While riding a Segway, you were struck by lightning!` | all four to 0, then `{"type": "Fluke", "sentence": "he died after being struck by lightning."}` |
| 36 male | 46 | damage, death | `While shopping at the sex toy store, you were struck by lightning!` | all four to 0, then `{"type": "Fluke", "sentence": "he died after being struck by lightning."}` |

The seed-4 card shows the family lines the port writes before a card's own line (`My father is no longer suffering from ringworm.`), and the two death rows are the whole new path end to end: the strike zeroes the four stats, `checkDeath` reads the flag, and the death record carries the table's `Fluke` cause with its `<pronoun>` resolved to the hero's own.

### 119.5 Shortcuts

- **One strike per life.** The game re-offers the card every year it fits; its own brake is the life byte `0x5e0`, which the port does not carry. `Hero::lightDone` stands in for it, because a second strike could only replay a death that did not happen the first time.
- **`hero[0xac]` read as the health the strike found.** The death roll compares a float at `0xac` against `GetRandomNumber(0, 100)`. `0xac` is not one of the four floats the lane just zeroed -- `0x88`..`0x98` are -- so it is some further state the port does not model, and the closest honest reading is the health value before the strike. A consequence worth stating: a hero at full health can never die of a strike in the port, because `100 < below(100)` is false whatever the draw.
- **The two musician-concert slots** of the real switch are not reachable: the port draws its own array with `lightRng_` and does not call `referenceToken("musician")`, which would have moved the main stream.
- **`Victim`, the thunder and the achievement** are UI-side: the category label at `[self+0x30]`, the sound at `[self+0x140]` and `acLightningStrike`. The port has no card categories, no sound and no achievements.
- **The follow-up scenario** linked at `[self+0x128]` is not pushed.
- **No `PresentedCountForScenario` cap** is needed: the game's gate has none either.

### 119.6 Verification

Three independent checks, plus the full batch every earlier section has had to survive.

**The probe** (`/tmp/qdir/lsres.py`, 80 lives -- seeds 1..40 in both sexes, 80 years each). It differs from every probe before it in one way that matters: it rebuilds the hero's four stats from the newborn block and each event's deltas, because this card's whole effect is a set of absolute values rather than a fixed delta. Output:

```
lives 80
lightning cards 77
lanes {'unharmed': 28, 'damage': 49}
scenes drawn 22 of 41
cards per life {0: 3, 1: 77}
hero age at the card min 18 max 64
lightning deaths 4
  death (28, 'male', 61, 'Fluke', 'he died after being struck by lightning.')
  death (28, 'female', 61, 'Fluke', 'she died after being struck by lightning.')
  death (36, 'male', 46, 'Fluke', 'he died after being struck by lightning.')
  death (36, 'female', 46, 'Fluke', 'she died after being struck by lightning.')
runtime 16s
failures 0
events 77
RESIDUE 0 {}
rc 0
```

Three things come out of it. The card is a once-per-life event even though the game's gate allows repeats -- `cards per life {0: 3, 1: 77}` is the flag at work, and the three zeroes are seeds whose lives ended before the one-in-five roll came up. Both lanes land: 49 damage to 28 unharmed is near the 2:1 `below(2)` predicts, and the unharmed lane is the rarer one because it needs the draw **and** the life byte the port does not model. And the card can kill: four deaths, at 61 and 46, both sexes in both cases, each type `Fluke` with the table's lightning sentence resolved to the hero's own pronoun -- the first deaths in this port that no annual roll produced. The age floor shows up exactly as written: the earliest card is at 18, the first year the gate allows.

**The test** (`tools/test_lightning.py`, in the repo, asserting rather than printing):

```
lives 80
lightning cards 77
lanes {'damage': 49, 'unharmed': 28}
lightning deaths 4
cards per life {0: 3, 1: 77}
ok
```

**The batch** (`/tmp/qdir/reg119.sh`): the build; `tools/coverage.py` gives `captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107` and `contentless entries: 2 -- ScenarioMiniPaywall x2`; `/tmp/qdir/portgap.py` gives `ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0`; the 109-age capture replay ends `covpush rc=0` with a zero-byte stderr; `/tmp/qdir/rescensus.py` gives `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`; the sweep gives 62 probes on 62 lines, every one `rc=0 residue=0`, with `lsres.py events=77`; and `tools/bench.sh /tmp/trace_c10.json` gives 167 lines that diff **zero** lines against the §118 run (`diff /tmp/qdir/bench118.txt /tmp/qdir/bench119.txt`).

Counters moved between §118 and §119, and this shift is larger than the previous two and easy to explain: the card zeroes or maxes four stats at once, so it changes what every age-gated family can draw for the rest of the life. `tools/test_coworker.py` on its own seeds: annoy 137 -> 148, behavior 119 -> 115, pranks 109 -> 108, rumors 92 -> 96, supervisor 114 -> 114, after hours 86 -> 81, team building 52 -> 52, `supervisors seen` 34 -> 40. The sweep: `ftres.py` 170 -> 163, `ahres.py` 86 -> 81, `giftres.py` 55 -> 47, `supres.py` 114 -> 114, `tbres.py` 52 -> 52. Earlier sections keep their quoted numbers, the §115 precedent.

The zero-line bench diff is the interesting one. The bench runs ages 0..34, where this card cannot appear before 18, and it reports the harness's own age-by-age streams and stat deltas rather than card counters -- so the drift above is real but does not reach it. `lightRng_` is what makes that true: the card draws its scene, its coin and its death roll on its own stream, and the main `rng_` sequence is exactly where it was in §118.

## 120. The supervisor who wants you: the hookup table read from both ends

Section 116 to 118 built the three cards that a supervisor pushes *at* the hero -- the
unprofessional remark, the team-building invitation, the after-hours invitation. This
section is the fourth member of that family and the only one that can run in the other
direction: sometimes the boss makes the move and the hero answers, and sometimes the hero
makes the move and the boss answers.

### 120.1 The class and the gate

`ScenarioSupervisorSeduce` sits at `il2cpp_dump.txt:55101`, the class after it in the dump
is `ScenarioSupervisorSeduceSuccess` at `il2cpp_dump.txt:55109` (the follow-up the card
pushes when the attempt is answered), and both are plain `: Scenario` subclasses.

```
class ScenarioSupervisorSeduce : Scenario
    field 0x170 SimCoworker _supervisor
    field 0x178 SimLover    _loverCandidate
    field 0x180 System.Boolean _targeted
    field 0x181 System.Boolean _gettingSeduced
    field 0x188 System.String _dataInboundLogVersion
    .ctor(SimCoworker, Boolean) @0x73f2e24b5c
    .ctor()                     @0x73f2e24b90
    RefreshScenario             @0x73f2e24b9c
    ChoiceSelectedAtIndex       @0x73f2e25de0
    ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f2e273c4
```

The gate `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f2e273c4` is the same shape section 116 read,
with one extra counter:

1. the hero must be at least eighteen (`age [x0+0x20] >= 0x12`);
2. he must have a job or be in the military (`CurrentlyHasAJob @0x73f2f0e040` or
   `CurrentlyInTheMilitary @0x73f2f0e0b4`);
3. a dictionary lookup on the life object followed by
   `Life::PresentedCountForScenario < 5` -- the card may show at most five times per life;
4. the hero's workplace must resolve (`SimWorkplace::get_Workplace @0x73f3008584`), which is
   also where the supervisor comes from.

There is no fame test, no prison test and no lover test here. The bookkeeping is the
loosest of the family, which is why the port can reach this card with no new state at all:
the supervisor identity written by section 116 (`h.supName` / `h.supFemale`) and the lover
slots the port already carries (`h.loverName` / `h.loverStatus`) are everything the class
touches.

### 120.2 One table, two column pairs, three button sets

The wording is not built in code. It comes from
`gamedata_plain/a16_coworker-hookup-scenarios-enc`, 24 lines -- a header and 23 rows -- with
seven columns:

```
Inbound Scenario, Inbound Log Version, Outbound Scenario, Outbound Log Version,
Sender Gender, Recipient Gender, Supervisor Appropriate
```

The card picks a column *pair*, not a row alone, and which pair depends on a direction byte
(120.3). The inbound cells are the boss's opening line and carry the `<coworker>` token for
him:

```
<coworker> just asked if you want to hook up in the <breakroom/bathroom stall/hall closet/supply room>.
<coworker> just told you that <he/she> would really love to manspread you.
<coworker> just informed you that <he/she> would be down for a late-night meeting, if you're game.
<coworker> just flashed a suggestive smile your way and asked you if you want to get a workout in after work.
```

and their log columns mirror them in the first person with the same bracket list shortened to
`<rb>`, so the journal has to repeat the body's pick:

```
<coworker> asked me to hook up in the <rb>.
```

The outbound cells are the hero's own line and never name a token, because the hero is
speaking:

```
You asked <coworker> to hook up with you in the <breakroom/bathroom/hall closet>.
You told <coworker> that there's a pretty package for her on the front desk, but there's an even prettier one inside your pants.
```

Three columns narrow the pool at pick time: `Sender Gender` and `Recipient Gender` are checked
against the two people's `EffectiveGender @0x73f30dbc30`, and `Supervisor Appropriate` -- an
`x` on 5 of the 23 rows -- marks the rows that may be delivered when the sender *is* the
supervisor.

The picker is
`DataHub::GetRandomCoworkerHookupScenarioForSenderGenderAndRecipientGenderAndIsSupervisorInbound(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean) @0x73f2cc7ca0`,
called at `0x73f2e250f4` with `(supervisor[0x1c], hero[0x1c], 1)`; the row's `Body` lives at
`+0x10` and its `Narrative` at `+0x18`, and both go through
`GetParsedBodyString @0x73f337bb5c` / `GetParsedNarrativeString @0x73f337bb64` before they are
shown.

Then there are three buttons, and the vocabulary is chosen from the two people's gender field
`[x+0x1c]`, from the direction, and from the hero's service:

```
same sex, hero advancing:   'Get at it'                 #21371   cell 0x5c607e0
                            'Let me get a piece of that' #28750   cell 0x5c607e8
other sex, hero advancing:  'Give it to {0}'            #21690   cell 0x5c34900
                            'Hit that'                   #22996   cell 0x5c607c0
boss advancing, hero free:  'Do {0}'                    #17950   cell 0x5c607b8
                            'Hook up with {0}'           #23093   cell 0x5c386f8
                            'Try to seduce {0}'          #44150   cell 0x5c468e8
always:                     'Reject {0} advances'        #35577   cell 0x5c46900
military:                   'Report {0} misconduct'      #35787   cell 0x5c607f0
civilian:                   'Report {0} to HR'           #35788   cell 0x5c607c8
```

`{0}` is the supervisor's object pronoun (`him` / `her`), so the port's case splits on
`h.supFemale` exactly as sections 116 to 118 already do.

### 120.3 The direction byte and the three lanes

`RefreshScenario @0x73f2e24b9c` opens with a ~57-pair lazy static initialisation (the string
literals above), then does three things: if `_supervisor` is null it fetches the supervisor
off the hero's workplace (`SimWorkplace::GetSupervisor @0x73f2fe8db8`) and stores it at
`0x170`; it calls `SimLover::GenerateLoverFromCoworker @0x73f3812d6c` and stores the lover
candidate at `0x178`; and the two bytes `_targeted` (`0x180`) and `_gettingSeduced` (`0x181`)
decide which direction this instance is running in. The title slot is a `csel` between
`'Seducer' #38395` (cell `0x5c468d0`) and `'Seductress' #38397` (cell `0x5c468d8`) on the
actor's gender, the who-string is assembled from
`RelationshipStatusStringAndCapitalize @0x73f30c9ad0` and
`NameStringAndIncludeFullName @0x73f30c999c` into the two role templates
`'your {0}, {1},' #68451` (cell `0x5c39a68`) and `'my {0}, {1},' #62743` (cell `0x5c39aa0`),
and a profile panel (Name / Title / Rank / Birthplace / Gender / Sexuality / Marital Status
and the rest of the coworker sheet) is appended -- that panel is UI and the port does not
model it.

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f2e25de0` lowercases the chosen label and runs two substring
tests in this order, `'reject' #64467` (cell `0x5c469b0`) then `'report' #64521` (cell
`0x5c45690`); anything else is an advance.

**Reject** (`0x73f2e26170`) moves the supervisor's relationship bar (slot `0x508`) by -4 and
the hero's discipline by +4 impact, and nothing else. Its unlock strings are the office
vocabulary: `'Not paying me enough' #32109`, `"I'm trying to work here" #26074`,
`"Give me a raise then we'll talk" #21700`, `'Strictly business' #40208`, `"I'm not a piece of
meat" #26017`. The journal is the row's own log column.

**Report** (`0x73f2e2641c`) pushes a bare `Scenario` carrying cell `0x5c607f8` and links it at
`[self+0x128]`; when the hero was the one being pursued it also calls
`SimWorkplace::ImpactWorkplacePerformance @0x73f2fe99d8` with 5, moves the supervisor's bar by
+5, and moves the hero's discipline by -3 impact -- the boss is protected, the hero pays. It
then pushes `ScenarioSupervisorSeduceSuccess` (`.ctor(Boolean) @0x73f2e27214`) with
`w1 = (_gettingSeduced == 0)`.

**Advance** first asks whether the boss would even accept:
`SimWorkplace::WillSupervisorAcceptHeroAttemptToSeduce @0x73f2fe95cc` (called at
`0x73f2e265f4`) plus the supervisor's interest float `[supervisor+0x244]`. The refusal branch
(interest <= 20.0, `0x73f2e265fc`) does `ImpactWorkplacePerformance(-4)`, supervisor bar -5,
hero happiness -4, then tests the supervisor's `[0x3e8]` vtable result against `0xe` (15).
The attempt branch (`0x73f2e26920`) compares the same interest float with `10.0` and with
`GetRandomNumber(0,100) @0x73f32ab2a8`. A win pushes
`ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineHR` -- the class section 116 also pushes -- so that HR disciplines
the hero for it (`.ctor(String,Int32) @0x73f2e2734c`, wording
`'trying to seduce <your/my> {0}' #67282`, cell `0x5c60ae0`). A loss writes
`'Your attempt to seduce your {0}, {1}, was unsuccessful.' #50219` (cell `0x5c60b48`) and
`'I attempted to seduce my {0}, {1}, but failed.' #23581` (cell `0x5c60b60`). The lane also
carries the reaction strings `'I seduced my {0}, {1}!' #25067`, `'It was all a test. You
passed.' #27599`, `"That's probably best" #41443`, the secret-keeping trio
`'{0}{1} said that this will remain a secret just between the two of you.' #70848` /
`'{0}{1} reminded you that snitches end up in ditches.' #70847` /
`"{0}{1} told you that it's a standing offer." #70869`, the adjective pairs
`'horny' #60382` / `'horny little' #60384` and `'nasty' #62777` / `'nasty little' #62778`,
and the memory line `'Friends say {0} once dropped {1} pants in front of {2} {3}.' #20737`.

Both lanes end on `Log(journal) @0x73f380158c` and a tail `RefreshUI @0x73f3580f5c`.

### 120.4 How the port reaches it

`Sim::seduceYear` (port/src/sim.cpp) is wired into the same year dispatch as the rest of the
family, right after the lightning strike, and runs on its own stream `seducRng_` so the main
`rng_` sequence -- and therefore every other card's timing -- is untouched.

```cpp
bool Sim::seduceYear(Life& life, AgeUp& out, int forcedChoice) {
  if (forcedChoice >= 0) return false;
  if (h.age < 18) return false;              // gate step 1
  if (!h.employed && !h.military) return false;  // gate step 2
  if (h.sedPresented >= 5) return false;     // gate step 3
  static const char* kTable = "a16_coworker-hookup-scenarios-enc";
  if (!seducRng_.chance(0.05)) return false;
  ...
  const bool inbound = seducRng_.chance(0.5);   // the game's _gettingSeduced byte
  ...
  const int pick = int(seducRng_.below(3));     // the game lets the hero choose
```

The port keeps the same three lanes and the same direction split, but draws the answer instead
of asking it: `pick == 1` is the reject lane (discipline +16 points, the game's +4 impact),
`pick == 2` is the report lane (no stat move; the pushed discipline scenario, the workplace
performance move and the supervisor bar are shortcut comments), and `pick == 0` is an advance
whose wording comes from the direction and whose outcome is a coin -- success writes
`'I seduced my supervisor, NAME!'` and moves nothing, failure writes
`'I attempted to seduce my supervisor, NAME, but failed.'` and costs happiness (the game's -1
impact, -4 points). While the boss is the one advancing the direct route costs discipline
(the game's -3 impact, -16 points) because HR becomes involved.

Four cards from a seeds 1 to 40 sweep, one per lane:

```
age 68, row 12, Seductress, reject
  Your supervisor, Willie Eyelash, winks at you and tells you that her door is always open
  for you, both literally and figuratively.
  Reject his advances                              discipline +16
  my supervisor, Willie Eyelash, suggestively told me that her door is always open for me.

age 27, row 13, Seductress, report
  Your supervisor, Willie Eyelash, tells you that she is happy that you're on the staff, but
  tells you that she would love to be on your staff.
  Report him to HR                                 no stat move

age 60, row 13, Seductress, advance
  Your supervisor, Willie Eyelash, tells you that she is happy that you're on the staff, but
  tells you that she would love to be on your staff.
  Hit that                                         discipline -16

age 42, row 12, Seducer, hero advances and wins
  You winked at Court Kurbain and told him your door is always open for him, both literally
  and figuratively.
  Hook up with him                                 no stat move
  I seduced my supervisor, Court Kurbain!

age 66, row 22, Seductress, hero advances and fails
  You told Sugar Moon that there's a pretty package for her on the front desk, but there's an
  even prettier one inside your pants.
  Try to seduce her                                happiness -4
  I attempted to seduce my supervisor, Sugar Moon, but failed.
```

The body opens in the second person in both directions, which is the table's own doing: the
outbound cells are written as the hero's line (`'You told <coworker> ...'`) and the port
substitutes the boss's name into the token, so the sentence names him twice over -- once as
the speaker's audience and once through the replacement.

### 120.5 Shortcuts

* The profile panel (Name / Title / Rank / Birthplace / Gender / Sexuality / Marital Status /
  Widow / Widower / Divorced / Married to / Straight / Gay) is not modelled; the port has no
  coworker sheet.
* The supervisor's relationship bar (slot `0x508`), the hero's happiness slot `0x408` on some
  branches, `ImpactWorkplacePerformance` and `WillSupervisorAcceptHeroAttemptToSeduce` are
  port-side comments: the port has no per-coworker bars and one workplace number, not a floor
  of them.
* The pushed scenarios -- the bare discipline report, `ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineHR`, and
  `ScenarioSupervisorSeduceSuccess` -- are not pushed. The success card exists only as the
  journal sentence here.
* The lover candidate (`SimLover::GenerateLoverFromCoworker`), the unlock strings, the
  secret-keeping trio, the adjective pairs and the obituary memory line are not modelled.
* The military branch of the third button (`'Report {0} misconduct'`) is modelled by service
  branch because the port tracks `h.military`; the civilian wording is used otherwise.
* The advance lane's win/loss coin is the port's own: the game compares the supervisor's
  interest float against a 0-100 draw, and the port has no interest float, so it draws the
  outcome directly.
### 120.6 Verification

The card has a probe of its own, `/tmp/qdir/sdres.py`: eighty lives (seeds 1 to 40, both
sexes, eighty years each) that reconstruct the hero's stats from the newborn block plus each
event's deltas and then check the card against the table row it claims to come from. It
checks the title (`Seducer` / `Seductress`), the table name, the age floor, the direction read
off the body, the row's own cell rebuilt as a pattern (the `<coworker>` token as a capture,
every slash list as alternatives, gender tokens as wildcards, with the role wording the port
adds stripped off first), the `Supervisor Appropriate` marker on inbound rows, the journal
shape with `<rb>` tied to a value that is actually present in the body, the choice set allowed
per direction, and the lane deltas.

```
lives 80
hookup cards 100
directions {'inbound': 58, 'outbound': 42}
rows drawn 21 of 24
choices {'Report him to HR': 11, 'Report her to HR': 16, 'Hit that': 11,
         'Reject his advances': 16, 'Let me get a piece of that': 10,
         'Reject her advances': 20, 'Hook up with him': 6, 'Try to seduce her': 4,
         'Give it to him': 2, 'Get at it': 3, 'Give it to her': 1}
supervisors seen 30
cards per life {0: 29, 1: 21, 2: 14, 3: 13, 4: 3}
hero age at the card min 20 max 78
runtime 17s
failures 0
events 100
RESIDUE 0 {}
rc 0
```

`tools/test_coworker.py` grew a hookup block (cap five, age floor, table, direction, row cell,
no leftover token, lane deltas, the two seduce journals, and the journal as the arbiter of the
name the card really wrote) and its final assertion now demands the hookup table in the set of
tables the run reached. Green:

```
coworker cards by table: {'a16_coworker-annoy-scenarios-enc': 151,
  'a16_coworker-behavior-scenarios-enc': 120, 'a16_coworker-pranks-enc': 108,
  'a16_coworker-rumors-enc': 92, 'a16_supervisor-unprofessional-scenarios-enc': 113,
  'after hours': 83, 'hookup': 100, 'team building': 51}
supervisors seen: 37
team building cards: 51
after hours cards: 83
hookup cards: 100
```

The counters moved against section 119's run (annoy 148 to 151, behavior 115 to 120, rumors 96
to 92, supervisor cards 114 to 113, after hours 81 to 83, team building 52 to 51) for the same
reason every section since 116 has moved them: the card writes happiness and discipline, so the
eligibility of the later years shifts. Section 119's quoted numbers stay as printed.

One real defect came out of the test rather than the probe, and it was in the port: the
possessive form was built by chopping the last character off the who-string and appending
`'s`, which is correct for the inbound wording (`your supervisor, NAME,`) but wrong for the
outbound one, where the who-string is the bare name -- the card read `You flashed a suggestive
smile Ram Smit's, way and asked her ...`, one letter short of the boss's name. The two forms
are now built explicitly (`whoBodyPoss` / `whoLogPoss`) for both directions. The probe's lazy
name capture had happily accepted the truncated name, which is exactly why the test asserts the
journal's own name is present in the body.

The full batch for this change:

```
cmake --build port/build -j8                     green
tools/coverage.py          captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107
                           contentless entries: 2 -- ScenarioMiniPaywall x2
portgap.py                 ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port 107 gap 0
rescensus.py               distinct residue tokens 0 total 0
covpush (seed 12345, ages 109)   rc=0, empty stderr
/tmp/qdir/allprobes.py     63 probes, every one rc=0, 62 with residue=0
                           (idres.py prints residue=? by design)
tools/bench.sh trace_c10   diff against section 119 is empty
```

The empty bench diff is the point of the separate stream: `seducRng_` keeps the card off the
main `rng_` sequence, so the ages 0 to 34 trace that every section quotes is still byte for
byte the same.

## 121. The witness: the street's first card, and the only one that asks what a bystander does

Section 119 put a card in the port that can end the life; section 120 put one in
the office. This one puts a card in the street, and it is the first entry of the
citizen family: a passer-by commits a crime in front of the hero and the hero
decides what a witness does about it.

`ScenarioEthicsWitnessCrime` sits at il2cpp_dump.txt:38414 and is the only class
between the two street families the port has left. It reads one content table and
one code-built string array, it has no follow-up of its own, and its gate asks
for nothing the port does not already track -- which is why it is the first card
after the supervisor hookup that can be ported without inventing a subsystem.

### 121.1 The class and its gate

The class carries four fields:

| Offset | Type | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x16a | System.Boolean | `_happenedOnWalk` |
| 0x170 | DataStreetPerson | `_streetPerson` |
| 0x178 | System.String | `_crimeString` |
| 0x180 | System.String | `_crimeAndPerpetratorString` |

Its methods are `.ctor @0x73f3bce8a0`, `RefreshScenario @0x73f3bce8c4` (186
instructions), `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex @0x73f3bcebac` (709) and
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush @0x73f3bcf6c0` (90). The constructor stores the
card's category `Citizen` (#15649, cell 0x5cb81f8) at [self+0x30] and its title
`Witness` (#47077, cell 0x5cb87f8) at [self+0x38].

The gate is four tests and one setting:

1. the hero's age at [x9+0x20] is at least 0x12 -- eighteen;
2. `Life::PresentedCountForScenario` on the class name is below four
   (`cmp w0,#3; b.gt` to the false return) -- so a life may see this card at most
   four times, half the supervisor family's cap;
3. `SimHero::CurrentlyInPrison @0x73f2f0e1d8` is false;
4. `System.Boolean KeepItClean() @0x73f32aba1c` returns false, tested with
   `eor w8,w0,#1`. This is the game's own censorship switch, and it is the first
   gate in the port that reads a setting rather than a stat: `KeepItClean` walks
   the life object down to `[life+0x48] -> [x8+0x14c]` and returns that
   value < 2, which normal play leaves at zero.

No income, no job, no place and no fame test appears anywhere in those ninety
instructions, so the card is offered to every adult in the street.

### 121.2 The sentence, and the two lists it comes out of

`RefreshScenario` clears the base byte 0x28, then draws the perpetrator:

```
_streetPerson = DataHub::GetRandomStreetPersonAndMustBeInNeed(false) @0x73f2ca4c58
_crimeString  = DataHub::GetRandomCrimeToWitness()                     @0x73f2ca31ac
```

The boolean argument to the first call is zero, so the picker is free to return
any row of `a16_street-persons-enc` -- 201 lines, 200 people, from `tourist` and
`magician` to `pimp`, `crackhead`, `frat bro`, `old geezer` and `milkmaid`. The
row's `Description` column holds the bare noun phrase with no article, and the
row's `Percent Male` column gives the sex the journal line needs.

The sentence then goes through the game's article helper and its two-element
format:

```
x20 = streetPerson[0x10]                       ; the row's Description, no article
AddIndefiniteArticleToString(x20, cell 0x5c2f928) @0x73f32aee9c
Format(cell 0x5c345b0 '{0} {1}', article + description, _crimeString) @0x73f52a71cc
   -> _crimeAndPerpetratorString, e.g. 'a homeless man robbing a bank'
```

and the body's {0} is one of two strings: `While on your walk` (#46721, cell
0x5c3d5d8) when the walk pushed the card, or `DataHub::GetRandomCircumstance`
@0x73f2ce2d08 otherwise -- the same 43-slot switch section 119 already reads.
The finished sentence is `Format(cell 0x5cb8800 '{0}, you witness {1}!' #70596)`
stored at [self+0x48], and the card raises its own bit at [self+0x110].

`GetRandomCrimeToWitness` builds its static array out of 33 consecutive cells,
0x5c554f0 to 0x5c555f0 in steps of eight, and the order is the list the port
now keeps:

| # | Crime | # | Crime | # | Crime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | smoking in a prohibited area | 11 | littering | 22 | vandalizing a convenience store |
| 1 | driving on the sidewalk | 12 | stealing someone's mail | 23 | throwing beer bottles into oncoming traffic |
| 2 | having sex in public | 13 | stealing a bike | 24 | masturbating in public |
| 3 | spanking a child | 14 | trespassing | 25 | drinking in public |
| 4 | keying a car | 15 | breaking into a car | 26 | being cruel to a dog |
| 5 | burning things in the street | 16 | jaywalking | 27 | slanging drugs on the street |
| 6 | filming porn in public | 17 | fishing without a license | 28 | soliciting a prostitute |
| 7 | graffitiing a wall | 18 | threatening an old lady | 29 | urinating in public |
| 8 | drinking and driving | 19 | streaking naked | 30 | kidnapping a child |
| 9 | trying to burn down a church | 20 | stealing a car | 31 | flying a drone |
| 10 | robbing a bank | 21 | selling drugs | 32 | forging documents |

Three buttons are built with `Scenario::.ctor(String,bool,bool) @0x73f2eb9c50`:
`Try to intervene` (#44129, cell 0x5cac6e8), `Call the police` (#14600, cell
0x5c3c1d0) and `Look the other way` (#29196, cell 0x5c4c800).

### 121.3 Three things a bystander can do

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` lowercases the label and formats the journal's first
clause once, `Format(cell 0x5cb8808 'I witnessed {0}.' #25813, _crimeAndPerpetratorString)`,
then substring-tests the label against `look`, `police` and `intervene` in that
order.

**Look the other way.** `SimPerson::ImpactKarma(-2) @0x73f30e4bfc` and then
`ImpactDiscipline(-1) @0x73f30e4cdc` -- the karma call comes first in this lane,
the reverse of the intervene lane. The journal is
`Format(cell 0x5cb84e8 '{0} I looked the other way.' #69585)`, and the lane also
raises a byte at `[life+0x70] -> +0x399`, which is the game's own "hero saw
something and said nothing" record. It is the cheapest of the three in
discipline and the most expensive in karma.

**Call the police.** `ImpactDiscipline(+2)`, then the interesting part:
`get_PlaceOfResidence` and `SimPlace::ShouldGetCapturedWhenInteractingWithPoliceInPlace`
@0x73f2f2782c decide whether the hero is swept up with the perpetrator. When that
returns true the game pushes `SimPlace::GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType(0)`
@0x73f2f16ab4 into the follow-up slot at [self+0x128]; when it returns false it
runs a five-draw and a ten-draw and branches twice more. Either way the journal
is
`Format(cell 0x5cb8838 '{0} I called the police on {1}.' #69535)`, with {1} the
perpetrator's pronoun -- `him` (cell 0x5c35d08) or `her` (cell 0x5c35d00) chosen
off `streetPerson[0x1c]`.

**Try to intervene.** `ImpactKarma(+3)` and `ImpactDiscipline(+3)` -- the only
lane that pays in both currencies. The journal is
`Format(cell 0x5cb8848 '{0} I stopped the {1}!' #69618)` over the row's bare
description, and then `GetRandomNumber(0,4)` picks what the intervention costs:
on a three or four the game pushes a scenario built with
`Format(cell 0x5cb8810 'You successfully stopped the {0} from {1}.' #49438)`, and
on a zero, one or two (the branch at 0x73f3bcf0ec) it builds the perpetrator
turning on the hero instead, with `The {0}` / `the {0}` (cells 0x5c3cb08,
0x5c3cac8) over the description. So the brave choice is the only one with a
chance of a second card.

All three lanes converge on a dismiss journal assembled with the obituary tokens
`<obit-he/she>` (#9301, cell 0x5c34a20), then `Log @0x73f380158c` and
`RefreshUI @0x73f3580f5c`.

### 121.4 How the port reaches it

`Sim::witnessYear` (port/src/sim.cpp, wired in the year dispatch right after
`seduceYear`) is the port's card for this class, and it is code-built in the same
shape as the lightning strike:

* the gate is `age >= 18`, `!h.inPrison`, `h.witPresented < 4` and a one-in-twenty
  coin. The `KeepItClean` test is dropped, because the port has no content
  setting to read and normal play leaves the game's own switch off;
* the perpetrator is a uniform row pick over `a16_street-persons-enc`, with the
  row's `Percent Male` column compared against a hundred-sided draw for the sex;
* the crime comes out of the port's copy of the same 33-entry array (a static
  `const char* const kCrimes[]` next to the other card pools), and the article is
  the port's existing `articleFor` helper (port/src/sim.cpp:1732) -- the same
  `a` / `an` split the game's `AddIndefiniteArticleToString` makes;
* the body's scene is a coin between `While on your walk` and the port's own
  `kCircumstancePublicScenes`, because the port has no walk to have happened on;
* the three lanes are drawn with `witRng_.below(3)` and the port keeps the
  discipline and karma moves (`pointsForImpact(-2)` -8, `pointsForImpact(-1)` -4,
  `pointsForImpact(2)` 8, `pointsForImpact(3)` 16) and the exact journal of each;
* the counter is `Hero::witPresented` (port/include/bl/game.h) and the stream is
  `witRng_` (port/include/bl/sim.h), seeded from the same life seed with a constant
  pair of its own -- the sixty-second stream the engine seeds -- so no other
  family's draw sequence moves.

Five cards the port drew, one per shape it can take:

| Seed | Age | Row | Body | Choice | Journal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 male | 44 | 143 | While on your walk, you witness a frat bro vandalizing a convenience store! | Look the other way | I witnessed a frat bro vandalizing a convenience store. I looked the other way. (karma -8, discipline -4) |
| 1 male | 63 | 68 | While on your walk, you witness a crackhead spanking a child! | Try to intervene | I witnessed a crackhead spanking a child. I stopped the crackhead! (karma +16, discipline +16) |
| 9 male | 52 | 145 | While on your walk, you witness a milkmaid drinking in public! | Call the police | I witnessed a milkmaid drinking in public. I called the police on her. (discipline +8) |
| 13 male | 44 | 43 | While on your walk, you witness a pervert masturbating in public! | Call the police | I witnessed a pervert masturbating in public. I called the police on him. (discipline +8) |
| 3 male | 32 | 193 | While out fishing, you witness a dating coach keying a car! | Look the other way | I witnessed a dating coach keying a car. I looked the other way. (karma -8, discipline -4) |
| 5 male | 34 | 41 | While taking out the trash, you witness an old geezer stealing a car! | Look the other way | I witnessed an old geezer stealing a car. I looked the other way. (karma -8, discipline -4) |

The last two rows show the circumstance half of the scene draw -- `While out
fishing` and `While taking out the trash` come out of the same 43-slot switch
section 119 wired -- and the `an old geezer` row shows the article helper doing
its job on a vowel.

### 121.5 Shortcuts

* `KeepItClean` @0x73f32aba1c is not read. The port has no censorship setting and
  the switch is off in every capture, so the card is offered as if it were off.
* `_happenedOnWalk` (0x16a) is drawn as a coin rather than carried: the port has
  no walk, and the flag only chooses which of the two {0} strings opens the body.
* The police lane's `ShouldGetCapturedWhenInteractingWithPoliceInPlace` chain --
  `SimPlace::GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType` and the two extra draws -- needs the
  place's crime list, which the port does not model (the same gap that keeps
  `ScenarioCrimeCapture` and `ScenarioCrimeFalseAccusation` unwired). The lane
  keeps its discipline move and its journal.
* The intervene lane's two follow-ups (`You successfully stopped the {0} from
  {1}.` and the perpetrator-turns-on-the-hero card) are not pushed: the port has
  no gate for either. The journal keeps the ``I stopped the ...!`` line.
* The byte at `[life+0x70]+0x399` (the hero looked away) and the card's own bit at
  [self+0x110] are not kept; nothing else in the port reads them.
* The `Witness` category label at [self+0x30] is not carried -- the port's cards
  have no category.

### 121.6 Verification

/tmp/qdir/witres.py -- 80 lives (seeds 1..40 x both sexes x 80 years), 21 s:

```
lives 80
witness cards 88
rows drawn 39 of 201
choices {'Look the other way': 24, 'Try to intervene': 34, 'call the police': 30}
scenes drawn 23 of 42
cards per life {0: 21, 1: 35, 2: 19, 3: 5}
hero age at the card min 19 max 73
runtime 21s
failures 0
events 88
RESIDUE 0 {}
rc 0
```

The probe reconstructs the sentence from the row it names: the body must be one
of the 42 scenes, the article-carrying description of the drawn row and one of the
33 crimes, exactly. It then checks each lane's journal and its exact delta set,
that no angle-bracket token survives, that the card never opens before 18 and
never appears more than four times in a life. Its first run reported two failures,
both in the probe: it had expected the karma move to be clipped when the hero had
no karma left, but the port reports the card's own move, not the clamped result --
the same reading every other card probe uses.

`tools/test_witness.py` is the repo's regression, built on the same checks and
run by the sweep:

```
lives 80 / witness cards 88 / lanes {'look': 24, 'intervene': 34, 'police': 30}
rows drawn 39 of 201 / cards per life {0: 21, 1: 35, 2: 19, 3: 5} / ok
```

Its first run failed on the last line for an honest reason: no life drew four
cards in this sweep, so the assertion that the cap is reachable was replaced by
one that the multi-card path is exercised (a life with three). The cap of four is
still checked in the other direction -- the sweep fails if any life draws five.

The full batch was green: `captured scenarios: 109  recoverable: 107` with
`contentless entries: 2 -- ScenarioMiniPaywall x2`; `ENTRIES 109 rendered-by-port
107 gap 0`; the residue census `distinct residue tokens 0 total 0`; 64 probes,
every one `rc=0` and all but the id probe at `residue=0`; and the ages 0..34 bench
trace byte-identical to section 120's, because `witRng_` keeps the card off the
main stream.

The sibling tests are green with the card in place. The coworker family's counters
are `annoy 149, behavior 119, pranks 109, rumors 94, unprofessional 110, after
hours 83, hookup 94, team building 52` with `supervisors seen: 38`, against
section 120's run of `151 / 120 / 108 / 92 / 113 / 83 / 100 / 51` and 37
supervisors. The witness card moves karma and discipline, and because a card that
fires owns the year, every family whose cards are tried after it in the dispatch
loses the years this one takes -- the same drift sections 116 and 117 recorded.
The lightning test still draws 76 cards and rolls 4 deaths, because the witness
card never touches `lightRng_`. The earlier sections keep their quoted numbers;
the fresh ones live here.

## 122. The drug find: the second card that can end the life, and the first one that pays

Section 121 followed a bystander who watches a stranger commit a crime. This card
is the same family read from the other side: the hero is walking somewhere, sees
a bag on the ground, opens it, and finds a drug he can hand in, sell, ignore, or
swallow. It is the port's second card with a death in it, the first whose death
sentence names the thing that killed the hero, and the first card the port ever
wired that pays money.

### 122.1 The class, and a gate that counts showings

```
class ScenarioEthicsFindDrugs : Scenario          il2cpp_dump.txt:38372
    field 0x16a System.Boolean _happenedOnWalk
    field 0x170 System.String  _narrative
    field 0x178 System.String  _containerString
    field 0x180 DataDrug        _drug
    field 0x188 System.Single   _value
    method @0x73f3bc8b34 .ctor()
    method @0x73f3bc8b58 RefreshScenario()
    method @0x73f3bc8ff8 ChoiceSelectedAtIndex(System.Int32)
    method @0x73f3bc9c00 ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush()
```

The gate at `0x73f3bc9c00` is ninety instructions and four tests, and three of
them are the witness card's own:

1. the hero resolves through the singleton at `0x5c30250`, and his age at
   `[x9+0x20]` must clear `0x15` -- twenty-one, three years older than the
   witness card asks;
2. `Life::PresentedCountForScenario @0x73f3736430` must be at most two
   (`cmp w0,#2` then `b.gt` to the false return), so a life sees this card at
   most three times;
3. `SimHero::CurrentlyInPrison @0x73f2f0e1d8` must be false;
4. `System.Boolean KeepItClean() @0x73f32aba1c` must be false -- the same
   censorship switch section 121 reads, which is off in normal play.

The gate draws nothing. Unlike the witness card, whose eligibility is a plain
older-than test, this one is offered behind the same one-in-twenty wall every
card since section 116 has used.

```
73f3bc9c60 ldr w9, [x9, #0x20]     ; hero age
73f3bc9c64 cmp w9, #0x15
73f3bc9c68 b.lt #0x73f3bc9cf4      ; younger than 21 -> false
73f3bc9cc8 cmp w0, #2              ; PresentedCountForScenario
73f3bc9ccc b.gt #0x73f3bc9cf4      ; three showings -> false
73f3bc9cf0 tbz w0, #0, #0x73f3bc9d08   ; not in prison -> keep going
73f3bc9d24 bl #0x73f32aba1c        ; KeepItClean()
73f3bc9d28 eor w8, w0, #1          ; the card needs it false
```

### 122.2 Six containers, fourteen drugs, four buttons

`RefreshScenario` opens with a twenty-eight cell lazy static init and then does
three things, in this order.

**A container.** `GetRandomNumber(0,6) @0x73f32ab2a8` picks one of six, and each
arm carries its own money band, drawn as `GetRandomNumber(0, hi) + lo`:

| roll | container | cell | value band |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | duffle bag | `0x5c554d8` #57755 | 5000 + 0..20000 |
| 1 | satchel | `0x5cb8208` #64903 | 5000 + 0..20000 |
| 2 | backpack | `0x5c567c8` #54735 | 5000 + 0..20000 |
| 3 | shopping bag | `0x5cb8230` #65575 | 2500 + 0..12500 |
| 4 | grocery cart | `0x5cb8200` #59990 | 50000 + 0..250000 |
| 5 | briefcase | `0x5c3bd48` #55238 | 2500 + 0..12500 |

The bands are literal immediates in the switch: `mov w24, #0x1388` and
`mov w20, #0x4e20` for the first three, `mov w24, #0x9c4` and
`mov w20, #0x30d4` for the shopping bag and the briefcase, and
`mov w24, #0xc350` with `mov w20, #0xd090` / `movk w20, #3, lsl #16` for
the grocery cart -- `0x3d090`, a quarter of a million, which is why the cart is
the only container worth the risk.

**A drug.** `DataHub::GetRandomIllegalDrug @0x73f2ca6dc8` answers a row of
`a16_drugs-enc`. The table is 27 lines wide-columned, and only the rows whose
`Illegal` column is marked are eligible: fourteen of the twenty-six.

**A sentence.** Two formats, both cells the loader keeps:

```
0x5cb8228 #70588  '{0}, you come across a {1} filled with what appears to be {2}.'
0x5cb8218 #24192  'I found a {0} full of {1}.'
```

The `{0}` of the first is `_happenedOnWalk ? 'While on your walk' : DataHub::GetRandomCircumstance() @0x73f2ce2d08`
-- the walk byte `0x16a` is only ever set by the small ctor at
`0x73f3bc8b34`, which the walk feature pushes. The second is the narrative, and
it is also the prefix every journal line opens with: `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`
builds it once with `Format(cell 0x5c31470 '{0}', _narrative)` before it tests a
single button.

Four buttons, each built with `Scenario::.ctor(String,bool,bool) @0x73f2eb9c50`:
`Turn it in to authorities` #44250, `Sell it` #38533,
`Pretend like I didn't see it` #34512 and `Consume all of it` #16228. The
dispatch lowers the label and runs `Contains @0x73f52aafdc` four times, in this
order: `turn` (cell `0x5c3f410`), `sell` (`0x5c35db0`), `pretend`
(`0x5c46ca8`), `consume` (`0x5cb82b0`).

### 122.3 The four lanes, and the one that kills

**Turn it in.** `ImpactDiscipline(5)` and `ImpactKarma(5)`, then one roll decides
whether the police believe him: `GetRandomNumber(0,1000)` against `100` minus the
health float at `hero+0x9c`. A healthy hero is never arrested; a battered one
sometimes is.

* clean: journal `'{0} I turned it in.'` #69635, the push
  `'You turned the {0} of {1} into authoritites.'` #49677 (the table's spelling,
  kept), the unlock `Model citizen`, and the obituary memory line
  `'Friends describe {0} as someone of strong moral fabric.'` #20679;
* busted: `happiness -6`, journal
  `'{0} I tried to turn it into authorities but they arrested me!'` #69633, one
  unlock drawn from four, the push
  `'The authorities arrested you as soon as they saw you carrying a {0} full of {1}!'`
  #41735 and `SimPlace::GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType(7)` at `[self+0x128]`.

**Sell it.** `ImpactDiscipline(-3)` and `ImpactKarma(-5)`, then
`GetRandomNumber(0,100)` against the same health float, and this time health has
to *beat* the roll:

* sold: `happiness +4`, `AdjustBankBalanceByAmount @0x73f2f0cd68` by `_value`,
  journal `'{0} I earned {1} by selling it.'` #69562 with a currency string, the
  push `'You earned {0} by selling the {1} full of {2}.'` #48420 and the unlock
  `Come up`;
* caught: `happiness -6`, journal `'{0} I was caught trying to sell it!'` #69641,
  the push `'You were caught trying to sell the {0} full of {1}!'` #49759,
  `GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType(3)` and the unlock `Busted`.

**Pretend.** `ImpactDiscipline(2)`, `ImpactKarma(2)`, journal
`'{0} I left it alone.'` #69582, the unlock `I'll leave happily`. Nothing else
happens, which makes it the only lane with no roll in it at all.

**Consume.** `ImpactDiscipline(-5)`, `ImpactKarma(-4)`, `happiness -5` and the
fifth stat slot `0x418` also `-5`, journal `'{0} I consumed it.'` #69544 -- and
then the death roll. `GetRandomNumber(0,5)` is compared against the row's
`Overdose Likeliness Score` at `[drug+0x24]`; if the draw lands under it, and
`SimPerson::IsVampire @0x73f30e1058` says the hero is not one, the card fills the
`DeathManager` at `[life+0x20]+0xa0` with the drug object and the hero's age,
calls `UpdateDeathType(4) @0x73f2fb077c`, invokes the kill at vtable `0x368`,
and pushes a follow-up scenario. Survivors get the push
`'You consumed the {0} full of {1}.'` #48210, the unlock `Never again`, the
addiction branch (`ShouldBecomeAddictedToDrug @0x73f2f1d674` then
`BecomeAddictedToDrug @0x73f2f1dcdc`) and the obituary line
`'Rumors suggest {0} once consumed an entire {1} of {2}.'` #36386.

The table's overdose rows are `Fluke` with a minimum age of 16, and the sentence
names the drug: `'<pronoun> died from a crack overdose.'` (row 16),
`cocaine` (17), `methamphetamine` (18) and a generic `pain pill` (19).

### 122.4 How the port reaches it

```
port/include/bl/game.h:786   int findPresented = 0;
port/include/bl/game.h:787   std::string drugDeath;   // the drug that kills the hero, when one does
port/include/bl/sim.h:501    bool findDrugsYear(Life& life, AgeUp& out, int forcedChoice);
port/include/bl/sim.h:650    Rng findRng_;   // ScenarioEthicsFindDrugs' own stream (REPORT.en.md 122)
port/src/sim.cpp:640         findRng_(seed ^ 0x452821e638d01377ULL ^ 0xbe5466cf34e90c6cULL),
port/src/sim.cpp:3633        if (findDrugsYear(life, out, forcedChoice)) return true;
port/src/sim.cpp:26856       bool Sim::findDrugsYear
```

The card is wired immediately after the witness card and draws on its own stream,
so every card before it behaves exactly as it did -- the ages 0..34 bench trace
does not move a line. The gate is age twenty-one, no prison, `findPresented < 3`
and `findRng_.below(20) != 0` to refuse. The container, its band, the drug pool
(fourteen rows whose `Illegal` column is marked) and the four lanes are the
switch and the lanes above, with `pointsForImpact` doing the stat mapping the
game does through `AttributeAdjustmentPointsForImpactScore @0x73f32b140c`:
`+5` is 50, `-4` is -30, `-5` is -50 and `-6` is -100, which is why the busted
lane can take a whole hundred happiness in one go.

The scene is drawn the way section 121 draws its own -- a coin between the walk
wording and the shared forty-one-slot scene switch -- because the port has no
walk feature to set `_happenedOnWalk`.

Six sampled cards, one per lane and per container class:

| seed / sex | age | row | card | lane |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 / male | 52 | 12 | While strolling through the park, you come across a backpack filled with what appears to be PCP. | pretend |
| 2 / male | 62 | 3 | During a baseball game, you come across a satchel filled with what appears to be methamphetamine. | sell, caught |
| 4 / male | 32 | 24 | While out for a walk, you come across a grocery cart filled with what appears to be crack cocaine. | consume |
| 4 / female | 41 | 15 | While returning a book to the library, you come across a grocery cart filled with what appears to be nitrous oxide. | turn in, clean |

The consume lane on the third card moved `karma -30`, `discipline -50`,
`happiness -50` and `health -50` and left the hero alive; the same lane on seed 6
and seed 10 killed him, and the death record names the drug the card drew:

```
{"type": "Fluke", "sentence": "he died from a crack overdose."}
{"type": "Fluke", "sentence": "she died from a cocaine overdose."}
```

`Sim::checkDeath` at `port/src/sim.cpp:23324` therefore grew a second pre-empt
beside the lightning one: when `drugDeath` is set it looks for the overdose row
whose sentence contains that drug's name, falls back to any overdose row, and
answers with the table's own `Type` and `resolve(Sentence)`.

### 122.5 Shortcuts

* **The walk byte.** `_happenedOnWalk` (`0x16a`) is written only by the ctor at
  `0x73f3bc8b34`, which a walk feature the port does not model pushes. The scene
  is a coin between `While on your walk` and the shared scene switch, the same
  compromise section 121 made.
* **The two `GetRandomNumber(0,1)` guards.** `RefreshScenario` rolls one draw and
  skips the whole sentence pair when it is nonzero, which can never happen with
  the engine's own `Range(0,1)`; the port builds the sentence unconditionally.
* **The pushes and unlocks.** The four pushed follow-ups (the two crime
  scenarios, the consume follow-up, the arrest line), the seven unlock strings,
  the three obituary memory lines and the achievement are UI-side and unmodelled.
* **Addiction.** `ShouldBecomeAddictedToDrug` and `BecomeAddictedToDrug` want a
  `SimAddiction` list the port does not carry, so the consume lane's addiction
  branch is a comment.
* **The money arm** moves `h.money` directly, the way the port's other money
  cards do, and formats it with the loader's own `money()`.

### 122.6 Verification

The probe (`/tmp/qdir/fdres.py`, eighty lives: seeds 1..40 in both sexes, each
played to eighty) reproduces the card from the loader's own data and checks every
lane:
