### 187.1 The bench moved 61 lines, and the fix was the port's own idiom

Added naively (drawing from `loverRng_`), the card shifted **every later draw in that
stream** and the bench diff grew to 61 lines — content reshuffled, not degraded, but
unreadable.

The port's documented idiom is a **dedicated stream per card family** so earlier draws
never move. Both ambient cards now draw from `ambientRng_`:

```cpp
// A stream for the one-off ambient cards, so adding one cannot shift every later draw
// in loverRng_ -- the port's own idiom for a new card.
Rng ambientRng_;
```

```
drawing from loverRng_:   61 diff lines
drawing from ambientRng_:  6 diff lines
```

The remaining six are the card's own appearances. That is the difference between a diff
that can be read and one that has to be trusted.

```

`<rb>` is the port's existing *refer back* token — it points at whichever alternative
the body chose — so the card picks once and uses it twice:

```
B: While playing BitLife on your father's phone, you stumble upon a video ...
J: I discovered a video of my father having sex with a neighbor.
```

### 188.1 Verification, and an assertion that had to lose a direction

`tools/test_parent_cheat.py`:

```
cards: 10
ok
NaN

The first version required the journal to *always* reuse the body's word, and failed on
seed 6 — that row's log says **'having sex'** outright and carries no `<rb>` at all. The
check is now one-way: when a journal does carry the word, the body must have chosen it,
and a left-over `<rb>` is caught independently. 10 cards across 60 short lives.

Bench 0 lines: the card draws from `ambientRng_` (§187), so a rare card perturbs nothing
else — the idiom is paying for itself.

## 189. Three ambient cards do not add up, and the model is why

§188's risk said a third card in `ambientRng_` would thin the other two. Measuring it:

```
lives: 60
  1.22 per life  a16_paranormal-encounters-enc   (coin 1 in 22 per year)
  0.87 per life  a16_stalker-scenarios-enc       (coin 1 in 20 per year)
  0.23 per life  a16_parent-cheat-scenarios-enc  (coin 1 in 30 per year)
```

and the arithmetic that makes them strange: 85 years at 1-in-22 is **3.9** paranormal
encounters per life if the coin were per year, and 1.22 if it were per life. The truth is
neither, and the reason is the port's own model.

### 189.1 One card per year, so ambient cards exclude each other

`dispatchYear` returns as soon as a card fires. Three ambient cards therefore **compete for
the same year**, in dispatch order, and each one's effective rate is its share of the
years the earlier ones left.

```
paranormal  0.037 per year  (1/22 minus the years lost to nothing before it)
stalker     0.012 per year
parent-cheat 0.004 per year
```

That is not a bug in any one card — it is a property of the queue-less model, and it is
the same property that makes the table-driven families thin: every pool in
`relationshipYear` competes with every other pool in it.

### 189.2 The fix, and why it is not in this round

The ambient cards should be **one entry point that picks among the three by weight**, so
the total rate is set once and the tables divide it. That is a small restructure of three
functions into one chooser plus a shared picker — and it changes every measured rate in
§189.1, so it wants a round of its own rather than the tail of this one.

Recorded with the numbers so the next round can measure the change against them.

## 190. One ambient card a year, chosen by weight

§189's fix landed: the three functions are one entry point.

```cpp
bool Sim::ambientYear(Life& life, AgeUp& out, int forcedChoice) {
  if (forcedChoice < 0 && ambientRng_.below(12) != 0) return false;
  const int roll = int(ambientRng_.below(100));
  if (roll < 55) return paranormalEncounterYear(life, out, 0);
  if (roll < 90) return stalkerYear(life, out, 0);
  return parentCheatYear(life, out, 0);
}
```

The sub-cards are called with a non-negative `forcedChoice`, which is how they skip their
own coins — no signature changed, and no card had to learn a new flag.

### 190.1 Measured, against §189.1

```
                     before (§189.1)      after
a16_paranormal       1.22 / life          1.25 / life
a16_stalker          0.87 / life          0.32 / life
a16_parent-cheat     0.23 / life          0.07 / life
total                2.32 / life          1.63 / life
```

The competition is gone: the total is now set by one coin, and each table gets a share of
it rather than fighting for the year.

### 190.2 The split is gate-limited, not weight-limited

The weights are 55/35/10 but the outcomes are 77/20/4, because a chosen sub-card can still
**decline** — no living parent for the parent-cheat rows, no stalker rows for the hero's
gender, no eligible child. Those declines cost the year, which is the one place the merge
did not improve on the old behaviour.

That is stated rather than tuned away: making the weights compensate would be fitting a
distribution the game does not publish.

## 191. Correction: the pools do not compete the way §189 said

§189 generalised from the ambient cards: *every pool inside `relationshipYear` competes
with every other pool in it.* Measuring the eleven pools says that is not the story.

```
pool                                        per life   coin
a16_hookup-scenarios-enc                        0.43    0.06
a16_lover-cheat-scenarios-enc                   0.62    0.08
a16_lover-suspicious-scenarios-enc              0.67    0.08
a16_make-love-rejections-enc                    0.58    0.10
a16_lover-make-love-nags-enc                    0.50    0.07
a16_parent-lover-disapprovals-enc               0.07    0.06
a16_school-classmate-flirt-scenarios-enc        0.00    0.05
a16_coworker-hookup-scenarios-enc               0.97    0.05
a16_lover-marriage-nags-enc                     0.18    0.10
a16_relationship-counseling-scenarios-enc       0.05    0.10
a16_breakup-scenarios-enc                       0.02    0.30
```

### 191.1 What the numbers actually show

* **`coworker-hookup` fires at about twenty times its coin** (0.97 per life against 0.05
  per year). It has a second site: `kTable` at `sim.cpp:20075`, a card of its own, so the
  same table is drawn by two different cards and the coin describes only one of them.
* **`breakup` fires at one-fifteenth of its coin** (0.02 against 0.30). Its gate is
  `relationship < 30`, which the port rarely reaches, so the coin is almost never
  consulted -- a **gate** effect, not an ordering one.
* **`school-classmate-flirt` never fires**: it needs `!h.orphan && h.age <= 25`, and the
  lives that reach it are already past that band when a partner exists.
* The middle of the table looks orderly precisely because those pools are *first* in the
  chain and their gates are broad.

So the ordering effect is real but small; **gates and duplicate sites dominate**. §189's
generalisation was one step too broad, and it matters: the fix it implies -- restructuring
`relationshipYear` into one weighted chooser -- would not move `breakup` (gate) or
`coworker-hookup` (two sites) by a single event.

### 191.2 What would move them

| pool | cause | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `coworker-hookup` | two sites, one table | merge the two cards, or give each its own table |
| `breakup` | gate `relationship < 30` never reached | check whether the score decays at all |
| `school-classmate-flirt` | age gate versus when a partner exists | nothing -- the gate is the game's |
| the middle four | broad gates, first in the chain | the weighted chooser would apply here |

### 191.3 The honest state

Four measurement corrections have now come from believing a number one step too broadly:
§155, §161, §167 and this one. The pattern is consistent -- **the instrument is right and
the interpretation overshoots** -- and the guard that has worked each time is looking at
the specific case instead of the aggregate.

## 192. The relationship floor: the gate is reachable, and two cards get there first

§191 left one question: `breakup` fires at 0.02 per life against a coin of 0.30, because
its gate is `relationship < 30`. Is the gate reachable at all?

`Hero::relationshipLow` now tracks the lowest the score ever reached, and `final` reports
it:

```
lives 30   min 0   median 48   max 100
below 30: 7 lives      below 40: 12 lives
```

So the score **does** fall below 30 — in 7 of 30 lives — and the gate is not the problem.

### 192.1 Then why does the table barely fire

Because two other paths reach the same moment first:

* **counseling rescues it.** `relationship < 35 && fire(counseling, 0.10)` restores +12,
  so the years spent under 30 are few;
* **`loverLeavesYear` (§164) ends it.** It fires on a 1-in-12 coin and, when its
  `Wish … well` lane comes up, records the ex and clears the pairing — which means the
  break-up table's 0.30 is concentrated in the handful of years both of those miss.

```
breakup table   0.02 / life
loverLeaves     0.04 / life   (1/12 coin, half the lanes leave)
```

### 192.2 What this means

No defect: the pair ends, the ex is recorded, the announcement rides the same year. The
table pool is simply the *third* way to the same end, and its low rate is the measure of
how often the first two miss.

The one thing worth noting is that this ordering was accidental — §164's card was added
without knowing it would take work from §125's pool. The measurement now says so, and the
next card added to this family can be weighed against it rather than discovered later.

## 193. The duplicate site was real in the code and empty in practice

§191 named `a16_coworker-hookup-scenarios-enc` as drawn by two cards: `seduceYear`
(`kTable` at `sim.cpp:20075`) and the `relationshipYear` pool. One table, two owners, two
coins chosen separately — a real defect in the code.

The pool line is gone:

```cpp
// The coworker hookup is NOT fired here: seduceYear owns that table and pushes it with
// its own presented cap and stream (REPORT.en.md 193).
```

### 193.1 And the rate did not move

```
coworker-hookup per life:  0.97 before  ->  0.97 after
```

Every one of those cards was already coming from `seduceYear`. The pool's own 0.05 never
produced an event — it sits behind `fire()`, which renders a row and can decline, and in
practice it always declined.

So the defect was **real in the code and empty in the observations**: correct to remove,
worth nothing to measure. That is a third kind of finding to go with the two already in
this session's record (a right number read too broadly, and a wrong number read as a
fact), and it is the one that would be easiest to overstate — *"I fixed a duplicate"*
would be true and would imply a change nobody can see.

### 193.2 A test filter, wrong in the same way as §173's

`test_lover_counseling` failed on this change with a body that mentions a relationship
counselor but is a **different card** — *"The relationship counselor says that if you want
to make it work with …, then you will need to start making the bed more often."* The
filter was `"relationship counselor" in body`; it is now the demand's own wording.

```
lanes: {'Agree to go': 6, 'Refuse to go': 5}
ok
```

Bench 0 lines; `test_relationship_lifecycle` still holds its 9 arcs.

### 193.3 What is left of §191

Nothing: the two causes it named are both closed — the floor (§192) and the duplicate site
(here). The third item on its table, `school-classmate-flirt`'s age gate, is the game's own
condition and needs no port change.

## 195. The identity is a flag, not a name

§194 reported the gender card's identity and stored nothing, calling it a shortcut. Trying
to close that shortcut found a wrong assumption in the process:

```
rows: 28
  'Transgender Identity' non-empty: 18
  'Other Identity' non-empty:       10
  first row's 'Transgender Identity': 'x'
```

Both columns are **flags**, not names. There is no string in the table to store — every
value is 'x' marking which rows belong to which kind of beat. A field holding a name would
have been empty in 28 rows out of 28 and looked like a bug for a week.

### 195.1 What is stored

```cpp
// The hero has questioned or changed their identity. The table's two identity columns are
// flags, not names, so the port stores the fact rather than a string it would have had to
// invent.
bool identityQuestioned = false;
```

and the card sets it whenever the chosen row flags either column, with
`final.identityQuestioned` reporting it:

```
lives with identityQuestioned: 16 of 40
```

### 195.2 Why the first attempt was wrong

The first version read `trim(t.at(row, "Other Identity"))` into a string, stored it, and
printed `I identify as .` — an empty tail. The card still rendered, the test still passed,
and nothing failed until the identity was *read back* and found absent in forty lives. A
column that looks like a name and holds a flag is §191's lesson one level down: check the
value, not the header.

## 199. The termination card: decoded, wired, silent, reverted

`a16_termination-scenarios-enc` — 109 rows, `Condition, Scenario, Gender, Clean` — is the
hero being let go. The rows are readable, the reasons are a column (`Age`, `Addiction`,
`Disease`, `Overwork`, or blank), and the port can express the blank and `Age` cases.

It was ported, wired and then **removed**: it never fired.

```
cards: 0  of 30 lives
```

### 199.1 What the round established, in order

1. the gate looked wrong — `h.employed` is the **retirement** flag, and a retired hero
   keeps a job string (`employed False, job 'Receptionist'`), so the first version
   blocked itself; that was found and fixed;
2. it still did not fire; the port's own table registry contains the name (line 1329),
   the file is in `gamedata_plain`, and 60 of its rows pass the filter **when the CSV is
   read in Python**;
3. so the failure is between the port's CSV reader and this particular table — and that
   was not found in the round's remaining time.

### 199.2 Why it was reverted rather than left wired

A card that is registered, dispatched and never renders is exactly what §154 and §183
caught in other families. Leaving it in place would have made the next round's
"does it fire?" question start from a false yes. The function, its declaration and the
dispatch line are gone; the decode above is what survives.

Bench back to **0 lines**, which is the check that the revert was complete.

### 199.3 The one-line diagnostic for next time

```
./build/blsim --script <spec> --templates   # lists the tables it loaded
```

Comparing that list against the registry answers "did the table load" before any card

## 200. A silent failure gets a voice

§199 could not explain why `a16_termination-scenarios-enc` never fired, and the reason it
could not is worth fixing on its own: `ensureTable` swallowed the exception.

```cpp
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  // The reason used to be swallowed, which is how §199's card ended up silently dead;
  // BL_TABLE_DEBUG surfaces it.
  if (std::getenv("BL_TABLE_DEBUG"))
    std::fprintf(stderr, "table load failed: %s (%s)\n", name.c_str(), e.what());
  return false;
}
```

### 200.1 What the switch immediately showed, and did not

With the card reverted (§199), nothing loads that table, so nothing printed -- correct and
unhelpful at once. It means the switch has to be used **while the card is wired**, and that
ordering is now written down: re-add the card, run with `BL_TABLE_DEBUG=1`, read the
exception, remove the card again if it still cannot be explained.

### 200.2 Why this is progress rather than another measurement round

Every silent card this session has had the same shape: something returned false and
nothing said so. §154's `giftYear`, §183's custody chain and §199's termination card were
all found by *counting events*, which is slow and indirect. The switch makes the next one a
one-line question.

Bench **0 lines**: the switch is inert unless the variable is set, which is what makes it
safe to leave in.

## 201. The termination card, second attempt: it was the gate all along

§199's card is ported, and `BL_TABLE_DEBUG` printed **nothing** — the table loads fine.
The gate was the whole problem:

```cpp
// 'employed' is the retirement flag, not "has a job": a retired hero keeps the job string
// and 'employed' is false, so a gate on it blocks the card for most of a life.
if (h.job.empty()) return false;
```

```
cards: 18  of 30 lives      bench 0 lines
```

### 201.1 What §199 got wrong, precisely

§199 fixed the gate to `h.job.empty()` and still measured zero. The fix was right; the
measurement ran against a build where the function had already been pulled out of the
dispatch, so the card could not fire whatever its gate said. Two rounds were spent on a
line that had already been corrected — the second round's revert was the thing hiding it.

That is a new failure mode for this session's list: **a revert hid a fix**, which is why
the re-add was the right next step and the debug switch was not the answer (it printed
nothing because nothing was wrong with the load).

## 364. The zoo's staff split and the division-of-labor card

The park's staff are one pool, and every helper that looks at them reads the same
counter. `SimZoo::GetOperationsManagersStaffSize` (0x2b57bd8) is only a plot-size
lookup - the int array at data 0xfc5284 is `{10, 20, 40}` for small, medium and
large, and a park with no plot or an unknown one gets nothing. `SimZoo::.ctor`
(0x2b56f60, whose only caller is `SimPlace::RefreshAvailableZoos` at 0x2a4a4ac)
then splits that pool at random: custodial takes `[0, N/2)`, security takes
`[0, whatever is left]` inclusive, and customer relations get the remainder. So a
fresh park never starts at zero in all three counters.

After that, only the custodial counter is ever read, and every helper misspells
its own field while doing it:

| helper | bands off the custodial share | returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GetZooCustodialScore` 0x2b65a90 | >75 / >50 / >25 / else | 90..100 / 50..75 / 20..40 / 1..10 |
| `GetCustomerRelationsTicketSalesBumpPercentage` 0x2b65ba4 | the same four bands | 0.20..0.25 / 0.10..0.15 / 0.02..0.08 / 0 |
| `GetChanceOfSecurityBreach` 0x2b65cb4 | the same four bands | 0 / 5..10 / 10..20 / 20..30 |

The ratio is `counter / divider * 100` with the float array at data 0xfc5328
({10, 20, 40}), and there is no divide-by-zero guard: a park with no plot leaves
the divisor at zero, the division yields infinity or NaN, and an AArch64
comparison against NaN takes every band test as false, so every helper lands on
its lowest band. The three getters and three setters at 0x2b56de0-0x2b56e08 have
no callers at all, and the security and customer-relations counters (zoo+0xd0 and
zoo+0xd8) are written but never read by any logic - the names of the helpers do
not describe what they read.

Each helper is consumed by exactly one card: the cleanliness card needs the
custodial score under 20, the customer-service card needs the bump to be exactly
zero (a `fcmp` against 0.0, so only the lowest band qualifies), and
`ScenarioZooAgeUpTheft::ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` (0x29aa4a8) fires when
the breach chance beats `GetRandomNumber(0, 101)`. Answering either the
cleanliness or the customer-service card with "Reallocate labor resources" pushes
`ScenarioZooEmployeeManagerStaffManagement` (ctor 0x29e17b0, `RefreshScenario`
0x29e19f8, `MiniGameCompleted` 0x29e1b2c): title #17882 "Division of Labor" under
the zoo exterior #50857, body #11155 "Allocate your zoo's staff resources
today!", journal #24888 "I reallocated my zoo's work force.", and minigame id
0x30. `MiniGameCompleted` writes its three answers straight back into zoo+0xd0,
+0xd4 and +0xd8.

### The port

`Hero` carries the three counters plus the plot size
(`zooStaffCustodial`, `zooStaffSecurity`, `zooStaffCustomerRel`, `zooSize`).
`Sim::ensureZooFields` draws a plot size and calls `Sim::zooSplitStaff`, which
mirrors the constructor's three-part split from its own stream
(`zooSplitRng_`). The three band helpers became `Sim::zooCustodialScore`,
`Sim::zooCustomerBump` and `Sim::zooBreachChance`, all reading the custodial
counter through `Sim::zooCustodialRatio`, and the two card gates now ask them
instead of the flat coins the earlier sections carried. Answering either card
with the first option pushes `kPendingZooDivision`, which renders the
division-of-labor card and applies a fresh split.

The harness hook `zoo_staff` pins the share - "high" gives custodial the whole
pool, "low" gives customer relations the whole pool - so a test can reach the
bands without playing the minigame.

**Ceilings.** The minigame board itself is not modelled: the card re-splits the
pool at random instead of taking three slider answers, which is the same
approximation the other mini-game cards in this port use. The split is applied at
park creation and on each division card, but hiring or dismissing staff does not
re-split the counters, because the port keeps a head-count rather than a roster.
The no-guard NaN path is reproduced only as far as the lowest band, since the
port clamps an empty pool to a zero ratio rather than performing the division.

**Verified.** `_re/tools/test_zoo_staff.py` walks twelve seeds with the custodial
share pinned high and finds no cleanliness card, no customer-service card and no
theft; it forces the first answer on both cards and finds the division card with
its title, body, single "OK" and journal line and no stat deltas; and it checks
that a low share still leaves theft available (3 cards).

The full 148-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (3afbd13c..., 148 PASS /
0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_zoo_staff.py` walks the split and both hand-offs, and the
gift-shop correction shipped in the same commit is covered by
`_re/tools/test_zoo_merch_order.py`.
## 363. The gift shop and the merchandise order

The zoo's gift shop is a stock list on the park, and every unit on the shelves was put
there by the player. `SimZooGiftShopItem` (ctor `0x2b6c0d0`) is built from one row of
`a16_zoo-gift-shop-item-enc` (Product, Plural, Price Per Unit, Min Sale Price, Max Sale
Price, Popularity Score): the ctor sets `PricePerUnit` from the row's localised cost,
`MaxUnits = 500` and `_condition = 100`, and leaves `Name` unset until
`SetFeaturedAnimal 0x2b6c480` writes `Capitalize(animal.Name + ' ' + Product)`. The list
itself (`zoo+0x68`) starts empty: the item ctor has exactly one caller, `AddProduct
Refresh 0x29efaf0`, and the whole stocking path is the shop menu's three cards —
`AddProduct` (units slider) → `BuildDetails 0x29f0420` → `SetPrice 0x29f1a8c`, which
debits `PricePerUnit * units` from the park's pot. `AdjustPrice 0x29f20a0` moves the tag
later.

Trade is one pass in `SimZoo::IncrementAge 0x2b592bc`, which calls
`item.IncrementAge 0x2b6c1b0` before it does the books. Popularity is
`0.7 * animalPop + 10 * (1 - (sell - min) / (max - min)) + 4 * PopScore` and the sales
percentage comes from a band that narrows as the line gets popular:

| popularity | percentage drawn |
|---|---|
| > 80 | `[80, 101)` |
| > 60 | `[60, 81)` |
| > 40 | `[40, 61)` |
| > 20 | `[10, 31)` |
| else | `[0, 11)` |

`UnitsAvailable -= trunc(pct / 100 * UnitsAvailable)` and
`LastYearsRevenue = SellPrice * sold`; the takings reach the bank through
`GetAnnualGiftShopRevenue 0x2b5d7ac`, which the park's gross (gate + attractions + shop)
sums in.

`ScenarioZooAgeUpMerchOrder` (.ctor `0x29a8a7c`, `RefreshScenario 0x29a8a88`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x29a91d0`, election `0x29a9354`) is the card that restocks a
line. `GetRandomDepletedGiftShopItem 0x29a8f2c` picks a product with no units left.
The election is a hard chain: a park, a hero of at least eighteen, a pot still above zero,
a depleted line and more than three years since the card last appeared. The card is titled
`#29996 'Merch Order'` under the `#50857 'Zoo'` exterior and its body is
`#50379 'Your gift shop has sold all of the '` + the catalogue Product + `#1958 ' featuring
'` + the animal's name + `#3532 ' the '` + its breed + `#4218 '!'`. Its table carries just
Cost Per Unit and Available Capital, and the buttons are `#33003 'Order more'` and
`#32186 'Nothing'`. The card writes no journal line of its own -- the native passes a null
narrative to `LifeLog` -- so the only line an order leaves is the one the order card writes.

Ordering chains `ScenarioZooGiftShopProductOrderUnits` (ctor `0x29f2d08`), which folds
the picker's slider into its own answer: the slider runs from one to
`min(floor(BankBalance / PricePerUnit), MaxUnits - UnitsAvailable)` and starts halfway
up. Its button `#34033 'Place order'` adds
`min(MaxUnits - UnitsAvailable, floor(slider))` units, takes
`PricePerUnit * units` out of the pot — with no affordability clamp, so the pot can go
negative — and answers with a plain card titled one of `#28046 'Just came in!'`,
`#41303 'That new gift smell'` or `#20426 'Flying off the the shelves!'` (the doubled
"the" is upstream) whose body is `#50408 'Your merch order of additional '` + the plural +
`#1958` + the animal + `#3532` + the breed + `#2644 ' just arrived!'` and whose table
reads Units Ordered then New Unit Count. The order's own journal line is
`#24749 'I ordered '` + count + `#2782 ' more '` + plural + `#1958` + animal + `#3532` +
breed + `#3753 " to restock the shelves in my zoo's gift shop."`

In the port the park's shelves are stocked when it is bought: three catalogue rows are
drawn (`Sim::zooSeedGiftShop`), each given a featured animal out of `zooHerd` (or the
park's single animal), a sale price inside the catalogue's band and a starting count. The
yearly pass (`Sim::zooGiftShopTick`) runs at the head of `Sim::zooRunYear` and adds the
shop's takings to the pot beside the gate. `Sim::zooMerchYear` is the family
`zoo-merch-order`, and its order answer folds the second card in: the units the slider
would allow are computed from the pot, the restock is applied, the journal line is
written, and the arrival is rendered by the shared plain card through
`kPendingZooFeedback` (`Sim::zooFeedbackYear`).

Ceilings: the shop menu is not modelled, so `AddProduct`, `BuildDetails`, `SetPrice` and
`AdjustPrice` have no port-side route and the only stock a park ever has is the three
lines it was bought with; the herd carries no popularity figure, so the animal's share of
the popularity formula is a flat 42 instead of `0.7 * animalPop`; the native gate is a
line with zero units, but its sale figure is truncated, which parks a line of one unit at
the gate for good, so the port reads two or fewer as sold out; the order card's slider is
folded into the answer and always orders the most the pot can pay for, so its own sentence
`#17618 'Determine how many more '` + plural + `#1958` + animal + `#3532` + breed + `#4192
" you'd like to order from your merchandise supplier."` and its Current Unit Count and
Featured Animal rows are never printed; the refusal's own tail is not recovered, so the
port writes the answer and nothing else; and the counts are grouped by a local helper
rather than `NumberGrouping`.

Verified: `_re/tools/test_zoo_merch_order.py` walks twenty lives and reads 25 merch cards
(13 answered "Order more", 12 "Nothing") over 9 featured animals, each body matching the
recovered sentence and its two rows, with no stat movement; the forced order lane writes
the journal line, keeps the count under `MaxUnits` and is answered by the arrival card,
and the forced refusal writes neither.

Correction: the first pass of this section put the order card's sentence and rows on the
merch card, because the two cards were recovered from the same sweep and the order card's
slider is folded into the answer here. The contract above is the one the code and the test
now follow; the order card's own heading, sentence and two extra rows are recorded in the
ceilings because the port never prints them.

The full 147-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (7096a8e5..., 146 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: the new
family's wheel ticket moved the lightning card onto a hero whose health the runner
carries as a float, so the strike's wipe came out one point further from the
reconstructed int than the test allowed (it accepted exactly -100 before); that check
now allows two points either way, which is the drift REPORT 247 already records. It was
re-run green.

## 362. The artist-in-residence's contract

The guest act the casino books has a contract length, and when it runs out the house
has one last chance to keep it. `SimCasinoCelebrity+0x324` is that length;
`SimCasinoAgeUpCelebrityContractRenewal` (.ctor `0x73f3a01254`, `RefreshScenario`
`0x73f3a005b8`, handler `0x73f3a00d0c`, eligibility `0x73f3a011ac`, pushed from
`SimCasino::IncrementAge 0x73f2f461cc`) fires the year it reaches zero and nothing else:
the gate is casino, a living celebrity, `ContractLength <= 0`, hero age >= 18 and out of
prison, and it draws no random number at all.

The card is titled `#16302 'Contract Renewal'` and says `Your casino's ` (#50268) + the
relationship word + `, ` (#5282) + the full name + `'s contract has ended.` (#4855), a
blank line, then pronoun 6 + `#1108 ' agent tells you '` + pronoun 0 +
`#4828 "'ll renew "` + pronoun 1 + `#1670 ' contract for the right price.'` followed by
the usual `\n\nWhat will you do?`. Its table holds `Current Salary` (#16832),
`Additional Expenses` (#10793) and `Last Year's Revenue` (#28503), and two bars carry
pronoun 6 + `#822 ' Fame'` and pronoun 6 + `#922 ' Popularity'`.

Its two answers do different things:

* `Let him/her go` builds a plain result card titled `#28535 'Laterrrr'` whose body is the
  name + `#1905 ' ended '` + pronoun 1 + `#3232 ' residency at your casino.'`, hands it a
  one-row table `#47424 'Years Booked'` over `SimCasinoCelebrity+0x32c`, removes the
  celebrity and writes the journal `My casino's ` + relationship word + `, ` + name +
  `#4924 "'s, contract expired and I decided not to renew it."`
* `Make him/her an offer` chains `ScenarioCasinoAgeUpCelebrityContractOffer`
  (.ctor `0x73f39ff010`, `RefreshScenario` `0x73f39ff03c`, handler `0x73f39ff8c4`). That
  card is titled `Contract`, exterior `Celebrity`, and asks `#17334 'Decide the terms of
  your new contract with '` + name. It offers a dropdown `#28715 'Length'` over the
  hard-coded list {2, 3, 5, 7, 10} rendered as `#69718 '{0} Years'`, and a slider
  `#36642 'Salary'` between `MinimumCelebritySalary` and a local 500000 whose default is
  the midpoint. Its one real button is `Make him/her this offer`.

The offer is scored, not chosen: fame above 49 pays more from a salary at or under the
local 350000 than above it (`10 + rand(0,5)` against `15 + rand(0,10)`), fame at or under
49 pays more from a salary at or above the local 75000 (`10 + rand(0,10)` against
`15 + rand(0,15)`); casino popularity at 50/40 adds `rand(0,10)` / `10 + rand(0,10)` /
`20 + rand(0,10)`; fame at 50/40 adds the same three windows; the celebrity accepts when
the total is at least `rand(0,101)`. Accepting writes both fields back, and the journal
reads `My casino's ` + relationship word + `, ` + name + `'s, contract came up for renewal
and ` + pronoun 0 + `#1714 ' decided to stay after I offered '` + pronoun 2 +
`#1022 ' a salary of '` + the salary. Refusing removes the celebrity, takes two
popularity and writes `#3154 ' refused the terms of the new contract.'`. The result cards
are `#50080 "You've got a deal"` with `#1133 ' agreed to the terms of '` + pronoun 1 +
`#2816 ' new contract and will continue performing at your casino.'` and
`#49951 "You're crazy"` with `#3183 ' refused your new contract offer and will not
perform at your casino anymore.'`; the accepted card carries `#36021 'Residency
Duration'` and `#31365 'New Salary'`.

The booking side writes the same two fields: `SimCasino::HireCelebrity 0x73f2f4b4e8`
takes the salary and the length as arguments, and both call sites in the booking card
pass the value of the same {2, 3, 5, 7, 10} dropdown, so no table column ever supplies
a contract length.

The port now keeps `casinoCelebSalary` and `casinoCelebContract` on the hero, ticks the
contract down by one every year in `Sim::casinoYear` before its own coin, draws both
fields at booking, and implements the renewal card in `Sim::casinoCelebRenewYear`
(`_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`) as the family `casino-celeb-renew`.

Ceilings: the port has no dropdown and no slider, so the contract length is drawn from
the native list and the salary is fixed at the slider's default midpoint (275000 in the
United States); the booking salary is drawn from the same band in whole thousands
rather than chosen; the Hollywood Star button is omitted because the port has no
in-app-purchase path behind it; the card's table and bars are not rendered, as the port
draws no stat rows on age-up cards; the offer card is folded into the renewal card's
answer because the port shows one card per year, with the result arriving on the shared
follow-up card (§352) instead of a chained child; and `Current Salary`, `Additional
Expenses` and `Last Year's Revenue` are not modelled, the last two having no port
counterpart for a guest act.

Verified: `_re/tools/test_casino_renewal.py` walked twenty seeded lives with a booked
act and measured 20 renewal cards over both answers (11 letting the act go, 9 making an
offer), 11 `Laterrrr` results, 7 refusals and 2 acceptances, each result card naming the
same act as the renewal card and each journal matching its own arm; a life without a
casino draws no card.

The full 146-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (4351b43c..., 146
PASS / 0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_casino_renewal.py` walks the card, both answers and
every result card, and nothing else moved.

## 361. The act cards' gates and the door

The four punter cards of 350 and 351 shared one invention: each ended its eligibility
test with a ten per cent coin. The recovered contracts draw nothing at all.
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` for the two act cards (`0x356df38` complaint,
`0x3571104` compliment) and the two amenity cards (`0x356beb4`, `0x356ffe8`) is a hard
AND gate: the entity list holds one row whose theme sits on the right side of the
house theme, the casino has at least one gambler, the hero is eighteen or older, out
of prison, and enough years have passed since the class last fired (2/4/2/2 for
complaint-act, compliment-act, complaint-amenity, compliment-amenity). The coin is gone
from all four cards.

The act complaint's ban answer then does more than show the punter out:

* `SimCasino::RemoveGambler 0x2ab0004` and `SimCasino::ImpactPopularity 0x2aafdfc` with
  −2, as before.
* a snippet drawn by `DataHub::GetRandomCasinoBannedGamblerSnippetForCraziness 0x26c67b8`
  from the punter's craziness, out of `a16_casino-banned-gambler-snippet-enc` — the port
  bands it on `Min Gambler Craziness` / `Max Gambler Craziness` with a craziness drawn
  from its own stream.
* a journal tail: `pron(5)` + `' '` + the row's `Log Version` + `' on '` + `pron(1)` +
  `#4005 ' way out.'`, appended to the ban line the card already wrote.
* a plain follow-up card titled `#50001 "You're outta here"`, whose body is
  `'You banned ' + name + #2145 ' from your casino.\n\n' + pron(5) + ' ' + snippet +
  ' on ' + pron(1) + ' way out.'`. The port queues it through the feedback card 352
  already renders.

A ban now reads, in the port, `I banned my casino's gambler, Bacardi Flooren, from my
casino after she complained about Rutabaga Top Laugh Hour. She loudly exclaimed, "This
place will be out of business next week," while on her way out.` and a second card
follows with the same sentence under "You're outta here".

Ceilings: the native writes the two statements into separate narrative slots and the
port prints them as one line; the follow-up card's child scenario is only partially
recovered, so the port renders its text with the shared plain card rather than a class
of its own; and the two unresolved virtual slots the answers touch (`+0x738`, `+0x508`)
stay mapped onto the port's per-gambler happiness and popularity counters, as 322
recorded.

Verified: with the coin gone the cards fire every eligible year, so
`_re/tools/test_casino_act.py` now sees 137 complaint cards over twenty seeds (36 of
them bans, each with its walk-out tail and a follow-up card) and 83 compliments;
`_re/tools/test_casino_amenity.py` sees 161 complaints and 107 compliments, and
`_re/tools/test_casino_punter.py` is unchanged at 27 lost punters.

The full 146-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe
(4351b43c..., 146 PASS / 0 FAIL). The 362 card shipped in the same commit and is

## 360. The casino's relationship words

Every casino card that names a punter opens with a relationship slot, and three of
the recovered contracts read the same two getters for it. Neither returns a rank.

`SimCasinoGambler::RelationshipStatusString` speaks the gambler's **type**: the three
words are `'casual gambler'`, `'high roller'` and `'Mafia member'`. The complaint and
compliment cards (§358, §359) both print it, and the launder card's journal reads the
same slot through the member's own getter at vtable `+0x4f8`.
`SimCasinoCelebrity::RelationshipStatusString` returns one fixed literal, `#54414
'artist-in-residence'` — which is why the demand card (§356) reads that way and why
no celebrity card ever varies it.

The port had one helper, `casinoTierWord`, printing `Beginner` / `Amateur` / `Novice`
/ `Regular` / `High Roller` — an invention from §322 that every gambler card inherited.
It is replaced by two:

* `casinoGamblerStatus` keeps the §357 style draw (the port tracks a gambling style per
  regular rather than a gambler record) and prints `'high roller'` for style 5 and
  `'casual gambler'` otherwise. `'Mafia member'` cannot be drawn because the port has no
  mafia regulars (§357's ceiling), so the third word exists only where a card is pushed
  by a mafia member.
* `casinoCelebStatus` returns the fixed `'artist-in-residence'`.

Call sites: the two act cards and the two amenity cards take the gambler word, the two
celebrity cards (complaint, compliment) and the two death/resignation cards take the
fixed word, and the launder journal now spells `My casino's Mafia member, "…"` directly.

Ceilings: the high-roller boundary is read off the port's own style ladder rather than
the native `GamblingStyle +0x30c == 5` test, because the port has no per-gambler record;
and `'Mafia member'` is inferred from the vtable getter's ownership (only a mafia member
pushes that card) rather than from the getter body, which is an unresolved il2cpp slot.

Verified: the seven casino tests that pin a relationship word
(`_re/tools/test_casino_act.py`, `test_casino_amenity.py`, `test_casino_death.py`,
`test_casino_mob.py`, `test_casino_punter.py`, `test_casino_resignation.py`,
`test_casino_gambler_new.py`) were re-run green against the rebuilt binary.

## 359. The compliment card's own contract

The praise twin of 358, `ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplimentGame`, was ported from a
reconstruction and has now been checked against its own disassembly. Addresses:
`.ctor 0x3572578` (a two-instruction tail into `Scenario::.ctor(false)`),
`RefreshScenario 0x3571344`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x3571cf8`,
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x3572134`, pushed from
`SimCasino::IncrementAge 0x2aacf04` with no draw at the push site.

**Eligibility is a hard AND gate, not a coin flip.** The predicate enumerates the
gambler list and requires that some regular's favourite game has no installed room
(`cmp w21,#5` bounds the game-type enum), then hero age ≥ 18, not in prison, and
`Life::YearsSinceScenario` of this class greater than 4 (`cmp w0,#4 ; cset w8,gt`).
There is no presented-count cap and no separate ownership test — the casino is taken
from the hero's own life object.

**The body names a favourite the casino does not have.**
`SimCasinoGambler::GetRandomFavoriteGame 0x2c28920` is drawn and then rejected while
`GetFavoriteGames` contains it among the installed rooms, so the printed game is a
missing one, capitalised by `CapitalizeAllMajorWordsInString 0x2e15700`. The sentence
is nine parts — `#50268` "Your casino's ", `RelationshipStatusString 0x2c2812c`,
`#5282` ', ', the full name, `#5672` ', is complimenting your casino for having ',
`PronounStringForType(1)`, `#1953` ' favorite game, ', the game, `#6312` '.' — then
`#46` and the parsed row from
`GetRandomCasinoGamblerGameRoomComplimentForHappiness 0x26c89bc` (banded on the
gambler's own happiness, bracket dictionary holding only the person) and `#146`
'\n\nWhat will you do?'. Title `#16100 'Compliment'`; ExteriorTitle is never written.

**The relationship slot is the type word again.** `RelationshipStatusString` returns
`'casual gambler'` / `'high roller'` / `'Mafia member'` — the same correction 358 made
on the complaint card.

**Journal and effects.** RefreshScenario seeds the journal with `#25215 "I thanked my
casino's gambler, "` + name + `#5547 ', for '` + possessor + `#1659 ' compliment about
my casino.'`, which is what thanking logs. Thanking also moves addiction −1 and the
two unidentified vtable slots by −1 and +1. Giving moves addiction +2 and the slots by
−2 and +2 and appends `#341` + name + `#5857 ', some free games after '` + subject
pronoun + `#1660 ' complimented my casino.'`. Ignoring appends `#351` + name +
`#5350 ', after '` + subject pronoun + `#1660` and then calls
`SimCasino::ImpactPopularity(-2)`; thank and give skip that call. The handler draws
nothing, writes no follow-up scenario and touches no money.

Port: `Sim::casinoComplimentYear` (`_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`) lost its
`chance(0.10)` gate for the native predicate — it collects the catalogue games with no
`CasinoRoom` and returns without a card when none is missing — draws the printed game
from that list instead of a generic `<casino-game>` resolution, and prints the type
words instead of the port's rank ladder.

Ceilings: the two vtable slots stay paired with the port's popularity bar (the same
shortcut 324 recorded); the port keeps its own style draw to choose between `'casual
gambler'` and `'high roller'` because it has no per-gambler entity; `'Mafia member'`
never prints for the reason 357 recorded; the row's bracket dictionary holds only the
person, as native.

Verified by `_re/tools/test_casino_compliment.py` (its tier set narrowed to the two
recovered type words):

The full 145-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (ed9c87e9..., 145 PASS /
0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_casino_compliment.py` exercises the card and its narrowed
type words, and nothing else moved.

## 358. The complaint card's missing game

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplaintGame` is the casino age-up card that fires when a
regular cannot play what he wants. Its own addresses are `.ctor 0x356f760`,
`RefreshScenario 0x356e188`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x356eaf0`, eligibility
`0x356f31c`, and it is constructed from the ordered push cascade in
`SimCasino::IncrementAge` at `0x2aaced8`.

**Eligibility draws nothing.** There is no coin flip, no win rate and no units check in
it: it walks the gambler list, asks whether some regular's favourite game type has no
installed room, then requires the hero to be eighteen or older, out of prison, and more
than two years past the last card of this class. The winner is the last qualifying
regular with its first missing favourite, and when no regular qualifies but the
question answers differently the fallback is one random regular and one random
favourite. The game's printed name comes from `GetNameStringForGameType 0x2aa9a40`;
the paragraph under the sentence comes from
`GetRandomCasinoCasinoGameRoomComplaintForHappiness 0x26c6f20` filtered by that
regular's happiness and parsed with `<hero-casino>` bound to the house. The title is
`#16066 'Complaint'`, the sentence is "Your casino's {relationship}, {name}, is
complaining that your casino doesn't have {pronoun} favorite game, {game}." and the
buttons are 'Ban {them} from my casino', 'Apologize for the inconvenience' and 'Ignore
{them}'.

**The relationship slot speaks in types, not ranks.** It is
`SimCasinoGambler::RelationshipStatusString`, whose words are `'casual gambler'`,
`'high roller'` and `'Mafia member'` — the five-step Beginner/Amateur/Novice/Regular/
High Roller ladder earlier sections of this report used is the port's own invention and
does not appear on this card.

**One card a year.** The native push site is an ordered if/else cascade over the casino
age-up classes, so a year can carry at most one of them, and the first eligible class in
the order wins.

Port: `Sim::casinoComplaintYear` (`_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`) lost its
`chance(0.10)` gate and now asks the native question directly — it scans
`a16_casino-casino-game-room-enc` for the first game the hero has no `CasinoRoom` for
and returns without a card when every game is installed. It also gained the two-year
cooldown, kept in the new `Hero::casinoComplaintAge` field, and its relationship slot
now prints `'high roller'` for a style-5 regular and `'casual gambler'` otherwise.

Ceilings: the port has no per-regular favourite list, so the casino's whole game
catalogue stands in for the regulars' favourites; it has no mafia regulars yet (the
ceiling recorded in 357), so `'Mafia member'` never prints; the cascade is not modelled
as an order because the wheel already yields one family card a year; and the praise twin
(`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplimentGame`) keeps the rank ladder because its own
contract was not recovered.

Verified by `_re/tools/test_casino_complaint.py`, which also had its mood-row matcher
widened from a `\S+` wildcard to `.+?` because the shipped rows substitute multi-word
pools such as `<friendly advice/constructive criticism/an honest assessment/the obvious
next step>`.

The full 145-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (e2f504b1..., 145 PASS /
0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_casino_complaint.py` exercises the card, its two type
words and the widened mood rows, and nothing else moved.

## 357. The new regular's card

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerNew` is the casino's only purely informational card
among the twenty-two `SimCasino::IncrementAge` pushes: nobody is asked
anything, a gambler simply starts turning up. Native class: `.ctor 0x3573804`,
`RefreshScenario 0x3572d4c`, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x357373c`,
pushed from `SimCasino::IncrementAge` at `0x2aacea0`. It declares no
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` override at all. Its fields are `_narrative +0x170` and
`_casino +0x178`.

### Eligibility

The check draws nothing: the casino (`Life+0x5f8`) must be present, the hero
must be 18 or older, not in prison, and
`YearsSinceScenario(#37053 'ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerNew') > 4`. So the card
can only land once every fifth year, and it lands the first year the cooldown
is clear -- there is no chance roll anywhere in the chain.

### What the refresh builds

`PersonGenerator::GenerateRandomCasinoGambler 0x338bba8(place, noMafiaGate)`
makes the person. Its second argument is computed by the card: if the hero has
no mafia special job, the country is asked for its mobs
(`DataHub::GetAllMafiaMobsForHostCountryCode 0x2856588`) and the gate stays on
only while `SimCasino::GetMafiaMembers 0x2ab1128` returns an empty list. The
name is then retried up to fifty times
(`Generation` helper `0x25241d8`, `FullName 0x2b2c2bc`) against the hero's
known people so a new regular cannot share a name with somebody the hero
already knows. Finally `SimCasino::AddGambler 0x2ab3a90` and
`SimCasino::ImpactPopularity 0x2aafdfc(+2)`.

```
Title  #31317 'New Gambler'
Body   #9953 'A ' + GamblerTypeString + #2805 ' named ' + name +
       #2583 ' is now frequently gambling at your casino.'
```

Table rows, in insertion order: `Age` #10954 over
`NumberGroupingStringForAmount`, `Occupation` #32523 over
`ShortOccupationString` capitalised, `Gambling Style` #20993 over
`GetGamblingStyleString` capitalised, `Favorite Games` #19976 over
`GetFavoriteGamesString`. The two bar graphs are `Money` #30360 over the
gambler's own money (`+0xbc`) and `Addiction` #10777 over `+0x368`. The single
choice is #32432 `OK`, and `HasDismissButton` is cleared, so the card cannot be
waved away without pressing it.

Journal: `#9953 'A ' + GetGamblingStyleString + #2157 ' gambler named ' + name +
#1478 ' began frequenting my casino.'`

`GamblerTypeString 0x2c28130` is a different string from
`GetGamblingStyleString 0x2c284b8`: the type is `casual gambler` / `high
roller` / `Mafia member`, the style is the five-rung ladder
`Beginner`/`Amateur`/`Novice`/`Regular`/`High Roller`. The body prints the
type, the journal prints the style.

### What the port does

`Sim::casinoGamblerNewYear` (`_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`, registered as
`casino-gambler-new` with one ticket and the `ownsCasino` gate) runs on its own
`casinoNewRng_` stream. The cooldown is `casinoGamblerNewAge` plus the native's
four-year gap, and the newcomer's details are drawn when the card fires: style,
gender, name, age (21-65), money, addiction, one career name out of
`a16_careers-enc` and one or two game names out of
`a16_casino-casino-game-room-enc`.

Ceilings, all marked `shortcut:` in the code:

- the port has no gambler entity, so the newcomer is printed and then only
  counted; their style is pushed onto `casinoGamblerStyles` so the other
  casino cards can draw it;
- the mafia branch of the native generator is not modelled -- every newcomer
  is an ordinary gambler, so `Mafia member` never appears in the body;
- the fifty-attempt name collision retry collapses to a single draw (the
  name pool cannot repeat across cards, but it can repeat across years);
- the two bar graphs are body lines rather than bars;
- the card is one wheel ticket, while the native pushes it independently of
  the other twenty-one cards, so in the port it can be skipped in a year it
  would natively have fired.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_casino_gambler_new.py` walks ten seeds and says `cards: 50 |
styles: ['Amateur', 'Beginner', 'High Roller', 'Novice', 'Regular'] | names: 10`.
It matches the whole body against the row and bar layout, checks that every
style word comes from the ladder and that the body's type word agrees with it
(a `High Roller` is a `high roller`, nobody else is), that the journal repeats
the same name and style, that no two regulars arrive inside the same five
years, and that a hero without a casino never sees the card.The full 145-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (77c7e0db..., 145 PASS /
0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_casino_gambler_new.py` exercises the card, its rows and
its two bar values, and nothing else moved.

## 356. The guest act's demand card

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpCelebrityDemand` is the artist-in-residence's own card: the
celebrity wants a perk kept on hand before every performance, and obliging it
satisfies the demand while refusing earns an insult. The native class is
`.ctor 0x3568614`, `RefreshScenario 0x3567260`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x3567ac8`, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x356845c`, and it is pushed from
`SimCasino::IncrementAge` at `0x2aacac8` -- the second rung of that method's
**ordered if/else cascade**, not an independent roll: at most one casino age-up
card is built in a year. Its fields are `_narrative +0x170`, `_casino +0x178`,
`_celebrity +0x180`, `_perk +0x188`, `_perkData +0x190` and `_perkString +0x198`.

### Eligibility and the row

The chain runs casino -> celebrity -> `Alive (+0x18)` -> the celebrity's
satisfied-demand count `< GetCasinoCelebrityDemandCount() 0x26c7ea0` -> a roll
of `GetRandomNumber(0,101)` that has to land **under 80 when the celebrity's
craziness (+0xc0) is above its fame (+0xb4) and under 50 otherwise** -> hero age
>= 18 -> not in prison -> `YearsSinceScenario(#37039) > 1`. Note the roll comes
before the age, prison and year tests.

The row is not a table draw from the card: `GetRandomCasinoCelebrityDemand (list) 0x26c8094` reads `a16_casino-celebrity-demand-enc` and excludes every
`Index` the celebrity already has in `_requiredIdPerks (+0x348)`. The item then
goes through the game's bracket parser with `DoNotCapitalize=1`, takes `some `
(#65874) when its `Plural` cell is set and an indefinite article when its `Uses Indefinite Article` cell is set -- in that order, both flags can be set.

Body, wrapped end to end:

```
"Your casino's " + RelationshipStatusString + ", " + FullName +
", is demanding you provide " + pron(2) + " with a perk, or " + pron(0) +
" won't perform." + #46 + pron(9) + " demanding you have " + _perkString +
" on-hand before each of " + pron(1) + " performances." + #6348
```

`SimCasinoCelebrity::RelationshipStatusString 0x2c277a0` is the single literal
#54414 `artist-in-residence`. The title is #17489 `Demand` (#146 is the
`What will you do?` cta).

A `TableDictionary` (+0xa0) and a `TableOrderArray` (+0xa8) carry two rows:
`Additional Expenses` #10793 is `GetYearlyExpenseForPerk 0x2c276d0`, the local
cost of the row's `Cost (+0x24)` times twelve, and `Request` #35890 is the item
with `CapitalizeAllMajorWords`. A `BarGraphArray` (+0xb8) carries `pron(6) + Fame` #822 over `Att_fame (+0xb4)` and `pron(6) + Popularity` #922 over the
celebrity's own `_popularity (+0x338)`.

Choices, stored order: `Concat(#32516 'Oblige ', pron(2))` and #35505
`Refuse`, dispatched by `Contains('oblige')` else `Contains('refuse')`.

Oblige calls `SimCasinoCelebrity::AddPerk 0x2c275a0(celebrity, row.Index, perk)` and `ImpactPopularity 0x2c27830(celebrity, row.Celebrity Popularity Impact)`. Refuse writes no state at all: `GetRandomInsultForGender 0x2808580 (hero.Gender)` gives an insult, `msg = pron(5) + #1591 ' called you ' + insult + #6312 '.'`, and the card's reaction is `pron(5) + #4172 ' yelled at you for refusing ' + pron(1) + #3227 ' request.' + #46 + msg + #6312 '.'` -- which
**renders with a double period** because `msg` already ends in one. Neither
answer touches money.

Both answers then push a plain `Scenario` whose title comes from
`PickRandomFromStringArray` over the single literal #27654
`It's a NEED, not a  want` (the double space is in the literal). The oblige
body is `'You began providing ' + perk + #1997 ' for ' + FullName + #1469 ' before each of ' + pron(1) + #3037 ' performances.'`; the refuse body is the
same reaction sentence. The narrative on the card itself is
`'I began providing ' + perk + ' for my casino's ' + status + ', ' + FullName + '. '` on the oblige lane and `"I refused to give in to my casino's " + status + ", " + FullName + "'s, demand for " + perk + "."` on the refuse lane.

### What the port does

`Sim::casinoCelebDemandYear` (`_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`, registered as
`casino-celeb-demand` with one ticket and the `ownsCasino` gate) runs on its own
`casinoDemandRng_` stream so no other family's sequence moves. The celebrity's
fame is not modelled anywhere in the port, so it is drawn once (20-99) the
first time the card is reachable and kept on the hero; the demand's own
popularity starts at 50 and is clamped to 0-100.

The satisfied demands are kept as a `std::vector<int> casinoCelebPerks` of
table `Index` values, which is the port's stand-in for `_requiredIdPerks`.
Everything else follows the native text: the `Plural` and `Uses Indefinite Article` prefixes in the native order, the two dictionary rows rendered as
`label: value` body lines (the ledger's own precedent), the two bars rendered
as `His Fame: 58` / `His Popularity: 50` body lines, and both follow-ups
pushed as the existing `kPendingCasinoFeedback` card from REPORT 352.

Ceilings, all marked `shortcut:` in the code:

- the native roll happens before the age/prison/year gates, the port tests
  those gates first and draws once when it is already reachable;
- the exclusion list is the port's own vector, not the celebrity object's;
- fame is a flat 20-99 draw rather than the native attribute;
- the yearly expense prints `Cost x 12` without the country's local-cost
  conversion (the port works in the printed currency throughout);
- the two bar graphs are body lines, not graphs;
- the follow-up is the shared feedback card rather than a fresh scenario
  class, so it carries the standard one-button close.

### A port defect fixed on the way

`a16_company-name-structure-enc` has one row whose suffix cell is not a word
but a token: `Corporate,<color> <suffix>,,<type>,`. `Sim::companyName`
(`_re/port/src/sim.cpp`) had no `<type>` handler, so a company founded with the
`Corporate` type printed `Global <type>` verbatim, and `Corporate` is a real
type -- `a16_careers-enc:23` is `Accountant,Corporate,...`. The handler now
draws from that token's own file, `a16_company-name-type-enc` (a single `Type`
column), and the token never survives. No script key surfaces an employer name
today, so this is a correctness fix that changes no card text.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_casino_demand.py` walks twenty seeds with a seeded guest act
and says `cards: 150 | lanes: {'Refuse': 70, 'Oblige him': 80} | follow-ups: 80 oblige / 68 refuse | fame: [21, 28, 31, 34]`. It checks the body against the
table's own items (slash pools matched word for word, single tokens accepted
as a wildcard because their text lives in the game's dictionaries), the
pronoun agreement across all four substitutions, the `Request` row's
capitalisation, both narratives, both follow-up bodies including the double
period, that neither lane moves money, that two demands never land in adjacent
years, and that a hero without a casino never sees the card.The full 144-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (e223d1c6..., 144 PASS /
0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_casino_demand.py` exercises the card, both lanes and both
follow-ups, and nothing else moved.

## 355. The casino's death cards

Two age-up cards take a person off the casino's books for good. `ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerDeath` (`.ctor` 0x35bdcb0, `RefreshScenario` 0x35bdcf0, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x35be0e8, pushed at `SimCasino::IncrementAge` 0x2aac974) covers a regular on the floor; `ScenarioCasinoCelebrityDeath` (`.ctor` 0x3593210, `RefreshScenario` 0x3593250, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x359360c, pushed at 0x2aace2c) covers the guest act in residence. Neither has a `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush`; both are decided inline in `SimCasino::IncrementAge`.

### When somebody dies

The gambler loop walks `SimCasino+0xc8` `GamblersList`. A gambler already flagged dead (`+0x18`) only gets `SimPerson::IncrementYearsSinceDeath` 0x2c47234. A friend (`IsFriend` 0x2c399d8) or the hero's current lover (`IsCurrentLover` 0x2c46f70) never dies. Everyone else has their script refreshed with `SimThirdPersonScript::UpdateStatesForAge` 0x2c5045c(script, gambler.Age), and the death age is then read back out of `[script+0x18][+0x60]`; while `gambler.Age` is under it nothing happens, and once it is over it the person is stamped dead. The celebrity path is the same check applied to the single celebrity slot at `SimCasino+0xe0`, except that one is only the friend and current-lover exemption, and a celebrity already dead just empties the slot.

Either death is worth a `deathString` of `#57525 'died of old age'` when the person was older than 69 and `#57524 'died of natural causes'` otherwise, and both literals carry their own verb.

### The card

Title `#17288 'Death'`, colour scheme 1, focus person the one who died. The body is `String::Format` over `#50270 "Your casino's {0}, {1}, passed away at the age of {2}.\n\n{3} {4}."` with `{0}` the person's own `RelationshipStatusString` (`SimCasinoGambler::RelationshipStatusString` 0x2c2812c, `SimCasinoCelebrity::RelationshipStatusString` 0x2c277a0), `{1}` the full name, `{2}` the boxed age, `{3}` the capitalised pronoun and `{4}` the `deathString`. Both cards offer the same two answers, `#12413 'Attend '` + possessive pronoun + `#2153 ' funeral'` and `#39181 'Skip it'`, dispatched by `String::Contains` on the lowered label ('attend' 0x4e10fdc, 'skip'). Attending is worth `SimPerson::ImpactKarma` 0x2c4abfc(+1); skipping is worth nothing. The gambler's journal is `#1771 ' died.'` appended to their name. The celebrity's journal is the narrative the constructor was handed, `pronoun + #1753 ' died ' + deathString + #6312 '.'`.

`RefreshScenario` removes the person from the casino (`SimCasino::RemoveGambler` 0x2ab0004 for a regular, `SimCasino::RemoveCelebrity` 0x2ab1654 for the act) and stamps their script's death age.

An old guest act's journal therefore reads `He died died of old age.` — the pronoun-and-verb sentence in the constructor is composed around a `deathString` that already starts with "died". That duplication is upstream and is kept here, the same way the zoo keeper's 354 pair is kept; the body, which spells the verb once, reads naturally.

### The port

`Sim::casinoGamblerDeathYear` and `Sim::casinoCelebDeathYear` (both in `_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`) are two families at one wheel ticket each, gated on `hero.ownsCasino`, `age >= 18` and not being in prison, named `casino-gambler-death` and `casino-celeb-death`. The draw of a funeral answer and the tier word (`Sim::casinoTierWord`) come off a new `casinoDeathRng_` stream so the other casino families keep their sequences. The card's `out.choice` is set from the drawn answer, and the karma point is added only for the funeral.

Ceilings: the port keeps a count of regulars rather than a persistent list, so a death draws one regular lazily — a name, a gender, a starting age of 18..62 and a lifespan of 55..85 — and removes that one from the count; a new regular can appear later. The guest act's age is likewise drawn against the year the act was booked, using the `casinoCelebMetAge` stamp 352 introduced. The friend and current-lover exemptions are not modelled, because the port's regulars and guest acts are never either. A regular who has already died is not tracked with a years-since-death counter. The tier word is drawn from the same stream as the card rather than read off the person, matching the shortcut 352 already records.

### Verified

- `_re/tools/test_casino_death.py` pins each family in turn, twenty-five seeds apiece: `gambler cards: 20 | celeb cards: 14 | lanes: {'gambler': 3, 'celeb': 2}`.
- Every body matches `Your casino's <tier>, <name>, passed away at the age of <age>.` followed by the cause; no card names a person younger than 55, the cause is "died of old age" exactly when the age is over 69, the attending answer's pronoun agrees with the body's, the karma point lands only for the funeral and not for the skip, and the gambler's journal reads `<name> died.` while the celebrity's reads the doubled sentence.
- Both answers show up for both families, and a hero who owns no casino sees neither card even with the family pinned.

The full 143-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (4883ea69..., 143 PASS /
0 FAIL): `_re/tools/test_casino_death.py` exercises both cards and both
answers, and nothing else moved.

## 354. The zoo keeper's death

The zoo's IncrementAge chain has one card the park does not choose: the keeper dies.
`ScenarioZooEmployeeDeath` (`.ctor` 0x29d8554, `RefreshScenario` 0x29d8588,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x29d8ad8) is pushed at 0x2b59b38 from a loop that walks every
keeper in `EmployeesList` and asks the death question of each. The card carries the keeper
and the cause string on its own fields (`+0x188` and `+0x178`).

The loop is the interesting part. A keeper who is already dead is skipped with
`IncrementYearsSinceDeath`; so is one who is a friend or the current lover of the hero —
those never die. For everyone else the native reads the keeper's script, stamps the
keeper's age into it, and compares that age with the death age stored on the script
(`[script+0x18][+0x60]`). Only a keeper at or past that age produces the card, and the card
removes them from the list (`SimZoo::RemoveEmployee` 0x2b5df88) the moment it is shown.

The cause string is chosen at the same time: #57525 `'died of old age'` for a keeper over
69, #63111 `'of natural causes'` otherwise. Those two literals are not the same shape — one
carries its own verb and the other does not — while the body format #50546 and the journal
both read "{0} died {1}". An old keeper therefore produces "He died died of old age" in both
places. That duplication is upstream, and this port reproduces it rather than correcting it.

Body: #50546 `"Your zoo's {0}, {1}, passed away at the age of {2}.\n\n{3} died {4}."` with
the employee type, the full name, the age, the capitalised pronoun and the cause. Title
#17288 `'Death'`. Journal: `'My zoo's '` (#510) + employee type + #5282 `', '` + name +
#5501 `', died '` + cause + #6312 `'.'`. The card drops the hero's happiness by two (the
0x408 slot) whichever answer is given.

| Answer | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Attend `{0}` funeral | journal #266 `'\nI attended '` + pronoun + #2154 `' funeral.'` |
| Skip `{0}` funeral | journal #400 `'\nI skipped '` + pronoun + #2154 `' funeral.'` |

### The port's card

`Sim::zooEmployeeDeathYear` sits with the zoo's other cards in `_re/port/src/sim.cpp` and
runs on `zoo-employee-death` at one ticket, with its own stream `zooStaffRng_` for the two
numbers the native reads off the keeper's script. The keeper's hire age is already stamped
by 353, so the port only needs the age they were hired at (drawn 18..45) and the age they
die at (drawn 55..85); the age on the card is the hire age plus the years served since
`zooEmployeeHiredAge`. Nothing is drawn until the first year the card is reachable, so the
years before it leave every other zoo card's sequence untouched.

Ceilings:

- The native reads each keeper's death age from their script and can bury several keepers
  at once; the port has one keeper, so it draws a lifespan instead and can bury only that
  one.

## 353. The zoo keeper's resignation

The zoo's IncrementAge chain calls one more card after the pregnancy and before the
cleanliness report: `ScenarioZooAgeUpEmployeeResignation` (`.ctor` 0x29a4e98,
`RefreshScenario` 0x29a4ea4, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x29a5864,
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` 0x29a5ebc), pushed at 0x2b59ce8. It is the zoo's
counterpart to the casino's two resignations in 352, and it is the only zoo card that takes
a member of staff away from the park.

Eligibility asks for a zoo that has been open `YearsOwned >= 6`, a hero of 18 or more who
is not in prison, `YearsSinceScenario > 3`, and a disgruntled employee from
`SimZoo::GetDisgruntledEmployee` (0x29a5558). The native calls a keeper disgruntled on
either of two grounds: the last time the hero interacted with them is more than three years
past, or their salary has not moved in five years and is still at or below 500.

The body names the keeper by employee type and full name, then adds a colour sentence drawn
from `a16_zoo-employee-resignation-color-enc`. That table has 33 rows and the header
`String,Gender,Employee Type,Min Competence,Max Competence,Commonness Score`; the row is
picked by `Commonness Score` inside the window `Min Competence`..`Max Competence` that
holds the keeper's competence, and its tokens `<he/she>` / `<his/her>` resolve to that
keeper. One row names `<zoo-other>`, a competing park. The sentences carry their own full
stop and open on the lowercase pronoun token, so the card shows "She is more interested in
working at an aquarium than a zoo." Text: #5713 `', is resigning from '`, #3066
`' position at your zoo.'`, then the colour, then #6348 `"\n\nWhat will you do?"`.

The three answers are the same shape as the casino's, minus the toss:

| Answer | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Wish `{0}` well | the keeper leaves; the hero's happiness slot takes -2; journal #471 `'\nI wished '` + pronoun + #4019 `' well.'` |
| Offer `{0}` a raise | the keeper stays; the native chains `ScenarioZooEmployeeSalary` |
| Insult `{0}` one last time | the keeper leaves; discipline -2 and karma -3; a follow-up `Scenario` titled one of #11409 `'And stay out'`, #45203 `'Useless mutt'`, #48310 `'You dirty, mangy, ugly-'`, #32862 `'Only animals could love you'`, with body #47921 `'You called '` + pronoun + the insult + a full stop (the tail's own literal is not recorded) |

### The port's card

`Sim::zooEmployeeResignYear` sits beside the zoo's other cards in `_re/port/src/sim.cpp`,
with its own stream `zooResignRng_` so the years the card does not fire are unchanged. It
runs on `zoo-employee-resign` at one ticket. The gate is the native one where the port can
express it: a zoo open six years, a hero who is an adult and out of prison, a four-year
cooldown, and a keeper who has not been spoken to for three years. The colour row is picked
by `pickWindow` over `Min Competence`/`Max Competence`, then capitalised and given a
full stop only when it does not already end in one — the rows in this table do, unlike the
supervisor warnings of 325.

The hire date is stamped at both hire sites (`ensureZooFields` and the applicant branch of
`zooYear`), because the native's "three years without an interaction" needs a reference
point the port does not otherwise keep. That applicant branch used to narrate a resignation
when the keeper left; the narration is gone, and the step now only ever brings an applicant.

Ceilings:

- The native disgruntlement test has two clauses and the port has no keeper salary, so the
  hire age stands for both.
- `<zoo-other>` becomes "a rival zoo"; the port has no competitor parks.
- The raise chains `ScenarioZooEmployeeSalary`, whose body is not recovered, so the keeper

- The insolent answer's follow-up uses the shared insult pool of 343 and boxes the sentence

## 352. The casino's two resignations

Both of the casino's performers can hand in their notice: the guest act and the act in
residence. The answers are the same three - offer more money, beg them to stay, wish them
well - and the toss that decides a beg is the guest's relationship strength on one card
and the house's own popularity on the other.

`SimCasino::IncrementAge` at `0x2aaca9c`, and holds the narrative at 0x170, the casino at
0x178 and the celebrity at 0x180. Eligibility wants the casino and a living guest, the
guest to have been acquired through the Hollywood star item, the hero's age at their last
meeting to be at least four years old, their relationship strength at or below 40, the hero
to be 18 and out of prison, and YearsSinceScenario above 2.

RefreshScenario sets the title to `#36027` "Resignation" and the focus to the guest. The
body is `#50268` "Your casino's ", the relationship status, `#5282` ", ", the full name, `#5683`
", is informing you that ", the type-8 pronoun ("she's"/"he's"), `#3239` " resigning from
performing at your casino.", a blank line, the capitalised subject pronoun (type 5), `#3307`
" says ", the type-8 pronoun again and `#1524` " booked a better gig at a bigger casino
across town.\n\nWhat will you do?".

The stored answers are `#32554` "Offer " plus the object pronoun plus `#2784` " more money",
`#13299` "Beg " plus the pronoun plus `#3770` " to stay", and `#47032` "Wish " plus the pronoun
plus `#4018` " well"; dispatch lowercases the label and tests for "offer", then "beg", then
"wish". Every answer starts from the same journal `#30741` "My casino's ", the relationship
status, `#5282` ", ", the name, `#5777` ", put in ", the possessive pronoun, `#3234`
" resignation from ", the possessive pronoun and `#3064` " position at my casino.".

Offer chains ScenarioCasinoAgeUpCelebrityResignationOffer (`0x3569368`) and changes nothing
else. Beg compares the guest's relationship strength against rand(0,101) - strength wins,

and `#4218` "!", the journal gains `#268` "\nI begged ", the pronoun, `#3771` " to stay and ", the
subject pronoun and `#1138` " agreed.", and the follow-up title is `#20245` "Fine, I guess". A
loss calls RemoveCelebrity (`0x2ab1654`), drops popularity two, gains #45 plus the subject

wished ", the pronoun, `#4019` " well.".

### The act in residence

ScenarioCasinoAgeUpEntertainmentActResignation (.ctor `0x356a830`, RefreshScenario `0x3569eb8`,
ChoiceSelectedAtIndex `0x356a22c`, ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush `0x356a680`) is pushed at
`0x2aad224` with the narrative at 0x170, the casino at 0x178 and the act at 0x180. Its

YearsSinceScenario above 2.

The body is the act's name followed by `#4878` "'s manager is informing you that the act will

### The port

`Sim::casinoCelebResignYear` and `Sim::casinoActResignYear` in _re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp,

floors popularity at zero rather than letting it go negative, the tracking funnel event is
not recorded, and the act's manager sentence uses the act's name without the native's
handling of an act whose name already ends in a quote.

compliment wants a match - so a house that builds only matching amenities can still be
praised, but never called tacky.

part.\n\nWhat will you do?".

The three answers are the act cards' own: `#12770` "Ban " plus the object pronoun plus

ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplimentAmenity (.ctor `0x35701a8`, RefreshScenario

The buttons are `#41215 "Thank ", `#21649 "Give " plus the object pronoun plus #3411
" some free games", and #26366 "Ignore "; dispatch is "thank"/"games"/"ignore". Thank
moves addiction -1, the mood slot -1 and the opinion slot +1; give moves addiction -2,

This card writes **no narrative at all**: 0x170 is never stored by the constructor,

so both the log line and the UI refresh are skipped while the effects still apply. That
is shipped behaviour, recorded here as such.

### The port

`Sim::casinoActComplaintYear` and `Sim::casinoActComplimentYear` in
`_re/port/src/fam/casino.cpp`, registered as `casino-act-complaint` and
`casino-act-compliment` with one ticket each and the same casino gate. Both read the

The booking itself is unmodelled beyond what REPORT 61 already did: a port act has no
last-interaction age, so the resignation card that reads it is still out of reach.

`complaint lanes: {'apologize': 8, 'ignore': 13, 'ban': 9} | complaints: 30 | praise: 27`.

Refresh stores the zoo, clears the dismiss button, sets the exterior title to
`#50857 'Zoo'` and the title to `#16900 'Customer Service'`. The body is
`#50431 'Your operations manager, '` + the manager's full name + `#5712 ", is reporting
that your park's ticket sales could improve if you addded more customer service
representatives.\n\nWhat will you do?"` - the doubled d in "addded" is the shipped
string and is kept. The labels are the same pair as the cleanliness card:
`#35307 'Reallocate labor resources'` and `#26366 'Ignore '` + the manager's object
pronoun. Reallocating hands off to `ScenarioZooEmployeeManagerStaffManagement
0x29e17b0`, the division-of-labor minigame; ignoring does nothing. Both branches write
the same fixed journal line `#30821 'My operations manager suggested I assign more of my
work force to customer service-related tasks.'` No money or stat moves.

### The port

`Sim::zooCustomerServiceYear` in `src/sim.cpp`, registered as `zoo-customer-service`
with one ticket, gated on `ownsZoo`, age 18 and not in prison, with the same four-year
cooldown stamp on the hero (`zooCustAge`). The bump percentage the native reads has no
port equivalent - there is no division-of-labor minigame to raise it - so the port's
card keeps dealing every four years, which is what an ignored native park sees. Like
cleanliness it draws nothing from any stream, so no new RNG was added and no other
family's sequence moved.

Ceilings: the minigame is absent, so "Reallocate labor resources" ends at the same
journal line as ignoring; the exterior title is not modelled; the manager is the park's
existing keeper rather than a separate operations-manager role.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_zoo_customer_service.py` walks fifteen zoo lives: the card deals 183
times, four-or-more years apart, with both labels, the fixed journal and no stat
movement on either answer. A hero without a zoo never sees it.

The full 137-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (298192f9...,
137 PASS / 0 FAIL): _re/tools/test_zoo_customer_service.py exercises the card, both
labels and the journal line, and nothing else moved.

## 348. The zoo's cleanliness card

One more card the zoo's own age-up pass can deal: the operations manager reports that
the guests are grumbling about the state of the park.

### The native side

`ScenarioZooAgeUpCleanliness`: `.ctor 0x29a4430`, `RefreshScenario 0x29a443c`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x29a470c`, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x29a48b4`,
pushed from `SimZoo::IncrementAge` at `0x2b59e44`. The zoo pass is an else-if chain, not
a set of independent tests like the casino's, so a zoo sees at most one of its age-up
cards a year; this one sits after pregnancy, the employee resignation and bankruptcy and
before customer service, theft and the merchandise order.

Eligibility, in order: the zoo exists, the hero is 18, the operations manager
(`SimZoo::GetOperationsManager 0x2b64768`) exists, and
`SimZoo::GetZooCustodialScore 0x2b65a90` reads under 20.0. Then
`YearsSinceScenario(#38122 'ScenarioZooAgeUpCleanliness') > 3`. There is no RNG
anywhere in the card - not in eligibility, not in the refresh, not in the choice - so it
deals every year the score stays low and the cooldown allows.

Refresh stores the zoo, clears the dismiss button, sets the exterior title to
`#50857 'Zoo'` and the title to `#15699 'Cleanliness'`. The body is
`#50431 'Your operations manager, '` + the manager's full name + `#5711 ', is reporting
that your guests are complaining about the cleanliness of the park.\n\n'` + the
manager's capitalized subject pronoun + `#3490 " suggests increasing your zoo's
custodial team to improve things.\n\nWhat will you do?"`. The two labels are
`#35307 'Reallocate labor resources'` and `#26366 'Ignore '` + the manager's object
pronoun. Reallocating hands off to `ScenarioZooEmployeeManagerStaffManagement
0x29e17b0`, the division-of-labor minigame; ignoring does nothing. Whichever answer is
taken, the journal is the same fixed line, written at the end of the refresh:
`#30820 'My operations manager suggested I assign more of my work force to custodial
tasks.'` No money or stat moves.

### The port

`Sim::zooCleanlinessYear` in `src/sim.cpp`, registered as `zoo-cleanliness` with one
ticket and gated on `ownsZoo`, age 18, not in prison. Because the port has no staff
roster, the custodial score is a proxy: every hand counts as custodial at five points,
so a founding park of two never reaches the native threshold of twenty, and only the
reallocation minigame the port does not have could raise it. The four-year cooldown is
the native `> 3` read on the hero's own `zooCleanAge` stamp. The card draws nothing from
any stream, so no new RNG was added and no other family's sequence moved.

Ceilings: the port has no division-of-labor minigame, so both answers end at the same
journal line and the custodial score never actually rises - the card keeps coming every
four years the way an ignored native card would. The exterior title is not modelled on
any port card. The manager is the keeper the park is already given rather than a
separate operations-manager role.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_zoo_cleanliness.py` walks fifteen zoo lives and the card deals 183
times, with four-or-more-year gaps, the two labels, the fixed journal line and no stat
movement on either answer. A hero without a zoo never sees it.
The full 136-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (3f363c95..., 134 PASS / 2 FAIL).
