Both failures are test-side and were fixed here without a code change: the birth card's sentence check knew only the single-birth wording, but the same card reports twins and triplets after its 1-in-50 roll (REPORT 340), so the check now accepts the multiple forms; and the morning-after check counted only the supervisor hookup cards as earning a morning card, while a successful seduction inside the workplace discipline card queues the same card (REPORT 325), so that check now counts it too. Both were re-run green.

## 347. The casino's three punter cards

The casino's age-up pass keeps a small cast of regulars, and three of the cards it can
deal are about them: one regular stops coming, and two are about the guest act the
casino has booked - the regular who complains the act does not fit the house theme, and
the regular who compliments the booking when it does.

### The native side

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerLost`: `.ctor 0x3572d40`, `RefreshScenario 0x35725c4`,
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x3572af4`, pushed from `SimCasino::IncrementAge` at
`0x2aacecc`. It overrides no choice handler, so it deals one button: `#32432 'OK'`.
Eligibility reads the punters and needs one who has been coming for five years or more
(`hero.Age[+0x20] - gambler[+0x308] >= 5`); the hero must be 18, out of prison, and
`YearsSinceScenario(#37052 'ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerLost') > 4`. Refresh drops a
popularity point (`SimCasino::ImpactPopularity(-1)` at `0x3572740`), removes the punter
(`SimCasino::RemoveGambler 0x2ab0004`), sets the title `#20989 'Gambler Lost'` and the
body `FullName + #2297 ' has stopped gambling at your casino.'`. One row follows, keyed
`#20993 'Gambling Style'`, with the style string capitalized; the two bars are
`#30360 'Money'` and `#10777 'Addiction'`. Journal: `#30743 "My casino's gambler, "` +
`FullName + #5863 ', stopped playing at my casino.'`.

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplaintCelebrity`: `.ctor 0x356d128`,
`RefreshScenario 0x356c0f8`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x356c61c`,
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x356cfec`, pushed at `0x2aacf50`. Eligibility: the
guest must still be alive (`SimCasinoCelebrity+0x18`), the casino must have punters,
`System.String::Equals(get_GenreData(celebrity)[+0x18], casino.Theme[+0x38], w2=5)` must
be FALSE - the card only fires when the act's genre does not belong to the house theme -
then age 18, not in prison, and `YearsSinceScenario(#37045) > 2`. Refresh seats a punter
(`GetRandomNonMafiaGambler 0x2ab0c24`) and builds the body from `#50268 "Your casino's "`,
the punter's relationship status (`#5282 ', '`), the punter's full name (`#5666 ',
is complaining that '`), the guest's full name (`#4839 "'s "`), `#46`, the punter's
pronoun (`#3304 ' saying '`), the guest's first name, `#4839` again, the act's genre
(`#2794 " musical stylings don't fit the "`), the house theme (`#3556 " theme you're
trying to establish.\n\nWhat will you do?"`). Title `#16066 'Complaint'`. The three
labels are `#12770 'Ban '` + object pronoun + `#2104 ' from my casino'`,
`#11554 'Apologize for the inconvenience'` and `#26366 'Ignore '` + object pronoun,
dispatched by `Contains("ban")`, `Contains("apologize")`, `Contains("ignore")`. Banning
removes the punter, drops two popularity points, pushes the banned-gambler feedback card
(`#50001 "You're outta here"` over a snippet from
`a16_casino-banned-gambler-snippet-enc`) and journals
`#23602 + #5567 + #5282 + #6086 ',.'` - the literal hard-codes "she" and ends in a comma
followed by a full stop. Apologizing adds two addiction, drops two popularity and adds
one punter happiness, journaling `#23453 + #5551 + #5282 + #6312 '.'`. Ignoring takes two
addiction away, adds two popularity and drops one happiness, journaling
`#24467 + #4921 + #5282 + #6312 '.'`.

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplimentCelebrity`: `.ctor 0x35709f4`,
`RefreshScenario 0x3570214`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x3570678`,
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x35708b8`, pushed at `0x2aacf7c`. It is the same card
with the comparison inverted - `Equals(get_GenreData(celebrity)[+0x18], theme)` must be
TRUE - and a longer cooldown (`YearsSinceScenario(#37049) > 4`). The body is
`#50268 + #5282 + #5669 ', is complimenting you for booking '` + guest full name +
`#3732 ' to perform at your casino.'` + `#46` + the punter's capitalized pronoun
(`#3309 ' says each performance is somehow better than the previous.\n\nWhat will you
do?'`); title `#16100 'Compliment'`. Its three labels are `#41215 'Thank '`,
`#21649 'Give '` + pronoun + `#3411 ' some free games'` and `#26366 'Ignore '`. Thanking
takes one addiction, one popularity point and gives one happiness; giving free games adds
two addiction, drops two popularity and adds two happiness; ignoring drops two
popularity. This card writes no journal at all.

The genre comparison is worth recording exactly: `get_GenreData 0x2c27354` returns the
singer-genre record, and the field read for the comparison is that record's `+0x18`, its
theme, not the genre word printed in the body (`SimCasinoCelebrity+0x318`). The shipped
table keeps the two vocabularies apart - its 62 rows carry 8 themes (Hollywood, Medieval,
Roman, anime, circus, outer space, pirate, speakeasy) and no genre name is also a theme
name - so a comparison against the genre word itself would fire the complaint card every
year and never the compliment. The port compares the same field.

### The port

`Sim::casinoGamblerLostYear`, `Sim::casinoCelebComplaintYear` and
`Sim::casinoCelebComplimentYear` in `src/fam/casino.cpp`, registered as
`casino-gambler-lost`, `casino-celeb-complaint` and `casino-celeb-compliment`, each with
one ticket, and each drawing from its own stream `casinoGuestRng_` so the two older
casino cards keep their sequences. The three cooldowns are kept on the hero
(`casinoGamblerLostAge`, `casinoCelebComplaintAge`, `casinoCelebComplimentAge`). The
punter is the port's regular, whose tier word comes from the five gambling styles the
casino already tracks; the guest act is the one the casino's own celebrity event seats,
and the port now keeps that act's genre and the genre's theme
(`casinoCelebrityGenre`, `casinoCelebrityGenreTheme`) when the act appears, drawing both
off `a16_casino-casino-singer-genre-enc`. The cards move the port's counters rather than
the native's per-gambler records: `casinoGamblers`, `casinoPopularity`,
`casinoGamblerAddiction` and `casinoGamblerHappiness`.

A pinned family never sees the celebrity event that seats a guest, so the harness grows
one key: `"casino_guest": "same"` seats a guest whose genre belongs to the house theme
and `"diff"` one whose genre does not (`Sim::seedCasinoGuest`). It is a harness hook, not
a game path.

Ceilings: the port has no per-punter records, so the five-year spread the losing card
needs becomes "the casino has regulars", and the money and addiction bars on that card
are not drawn. The banned punter's feedback card and its snippet are not pushed - the
journal carries the branch, as in sections 322 and 345. The complaint body's pronoun is
type 9, which has no recovered argument order, so the port prints the lowercase subject.
The guest's genre is a draw, not a field of a celebrity entity the port does not have.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_casino_punter.py` walks twenty lives per card with a seeded casino. The
losing card deals 27 times with the punter named in body and journal; the complaint card
deals in all three lanes (15 bans, 15 apologies, 7 ignores) with the punter and guest
matching between body and journal, and never when the guest's genre belongs to the house
theme; the compliment card deals 31 times and never when the genre does not. Both
celebrity cards respect their cooldowns (three years measured for the complaint) and
move no visible stat.

The full 135-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (d1509fd5..., 135 PASS / 0 FAIL).

## 346. The zoo's theft card

The park's animals can be stolen. This is the last of the zoo's own age-up cards; the
triage of all `244 `ScenarioCasino*` / `ScenarioZoo*` classes is in this section too,
because it is what decided the ordering of the rest.

### The triage

244 classes carry a `ScenarioCasino` or `ScenarioZoo` name: 121 casino, 123 zoo. Only
37 of their constructors are called from an age-up pipeline at all - 22 from
`SimCasino::IncrementAge` (`0x2aac1cc`), 11 from `SimZoo::IncrementAge` (`0x2b592bc`)
and 4 from `SimZooAnimal::IncrementAge` (`0x2b67aac`). The other `207 are menu-only:
they are opened from a management screen the port does not have, so they cannot fire in
a life at all. Of the 37, this section takes the zoo's theft card; the zoo cleanliness
card, the casino's new/lost/celebrity gamblers and the twelve further age-up cards whose
addresses are recorded in `/tmp/qdir/az_methods.txt` wait for their own sections. The
eight unported table games stay on the list for the same reason as the menu cards.

### The native side

`ScenarioZooAgeUpTheft` - `.ctor 0x29a9424`, `RefreshScenario 0x29a9430`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x29a9e08`, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x29aa4a8` - is
pushed from `SimZoo::IncrementAge`.

Eligibility, in order: the zoo; the hero; `hero.Age >= 0x12`; `zoo.YearsOwned (+0x20)
>= 6`; `GetRandomAnimalToSteal(zoo)` returns something; then a chance roll - `chance =
SimZoo::GetChanceOfSecurityBreach 0x2b65cb4`, `roll = GetRandomNumber(0, 0x65)`, and
`if (chance <= (float)roll) return false`; finally `YearsSinceScenario(ScenarioZooAgeUpTheft)
> 3`.

`GetChanceOfSecurityBreach` divides the park's custodial staff (`+0xd4`) by a plot-size
divisor - `w9 = PlotSize (+0x18) - 1` into `floatTable[0xfc5328] = {10.0, 20.0, 40.0}` -
times 100, and bands the result: above 75 it is `0.0f`, above 48 it is
`GetRandomNumber(5, 0xb)`, above 25 `GetRandomNumber(0xa, 0x15)`, otherwise
`GetRandomNumber(0x14, 0x1f)`. The breach percentage is compared against a uniform roll
of 0-100, so a well-staffed park on a big plot is very nearly safe and a small park with
no custodial staff is nearly always hit.

`GetRandomAnimalToSteal 0x29a990c` builds a weighted list over every habitat's animals:
rare breeds (`+0x55`) are skipped, and each remaining animal is appended N times where N
follows `MaximumAnimalValue (+0x58)` - 1,000,001 and up is 10, 500,001 is 5, 50,001 is 3,
1,001 is 2, and anything cheaper is 1. One uniform draw over that list picks the victim.

Text. Exterior title `#50857 'Zoo'`, title `#42786 'Theft'`, dismiss button on. The body
is `#50431 'Your operations manager, '` + the manager's full name + `#5709 ', is reporting
that someone snuck into '` + the zoo's name + `#1236 ' and stole '` + the animal's name +
`#3532 ' the '` + the breed + `#4218 '!'`, then `#46 '\n\n'` + `PronounStringForType(5)` +
`#3491 " suggests increasing your zoo's security team to avoid further thefts.\n\nWhat
will you do?"`. The no-manager fallback body is #10273 / #1235 / #3532 / #4229. The
journal is `#11308` + `#3532` + `#2115 ' from my zoo.'`. Two buttons: `#20125 'File a
police report'` and `#10543 'Accept the loss'`, dispatched on `Contains('police'
#63774)` and `Contains('loss' #61914)`.

Accepting the loss calls `SimZoo::RemoveAnimal 0x2b5dc80` and appends `#307 '\nI decided
they could keep '` + `PronounStringForType(2)` + `#6312 '.'` to the journal. There is no
money and no feedback card.

Reporting it rolls `GetRandomNumber(0, 3)`. On 0 - one time in three - the animal comes
back and is *never removed*: the card is titled from a pool of `#34225 'Poached the
poacher'`, `#50888 'Zoonapper case: Solved'`, `#46111 "We got 'em boys"`, its body is
`#42269` / `#3532` / `#4218 '!'` + `#135 '\n\nThey returned '` + `PronounStringForType(2)`
+ `#1256 " and warned you to improve your zoo's security."`, and the journal gets `#336`.
On 1 or 2 the animal is removed: the pool is `#50887 'Zoonapped!'`, `#21062 'Gather a
search party?'`, `#21056 'Gary Come Home~'`, the body is `#42305` / `#3532` / `#6312 '.'`
+ `#141 "\n\nThey warned you to improve your zoo's security."`, and the journal gets
`#337`. Either way the whole thing costs no money and moves no stat, so the card is
report-and-choice only.

### The port

`Sim::zooTheftYear` sits with the other zoo functions (`_re/port/src/sim.cpp`) and is
registered as `"zoo-theft"` behind `l.hero.ownsZoo` with one ticket and its own stream
`zooTheftRng_`.

The gate is the native one: a zoo, age 18, not in prison, `h.age - h.zooOwnedSince >= 6`,
a non-empty herd, and `h.zooTheftAge` at least four years back. A ten percent coin
replaces the native randomness entirely for the push (the native card has no roll of its
own at push - it is the breach chance that decides), and the breach is then computed from
the hero's staff count and attractions.

Because the port has no staff assignment and no plot size, every hand counts as custodial
and the plot size is read off the attractions - fewer than three is a plot of 1, fewer
than six is 2, otherwise 3 - which feeds the same dividers and bands. The breach is
compared against `below(101)` exactly as native.

The victim is drawn from `h.zooHerd` (REPORT 344) with the native value bands, rare
breeds excluded. The manager is the park's keeper, `h.zooEmployee`. The body, the journal
and both button labels are the port's own strings in the native wording; the police roll
is `below(3) == 0` for the animal's return, and the herd entry is erased on both loss
paths and the count left in `h.zooAnimals` updated.

### Ceilings

The manager is the keeper the park already has rather than a separate operations manager,
because the port staffs one role.

There is no follow-up card. The police success and failure cards - both title pools and
both bodies above - are transcribed here but not pushed; the journal sentence has to
carry the outcome instead.

Plot size is a function of the attractions, not of a plot the hero can size; every member
of staff counts as custodial. Both matter only through the band arithmetic.

The herd is seeded from the names table, which leaves its breed blank for a generic
species - `Bird`, `Bear`, `Elephant` - so those animals take the lowest breed the
animals table lists for that species instead of a random one, which keeps the seeding
stream unchanged.

The card carries no money and no stat change at all, which is why its `deltas` are all
zero: the native effects are the animal's removal and a journal sentence.

### Verified

Measured by `_re/tools/test_zoo_theft.py` over seeds 1-40:

`cards: 43 | lanes: {'File a police report': 22, 'Accept the loss': 21} | tails: {'keep': 21, 'back': 11, 'lost': 11}`

The test asserts the body and the journal name the same animal, that the breed is a real
row of `a16_zoo-animals-enc`, both choices and all three journal tails, that the card
moves no money and no stat, that consecutive cards for one hero are at least four years
apart, and that a hero without a park never sees it.

The full 134-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (acfb4814...,
134 PASS / 0 FAIL): _re/tools/test_zoo_theft.py exercises the card, both choices and
all three journal tails, and nothing else moved.

## 345. The casino's two mob favours

A made man who owns a casino gets asked for things. The native game pushes two
cards from the house's own age-up queue: the family wants a cut of its take
laundered through the casino's books, and the family wants an empty storage room
and a free hand for an hour. Both sit behind a flag of their own - the hero must
have already leant a mafia member out to rough up a gambler - so a hero who only
joined the family and bought a casino never sees either.

### The native side

**Laundering.** `ScenarioCasinoAgeUpMafiaMemberLaunder` (ctor `0x35775a4`,
`RefreshScenario 0x3576890`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x3576fcc`,
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x357749c`; fields `+0x170` narrative,
`+0x178` casino, `+0x180` cut, `+0x188` member, `+0x190` amount) is pushed from
`SimCasino::IncrementAge` at `0x2aad298` (eligibility) and `0x2aad2b8` (ctor).
The gate runs in this order: a casino exists; `SimCasino::GetMafiaMembers` has at
least one member; `SimCasino+0x99` is set; the hero is 18 or older; the hero is
not in prison; and `Life::YearsSinceScenario` against the class-name literal
#37058 is greater than one.

`RefreshScenario` draws one member at random and, in local currency, an amount
between 100,000 and 500,000 rounded to the nearest ten
(`DataCountry::GetLocalCostForAmountWithMinimumCostAndRoundTo` then
`GameReference::GetRoundedNumber(..., -1.0)`), then the cut as
`amount * GetRandomNumber(10, 21) / 100` rounded the same way - so 10 to 20% of
the amount. The title is #19974 "Favor", the exterior title is never written, and
the body is built from literals:

> " #4259, the member's own nickname, " #4262, #2517
> " is asking for a favor on behalf of ", `PronounStringForType(member, 1)`,
> #898 " Mafia family.", #46, `PronounStringForType(member, 5)`, #1352
> " asks if you could launder some money through your casino and promises to give
> you a cut if you agree.\n\nWhat will you do?"

The two figures also go into a table dictionary under #11284 "Amount" and #50123
"Your Cut", in that order. The journal, #30741 on the front, is
`"My casino's " + <status> + ', "' + nickname + '" ' + <name> + ", asked me to
launder " + <amount> + " through my casino and offered me " + <cut> + " to do so."`
(#5283, #5395, #3575, #3658). The choices are stored in order - #17913 "Do it",
#35505 "Refuse" - and dispatch on a lowercased `Contains` of "do" (#57641) and
"refuse" (#64441).

Doing it moves the member's `+0x508` up two, calls
`SimCasinoGambler::ImpactAddictionlevel(member, -2)`, moves `+0x738` down two,
pays the cut into the hero's bank balance, puts the full amount into the casino's
bank balance, and appends #238 "\nI accepted the bribe." to the journal.
Refusing puts a feedback card in front of the next scenario - a title drawn from
#25931 "I'll remember that...", a body of #3281 and #2190 with the member's own
pronouns, and a relationship bar graph - then moves `+0x508` down three, calls
`ImpactAddictionlevel(-2)`, moves `+0x738` up two, and appends #390
"\nI refused the bribe.".

**The interrogation.** `ScenarioCasinoAgeUpMafiaMemberInterrogation` (ctor
`0x3576884`, `RefreshScenario 0x3575c08`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x357627c`,
eligibility `0x357677c`; fields `+0x170` narrative, `+0x178` casino, `+0x180`
member, `+0x188` offer) is pushed at `0x2aad328` / `0x2aad360` through the same
gate, against its own class-name literal #37057. The offer is the same localized
100,000 to 500,000 rounded to ten, the title is the same "Favor", and the body
leaves the nickname out:

> <name> + #2517 + `PronounStringForType(member, 1)` + #898 + #46 +
> `PronounStringForType(member, 5)` + #1350 " asks if " +
> `PronounStringForType(member, 1)` + #897 " Mafia family members could
> \"interrogate\" someone in one of your casino's empty storage rooms and offers
> you some cash if you agree.\n\nWhat will you do?"

Its journal is <name> + #1344 " asked me to let " + `Pronoun(2)` + #2466
" interrogate someone in my casino's empty storage room. " + `Pronoun(5)` +
#2884 " offered me " + <offer> + #3717 " to let " + `Pronoun(2)` + #6312 ".";
the choices are the same two. Doing it pays the offer into the hero's bank
balance, moves `+0x508` up two, calls `ImpactAddictionlevel(-2)`, moves `+0x738`
down two, and appends #71 "\n\nI accepted the bribe" (no full stop). Refusing is
the launder refusal's shape again: `+0x508` down three, addiction down two,
`+0x738` up two, journal #83 "\n\nI refused the bribe".

Both accepted branches then roll `GetRandomNumber(0, 101)` and, on 20 or less
(about 20.8% of the time), chain a police-investigation card in front of the next scenario with
the member and the money as its fields. That card's identity is inferred from its
field shape and the shared follow-up, not from a proven literal.

### The port

`Sim::casinoMafiaLaunderYear` and `Sim::casinoMafiaInterrogYear` live in
`src/fam/casino.cpp` beside the other two casino cards. They gate on
`h.ownsCasino && h.mafia`, need the hero 18 and out of prison, keep their own
cooldowns (`h.casinoLaunderAge`, `h.casinoInterrogAge`, at least two years
between asks) and coin 12% a year each off a stream of their own,
`casinoMobRng_`, because `casinoCardRng_` already drives the complaint and
compliment cards and extra draws there would move their sequences.

The member is drawn by `mafiaToken("mafia-colleague")` for the name and gender,
and the nickname from `a16_mafia-nicknames-enc` filtered by the hero's own
`Mob Country` and then by gender; the table's `<first-name>` and `<last-name>`
tokens are filled from the drawn member, and a country with no rows in the table
falls back to the whole gender-matched pool. The member's relationship-status
getter (`+0x4f8`) is not recovered, so the journal uses one of the casino's own
five tier words, Beginner through High Roller, where the native prints that
string. Money prints as a dollar sign and digits where the native runs
`CurrencyStringForAmountWithBigNumberShorthand`, and the two table rows ("Amount",
"Your Cut") are not carried because a port card has no table surface. The two
stat slots the native moves live on the hero as `h.casinoMobMood` and
`h.casinoMobView`.

### Ceilings

- The two vtable slots behave as a mood and as an opinion of the hero (+2/-3 and
  -2/+2); neither is a named method in the dump, so the port keeps them as two
  hero-side counters that no other card reads.
- The member's `+0x4f8` status string, the nickname's pool order when the hero's
  mob country has no rows, and the police follow-up card are all unrecovered or
  inferred. The follow-up is not pushed.
- The refusal's feedback card and its relationship bar graph are not reproduced;
  the port writes the journal line and moves the two counters only.
- The gate's `SimCasino+0x99` (hero has already used a member to rough up a
  gambler) has no port equivalent, so membership of the family stands in for it.
- Amounts are drawn flat in dollars; the native converts them with the hero's
  country cost table first.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_casino_mob.py` walks twenty lives with a casino and the family.
Measured: `cards: {'launder': 14, 'interrog': 10} | lanes: {'Do it': 13, 'Refuse': 11}`.
Every card is checked for the title "Favor", the two choices, an empty residue,
all-zero stat deltas, the body's own wording, the journal line's name and
nickname agreeing with the body, the answer's tail line, and a two-year gap
before the same favour returns. Controls: a hero with a casino and no family, and
a hero in the family with no casino, get neither card. Same seed, answering "Do
it" leaves the hero richer than answering "Refuse".
The full 133-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (ca4a5271..., 131 PASS /
2 FAIL). Both failures are test-side and were fixed here without a code change: the
mischief card's helper pinned one seed and assumed the card would sit at the step whose
answer it forced, but a life's choices are indexed by card, so it now searches lives for
a forced card that really carries the forced answer; and the robbery card's result can
now be separated from the pick by a drained pending card, or never arrive at all when
the pick is the last card of the life, so that check walks forward over the age's own
events. Both were re-run green.


## 344. The zoo's animals, pregnant and dead

Every card in the park's life cycle names one animal: the vet reports that a
particular female is pregnant, a particular mother hatches a particular chick, a
particular animal dies at a particular age. The port kept the park's animals as a
count plus one animal triple for the cards' tokens, so none of these stories had
anywhere to live. This section gives the park a herd, and the three cards that
act on it.

### The native side

``SimZoo`` keeps a ``List<SimZooAnimal>`` (``zoo+0x100`` is the pregnancy
candidate list, ``zoo+0x130`` the zoo's own card queue, ``zoo+0x20`` the park's
years owned). Each ``SimZooAnimal`` carries its own age (``+0x30``), health,
pregnancy flag (``+0x44``), death type (``+0x3c``) and the row of
``a16_zoo-animals-enc`` it belongs to: ``Breed``, ``Maturity Age``,
``Average Lifespan``, ``Breeding Likelihood`` (1-5), ``Lays Eggs``.

**Pregnancy.** ``ScenarioZooAgeUpAnimalPregnancy`` (``.ctor 0x29a2318``,
``RefreshScenario 0x29a2324``, ``ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x29a2824``,
``ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x29a28c8``) is pushed from
``SimZoo::IncrementAge`` at ``0x2b59c64``, and only when the zoo's own queue holds
at most one card. There is no chance roll on the card itself. The candidate list
is built by ``SimZoo::CreateAgeUpPregnancyPossibleFemaleAnimals 0x2b5b2a8``: a
mature female who is not already pregnant, in a park that also holds a mature male
of her breed, admitted when ``GetRandomNumber(0,100)`` comes in under her breed's
``Breeding Likelihood`` mapped through the table at ``0xfc52f0``
(``{20,40,60,80,90}`` for 1-5). The eligibility gate adds age 18, a veterinarian
on the staff, a non-empty list, and ``YearsSinceScenario > 3``. ``RefreshScenario``
draws one of the candidates and calls ``SimZooAnimal::Impregnate 0x2b6a2f0``.

The card is titled ``#18563 'Eggs'`` when the breed lays eggs and ``#34481
'Pregnancy'`` when it does not, with the park as its exterior title. Its body is
``#50545 "Your zoo's veterinarian, "`` + the vet's name + ``#5707 ', is reporting
that '`` + the animal's name + ``#3532 ' the '`` + its breed + ``#2679 ' laid some
eggs!'`` or ``#2609 ' is pregnant!'``. The journal line is ``#24006 'I discovered '``
+ name + ``#3532`` + breed + ``#2680 ' laid some eggs.'`` or ``#2610 ' is
pregnant.'``. One button, ``#32432 'OK'``.

**Birth.** One year later``SimZooAnimal::IncrementAge 0x2b67aac`` resolves the
pregnancy into one of three cards: the birth at ``0x2b67d44``
(``ScenarioZooAgeUpAnimalBirth``, ``.ctor 0x299dd5c``), the failure at
``0x2b67d20`` (``.ctor 0x299ea48``) or the Golden Pacifier at ``0x2b67cfc``
(``.ctor 0x299ef8c``). The ladder is: a park younger than six years always gets
the plain birth; after that a complication is forced by the mother's health at or
below 40, or by her age reaching 0.7 of the breed's average lifespan, or else by
``GetRandomNumber(0,100)`` landing at 15 or below; the complication becomes the
Golden Pacifier only when ``DoesUserHaveAccessToGoldenPacifier`` says so, and the
failure card otherwise.

The birth card's title is ``#12665 'Baby '`` + ``CapitalizeAllMajorWordsInString``
of the baby's breed; its body branches on whether the breed lays eggs
(``#10146 'A newborn '`` + gender + breed + ``#2654 ' just hatched from one of '``
+ the mother + ``#4867 "'s eggs.\n\nWhat will you name "`` + pronoun + ``#9923
'?'``) and otherwise reads mother + ``#2653 ' just gave birth to a baby '`` +
gender + breed + ``#4230 '!\n\nWhat will you name '`` + pronoun + ``#9923``. The
name comes from an input field whose default suggestion is
``DataHub::GetRandomZooAnimalNameForBreedAndGender 0x27d21a4``; the journal is
``#2304/#1895`` (eggs) or ``#2168/#6030`` (live). The failure card is titled
``#18277 'Duds'`` for eggs and ``#17288 'Death'`` for live births, with ``#31950
'None of '`` + mother + ``#4864 "'s eggs hatched."`` or the newborn dying in
childbirth, and journals ``#24009/#4866`` and ``#24008/#4849``.

**Death.** ``ScenarioZooAnimalDeath`` (``.ctor 0x29b3530``, ``RefreshScenario
0x29b3614``, ``ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x29b398c``) is pushed from four places:
natural old age in ``SimZooAnimal::IncrementAge 0x2b67f30``, a predator in
``SimZoo::IncrementAge 0x2b5a6d8``, disease in ``SimZooAnimal::ProcessDiseases
0x2b68ad0``, and the vet's own cards. The natural case needs a park six years old,
an animal already past its breed's average lifespan, and
``GetRandomNumber(0,100)`` at 40 or above. The refresh removes the animal from the
zoo first, titles the card ``#17288 'Death'`` and sets the body as
``#70317 '{0} the {1} died at the age of {2}.\n\n{3}'`` over the name, the breed,
the age and the death sentence. Two buttons: ``#23017 'Hold a memorial for '`` +
object pronoun, and ``#22584 'Have '`` + object pronoun + ``#3505 '
taxidermied'``. The memorial branch moves no stat and no money at all; the
taxidermy branch hands the animal to ``ScenarioZooAnimalTaxidermy``
(``.ctor 0x29b3b40``), whose prices are the animal's market price times 0.33 for
the good taxidermist and times 0.165 for the cheap one.

### The port

``bl::Hero`` gains a herd (``ZooHerdAnimal``: species, breed, name, female, age,
pregnant, health), the age the park was bought (``zooOwnedSince``), the age of the
last pregnancy card (``zooPregAge``, the four-year cooldown) and a
``zooHerdSeeded`` flag so the animals are only put there once.
``Sim::zooSeedHerd`` fills it from ``a16_zoo-animal-names-enc`` when the park is
bought; ``Sim::zooAnimalNameFor`` is the default name suggestion of a breed and
gender; ``Sim::zooLifecycleYear`` is the family, registered with two tickets and
its own stream (``zooLifeRng_``) so nothing else moved.

The family ages the herd first, then resolves a pregnancy from last year (birth or
failure), then offers a death, then reports a new pregnancy, so a life never gets
two of these cards in one year even when the native queue would have carried two.
The candidate list follows the native builder exactly: mature female, no existing
pregnancy, a mature male of her breed in the herd, and her breed's Breeding
Likelihood under a 0-99 roll. The cards carry the same titles, bodies and journal
lines, and the death card's own -2 impact rides the port's impact conversion
(``pointsForImpact(-2)``, eight happiness).

### Ceilings

- The Golden Pacifier arm needs the in-app purchase, which the port does not model,
  so every complication takes the failure lane.
- The vet is a name from the zoo's token cache, not an employee entity, so the
  pregnancy card needs no hire; the native card needs a veterinarian on staff.
- Only one lifecycle card a year; the native queue can carry a pregnancy, a birth
  and a death in the same pass.
- Predator murder (5% a year, one kill per habitat), the disease pass, the vet's
  check-up menu cards, the euthanasia chain and the taxidermy card with its two
  prices are not modelled.
- The birth card's habitat and overflow follow-ups are not modelled; the baby
  simply joins the herd and the park's animal count.
- The herd is seeded young (0-5) with full health, and the health arm of the
  complication ladder therefore never fires; the age arm and the 0-99 roll do.
- The death-scenario row's brackets are parsed against the dead animal's gender,
  not against an "other animal" as some rows expect.

### Verified

``_re/tools/test_zoo_lifecycle.py`` walks sixty lives with a zoo and reads every
lifecycle card: the four card kinds, the eggs/live branch of each of them against
the breed's ``Lays Eggs`` cell, the titles, the full body and journal forms, the
death body's ``died at the age of`` line, the two death buttons, the -8 happiness of
a death and the four-year cooldown of the pregnancy card. Measured: birth 12, death
131, eggs 10, failure 3, live 6, pregnancy 16. A hero without a zoo never gets one
of these cards, and neither does a minor.

The full 132-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (c93b4405...,
131 PASS / 1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change:
the troll-outbound card lives in the dumb pool, and the two tickets this family added
pushed its first appearance from below seed 31 to seed 41, so that sweep now walks ninety
lives (measured 4 cards over seeds 1-90). It was re-run green.

## 343. The insult's comeback card

The workplace discipline card's insult button (REPORT 325) left its own aftermath out:
the native game pushes a second, dismiss-only card that titles itself with a comeback and
repeats the sentence the button wrote. This section ports that card and, with it, fixes
whose gender the insult word is drawn for.

### The native side

The insult branch of `ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineSupervisor::ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`
(0x299cbb0) builds a four-entry ArrayList of comebacks and then picks the card's two
strings: `PickRandomFromStringArray` (0x2e165f8) takes #39989 `Stay classy`, #40899
`Take that`, #41445 `That's right` or #48825 `You heard me` for the title, and
`GameReference::GetRandomNumber(0,3)` (0x299cc84) chooses one of three sentence forms.
Only the first form's fields are established — #47966 `You called your {0}, {1}, {2}.`
over the supervisor's relationship status, the supervisor's full name and the insult word
— so that is the sentence the port writes. The card itself is a plain
`Scenario::.ctor(title, body, next)` (0x2a25500) with no choices: its only effect is the
journal line #69007 `{0}\nI called {1} {2}.`, which repeats the sentence and then says who
was called what.

The insult word comes from `DataHub::GetRandomInsultForGender` (0x2808570), and the
argument is the *insulted person's* gender, not the hero's. The port's `insultToken` was
filtering `a16_insults-enc` by the hero's own gender, which only showed when the
supervisor's gender differed from the hero's; the new `insultTokenForGender(bool)` takes
the gender to filter for and both workplace cards now pass their own subject's — the
supervisor for the discipline card's allegation and for this card.

### The port

The insult lane now draws the comeback (`discRng_.below(4)` over the four lines) and the
insult word, writes #47966 over `"your supervisor, " + name` and pushes
`kPendingInsultComeback`. `Sim::insultComebackYear` renders it with the comeback as the
title, the sentence as the body and #69007 as the narrative, then clears the three hero
fields (`insultComeback`, `insultSentence`, `insultWord`) so the card cannot reappear.
One card per year-up is the port's idiom, so the card arrives in a later year than the
discipline card that caused it rather than immediately after the dismissal (ceiling).

### Ceilings

- Two of the three sentence forms (#49529 and #49527, both `You told your {0}, {1}, that
  ...`) are recovered as templates but their argument slots are not established, so the
  card always uses the `called` form.
- The card arrives one age-up later than it does in the game, because the port drains one
  pending card per year (the same shape as every other follow-up card here).
- The work-performance, achievement and Apollo16 people-insulted tracker writes that ride
  the button are not modelled; the port keeps its own `supInsulted` counter (REPORT 325).

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_insult_comeback.py` drives thirty lives with the insult lane forced and
asserts, for all 276 comeback cards: the body is #47966 over a supervisor name and an
insult word with no bracket tokens left; the card has no choice and moves no stat; the
journal repeats the same word with the supervisor's own object pronoun; the word belongs
to `a16_insults-enc`'s pool for the gender that pronoun implies; and a workplace
discipline card was seen earlier in the same age-up. All four comebacks appeared.
Measured: `comeback cards: 276 | titles: 4` over seeds 1-30.

The full 131-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (6bd5433c..., 131 PASS /
0 FAIL).

## 342. The hero's own pregnancy

The pregnancy card of REPORT 338 only ever arrives when the hero is the father. The
game's other half of that chain — the hero carrying the baby herself — was missing: a
female life could not conceive, and no card asked her about it.

### The native side

The pregnancy lives on SimPerson+0x48 whoever carries it. When the hero is the mother,
SimHero::IncrementAge calls
`SimPregnancy::GetResultingPregnancyForMotherAndFatherAndTypeAndAssignToMother`
(0x2b3a438) with the hero as the mother and her current lover as the father, after
`HasBasePregnancyEligibility` (0x2b3a604) checks the mother's gender, the absence of an
existing pregnancy, her `OnBirthControl` flag (+0x50), that neither parent is a vampire,
and her age (13 to 55, `IsEligibleForDeterministicConception` 0x2b3a8cc). The two rolls
are the ones the lover lane already uses: `GetNaturalConceptionAgeProbability` over the
mother's age (0/45/70/40/20/6/3/0 for the bands under 13, 13-17, 18-34, 35-39, 40-44,
45-49, 50-54 and over 54), then her own fertility (`SimPerson+0xa4`) against a draw from
0 to 119.

`ScenarioPregnancy` then picks its body by who is carrying it (IsMotherHero at
0x2573c24): when the pregnancy's Type is 2 or 3 (`and w8,#0xfffffffe; cmp #2` at
0x2573c38) the card says #47766 `You are pregnant!` and journals #26043 `I'm pregnant!`;
otherwise, when the father is the current lover (0x2573c7c/0x2573c88), it says #47765
`You are pregnant with your {0}, {1}, baby!` over the lowercased relationship string and
his name, and journals #23614 `I became pregnant with my {0}, {1}, baby!` Both sit over
the #68715 `{0}\n\nWhat will you do?` wrapper with the same two stored choices, 'Keep the
baby' (#28214) and "Don't keep the baby" (#18038); the Golden Pacifier option (#45179)
is offered on top when the pregnancy's Type is 1 and the monetization flag is set.

The decline clears the hero's own +0x48 slot (0x2574a54), fires the same unnamed -6
impact through the person's vtable slot +0x508 (0x25745c8), and logs #48177 `You chose not
to keep the baby!` with a flavour title picked from #32116/#19874/#47091.

Resolution is the next age-up: SimHero::IncrementAge makes the virtual
`ShouldSufferMiscarriage` call (0x2c47514) and pushes `ScenarioMiscarriage` (0x2573044 at
0x2a6378c) when it says yes and `ScenarioBirth` (0x256c9cc at 0x2a637b8) otherwise. With
the hero carrying it, the miscarriage speaks in her own voice: #49447 `You suffered a {0}
miscarriage and lost the baby!` over the trimester descriptor, journal #25197 `I suffered a
{0} miscarriage!`, and for the 1-in-10 typed loss #48616 `You had {0} and lost the baby!`
with journal #24334, at a -5 impact and a fertility multiplier of 0.8. The birth card's
#70148 takes 'You' (#47521) as its {0}, so it reads `You just gave birth to a baby girl!`,
and the journal is the hero-mother line #24209 `I gave birth to {0} named {1}{2}.`

### The port

`Sim::conceptionTick` now runs a hero-as-mother branch before the lover's: a female hero
with a living male lover, off birth control, between 13 and 55, draws her fertility once
(`heroFertility`, a 0-100 draw in the shape of `SimPerson+0xa4`) and rolls the same two
checks. A success sets `heroPregnant` and remembers the father's name.
`Sim::pregnancyTick` then makes her own `ShouldSufferMiscarriage` decision — her own age
band and her own three stats, since the carrying person really is the hero this time —
and queues the new `kPendingHeroMiscarriage` or `kPendingHeroBirth`.
`Sim::heroPregnancyYear`, `Sim::heroMiscarriageYear` and `Sim::heroBirthYear` are the
three cards, on the same literals: the father-aware and generic pregnancy bodies with
their journals, the two choices, the -6 decline with #48177, the hero-mother miscarriage
sentences with the -5 impact, and the birth with 'You' as the parent, #24209 as the
journal, and the children pushed with `isHeroes` true and the father as their other
parent. Multiples reuse the birth card's own rolls (REPORT 340).

### Ceilings

- Only the natural lane exists. The game's other creation paths — IVF, fertility
  treatment, a surrogate, the threesome paths and the Golden Pacifier override — are not
  modelled, so the Type 2/3 generic body (#47766) is reachable here only when the father
  has no name.
- The Golden Pacifier choice (#45179), its paywall and the `DoesUserHaveAccessToGoldenPacifier`
  branch are not offered; the IAP entitlement exists in the store table and nothing reads it.
- Fertility is a one-off draw rather than `Att_fertility`, the hero's birth-control flag
  stands in for the couple's, and the vampire exclusion is not modelled because the port's
  lover is not a person.
- The naming prompt is replaced by the game's own pool (REPORT 340's ceiling), so the
  children are named from `drawFirstName` with no repeats rather than by the player.
- The decline's flavour title list (#32116/#19874/#47091), the achievements
  (acMother25 #53411, acTriplets #53571, acParent100 #53454, acHaveChildren10 #53331), the
  zodiac and easter eggs, #47769 `You are the {0}{1} of {2}...` and the legal-guardian
  branch are not modelled.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_hero_pregnancy.py` walks twenty female lives with a partner and asserts,
for every hero pregnancy card, the father-aware body and the choice set; that a keep is
followed within the year by either the hero-mother birth body or the hero's own
miscarriage sentence; that every birth's journal matches #24209, adds exactly the twins or
triplets the body names, names each child distinctly, marks them `isHeroes` and gives them
the father as their other parent; that a decline moves happiness by the -6 step and logs
#48177; and that a male hero never sees the card.
Measured: `cards: 18 | keeps: 8 | declines: 10 | births: 8 | losses: 0` over seeds 1-20.

The full 130-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (ab581fa3..., 129 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: the break-up
announcement's guard looked only at the single event immediately before it, and a hero
pregnancy card can now drain in the same age-up, so that check walks back over the age's
own events instead. It was re-run green.

## 341. The friend's YouTube card

The relationship menu has its own cards, and one of them is watching a video with a
friend. The port has never had it: the friend families offer advice, pranks, rumours,
parties and a few darker cards, but no video.

### The native side

`ScenarioFriendYouTube` is a single-shot `Scenario` subclass (`.ctor` 0x37c1a0c,
`RefreshScenario` 0x37c1a80, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x37c1cf4, `_friend` at +0x170).
The constructor alone writes the title 'YouTube' (#50104) into +0x38 and sets
HasDismissButton (+0x28); `RefreshScenario` writes no title.

It is not a random push. The card is one item of the relationship menu built by
`LifeInterface::RelationshipItemArrayForFriend` (0x30e021c): the item is offered when
the hero is at least six (`hero.Age` +0x20 against 6 at 0x30e1c04/0x30e1c08) and the
friend `LivesInSamePlaceAsHero` (0x2c4cb28 at 0x30e1c1c). There is no cooldown and no
relationship-status condition on the menu item; the item's title is 'Watch YouTube'
(#46029) and its label 'Watch YouTube with {0}' (#46031) over the friend's object
pronoun.

`RefreshScenario` writes only the body, a dropdown and a choice:

- the body is #46030 `Watch YouTube with your {0}, {1}, today!` with {0} the friend
  relationship string (`FriendRelationshipStatusString` 0x2c4769c: 'friend' #59280,
  'best friend' #54905, 'enemy' #58371) and {1} the friend's first name;
- the dropdown (+0xc8) is one `ScenarioDropDown` titled 'Pick your channel' (#33846)
  whose contents are up to five distinct channel names (the loop at 0x37c1b88-0x37c1bfc
  re-draws while the name is already in the list) with default index 0;
- the choice array holds one choice, green-styled, labelled 'Watch it with {him/her}'
  (#46046).

`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` discards its choice index: the selection it acts on is the
dropdown's `get_Item(0)` (0x37c1e94), resolved to a row through
`DataHub::GetYouTubeChannel` (0x282f534). The accept is a threshold, not a roll: the
friend's `GetTotalHeroRelationshipStrength` (0x2c3884c) above 20.0 (fcmp at 0x37c1f34,
b.le at 0x37c1f3c) accepts, and so does any channel whose EnjoymentScore is 5
(0x37c1f4c/0x37c1f50); everything else refuses.

On the accept:

- the game logs #25746 `I watched {0} on YouTube with my {1}, {2}.` with the channel, the
  relationship string and the first name;
- the impacts are guarded by a per-friend stamp: `friend+0x15c
  HeroAgeAtLastWatchedYouTube` against the hero's age (0x37c20a4-0x37c20b0) — when they
  are equal only the log happens. Otherwise the stamp is written and the friend gains +4
  when the channel's EnjoymentScore is 5 and +2 otherwise (csel at 0x37c20d4 into the
  person's vtable slot +0x508), and the hero gains one happiness point (vtable +0x408);
- two enjoyment bars are rolled: 70 + `GetRandomNumber(0,31)` each
  (0x37c1fc0/0x37c1fd4), except that an enemy friend (FriendStatus 3) stays on 0..30,
  and a 1-in-6 roll (0x37c2038) together with a channel whose EnjoymentScore is at most 4
  re-rolls both bars over 0..100 (0x37c2068/0x37c207c);
- a follow-up `Scenario` is chained at +0x128 whose title is drawn from the channel
  presenter's own gender list — male "He's great!" #22747, 'His editing is clean' #22985,
  "Man's a legend" #29643, "That's my guy" #41418, 'I need his merch' #24699; female
  "She's great!" #38866, 'Love her style' #29247, "She's hilarious" #38867, 'She has a
  stan in me' #38853, 'I need her merch' #24698 — and whose body is #47624 `You and your
  {0}, {1}, watched {2} together on YouTube.`, with two bar graphs ('Your Enjoyment'
  #50126 and '{His/Her} Enjoyment' #69502) and the reused hookup sound
  (a16_sndHookupMale.aiff #52901 for a male hero, the female file #52900 otherwise);
- two channel hooks ride the accept: 'Jacksepticeye' (#27880) sets the challenge byte
  `Apollo16ChallengeTracker+0x28` and 'Bijuu Mike' (#13477) grants the achievement
  'acBijuuMike' (#53220).

The refusal moves the hero's happiness down 2 (vtable +0x408 with -2), logs #30994 `My
{0}, {1}, refused to watch {2} with me on YouTube.` and chains a follow-up titled
'Seriously?' (#38651) whose body is #50758 `Your {0}, {1}, refused to watch {2} with you
on YouTube.` Both branches end on `LifeLog::Log` and a UI refresh.

The channels themselves are `a16_youtube-channels-enc` (63 rows: Channel, Commonness
Score, Enjoyment Score 2..5, Gender), loaded by `DataHub::LoadYouTubeChannelSet`
(0x26f7250) into DataHub+0x580 and read back by `GetRandomYouTubeChannel` (0x282f0c0,
the dropdown draw) and `GetYouTubeChannel` (0x282f534, the by-name lookup). The card
never touches the table itself.

### The port

`Sim::friendYouTubeYear` takes the shape of the other friend cards. The menu does not
exist, so the friend family offers the card itself on `ytRng_` with one wheel ticket and
a 6% coin; the gate the game states is kept (six and up, and not in prison), and the
friend is a `<friend>` draw plus a coin for the pronoun. The channel is drawn uniformly
from the table's 63 rows, the friend's relationship strength — which the port has
nowhere to store — is drawn on the same stream, and the accept applies when that
strength is over 20 or the channel's EnjoymentScore is 5. The body, the one choice, the
two journals and the follow-up bodies are the literals above; the accept moves happiness
up one point through the port's impact conversion and the refusal down two.

### Ceilings

- The port has no relationship menu, so the card fires from the friend family on a coin
  instead of being offered per friend; and it has no friend entities, so the name and
  gender are drawn, the relationship string is always 'friend', the +2/+4 friendship move
  has nowhere to land, and the per-friend `HeroAgeAtLastWatchedYouTube` stamp is replaced
  by the family's once-a-year cadence.
- The dropdown became a uniform row draw: the five-name dedupe, the stored pick order and
  the default index are not modelled, and `GetRandomYouTubeChannel`'s CommonnessScore
  weighting is not decoded, so the draw is uniform over the 63 rows.
- The card's own HasDismissButton lane (closing the card without choosing) is not
  modelled; the port's single option is the green choice.
- The two enjoyment bar graphs, the follow-up card's own title, the reused hookup sound,
  the 'acBijuuMike' achievement and the Jacksepticeye challenge byte are not modelled:
  the follow-up is folded into this card's body as a title line and a body line, the way
  the magazine shoot folds its follow-up (REPORT 335).
- 'best friend' and 'enemy' never appear because the port's drawn friend carries no
  status, so the enemy branch of the bar roll is unreachable here.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_friend_youtube.py` walks forty funded lives with the card enabled,
resolves every card's `row` back to the channel table and asserts the body's three parts
against that row (the card's own body, the quip from the gender list the channel's Gender
column names, and the follow-up body naming the friend and the channel), the choice
label, the journal shape with the channel and the friend's name, the happiness delta (+4
on the accept and -8 on the refusal, both through the port's impact conversion), one card
per age, no residue, and that a five-year-old never sees the card.
Measured: `cards: 71 | accepts: 49 | refuses: 22` over seeds 1-40.

The full 129-test suite passed on the binary these notes describe (e982b98e..., 129 PASS /
0 FAIL), the new test included.
## 340. Twins and triplets

The birth card has always been able to deliver more than one child. The port
delivered one.

### The native side

`PersonGenerator::GenerateHeroChildArrayInPlaceWithParentsAndGeneration`
(0x337bed0, 0x638 bytes) builds the whole batch in `ScenarioBirth::RefreshScenario`
rather than in a choice handler:

- the multiples roll at 0x337c1c8 is `GetRandomNumber(0, denominator)` with the
  denominator 50 for an ordinary pregnancy and 8 when the pregnancy is a donor or
  surrogate one (mother "Anonymous", father "Donor"); a zero means more than one
  child, anything else means the single-child path;
- a second roll at 0x337c1f4 is `GetRandomNumber(0, 10)` and the class materialises
  three children when it lands on zero, two otherwise (`cinc` on the compare);
- the loop at 0x337c310 takes the count, so a multiple birth is 2 or 3 children and
  never more;
- gender is decided once, in `GenerateChildInPlaceWithParentsAndGeneration`
  (0x337adcc): a gender argument of 2 draws `GetRandomNumber(0,2)` and stores the
  result, and the twin copy at 0x337c3a8 writes the same `Gender` and
  `GenderAtBirth` into every extra child, so a multiple birth is all boys or all
  girls;
- each extra child copies the first child's inherited stats (0x337c3c8) and shares
  its emoji through `PersonEmojiScript::GetDuplicateEmojiScript` (0x337c388);
- `SimChild.Twins` (+0x1fc) is written on every child as the number of siblings the
  birth produced (0x337c34c for the first child, 0x337c378 for the rest), so one
  value describes the whole batch.

The card's two bodies follow: a single child gets #70148 `{0} just gave birth to a
baby {1}{2}!` and a multiple birth gets #70149 `{0} just gave birth to {1} {2}{3}!`
with `{1}` the twin or triplet word (#67315 / #67250) and `{2}` "boys" or "girls"
(#55180 / #59794). The naming widgets differ too -- 'Select name' #38475 against
'Select names' #38476 -- and the multiple-birth naming rows label each child with
#69434 `{0} #{1}`.

### The port

`Sim::birthYear` now runs both rolls on its own `birthRng_` stream (so the extra
draws cannot shift any other card's sequence), shares the single gender draw across
the batch, and pushes every child with `twins = kids - 1`. The port has no text
entry, so the naming prompt is still replaced by the game's own name pool, but a
multiple birth draws a fresh name per child and re-draws on a collision, the way the
game's prompt does; the journal names every child and the body uses the multiple
form. `script.cpp` exposes the new field so the test can see it.

### Ceilings

- The donor/surrogate denominator of 8 never applies: the port has no surrogate or
  anonymous-donor pregnancy, so every pregnancy rolls against 50.
- The port draws names from `drawFirstName` instead of the game's name prompt, and
  it does not apply the game's same-first-letter rule
  (`GetRandomFirstNameForGenderAndTryToStartWithSameLetterAsName`) to the later
  children.
- The inherited-stat copy and the shared emoji are not modelled: the port's children
  carry no stats or art.
- `SimChild.Twins` is written and exported but no port card reads it yet; the
  'Twins'/'Triplets' labels on the game's own family screen (#44280 / #44030) are
  not modelled either.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_birth_multiples.py` walks 120 funded lives with partners and asserts,
for every multiple birth it finds, that the body uses the twin/triplet form with the
right plural, that the child array gains exactly two or three children at that age
with the same gender, distinct names, the right `twins` count and the right other
parent, and that the journal names the birth and every child; singles keep their own
body. Measured: `births: 92 | singles: 90 | multiples: 2 | triplets: 0` over the
120 lives (each birth rolls 1-in-50, so the sample is thin by construction: the
run does reach the multiple path, but a triplet birth is rarer still).

The full 128-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (d9811a72..., 127 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: the birth regex
in test_pregnancy only matched the single-child body, so a multiple birth never cleared the
one-at-a-time flag that walk keeps and the next pregnancy card tripped its assertion; the
regex now matches both bodies (re-run: 75 pregnancy cards, 42 births).
## 339. The HR investigation

The workplace cards have an escalation behind them. When the hero attacks the
supervisor or succeeds in seducing them, the game pushes
`ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineHR`: a card with no choices, no dropdown, no table and
no eligibility test, that decides while it is being built whether the hero keeps
the job.

### The native side

`ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineHR` keeps a reason string, the seriousness its caller
passed, and the narrative it will log: `_reasonString +0x170`, `_seriousness
+0x178`, `_narrative +0x180`. Its class block has exactly three methods --
`.ctor(String,Int32) 0x298d34c` (0x74 bytes), `RefreshScenario 0x299ba04` (0x820
bytes) and `DismissSelected 0x299c224` (0x6c bytes, tail-calling `LifeLog::Log`
with the narrative). There is no `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` and no
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush`: nothing in the game rolls this card up on its
own, it only ever arrives pushed.

`RefreshScenario` builds the title from an `ArrayList` and takes one with
`PickRandomFromStringArray 0x2e16608`. The military pool is four lines -- #30662
`Must tread lightly`, #32756 `On thin ice`, #13345 `Being watched`, #44708 `Under
the microscope` -- and the civilian pool five -- #35312 `Really? HR?`, #46879
`Who's the narc`, #10265 `A whole investigation?`, #27761 `It's not that serious`,
#42939 `These people are so touchy`. So "On thin ice" is nothing more than one of
this card's titles; it is not the name of an escalation card of its own.

The body and the narrative are the caller's reason literal with its
`<your/my>` token rewritten -- `String::Replace(_reasonString, #9866 '<your/my>',
#68371 'your')` for the body at 0x299bc50 and `#62676 'my'` for the narrative at
0x299bdd0 -- then wrapped by `Format` with the class's own template: military #50274
`Your chain of command has formally reprimanded you for {0}!` and #25711 `I was
reprimanded by my chain of command for {0}!`; civilian #22392 `HR has launched an
investigation into you for {0}!` and #22394 `HR investigated me for {0}!`. The body
is stored at `+0x48` and the narrative at `+0x180`. No bracket parser, no table.

Then the arithmetic. Every path adds the seriousness to the workplace's trouble
points (`SimWorkplace+0x24 TroublePoints += _seriousness`, 0x299be1c). The score is
`int(strictness * multiplier + TroublePoints * (military ? 10 : 5))`, where
strictness is the workplace's `ManagementStrictness` (`SimWorkplace+0x14`) and the
multiplier comes from the seriousness: 0.25, 0.5, 1.1, 1.0 and 204 (the last two
constants live at 0xfaaa44 and 0xfaf714). The hero is let go when
`score >= 26 && rand(0,200) < score` -- the `cmp w20,#0x1a` at 0x299c038 and
`GetRandomNumber(0,200)` at 0x299c064. Because the multipliers are small and trouble
points only ever grow, a serious incident early in a career is a reprimand and the
same incident later is a dismissal.

Termination does not happen here: the card chains `ScenarioJobTermination(8)`
(0x387dc8c) behind the Golden Resume guard at `GameVars+0x1c8`, or
`ScenarioMilitaryTermination(occupation, 8)` (0x39b313c) in the military, through
`Scenario+0x128`. When the hero survives, the card calls
`ImpactWorkplacePerformance(-_seriousness)` (0x2b4f9d8) and one unnamed person
method through vtable slot `+0x408` with `-min(_seriousness,3)` (0x299c184). Every
path, dismissal or not, bumps `Apollo16ChallengeTracker+0x40 <NumTimesReportedToHR>`
(the shared tail at 0x299c1c0).

The constructor has exactly fourteen call sites, each a workplace card passing its
own reason and seriousness: gift 1 #67281 `trying to give <your/my> {0} {1}`;
hookup 4 #62079 `making an unwanted sexual advance toward {0}`; instigate 2 #66088
`started an untrue rumor about your {0}, {1}`; insult 2 #55438 `calling <your/my>
{0} {1}`; spend-time 2 #54552 `attempting to fraternize with an {0}`; supervisor
seduction 4 #67282 `trying to seduce <your/my> {0}`; reported-to-HR 1 #62083
`making too many complaints`; annoying, inappropriate, prank and rumor 4 #54549
`attacking {0}`; the unprofessional supervisor 5 #54546 `attacking <your/my> {0}`;
the dealer's item card with dynamic arguments; and friend recruit 2 #54552.

### The port

`Sim::hrDisciplineYear` is a pending card, `kPendingHrDiscipline`, opened by the two
workplace lanes the port already models:

- the unprofessional supervisor's attack lane (`Sim::supervisorYear`, the `pick == 0`
  branch) passes `attacking <your/my> supervisor` with seriousness 5, which is the
  native #54546 row;
- the successful supervisor seduction (`Sim::seduceYear`) passes
  `trying to seduce <your/my> supervisor` with seriousness 4, the native #67282 row.

The card rewrites the token itself -- `your` in the body, `my` in the journal --
takes its title from the military or civilian pool on `hrRng_`, adds the seriousness
to `h.troublePoints`, computes the score the native card computes, and folds the
termination into the same year the way REPORT.en.md 325 does: the #48756 or #48660
sentence is appended to the body and the hero loses the job (or the branch) with the
same six-point happiness hit.

### Corrections to 325

The termination sentence was wrong there. #48756 is `You have been let go from your
position as {1} for {2} for disciplinary issues.`, and `{2}` is the *reason row's own
label* (`Disciplinary Issues`, #17783) rather than the employer -- so the old port
text printed an empty slot (`... as Pornographer for  for disciplinary issues.`), and
on a hero with no employer it printed two spaces. The port now states the reason
once, `... as Pornographer for disciplinary issues.`, and the journal line keeps the
same fold: `I was let go from my job as Pornographer for disciplinary issues.` (#25739
has the same slot). The military sentence #48660 is unchanged.

### Ceilings

- Only two of the fourteen creation sites exist in the port, because only two of the
  workplace cards that call the constructor exist. The eight coworker incident cards,
  the gift and the fraternization cards are not modelled, so their reasons never
  reach this card.
- The workplace keeps no `TroublePoints` and no `ManagementStrictness` object in the
  port. `h.troublePoints` accumulates the seriousness faithfully, but the strictness
  the score reads is drawn once per hero over 0..100 and stands in (`shortcut`).
- `ImpactWorkplacePerformance(-seriousness)` and the unnamed vtable `+0x408` method
  have no counterpart in the port, so a reprimand moves no stat; only the dismissal
  lane has its own effect (the six-point happiness hit).
- The dismissal is resolved inside this card rather than by chaining a termination
  card, and only the #48756/#48660 bodies are reproduced; the job-termination card's
  own buttons and follow-up cards are not.
- The `<your/my>` reason is the port's own composition of the native tokens: the
  native `{0}` argument of #54546 and #67282 is a role word the port renders as
  "supervisor" directly.
- `NumTimesReportedToHR` is counted (`h.timesReportedToHR`) but no port card reads it.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_hr_discipline.py` walks forty funded lives and asserts that every
investigation card follows an attack or a seduction by at most one year, that the
card offers no choice, that its title belongs to the right pool, that the body and
journal match the military or civilian template with `your` and `my`, that a
dismissal body ends `for disciplinary issues.` and moves happiness by -6, and that a
reprimand moves nothing; the measured run reports `cards: 5 | reprimands: 2 |
firings: 3`, four civilian titles over `attacking your supervisor` and `trying to
seduce your supervisor`, and a separate thirty-life military sweep reaches the
military pool (`military sweep: 1`). A life that ends at seventeen never sees the
card.

The full 127-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (36518dac..., 125 PASS /
2 FAIL). Both failures are probe-side skew rather than behaviour: test_funeral and
test_witch_doctor each compile a small C++ probe against `port/include` and link the
port library, and at the time of the run the tree carried the next section's header
fields that the library had not been built with, so the two probes died on SIGABRT and
SIGSEGV. Stashing that work, rebuilding reproduced this exact binary byte for byte
(36518dac...), and both were re-run green on it (funeral: planning 58, cremations 7,
ashes 7; witch doctor: 30 remedy rows, 79 cures), so the section's own tree is
127 of 127.

## 338. The pregnancy card and the miscarriage

A pregnancy in this game is not a stat: it is a SimPregnancy object on the mother, and it is
played out over three beats. The conception roll happens on the hero's own yearly tick, the
card asks about it, and only on the *next* age-up does the game decide whether the baby
survives. The port had the last beat (REPORT.en.md 151) behind a shortcut coin and no card
before it. This section takes the roll, the card and the loss.

### The native side

The roll is `SimPregnancy::GetResultingPregnancyForMotherAndFatherAndTypeAndAssignToMother`
(vaddr `0x2b3a438`). Its two gates are the mother's age and her fertility: the age
probability comes from `GetNaturalConceptionAgeProbability` (`0x2b3a730`), whose table is
read straight out of `.rodata` -- 0% under 13, 45% for 13-17, 70% for 18-34, then 40%, 20%,
6% and 3% for the next four bands, and 0% from 55. `HasBasePregnancyEligibility`
(`0x2b3a604`) adds the rest: the mother is female, the father is not, the mother is 13 to 55,
she is not already pregnant (`SimPerson+0x48` is null), she is not on birth control
(`+0x50`), and neither parent is a vampire. The arithmetic itself is two draws:
`GetRandomNumber(0,100)` against the age percentage, then `GetRandomNumber(0,120)` against
the mother's `Att_fertility` (`+0xa4`). Any of the fifteen creation sites may call it, and
the hero's own lover pair is one of them, on `SimHero::IncrementAge`.

`ScenarioPregnancy` (`RefreshScenario 0x2573b04`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x2574344`) sets
only three fields: the body, the journal and the choice array. The body is a sentence chosen
by the pregnancy's relation flags -- `You are pregnant!` (`#47766`) for the hero-mother and
the mother-type ids 2 and 3, `Your {0}, {1}, is pregnant with your baby!` (`#50740`) when the
mother is the current lover, `... is pregnant with someone else's baby!` (`#50739`) when she
is not the father's, and `You are pregnant with your {0}, {1}, baby!` (`#47765`) for a
hero-mother whose partner is the father. The sentence goes into the standard wrapper
`{0}\n\nWhat will you do?` (`#68715`). The journal is the matching first-person line -- for
the lover-mother branch `{0} became pregnant with my baby!` (`#69869`) -- and the choice
array is stored in construction order: `Keep the baby` (`#28214`), `Don't keep the baby`
(`#18038`), and only when the pregnancy type is 1 and a monetization flag is set, `Use the
Golden Pacifier` (`#45179`). Nothing is randomized.

The classifier lowercases the chosen label and looks for `don't`; everything else that does
not contain `pacifier` is the keep lane. The decline clears the pregnancy object on both
parents, fires an unnamed `-6` impact through the person vtable slot `+0x508`, and logs one
of four lines: `You chose not to keep the baby!` (`#48177`) or `We chose not to keep the
baby!` (`#46097`), each with a `{0} ` prefix variant (`#69542` / `#69716`). The pacifier
lane is a paywall: without the entitlement the game opens
`ScenarioMiniPaywall(Scenario_Pregnancy)` (`#38206`) and rebuilds the card; with it, the card
logs `{0} insisted on keeping the baby!` (`#70059`) under the follow-up title `Overruled`
(`#33103`).

On the next age-up the game calls the virtual `ShouldSufferMiscarriage`
(`SimPerson::ShouldSufferMiscarriage`, vaddr `0x2c47514`) -- which is why no direct BL
reaches it -- and pushes `ScenarioMiscarriage` (`0x2a6378c`) when it answers true,
`ScenarioBirth` (`0x2a637b8`) when it answers false. The two are mutually exclusive and the
miscarriage is tested first. The base rate comes from the mother's age: 15% under 18, 7% up
to 29, 8% up to 34, and `3*age-105+8` percent from 35 on (23% at 40, 53% at 50). Her stat
average multiplies it -- doubling below 20, `x1.5` below 40, `x0.75` below 80, `x0.5` above
it -- and `GetRandomNumber(0,101)` is compared against the product. The Golden Pacifier is
consulted here too: with it, the answer is forced to false.

`ScenarioMiscarriage` (`RefreshScenario 0x25730a8`, `DismissSelected 0x25739c0`) has no
choice override at all: it is a dismiss-only card, and its effects fire in the refresh. The
title is `Miscarriage` (`#30203`) with the exterior `Baby` (`#12664`), and the sentence
family follows the same relation split as the pregnancy card: `You suffered a {0} miscarriage
and lost the baby!` (`#49447`) for the hero-mother and `Your {0}, {1}, suffered a {2}
miscarriage and lost the baby!` (`#50784`) for the lover-mother. The `{2}` slot is a
descriptor: `first-trimester` (`#58959`) or `second-trimester` (`#65123`) on a 1-in-4 draw,
and a further 1-in-21 replaces it with `blighted ovum` (`#55036`). One draw in ten takes the
rare branch instead: the title becomes `Pregnancy Loss` (`#34482`) and the sentence names a
typed loss drawn from `ectopic pregnancy` (`#58054`), `molar pregnancy` (`#62496`),
`stillbirth` (`#66149`) or `chemical pregnancy` (`#55704`), with the indefinite article
added and the body `... had {0} and lost the baby!` (`#50683`). The father who is the current
lover takes a `-2` impact, and the mother's fertility is multiplied by `0.8`.

### The port

`src/fam/birth.cpp` now plays the whole chain instead of one coin. `Sim::conceptionTick` runs
on the yearly tick: an adult hero with a partner of 13 to 55, no pregnancy in flight and no
birth control is rolled on `loverRng_` -- the age percentage first, then the partner's
fertility, which is drawn once as `0..100` and stored on the hero because the port's partner
has no person model. On success it pushes `kPendingPregnancy`. `Sim::pregnancyYear` renders
the card: title `Pregnancy` (`#34481`), the lover-mother sentence with the port's own
relationship word (girlfriend, boyfriend, fiancee, fiance, wife, husband), the wrapper, the
journal and the two buttons. `Sim::pregnancyTick`, which runs *before* the conception tick,
applies the recovered miscarriage arithmetic on the next age-up and queues either
`kPendingMiscarriage` or `kPendingBirth`; the pregnancy itself stays in flight until that
card drains, because the native object lives until the birth card is built and a second
conception behind a queued card would misread whose child was born. `Sim::miscarriageYear`
renders the dismiss-only card with both the trimester and the rare typed-loss branch;
`Sim::birthYear` is the arrival from REPORT.en.md 151, now reached as a pending card rather
than a family of its own, and its old 1-in-12 coin is gone.

The decline lane costs the hundred-point step of the impact scale, which is what `-6` maps
to, and appends `We chose not to keep the baby!` to the year's log.

### Ceilings

The mother is always the partner: the hero-mother lane needs the port's own pregnancy state,
its journals and its birth card, none of which exist here, so the conception tick only runs
for a male hero with a female partner. The partner's fertility, her stats (for the
miscarriage multiplier) and her birth-control flag are not modelled, so her fertility is
drawn once at 0-100, the hero's stat average stands in for hers, and the hero's
`onBirthControl` stands for the couple's. The Golden Pacifier is left out of the card: its
gate reads a monetization flag through `GameState`, which the simulation does not hold.
Multiples are not modelled: the native birth card rolls a denominator of 50 (8 for donor or
surrogate pregnancies) for twins and triplets, and the port always delivers one child. The
naming dialogue is a pair of dropdowns fed by the country's name arrays; the port names the
child from its own pool instead, which is the same shortcut REPORT.en.md 151 already
recorded. The five `GetRandomNumber` calls the native classifier makes below the labels, the
`Life::GetAllChildrenWithLoverAndMustBeNatural` filter and the relationship-strength
arithmetic are not reproduced, and neither are the achievements the three cards award.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_pregnancy.py` walks sixty fifty-age lives on the binary these notes describe.
It measures 81 pregnancy cards (43 kept, 38 declined), 37 births, 4 miscarriages and no rare
typed loss -- that branch is implemented but the sweep did not draw it. Every card body
matches `Your <word>, <name>, is pregnant with your baby!\n\nWhat will you do?`, its journal
is the same partner's name in `{0} became pregnant with my baby!`, and no card carries a
pacifier option. A kept card moves no stat; a declined card moves exactly the hundred
happiness points and logs `We chose not to keep the baby!`. The test walks each life as a
state machine: a kept card opens a pregnancy, no second card may open while one is open, and
every birth body and every miscarriage (with its trimester sentence and matching
first-person line) closes the one that is. No card fires below eighteen, and a hero with no
partner conceives nothing.

The full 126-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (fe46c41e..., 125 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: the wheel has
turned wider as the newer families joined, so an ambush elopement card is rarer per life and
test_lover_elope now sweeps sixty seeds instead of twenty (re-run: 16 wedding plans and 6
elopements over seeds 1-60).

## 337. The hero's own attack

Every card in these notes so far has had somebody else do something to the hero. This
one is the other direction: `ScenarioCustomAttack` (`_re/il2cpp_dump.txt:41714`) is the
card the relationship menus open when the player picks Attack on a person, and it is
the same class the supervisor's "Attack" button chains into and the one a vampire
hunter shows when they come for the hero.

### The native side
- `RefreshScenario 0x3841f64`: exterior title #16174 'Conflict', title #12341
  'Attack'. The card carries two drop-downs, "Pick your target" (#33947) over the
  people the hero actually has and "Pick your move" (#33897) over the moves and
  weapons available to them; the rows are formatted #69467 '{0} ({1})' and #69459
  '{0} (Weapon)'. There is exactly one button, "Attack {0}" (#12347) with the object
  pronoun, and the card dispatches on the two drop-down selections, not on the label.
- Nineteen constructor overloads carry the target: parent, sibling, lover, child,
  friend, troll, communard, street person, vampire, fight-club fighter, supervisor,
  generic `SimPerson` and a handful more. The class also holds the target's gender
  (+0x16c), whether they can fight back (+0x170), whether the hero can get busted
  (+0x1fa) and the four name strings the card and the obituary use (+0x1d0 to
  +0x1f0).
- The button's tail is short. `SimPerson::ImpactKarma(-5)` at 0x3846cc0,
  `ImpactDiscipline(-5)` at 0x3846ce4, then the target's attitude down two through a
  vtable slot, then the sentence: `DataHub::GetRandomColorAssault` at 0x3846d44 draws
  a row of `a16_assaults-enc` with the `Clean` filter on, and its Outbound Scenario
  column (+0x18) is printed with the inline token pairs replaced for the hero and for
  the target's gender.
- What happens next depends on the target. `WillRelativeFightBack` at 0x3847d2c hands
  a relative or lover the port's own assault card (`ScenarioAttackInbound`, section
  113); `SimHero::GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType` at 0x384798c starts the crime chain
  when the attack can be reported; `HandleDeathOfRelative` at 0x3847704 runs when a
  family member is killed, and the achievement manager is told at 0x3847740.
- The table: `a16_assaults-enc`, header `Body Part, Outbound Scenario, Inbound
  Scenario, Clean`, 228 data rows. 217 carry a `Clean` outbound sentence; the other
  eleven are the impolite variants the content setting filters out. The tokens in the
  sentences are `<you/I>`, `<your/my>`, `<his/her>`, `<him/her>`, `<he/she>` and
  `<himself/herself>`: pairs of forms rather than dictionary tokens. The first of the
  pair is the card's own second person, the second is the journal's first person, and
  the possessive forms follow the victim's gender.

### The port
`Sim::customAttackYear` is its own family with its own stream (`atkRng_`, tickets 2)
because the native card has no yearly push: it opens from a menu the port has no UI
for. The family offers it when the hero is eighteen and out of prison, at most once
every three years, takes a target from the people the port actually keeps -- the
living family, the children, the partner and the workplace supervisor -- and then
draws one of the 209 usable sentences and renders the card:

- title Attack (#12341), body "How will you attack your big sister, Ali?" (#23258),
  one button "Attack her" (#12347);
- the journal is the same sentence in the first person, which is what the token pairs
  are for: "I tugged on her earlobes, bruising them badly!";
- karma and discipline both move five points down: -50 each.

### Ceilings
The port has no drop-downs, so the target and the sentence are drawn rather than
picked; the move list is the drop-down's own content, and the port draws the sentence
the card prints once a move has been chosen. Eight of the 217 clean rows are skipped
because their sentence carries the move list or a body part as an inline token
(`<a knee/an elbow strike/a headbutt/...>`), which belongs in the drop-down and not in
a sentence. The target's attitude (-2 through vtable +0x408) is not modelled because
the port keeps no relationship scale on a person, so the two stat impacts are the
whole effect. The fight-back counterattack, the crime chain, the target's death, the
achievement and the obituary are left out: each needs a subsystem the port does not
have yet, and section 113's inbound card only renders for the friend-weapon encounter
that queues it. The card also only fires at eighteen and up, while the native menus
allow it at any age where a target exists.

### Verified
Sixty attack cards over forty lives (seeds 1-40), each with a body of the shape "How
will you attack your ...?" and the button "Attack him" or "Attack her". The targets
the port offered: mother, father, big brother, little sister, little brother, nephew
and niece. Every journal line is a row of ~a16_assaults-enc~ with its tokens filled
("I ripped off her pointer finger!", "I give her a karate chop to the gullet, bruising
her larynx!") and no bracket token left behind, and every card moves karma and
discipline by fifty points down. Two cards are never closer than three years (the
shortest gap measured is 3). A seventeen-year-old never sees one even with every
choice forced, and forcing every choice across a seventy-year life yields eighteen
cards.

The full 125-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (3c0bd533..., 122 PASS /
3 FAIL). All three failures are test-side and were fixed here without a code change: the
family this section adds widened the wheel, so a funded life meets the aircraft's annual
repair check and the horse racing invite fewer times, and their thresholds now sweep more
lives (re-run: 41 repairs with 7 scraps, 64 invites with 5 wins); the witch doctor's probe
aborted on its first run and was green when re-run (30 remedy rows, 79 cures).

## 336. The book deal

A famous hero can pay a publisher to bring out a book, and the sales decide how it is
remembered. This section ports that deal — the offer the place builds, the fee that comes
out of the hero's book appeal, the proceeds roll, and the ten-step ladder that turns them
into one clause of the sales line.

### The native side

`SimBookOpportunity 0x2b109d4`: `+0x10 PublisherName`, `+0x18 Cost`,
`+0x20 BookTitle`, `+0x28 Proceeds`, `+0x2c HeroAge`. The ctor fills the cost, the
proceeds and the hero's age and leaves the title for the player to choose.
`HeroBookAppealScore 0x2b10bd8` is `0.25 * (ageBand + 2 * Att_fame + Att_intelligence)`,
with the age band 100 below 18, 30 below 25, then 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90 at the decade
marks and 0 from 60 up. `GetCostAmount 0x2b10a54` is
`20000 + (1 - appeal/100) * 80000` through
`DataCountry::GetLocalCostForAmountWithMinimumCostAndRoundTo(amount, 1000, 100)`.
`GetProceedsAmount 0x2b10b14` is `GetRandomNumber(0, (int)(2 * base * (1 + appeal/100)))`
with `base` 250000, or 500000 once the appeal reaches 70.

The place builds the offer in `RefreshAvailableFameOpportunities`, after the fame gate:
`Att_fame >= 10`, no more than four books in `SimFame.BookArray`, at least three years
since the last one, and only when the appeal beats `rand(0,100)`. The publisher is a random
company of the Publisher type and its name is formatted into the opportunity.

`ScenarioFameBook`: `.ctor 0x3735c60`, `RefreshScenario 0x3735cdc`,
`DismissSelected 0x37365cc`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x3736638`. Title `#13887 'Book'`,
body `Format(#69989 '{0} has agreed to edit and publish your book.', publisher)`, a
drop-down of five biography titles drawn from `a16_biographies-enc` (its
`<hero-name>`-style tokens parsed before they reach the list), and one button
`#47246 'Write it'`. Accepting takes the drop-down's title, pays the cost, credits the
proceeds, appends the book to the fame array, clears the place's offer slot and logs
`#24772 'I paid {0} to {1} to publish my book, "{2}". It {3} and grossed {4} in sales.'`
with the outcome clause from `OutcomeString 0x2b10cdc`: proceeds against cost in ten
steps — over 800000 overnight bestseller, over 3x bestseller, over 2x commercial success,
over 1.5x well-received, over 1x mixed reviews, over 0.9x poor reviews, over 0.7x not
well-received, over 0.5x commercial failure, over 0.25x terrible reviews, else absolute
flop. The follow-up card's title is one of `#23143 'Hot off the press'`,
`#20425 'Flying off the shelves'` and `#32803 'One for the book'` over the body
`#50244 'Your book, "{0}", {1}.'`. Dismissing logs
`#69994 '{0} has agreed to publish my book for {1}.'`, which is the literal the card
carries as its narrative.

### The port

`Sim::bookOpportunityYear` runs the same gates on the hero's own yearly tick (fame at
least 10, at most four books, three years since the last, and `appeal > rand(0,100)`),
draws the publisher through the port's own `companyName("Publisher")`, fixes the cost and
rolls the proceeds, and queues `kPendingBookOffer`; `Sim::fameBookYear` renders the card
