and answers it. Titles come from `a16_biographies-enc` filtered by the hero's gender and
resolved through the port's bracket parser. The book's own stream is `pubRng_` — the name
`bookRng_` already belonged to the reading card over `a16_books-enc`.

### Ceilings

The five-title drop-down is a random draw from those five instead of the player's choice, so
the card cannot be steered. The two vtable impacts the accept lane makes (one on the
proceeds and one on the cost side) are unnamed in the source and their amounts are
unrecovered, so the port records the money and the sales line without a stat move — a
ceiling, not an omission of recovered behaviour. The dismissal's narrative literal is
carried verbatim even though it reads like an acceptance. The place's offer slot, the
cult/politician/royal side cards, the obituary line, the Apollo16 flags and the achievements
are not modelled, and neither is the book's own shelf beyond the count the gates read.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_fame_book.py` over 30 famous lives (seeds 1-30): 277 offers, 128 accepted,
149 refused and 7 distinct outcome clauses. Every offer names one publisher twice and quotes
a fee that is a multiple of 100 and at least 1000 and that pins an appeal inside 0-100; every
acceptance pays exactly the quoted fee, quotes the same publisher, grosses a figure inside
the proceeds ceiling the fee implies, and its outcome clause appears in both the log and the
card body; every refusal repeats the fee and the publisher. A hero with no fame is never
offered a deal, and the biography titles reach the log parsed, with no leftover token.

The full 124-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (ad014e34..., 123 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: test_crashout
asserted at least two crashout cards over thirty famous lives, and the family this section
adds widened the wheel enough to leave one; the test now walks sixty seeds (re-run: 2 cards).
## 335. The magazine photo shoot

A famous hero is offered a magazine shoot: a title from `a16_magazines-enc`, a pose the
magazine wants, and a fee the pose and the hero's appeal decide. This section ports that
offer and the shoot's outcome.

### The native side

The offer is not a random push — it is furniture on the hero's place of residence.
`SimPlace::RefreshAvailableFameOpportunities 0x2a431d4` runs on the yearly refresh (the only
gate is the age-equality check against `SimPlace+0x60 AgeAtLastFameOpportunityRefresh`, with
no numeric cooldown), clears the previous commercial offer, and rebuilds the magazine
opportunity into `place+0x220`. `LifeInterface::GetT4List 0x30f850c` turns a non-null
opportunity into a list item once the hero is 18 and out of prison.

The appeal is the hero's fame, adjusted: appearance above 90 makes it
`(fame + 200) / 3`, above 70 `(fame + 100) * 0.5`, and it is cut to a third for each of a
criminal record in the place, karma under 10 and appearance under 30. The pose ladder then
runs: fame over 80 asks for a topless shoot (pose 3) and falls back to swimsuit (pose 2) when
`appeal > 80`; fame at or under 80 rolls twice, swimsuit first and then clothed (pose 1).
Poses 4 (nude) and 5 (centerfold) have decodable strings but no producer — nothing assigns
them in this build.

`SimMagazineOpportunity::GetPaymentAmount 0x2b29464` reads a per-pose `{A, B}` pair —
15000/100000, 50000/150000, 50000/250000, 250000/1000000, 750000/2500000 — quarters both ends
for a male hero, cuts `B` to a third under appeal 70 and halves it under 90, then moves along
the line `A + (B - A) * appeal / 100` and rounds it through
`DataCountry::GetLocalCostForAmountWithMinimumCostAndRoundTo(amount, 1000, 100)`.

`ScenarioFameMagazine`: `.ctor 0x373c358`, `RefreshScenario 0x373c414`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x373c864`. Title `#29487 'Magazine'`, body
`Format(#70159 '{0} magazine has offered you a deal to appear {1} in its {2} issue.\n\nWhat
will you do?', title, AppearAsString, month)`, with the appearance strings `#55827 'clothed'`,
`#60870 'in a swimsuit'`, `#67124 'topless'`, `#63041 'nude'`, `#54422 'as the nude
centerfold'`. The month comes from `_monthNI`, bumped by `rand(0,4)` on every refresh and
read through a twelve-entry table of month names. The two buttons are stored `#23729 "I can't
do that"` then `#39046 'Sign me up'`, and the accept lane is the one whose label contains
`sign`.

Accepting credits the fee, rolls a `SuccessScore` (`rand(0,101)` one time in four, otherwise
`rand(0,61)+40`), makes one virtual stat call with 4, 3 or 2 by the score against 91 and 51,
costs `ImpactDiscipline(-2)` and `ImpactKarma(-2)`, logs
`#24080 'I earned {0} by appearing {1} in the {2} issue of {3} magazine.'` and opens a
follow-up card titled from the pose's own three-line headline pool over the body
`#48418 'You earned {0} by appearing {1} in the {2} issue of {3} magazine.'`. Refusing costs
`ImpactDiscipline(+4)` and logs
`#25508 'I turned down an opportunity to appear {0} in the {1} issue of {2} magazine.'`.

### The port

The port has no place object, so `Sim::magazineOpportunityYear` rebuilds the same opportunity
on the hero's own yearly tick — the appeal, the pose ladder, the row and the fee — and queues
it as `kPendingMagazineOffer`; `Sim::fameMagazineYear` renders the card and answers it.
`a16_magazines-enc` is 44 rows of `Title, Gender` (22 male, 22 female) and the row is drawn
uniformly from the hero's own half. Everything draws on one `magRng_`.

### Ceilings

The month counter starts at January and is not wrapped — the native index runs past the twelve
names and the body then quotes no month at all, which the port reproduces by leaving the cell
empty rather than inventing a rollover. Poses 4 and 5 are reachable in the port's ladder only
through the fame branch that returns 3, so their fee and appearance strings are carried but the
port never offers them; that mirrors the build's own single producer. The stat the virtual call
moves is read as fame (its name is unproven). The follow-up card is appended to the same year's
body because the port's age-up returns one card. The Reception bar graph, the obituary line for
a topless shoot and the `acPoseWank` achievement are not modelled, and the place's own
opportunity slot — so a coincidence of two offers, and the commercial and talk-show offers that
share the refresh — are not ported.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_fame_magazine.py` drives 30 famous lives (seeds 1-30) and 25 plainer ones at
fame 45: 471 cards, 294 accepted and 177 refused. Every card names a row of
`a16_magazines-enc` that carries the hero's own gender, quotes one of the three reachable
appearance strings and a month from the twelve-name table, and offers `I can't do that` /
`Sign me up`. A refusal costs discipline and moves nothing else; an acceptance credits exactly
the fee the log quotes (a multiple of 100, at least 1000, inside the pose's `A..B` band once
its worst-case penalties are applied), moves fame up and discipline and karma down by
`pointsForImpact(2)`, and appends the follow-up headline. The famous lives only ever see the
topless shoot, the fame-45 lives only the clothed and swimsuit ones, and no life is offered a
shoot at fame 0.
The full 123-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (c268c99f..., 122 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: test_paparazzi
asserted that a life started at fame 74 never sees the paparazzi card, but this section's
shoot pays fame, so a 74-fame life can cross the card's own fame >= 75 gate mid-life; the
test now tracks the running fame and asserts the card only appears once it is over the line
(re-run: 19 paparazzi cards, all three lanes, 5 of 10 lives at fame 75).

## 334. The aircraft's own life: wear, expenses, repairs and the scrapyard

The aircraft the hero buys in 222 was only ever a name in the port. In the native game it is
a `SimAircraft` object with its own age and condition, it costs money every year, it breaks
and it ends up scrapped; the repair card's price is not a table column but a formula over the
row's Cost. This section ports that object's whole life, so the aircraft the purchase card
sells behaves the way the game's does.

### The native side

`SimAircraft` fields: `+0x10 Age` (int), `+0x18 Condition` (float), `+0x1c YearsOwned`,
`+0x28 Loan`, `+0x30 AgeAtLastRepair` (an Age), `+0x40 ActiveRepair`,
`+0x48 NeedsToBeScrapped`, `+0x4c AgeAtLastMaintenance` (a game YEAR despite the name),
`+0x50 NumAnnualMaintenancesPerformed`.

`SimAircraft::.ctor 0x2b0f490` takes the row and a bool. The dealership passes true, and a row
whose `Min Age` is 0 comes out brand new (Age 0, Condition 100); every other combination rolls
`rand(0,3)` for one of three used-age modes — `MinAge + rand(0,5) + 1`,
`MinAge + rand(0,10) + 1`, or `MinAge + rand(0, LifespanYears - MinAge) + 1` — and then sets
Condition from the age tier: age 4 or less `61 + rand(0,40)`, 5 to 9 `20 + rand(0,81)`,
10 or more `1 + rand(0,100)`. AgeAtLastRepair and AgeAtLastMaintenance stay 0, so a fresh
aircraft cannot break for four years and its first maintenance-gap test is already satisfied.

`SimAircraft::MonthlyExpense 0x2b0fbc4` is `Cost / div` with the divisor picked by cost —
863 above 10M, 663 above 1M, 313 above 500k, 253 otherwise — floored at `500 * M`, where M is
the economy scale at `GameReference::Inst[+0xb8] -> [0] -> [+0x20] -> [+0x1d4]`.
`SimHero::IncrementAge` charges twelve of those per year through
`IncurAnnualLivingExpenses 0x2a75944`.

`SimAircraft::IncrementAge 0x2b0f7c4` ages it (Age, YearsOwned, the special feature's own
years) and then wears it: when `Age - NumAnnualMaintenancesPerformed` has reached
`LifespanYears` the Condition is multiplied by 0.9, otherwise it becomes
`100 * (1 - (Age - NumMaint)/Lifespan + 0.05 - rand(0,10)/100)`, whichever is lower, and it is
never clamped — so an aircraft near the end of its life can dip below zero and break more
often. The Golden Wrench pins Condition at 100 and skips the wear entirely.

`SimAircraft::IsRepairNeededAfterCheckForAnnualRepair 0x2b10284` has exactly one caller,
`SimHero::IncrementAge @0x2a6ca6c`, so the card is pushed once per aircraft per year. Gates
in order: the Golden Wrench means never; an aircraft at or past `1.25 * LifespanYears` whose
Condition is under 2.0, whose last maintenance is at least 2 years back and which carries no
loan sets NeedsToBeScrapped instead; an open ActiveRepair skips; and `Age - AgeAtLastRepair`
under 4 skips. Then the ladder gives the roll's ceiling by age against the lifespan — 100 past
it, 70 past 0.8 of it, 50 past 0.6, 25 past 0.4, 5 below — and the break happens when
`Condition + rand(0,20) < rand(0, max)`, the ladder roll drawn first. A break stamps
AgeAtLastRepair, picks a part and a broken term, and its cost is
`MonthlyExpense * {0.8, 2.0, 4.0, 7.0, 12.0}[PartCostScore - 1] * M`.

The part is uniform over `a16_aircraft-parts-enc` rows flagged for the aircraft's kind —
Helicopter, Jet or Propeller by the row's `Airplane Propulsion Type`, Glider, Blimp, Balloon;
an Airship, Seaplane or Hot Air Balloon row has no flag column and draws no break. The broken
term is a random element of the row's `Broken Terms`. `Only One Per Aircraft` is loaded and
never read.

`ScenarioAircraftRepair`: `.ctor 0x34202c8`, `RefreshScenario 0x3422dd8`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x34233c0`. Title is the make and model; the body is
`Format(#50577 'Your {0} has {1}.', GenericDescriptionString, AddIndefiniteArticle +
DescriptiveString)` wrapped by `Format(#68715 '{0}\n\nWhat will you do?', ...)`, and a
pushed card swaps in `Format(#50593 'Your {0} needs a repair.\n\n{1}', desc, random
OptionalDescriptions item)` when the part has any and `rand(0,3) <= 1`. The table dictionary
carries one row, key `#35747 'Repair'`, value the formatted cost. Buttons in stored order:
`#45180 'Use the Golden Wrench'` (an in-app purchase, so wrench owners only), `#35752
'Repair it'`, `#24668 'I might fix it later'`, dispatched by `Contains 'use'`,
`Contains 'later'` and otherwise paying. Paying debits the cost, clears ActiveRepair and logs
`#30911 'My {0} has {1}.'` followed by `#70735 '{0}I repaired the {1} on my {2}.'` with a
follow-up card whose title is one of four fixed lines and whose body is `#50579 'Your {0} is
back in service.'`; it touches no Condition and no repair counter. An unaffordable repair
opens `ScenarioInsufficientFinances`. Declining logs `#69029 '{0}\nI decided not to repair
it.'`, costs `ImpactDiscipline(-2)` only on a pushed card, and leaves the repair open — the
same aircraft never breaks again until it is fixed.

`ScenarioAircraftScrapPush`: `.ctor 0x3423fdc`, `RefreshScenario 0x3424070`,
`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x342424c`. Title make-and-model, body
`Format(#50617 'Your {0} will no longer fly and is beyond repair.', desc)` with a table row
`#10954 'Age'` / `Format(#69718 '{0} Years', Age)`, and one button `#38269 'Scrap it'`.
`SimAircraft::ScrapValue 0x2b0fcf4` is 0 at or below \$1,000,000; above it the value is
`Cost / 250,000,000 * 150,000 * M`, truncated to a multiple of 100 above 1000 and of 10 below.
A positive value is credited and logs `#50617` plus `#69322 '{0}\nThe scrapyard gave me {1}
for it.'` with a four-line follow-up title pool and the body `#42451 'The scrapyard gave you
{0} for it.'`; a zero value credits nothing and logs the body line alone. Both remove the
aircraft from the life.

### The port

`Hero` carries the object's state (`aircraftRow`, `aircraftAge`, `aircraftCondition`,
`aircraftAgeAtLastRepair`, `aircraftTickAge`, the open repair's part, term and cost, and the
two pending flags). `Sim::aircraftSetup` runs the ctor at purchase, `Sim::aircraftRunYear`
runs on the hero's own yearly tick — the same place the casino's and the zoo's books run —
and does the aging, the wear, the twelve months of MonthlyExpense, the scrap gate and the
break roll; `Sim::aircraftDescription` is GenericDescriptionString with the row's
Descriptive Name Override and Suffix. Breaks and scraps queue as `kPendingAircraftRepair` and
`kPendingAircraftScrap` and are answered by `Sim::aircraftRepairYear` and
`Sim::aircraftScrapYear`. All of it draws on one `aircraftRng_`, so no other family's
sequence moves.

The purchase card no longer filters on `Min Age`: that column is the aircraft's own age floor,
which the ctor reads to place a used aircraft's age, not a requirement on the buyer.

### Ceilings

The economy multiplier M is 1 — the object it lives in is not modelled, so MonthlyExpense's
500 floor and the repair and scrap formulas all run unscaled. The maintenance card is not
ported, so `NumAnnualMaintenancesPerformed` stays 0: wear follows plain age, and the
maintenance-gap gate is always satisfied for an aircraft whose row was bought used. The two
native callers' relative order (wear before or after the yearly expenses) is unrecovered and
the port wears first. The Golden Wrench is an in-app purchase and is not modelled, so no
aircraft is wrench-immune and the gated button is not offered. The repair card's table row is
rendered inline in the body (`Repair: $…`) because the port's card type has no table
dictionary. A repair still open at the hero's death, the InsufficientFinances card, the
follow-up cards' screen furniture and the achievements/obits are not modelled.

### Verified

`_re/tools/test_aircraft_life.py` over 40 funded lives (seeds 1-40, ages 70): 22 repair
cards, 13 paid, 9 declined and 2 scrapyard pushes. Every repair card names a model that is a
`a16_aircraft-enc` Descriptive Name and a broken term and part that are cells of the same
`a16_aircraft-parts-enc` row, quotes a `Repair: $…` price and offers `Repair it` /
`I might fix it later`; a paid repair's log reads `My … has a broken …\nI repaired the
broken … on my ….`, a refusal's log reads `…I decided not to repair it.` and moves discipline
down, and the scrap push's body is the beyond-repair line plus `Age: N Years` with the single
`Scrap it` button, after which the aircraft is gone from the life. `_re/tools/test_aircraft.py`
(purchase and the danger card) still passes: 9 purchases, 56 danger cards.

Aircraft repair and the scrap pull were the two cards this section was expected to deliver;
the scrap pull (`ScenarioAircraftScrapPull`, `.ctor 0x3423c90`) is a buy-back card the yearly
tick never pushes and is not ported.

The full 122-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (64075db9..., 122 PASS / 0 FAIL):
_re/tools/test_aircraft_life.py is the new test (22 repair cards, 13 paid, 9 declined, 2 scrapped
over 40 lives), _re/tools/test_aircraft.py still finds 9 purchases and 56 danger cards, and
nothing else moved even though the aircraft now takes money out of the hero's purse every year.

## 333. The vampire hunt's animal

A vampire's solo hunt can turn up an animal instead of a person. The port's hunt was one
narrative line (REPORT 70); this section adds the animal card the hunt pushes,
ScenarioVampireHuntAnimal, with its three answers and their follow-up cards.

### The native side

- Class: ScenarioVampireHuntAnimal, .ctor 0x29639e8, RefreshScenario 0x2963a2c,
  ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x2963c44; fields +0x170 activity, +0x178 DataAnimal, +0x180 narrative.
- Push: ScenarioVampireHuntLocation::ChoiceSelectedAtIndex (0x29650b0) hands the chosen
  location sentence to VampireHuntActivity::SelectScenarioByLocation (0x2969b8c). That
  builds {Animal, Human, Vampire} with the location row's three appearance likelihoods
  (a16_vampire-solo-hunt-location-enc), sorts them descending (Array.Sort, comparator
  0x296aca0) and walks them: the first entry whose GetRandomNumber(0,100) < 50
  (VampireBalancing.HuntLikelihoodPercent) wins, the last one if none does - 50% / 25% /
  25% in likelihood order. An animal builds this card; GetScenarioByHuntAppearance
  (0x296aae4) sends human and vampire to their own classes.
- The animal: DataHub::GetRandomAnimalForContinent (0x28151cc), uniform over the
  a16_animals-enc rows whose continent list holds the hero's continent, retried with
  'Europe' (#19103) when none does.
- Card: exterior title #45527 'Vampire'; title #8533 '<animal-title>' (the name title-cased);
  body #10080 'A juicy-looking <animal> you discovered while hunting <in-location> is
  tempting you.\n\nWhat will you do?', <in-location> being the location row's String Version.
  Choices in stored order, not shuffled, no dismiss: #20004 'Feed on it', #28743 'Let it go',
  #12363 'Attempt to rescue it'. RefreshScenario logs #24092 'I encountered <animal-indefinite>.'
- IsAnimalAttacking (0x29640e0) / IsAnimalFleeing (0x29641c4): GetRandomNumber(0,100)
  below 100 * clamp(score/5, 0, 1) of Aggression / Skittishness (multipliers 1.0), so 20%
  per point. Each call is a fresh draw.
- Feed: attack roll. No attack - the feed: title from the vampire title pool row
  BLOOD_IS_BLOOD_1 (DataHub::GetTitleForVampire, one of six cells), body #48404 'You drained
  <animal-indefinite> <in-location> and discarded its carcass.', essence + the row's Vampire
  Essence Gain (SimVampire::AdjustEssence), notoriety -1, happiness +1, journal #24154 'I fed
  on it for some essence.' Attack - a second attack roll and then a flee roll: a missed
  second roll or a landed flee roll is the runaway (title row LATER, body #27507 'It fled the
  scene after you attacked.', journal #27506); otherwise the animal hits back
  (AnimalAttackVampire 0x29642a8 -> AnimalAttackHero 0x2964b8c with HuntAnimalMaxDamage 2):
  damage 1 + clamp(Danger/5) truncated, health -damage, essence -damage, happiness -2, an
  'Ouch' card (#33037, body #41507 'The <animal> charged you!\n\nIt <attack-string> your
  <body-part>.') under a BLOOD_IS_BLOOD_2 card (#49619 'You tried to attack the <animal>, but
  missed!'), journal #23577. No notoriety in the attack.
- Let it go: no follow-up, no delta; only the encounter line stands.
- Rescue (AttemptRescue 0x2964350): success iff GetRandomNumber(0,20)+1 < 5 - Skittishness:
  happiness +3, karma +3 (SimPerson::ImpactKarma), title one of #13463 'Big heart' / #27886
  'Jane Goodall mode' / #39831 'Star citizen' / #27549 'It lives to see another day', body
  #49430, achievement acRescueAnimal, obit line #10221. Failure rolls GetRandomNumber(0,8)+1
  against Aggression: at or above, a harmless miss (journal #24091, body #50215, title #11716
  'Are you freaking crazy' when Danger > 3, else one of #13463 / #11440 / #13976 / #22480);
  below, the animal attacks (journal #24090 + #966 ' The <animal> <attack-string> me!',
  health -(Danger+1)); a hero left under 1 health dies through SimDeath::UpdateWithKillerAnimal,
  otherwise a 'Help!' card (#22821, body #41506 'The <animal> <attack-string> you!') with
  Scenario.Damage max(Danger-1, 1) and obit line #20693.
- No disease, rabies, money or career change anywhere in the class.

### The port

Sim::vampireHuntAnimalYear (src/fam/vampire.cpp) on its own huntAnimalRng_ stream, a
family offered to a vampire hero. It draws a location, walks the three sorted
likelihoods with the native 50% steps and builds the card only on an animal; the animal
pool, the attack/flee rolls, every branch's text and the numbers above are the native
ones. Stat moves go through pointsForImpact (health -damage, happiness +1 / -2 / +3,
health -(Danger+1)); the rescue attack kills through the walk card's animal death
(REPORT 326) when it would leave the hero under 1 health.

### Ceilings

- No hunt activity: the hunt arrives as an annual family (15% coin, no cooldown) and the
  location is drawn uniformly instead of being picked by the player.
- Human and vampire appearances end the turn; their classes are not part of this section.
- One card a year: the follow-up cards are appended to the encounter card's body as a
  title line and a body, in the native stacking order.
- <body-part> has no native source in this build (the parser's SelectedBodyPart accessors
  have no callers), so the port draws a gender-matching row of a16_body-parts-enc.
- Tied likelihoods keep table order (the native sort is unstable).
- The rescue gate's vtable slot +0x438 (-2 at Danger >= 2 and Aggression >= 2), the
  'Help!' card's Scenario.Damage, achievements and obituary lines are not modelled;
  notoriety and essence move by their raw native amounts on the port's bars.
- The 'all 7 continents' cell matches every continent, as on the walk card; the native
  loader's normalisation of that cell is unrecovered.

### Verified

_re/tools/test_vampire_hunt_animal.py over 80 vampire lives (seeds 1-80): every card's
animal is a North American (or all-continent) row, title the title-cased name, location a
String Version cell; outcome counts let go 63, fed 24, fled 28, hit 6, rescued 8, missed
45, attacked 15. Feed titles come from BLOOD_IS_BLOOD_1, runaway titles from LATER, hit
titles from BLOOD_IS_BLOOD_2 over an 'Ouch' card whose body part is a body-parts row;
deltas match (feed happiness +4, hit health -4 or -8 by Danger and happiness -8, rescue
karma +3 and happiness +16, rescue attack health by Danger), let go moves nothing, and a
non-vampire never sees the card.

The full 121-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (915ad0d2...). One test,
test_witch_doctor, failed on its first pass with an abort before any assertion of its own:
its probe is compiled against port/include while the archive it links had been built before
the aircraft work of section 334 touched those headers, so probe and library disagreed
about the hero's layout - which is exactly what the aircraft's new fields change. Re-run
against the archive built from the same headers the probe compiles against, it passes:
121 PASS / 0 FAIL, the witch probe reporting 30 remedy rows, 50 fatal, 306 neutral, 844 harm,
79 cures, 43 delayed.

## 332. The back-to-school title pool

Every back-to-school card's headline - the field trip, the dance, the house party, the
sleepover, the prom, and eleven other cards - is drawn from one table whose rows are
alternate wordings of the same title. The port had those headlines hardcoded; this section
takes the pool instead.

### The native side

* DataHub.LoadBackToSchoolTitlesSet (0x28f09f4) reads data/a16_back-to-school-titles-enc,
  splits it and, per row, parses the first cell into a BACK_TO_SCHOOL_TITLES enum with
  System.Enum::TryParse (0x28f0cec) and puts **every remaining cell** - the original title and
  all five option columns - into one list. The row object stores the enum at +0x10 and the
  list at +0x18.
* DataHub.GetTitleForBackToSchool(BACK_TO_SCHOOL_TITLES) (0x28f0e84) is a static getter with
  one enum argument. It finds the row with System.Enum::Equals (0x29cd054) and nothing else -
  no string compare, no Contains - then returns GameReference::PickRandomFromStringArray over
  that row's list. The returned string is **one of the row's six cells at random**, never
  necessarily the original title.
* 47 BL call sites, all with constant tags, across 16 classes: the four age-up cards
  (expulsion, field trip, prom royalty, sleepover), the dance cards, the
  activity cards (SchoolDanceActivity, HousePartyActivity, SleepOver), the school-change
  request, the scholarship card and SafeSex. Three sites pick between two tags with a csel
  (30/35, 31/36); the rest pass one enum. Every site writes the result into
  Scenario.Title (+0x38) or passes it as the title argument of Scenario::.ctor - 36 and 11
  respectively - and no site uses it as body text, a journal line or a choice label.
* 55 rows, no duplicate tags. Seven of them are never requested by any code path:
  WELCOME_TO_THE_SQUAD, ALREADY_WENT_TO_A_DANCE, NO_FRIENDS, FRIENDS_TIL_THE_END,
  PAJAMA_PARTY, I_HAVE_TO_WALK_MY_FISH and SLUMBER_PARTY_HEARTY; they can only surface
  through the getter's not-found fallback, which returns a random row's original title.
* The option columns are alternate headlines, not choice labels; no code reads them
  individually.

### The port

* `Sim::b2sTitle(tag)` reads the row by its index - the CSV order is the enum order - and
  draws uniformly from its six title cells on its own stream, `b2sTitleRng_`.
* Tags the port's own cards now use: the field trip's learning, socializing and goofing-off
  outcomes take 51, 52 and 53; a classmate turning the hero down takes 8; the dance takes 19
  when the hero goes alone, 9 with a partner and 18 with a classmate; the house party's wild,
  lively and chill rows take 2, 3 and 4; a sleepover refusal takes 40 when the hero did the
  asking and 28 when the classmate asked; and the prom takes 49 when the hero is crowned, 47
  when he loses and 50 when he declines to run.
* The sleepover's accept card and the rest of the port's cards keep their own titles: which
  tag, if any, their native cards request is not mapped here, so they are left unchanged.

### Ceilings

* The port maps each of its own outcomes onto one tag; the native cards often have more
  outcomes than the port models (the dance has thirteen tags, the party six), so the tags
  without a port outcome - the cancelled dance, the party that was already thrown three
  times this year, both sleepover excuse paths - are unused.
* The seven dead rows stay in the table but no port card draws them, which is the native
  behaviour too.
* The prom's nomination card keeps its own "Prom queen"/"Prom king" title; the native
  royalty card takes the pool's title only on the four outcome cards.
* Graduating from school has no native consumer for this table, so the port's graduation
  card keeps its own title.

### Verified

* 36 distinct headlines over 120 lives (seeds 1-120), each one a cell of the row for the tag
  the card's outcome selects: checked for the field trip's three focuses, the dance's three
  companions, the party's three rowdiness levels, both sleepover refusals, the dance refusal
  and the prom's three lanes (8 crowned, 7 robbed, 10 declined).
* The table still holds 55 rows and the suite's other cards' titles are unchanged.

The full 120-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (e0012097..., 119 PASS /
1 FAIL). The failure is test-side and was fixed here without a code change: the prom test
found its card by the fixed "Prom king"/"Prom queen" headline, which the outcome now draws
from this pool, so it finds the card by its registry class and the crown by the nomination
body instead (re-run: 11 prom cards, 3 won, 4 lost, 4 declined).

## 331. The coworker's compliment card

The peer next to the hero has his own compliment card, and it is not a copy of the agent's
or the employee's: it draws a magnitude from the coworker's personality, moves the
relationship once a year at most, and can land a cold "ignored you" instead of a warm reply.
It is also unreachable from a random push - the only two constructors are the relationship
list's payoff row and the generic compliment blueprint.

### The native card

* ScenarioCoworkerCompliment: `.ctor` 0x297f990, RefreshScenario 0x297f9bc (997 instructions),
  DismissSelected 0x2980950. Fields `+0x170` the coworker, `+0x178` the narrative; no
  ChoiceSelectedAtIndex, no random-push gate, and `+0x132`/`+0x133` are both set, so it is a
  dismiss-only information card with one button.
* `RefreshScenario` caches the hero's age on the coworker (`SimPerson+0x144`), takes a dead
  GetRandomNumber(0, 95) whose result is overwritten, and computes the magnitude as
  GetRandomNumber(0, bound) + bonus in three branches:
  - normally, when the relationship R is above 15: bonus = trunc((R + connection + coolness) /
    3) - the divide-by-three in the binary - and bound 30;
  - when R <= 15 and the coworker's willpower is under 30: bonus 30, bound 31;
  - otherwise: bonus 5, bound (int)R.
* Warm only when the magnitude clears 51 and the coworker is unimpressed by both counts:
  professionalism < GetRandomNumber(0, 100) and coolness > GetRandomNumber(0, 100). Both
  draws happen whatever the outcome.
* The bar graph is titled #69489 '{0} Appreciation' with PronounStringForType 6 and the
  magnitude clamped to 100.
* The relationship moves once per age-year, when the stored year differs from the hero's:
  +5 at 91 and above, +4 at 81, +3 at 41, +2 at 21, +1 at 11, nothing below.
* Body and journal come from a 3-way roll: #47966 'You called your {0}, {1}, {2}.' / #23686
  'I called my {0}, {1}, {2}.'; #49529 'You told your {0}, {1}, that {2} {3}.' / #25271 'I
  told my {0}, {1}, that {2} {3}.'; #49527 'You told your {0}, {1}, that you think {2} {3}.'
  / the same #25271 journal. {0} is the relationship word, {1} the coworker's name, {2} the
  compliment drawn for the coworker's gender from a16_compliments-enc, {3} the he's/she's
  pronoun. Title from #10079 'A joy to be around', #32583 'Office butterfly', #16115
  'Compliments to the office', #42929 "There's that smile", #22091 'Good natured'.
* A warm card continues: when the hero has no lover and the coworker's feelings for him are
  at least 81, the card chains ScenarioCoworkerHookup; then the hero's own compliment is
  drawn for the hero's gender and a journal sentence is appended - #69883 '{0} called me
  {1}.' or #70323 "{0} told me that I'm {1}." with PronounStringForType 5 - and the card
  chains a plain follow-up titled from #23233 'How nice', #30537 'Much appreciated', #43692
  "Today's gonna be a good day", #15211 'Careful now ;)', #18853 'Enough love to go around'
  whose body is the reply sentence (#69888 '{0} called you {1}!' / #70338 "{0} told you that
  you're {1}!").
* A cold card - magnitude at most 14 and coolness below GetRandomNumber(0, 100) - appends
  #68842 '{0}\n\n{1} ignored you.' to the body and chains nothing.
* The supervisor case: a coworker whose Type is SUPERVISOR takes a different bonus branch
  (professionalism above 85 in a job, 50 in the military, falls through to the relationship
  branch) and costs a relationship point with every coworker through
  SimWorkplace::ImpactRelationshipWithAllCoworkers(-1).
* The two constructor sites are LifeInterface::RelationshipItemArrayForCoworker (the list's
  'Pay {0} a compliment' row, pronoun 2, one card per click) and
  BluePrintCompliment::GetNextScenario (hero 6 or older, target older than 2, target not an
  abandoned child, one card per call).

### The port

* `Sim::coworkerComplimentYear` is offered from `Sim::coworkerYear`, because the port has no
  relationship list to click and the native card has no random push. The coworker's
  professionalism, coolness and relationship are drawn on the first card about him
  (coolness and professionalism 0-100, the relationship from the 40-60 tier the company
  generator uses), the magnitude follows the recovered branches, and the relationship moves
  with the recovered tiers.
* The card writes a16_compliments-enc as its table and the drawn row, so a test can check the
  compliment against the row the card reports.
* `Sim::complimentRow` (added for section 327) supplies the compliment; the pronoun comes
  from the coworker's stored gender, and the hero's own compliment for the warm reply from
  the hero's.

### Ceilings

* The push is a coin (0.12) on the coworker family's yearly turn; the native card has no
  random push at all, so its real frequency is whatever the player clicks in a relationship
  list the port does not have.
* A relationship starts in the recovered 40-60 tier and only grows, so the branches that need
  a relationship at or below 15 - and with it the "ignored you" arm - are implemented but
  cannot be reached in a port life, while the native roster can hold a thoroughly disliked
  coworker. The cold arm is kept because its arithmetic is recovered.
* The port keeps no connection score, so the average uses 50 in its place; the willpower
  branch (only reachable below 15 anyway) is not modelled and that case takes the fallback.
* The supervisor variant of the card is not offered - the port's supervisor has his own
  cards - so the different threshold and ImpactRelationshipWithAllCoworkers(-1) are
  recorded but unused.
* The bar graph is not modelled, so the magnitude only survives through the relationship
  tiers.
* ScenarioCoworkerHookup's internals are unrecovered, so the warm card stops at the reply;
  the plain follow-up card is not reproduced, and its reply sentence is written into the
  journal instead.
* The native counts the compliment on Life+0x3ac; the port keeps no such counter.

### Verified

* 41 coworker compliment cards over 80 lives (seeds 1-80): every one is dismiss-only
  (`choice` null), on a16_compliments-enc, at age 18 or later, with every stat delta zero and
  a title from the recovered five.
* All three frames fire - 16 "called", 12 "told", 13 "that you think" - and each body's
  compliment equals the Compliment cell of the row the card reports, with the journal mirror
  naming the same coworker.
* 5 warm cards carried the return-compliment journal sentence ("He called me ...", "He told
  me that I'm ..."); no card carried both a reply and an "ignored you" paragraph.
* A run with no job produced no coworker cards (control over seeds 1-20).

The full 119-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (a30b176b..., 119 PASS /
0 FAIL): _re/tools/test_coworker_compliment.py exercises the card, its three frames, the
warm reply and the per-year relationship tiers, and nothing else moved.

## 330. The employee respect card and its chain

The office has one more card the employee's own feedback card can hand to: ScenarioEmployeeRespect,
which the business annual report pushes every year. It is the only card in the family with buttons,
and three of the four buttons open a card of their own. This section ports the respect card, the
three chain cards, and the one lane that stays on the respect card and only writes a line.

### The native respect card

* ScenarioEmployeeRespect: `.ctor` 0x73f39d6df0, RefreshScenario 0x73f39d6e2c, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex
  0x73f39d76e0, DismissSelected 0x73f39d7a68. Fields `+0x170` the employee, `+0x178` the narrative,
  `+0x180` is-reaction, ColorScheme 5. Three callers, all recovered: SimBusiness::CreateAnnualReport
  (0x73f30706c8, the yearly push, is-reaction false), ScenarioEmployeeBonus::MiniGameCompleted and
  ScenarioEmployeeCompliment::RefreshScenario (both is-reaction true).
* Title: #36052 "Respect" on the yearly push. A card chained behind another card instead picks from
  #34362 "Positive reinforcement", #28812 "Let's keep this up, huh?", #30537 "Much appreciated",
  #10093 "A little CEO appreciation", #27547 "It just warms ya heart up".
* Body and journal are the two cells of a a16_employee-respect-scenarios-enc row (Scenario and Log
  Version) run through the bracket parser, with the `<employee>` token filled as "your employee,
  <name>," in the body and "my employee, <name>," in the journal.
* The row is drawn by DataHub::GetRandomEmployeeRespectScenarioForPushOrReaction (0x73f2c884a0) in
  five bands on the employee's bond with the hero - 1 up to 20, 2 up to 40, 3 up to 60, 4 up to 80,
  5 above - keeping the rows whose Score matches the band and whose Can Be Push flag is set (Can Be
  Reaction on the chained path), and falling back to the whole set when a band holds nothing.
* Four choices, in the order the card stores them: #21649 "Give " + Pronoun(2) + #1000 " a bonus",
  #35385 "Recognize ", #45990 "Warn ", #40891 "Take no action". The handler lowercases the label and
  matches by Contains, in that order; every arm ends with the journal line and a UI refresh.
* "Take no action" is the only arm that keeps the card: it appends #348 "\nI ignored ", Pronoun(2),
  "." to the journal, takes a karma point, docks the employee's `+0x408` slot by
  GetRandomNumber(1, 3), and drops their morale by 3.
* The other three arms chain a card: ScenarioEmployeeBonus, ScenarioEmployeeRecognize and
  ScenarioEmployeeWarn. The two plain ones are built inline (a Scenario with the employee at
  `+0x170` and ColorScheme 5); their type names are not exposed in the metadata and are identified
  by their byte-identical constructors and their adjacency to the bonus type in the type table.

### The three chain cards

* ScenarioEmployeeRecognize (`.ctor` 0x73f39d67c4, RefreshScenario 0x73f39d67f8, DismissSelected
  0x73f39d6cb8). Title picked from #18690 "Employee spotlight!", #30541 "Much deserved recognition",
  #19158 "Everyone take notes", #39835 "Star team member", #28197 "Keep it up!". Body is a row of
  a16_employee-recognition-scenarios-enc (Scenario, Commonness Score) with `<employee>` as "your
  employee, <name>," and `<company>` as the business name. Journal #24922 "I recognized my employee,
  " + the capitalised name + #5547 ", for " + Pronoun(1) + #2216 " hard work and effort." Effects,
  paid once per age: the employee's `+0x408` slot +3, competence +1, morale +2.
* ScenarioEmployeeWarn (`.ctor` 0x73f39d7a34, RefreshScenario 0x73f39d7afc, DismissSelected
  0x73f39d814c). Title picked from #34181 "Playing hardball", #29582 "Make my day", #49186 "You
  ready to go?!", #23365 "I WILL end you", #30882 "My turn". Body is a row of
  a16_employee-warn-scenarios-enc (Scenario, Risk Score, Commonness Score) with `<employee>` and
  `<employee-possessive>` tokens, the possessive built the same way as a person's name. Journal
  #25593 "I warned my employee, " + the capitalised name + ".". The row's Risk Score 1-5 sets the
  bite on the `+0x408` slot, competence and morale: -1/-1/-2, -2/-1/-3, -2/-1/-4, -3/-1/-5, -3/-2/-6;
  a warning when the employee has already been warned more than twice or shouted at three times
  bites once more (-1/-1/-2). The card then counts the warning and remembers the hero's age.
* ScenarioEmployeeBonus (`.ctor` 0x73f39cd850, RefreshScenario 0x73f39cdac8, MiniGameCompleted
  0x73f39cdddc) is a minigame card, not a choice card: a slider over the business's available
  capital, with a registry of five strings (#10716 "Actually, never mind", #21648 "Give", #51762
  "a bonus", #12531 "Available Capital", #13882 "Bonus"). Body either #23227 "How much of a bonus
  will you give your employee, " + name + "?" or #21729 "Give your employee, " + name + #5328
  ", a bonus today!". The largest bonus is max(1, min(average industry salary, working capital,
  the capital times 0.99 when it is over 2^24)) and the slider opens at a tenth of that. The award
  is decided by the registry key the player picked - "bonus" - and nothing else. A decline writes
  #284 "\nI considered giving my employee, " + name + #5326 ", a bonus and then decided not to."
  and moves nothing. An award writes #342 "\nI gave my employee, " + name + #5327 ", a bonus in the
  amount of " + the amount + "." and brackets the ratio: up to a quarter pays competence +0..1,
  morale +2 and the `+0x508` slot +1; up to a half the same for a step of 25; up to three quarters
  competence +1, morale +3 and `+0x508` +1..3; above that competence +1, morale +3 and `+0x508`
  +1..4. The bonus is debited from the business, the employee's appreciation bar is redrawn, a
  result card titled from #10089 "A lil something for you", #18071 "Don't spend it all in one
  place", #34971 "Put a smile on their face", #39427 "Some cheese to keep em runnin" reports
  #48508 "You gave your employee, " + name + #5329 ", a bonus.", and the card can chain the respect
  card back when half of the step plus the employee's morale beats GetRandomNumber(0, 101).

### The port

* `Sim::employeeRespectYear` (src/sim.cpp) is offered from `Sim::officeYear`, after the employee's
  compliment card: the yearly push is the business report, which the port does not run, so an office
  year is sometimes this card. A card chained behind the bonus card is dispatched through the
  pending-card queue in the same year, so a chain keeps showing its cards at one age.
* Bond bands, table, flags and Score come from a16_employee-respect-scenarios-enc; the token filler
  is `Sim::employeeCell`, which also resolves the slash lists the cells carry ("Employee of the
  <Day/Month/Week>") from the card's own stream.
* The `+0x408` slot the native moves has no recovered identity, so the hero keeps it as
  `ofcEmpRespect` (0-100, starting at 60); warnings also count `ofcEmpWarned`, and the bonus and
  the recognition remember the age they last paid so they pay once per age.
* The bonus amount is the recoverable part: working capital and the average salary come from the
  business block when the hero owns one, otherwise from the hero's own money and salary; the
  starting tenth of the ceiling is what the card pays, and the result is written into the journal
  instead of a second card.

### Ceilings

* The card's frequency is a coin (0.10 per office-family turn); the native frequency is the yearly
  business report, which the port does not model.
* The bonus minigame's slider is unrecovered: the port offers the two recovered buttons and always
  pays the ceiling's tenth, so the higher ratio bands are only reachable through money the port
  cannot raise. The result card, the analytics event and the Bitizenship check are not reproduced.
* A respect card that arrived from the bonus chain cannot chain another bonus card: the native chain
  has no depth limit and the port would loop.
* `pointsForImpact(0)` would draw from the main stream, so the competence step on the smallest
  bonus band is an explicit coin instead.
* Achievements are not modelled, so the native "spat" achievement on a warning is skipped, and the
  bonus's own result card is replaced by the journal line.
* The three chain cards' effects are applied at the age they show; the native recognition and bonus
  effects are gated on the hero's age matching the one stored on the employee, which the port only
  needs for its own repeat guard.

### Verified

* 15 respect cards over 25 office lives (seeds 1-25): each carries a16_employee-respect-scenarios-enc,
  a row flagged Can Be Push with a Score of 1-5, a body naming the employee, and a journal line
  naming the same employee; every card is at age 18 or later.
* The chain fires: 7 bonus cards, 3 recognition cards and 2 warning cards appeared in the same year
  as their respect card.
* 5 respect cards took the ignore lane: the journal ends "I ignored him." and the card's karma delta
  is -1.
* 3 bonus cards paid out, each writing "a bonus in the amount of $" into its journal.
* A hero with no office job drew no respect card (control run, seed 3).

The full 118-test suite ran on the binary these notes describe (5c806646..., 118 PASS /
0 FAIL): the respect card, its three chain cards and the ignore lane are exercised by
_re/tools/test_employee_respect.py, and nothing else moved.

## 329. The employee's feedback card

The boss's own compliment card: ScenarioEmployeeCompliment is the business employee's version of the
zoo keeper's card (328), bound to a SimEmployee and built by that employee's menu row. It reuses the
same table, titles and frames as the zoo card - "your employee" is the native text - and adds one
thing the zoo card does not have: an optional follow-up respect card, which is why this section also
records that card's contract.

### The native card

* Class ScenarioEmployeeCompliment derives straight from Scenario: `.ctor` 0x73f39ce884,
  RefreshScenario 0x73f39ce8b8, DismissSelected 0x73f39cf358. Fields `+0x170` the employee, `+0x178`
  the narrative. The constructor stores the employee and sets ColorScheme 5.
* RefreshScenario, in order:
  1. feedback-style flags `+0x132` and `+0x133`, so no buttons; ContributeToCommunityGoal, which can
     push a community-goal card in front of this one;
  2. title: #16110 "Complimentary" is written first and then overwritten by a pick from #41423
     "That's nice", #39352 "So sweet", #44059 "True love", #13459 "Big fan" - the default is dead;
  3. the year cache: the employee's `+0x144` is synced to the current year, and if it already held
     this year the magnitude is zeroed and both the relationship step and the return compliment are
     skipped;
  4. a magnitude of GetRandomNumber(0, 95), then +5, or GetRandomNumber(0, 20) when the employee's
     competence (`+0x220`) is under 20 - shown only in the card's bar graph;
  5. the compliment the hero pays: GetRandomComplimentForGender over the EMPLOYEE's EffectiveGender,
     then GetRandomNumber(0, 3) picks the frame: #47960 "You called your employee, {0}, {1}." with
     #23683 "I called my employee, {0}, {1}."; #49515 "You told your employee, {0}, that {1} {2}."
     with #25268 "I told my employee, {0}, that {1} {2}."; #49514 "You told your employee, {0}, that
     you think {1} {2}." over the same #25268. {0} is the employee's full name, {1} is
     PronounStringForType(8), {2} the compliment;
  6. the relationship gate: the employee's bond with the hero beats GetRandomNumber(80, 101), or
     failing that the employee's competence beats GetRandomNumber(70, 101); the bond impact is
     GetRandomNumber(2, 4) and is applied on every new year, gate or no gate;
  7. the return compliment when the gate passed: GetRandomComplimentForGender over the HERO's
     EffectiveGender, then GetRandomNumber(0, 2) - #50316 "Your employee, {0}, called you {1}!" with
     #69883 "{0} called me {1}.", or #50317 "Your employee, {0}, told you that you're {1}!" with
     #70323 "{0} told me that I'm {1}.";
  8. the third arm of that roll builds a child Scenario titled #27734 "It's mutual" and stamps a
     hero stat slot - and is DEAD CODE in 3.25.1, because GetRandomNumber is Next(min, max) and
     never returns its upper bound (REPORT.en.md 23.4);
  9. the optional respect card, only when the relationship gate failed: GetRandomNumber(0, 2) equal
     to 0 and the employee's `+0x21c` beating GetRandomNumber(0, 101) chains a ScenarioEmployeeRespect
     behind this card;
  10. the bar graph: #69489 "{0} Appreciation" off PronounStringForType(6), value clamp(w, 5, 100),
      overridden to GetRandomNumber(20, 100) when the mutual arm fired;
  11. effects: the bond slot `+0x508` gets the drawn 2..3, then ImpactMorale(1) and
      ImpactCompetence(1); the journal is the narrative through #68635 "{0}", and Life's
      NumTimesComplimentedSomeone (`+0x3ac`) is incremented.
* DismissSelected only writes the journal line; there are no choices.

### The respect card this chain can push

Recorded here because the compliment card is one of its callers, and recovered in the same pass:

* ScenarioEmployeeRespect (`.ctor` 0x73f39d6df0, RefreshScenario 0x73f39d6e2c, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex
  0x73f39d76e0, DismissSelected 0x73f39d7a68; fields `+0x170` employee, `+0x178` narrative, `+0x180`
  is-reaction, ColorScheme 5). Created by the yearly business report (SimBusiness::CreateAnnualReport
  0x73f3071620), by the employee bonus mini-game and by this card.
* Title: #36052 "Respect" when pushed; when it is a reaction, a pick from #34362 "Positive
  reinforcement", #28812 "Let's keep this up, huh?", #30537 "Much appreciated", #10093 "A little CEO
  appreciation", #27547 "It just warms ya heart up".
* Body: a row of a16_employee-respect-scenarios-enc (40 rows: Scenario, Log Version, Can Be
  Reaction, Can Be Push, Score), drawn by DataHub::GetRandomEmployeeRespectScenarioForPushOrReaction
  (0x73f2c884a0) in buckets on the employee's bond with the hero - 1 up to 20, 2 up to 40, 3 up to
  60, 4 up to 80, 5 above - keeping rows whose Score matches the bucket and whose Can Be Push (or
  Can Be Reaction) flag is set, then picking uniformly. Both cells are parsed: the Scenario cell is
  the body, the Log Version cell the journal, with the `<employee>` token filled as "your employee,
  <name>," in the body and "my employee, <name>," in the journal.
* Four choices, in stored order: #21649 "Give " + Pronoun(2) + #1000 " a bonus", #35385
  "Recognize ", #45990 "Warn ", #40891 "Take no action". "Bonus" opens ScenarioEmployeeBonus (its own
  card), "Recognize" and "Warn" open plain Scenarios whose text is unrecovered, and "Take no action"
  appends #348 "
I ignored ", Pronoun(2), "." to the journal, takes a karma point
  (ImpactKarma(-1)), docks the employee's `+0x408` slot by GetRandomNumber(1, 3) and drops their
  morale by 3.
* The bar graph is labelled #16054 "Competence" and shows the employee's competence; it stamps no
  stat.

### The port

* `Sim::employeeComplimentYear` (src/sim.cpp) is offered at the top of `Sim::officeYear`, for the
  same reason as the zoo card: the native card is a menu row and the port has no menus, so an office
  year is sometimes the employee's card instead of a work card. Its own stream is
  `officeCompRng_`; the coin is 0.10.
* The named employee the office family already carries supplies the name and gender; the card only
  needs the bond, so the hero gained `ofcEmpRel` (0-100, starting at 60). The employee's one work
  stat in the port, `ofcPerf`, stands in for the competence the native card reads, and the card
  moves it and the staff morale by `pointsForImpact(1)` (4 points each).
* The frames, titles, gate, return compliment and journal join are transcribed; the shared
  `Sim::complimentRow` helper (328) supplies the compliment pools for both genders.
* The respect card and the dead third arm are not implemented; this section is where their contract
  is recorded.

### Ceilings

* The card's frequency is a coin (0.10 per office-family turn), not a copied roll.
* The year cache is not modelled: a year holds one card, so the equality branch cannot be reached.
* The bar graph, its magnitude and the ColorScheme have no meaning outside the native UI: the draws
  are kept so the stream stays native and the number is dropped.
* The respect card is not pushed; the bonus, recognize and warn cards behind its choices are
  unrecovered, and a port year cannot hold two cards anyway.
* The employee's competence is the port's performance stat: the native card reads a separate
  competence field the port does not carry.
* NumTimesComplimentedSomeone and ContributeToCommunityGoal are not modelled.

### Verified

* 19 cards over 50 office lives (seeds 1-50): each is dismiss-only, titled from the four-title
  pool, at age 18 or later, with every stat delta zero and a16_compliments-enc as its table.
* All three frames appear (4 called, 5 told, 10 think) and one card carries the employee's return
  compliment, with its second paragraph naming the same employee.
* The journal is one entry: the mirror of what the hero said, and, when the employee answers, the
  return line under it.
* The row the card reports is an a16_compliments-enc row open to the employee's gender, and the
  pronoun the frame uses agrees with the gender read off the return line.
* A hero with no office job draws no card (control run, seed 3).

## 328. The zoo keeper's compliment card

The zoo's keeper is a person the hero can talk to, and the game has one card for it: the same
compliment the agent card (327) pays, bound to the keeper instead. It is not pushed by a yearly
set - the zoo employee's relationship list builds it - but its text and its effects are readable,
and the port already has a named keeper. This section ports
ScenarioZooEmployeeComplimentFeedback.

### The native card

* Class ScenarioZooEmployeeComplimentFeedback derives straight from Scenario: `.ctor` 0x73f2e5ec94,
  RefreshScenario 0x73f2e5ecc0, DismissSelected 0x73f2e5f6a4. The constructor stores the keeper
  at `+0x170` and nothing else: unlike the employee twin it never sets a colour scheme.
* Title: picked from #41423 "That's nice", #39352 "So sweet", #44059 "True love", #13459
  "Big fan". The constructor first stores #16110 "Complimentary" and that value is always
  overwritten before the pick, so it is dead in 3.25.1.
* RefreshScenario, in order:
  1. feedback-style flags `+0x132` and `+0x133` (collapse open lists on dismiss), so no buttons;
  2. the year caches: the hero's age is written into the keeper's `+0x320` unconditionally and into
     `+0x144` when it differs - `+0x144` is SimPerson's own
     "hero age at last compliment" field, the same one the agent card uses;
  3. SeasonsObjectiveController::ContributeToCommunityGoal, which pushes the card to the front of
     the queue - no stat moves;
  4. the compliment the hero pays: DataHub::GetRandomComplimentForGender over the KEEPER's
     EffectiveGender, then GetRandomNumber(0, 3) picks the frame:
     #47960 "You called your employee, {0}, {1}." with #23683 "I called my employee, {0}, {1}.";
     #49515 "You told your employee, {0}, that {1} {2}." with #25268 "I told my employee, {0}, that
     {1} {2}."; #49514 "You told your employee, {0}, that you think {1} {2}." over the same #25268.
     {0} is SimPersonName::FullName and the pronoun is PronounStringForType(8) - he's/she's;
  5. a magnitude the card only shows in its bar graph: GetRandomNumber(0, 95), then +5, or
     GetRandomNumber(0, 20) when the keeper's competence is under 20;
  6. the year gate: if the cached hero age equals this year, the magnitude is zeroed and both the
     relationship step and the return compliment are skipped - the card still shows;
  7. the relationship gate: the keeper's bond with the hero above GetRandomNumber(80, 101), or the
     keeper's competence above GetRandomNumber(70, 101); passing re-draws the magnitude as
     GetRandomNumber(2, 4) and that draw is what the relationship slot `+0x508` receives;
  8. the return compliment, filtered on the HERO's EffectiveGender, then GetRandomNumber(0, 2):
     #69883 "{0} called me {1}." or #70323 "{0} told me that I'm {1}.", with the body gaining
     #50316 "Your employee, {0}, called you {1}!" or #50317 "Your employee, {0}, told you that
     you're {1}!" over CapitalizeString(FullName);
  9. the mutual branch: the journal becomes #69343 "{0}\n{1}" over the two narrative lines, and a
     child Scenario titled #27734 "It's mutual" is pushed;
  10. the bar graph: #69489 "{0} Appreciation" off PronounStringForType(6), value clamp(w, 5, 100),
      overridden to GetRandomNumber(20, 100) in the mutual branch.
* Effects: the relationship slot `+0x508` (armed only when the magnitude is at least 1), and
  SimZooEmployee::ImpactCompetence(1) clamped to 0..100 - and nothing else: no morale, no
  achievement, no grant. Life's NumTimesComplimentedSomeone (`+0x3ac`) is incremented on every
  refresh.
* The only caller of the constructor is LifeInterface::GetZooEmployeeRelationshipList: the card is
  a menu item on the keeper's row, labelled #16100 "Compliment" / #16101 "Compliment " + the
  keeper's PronounStringForType(2). There is no yearly zoo push and no activity.
* Dead code: the third arm of the GetRandomNumber(0, 2) roll - Next(min, max) never returns max
  (REPORT.en.md 23.4) - and the title the constructor overwrites.
* The card reuses the EMPLOYEE literals verbatim, "your employee" and all; that is the native text,
  not a port shortcut.

### The port

* `Sim::zooComplimentYear` (src/sim.cpp) is offered at the top of `Sim::zooYear`, because the native
  card is a menu action and the port has no menus: a zoo year is sometimes the keeper's card and
  sometimes the park's. Its own stream is `zooKeeperRng_`.
* The hero has to own the zoo, be 18 or older, not be in prison, and have a keeper: the keeper is
  drawn when the zoo is bought (name, gender, role, competence) and cleared if the zoo is sold.
* `Sim::complimentRow` holds the pool both this card and 327 draw from: the rows of
  a16_compliments-enc whose Gender column is blank, "both" or the gender asked for.
* The keeper's gender and name are the zoo's own fields. The three frames, the four titles, the
  relationship gate, the return compliment's two forms and the journal join are transcribed; the
  competence nudge is `pointsForImpact(1)` (4 points), the port's own conversion for the game's
  AttributeAdjustmentPointsForImpactScore.
* The relationship slot is a new hero field, `zooEmployeeRel`, starting at 60.

### Ceilings

* The card's frequency is a coin (0.06 per zoo-family turn), not a copied roll: nothing in the
  binary pushes the card with a GetRandomNumber.
* The year cache is not modelled: a year can hold only one card, so the equality branch - which
  would suppress the band and the return compliment - cannot be reached.
* The bar graph and its magnitude have no meaning outside the card's own UI: the draws are kept so
  the stream stays native, the number and the label are dropped.
* The mutual branch's child card ("It's mutual") is not pushed, and the hero stat slot it stamps
  (`+0x408`, identity unrecovered) is not moved; the journal keeps both lines, which is what the
  mutual branch does.
* The relationship slot's identity is unrecovered; the port reads it as the keeper's bond and moves
  it by the drawn 2..3 when the gate passes.
* ContributeToCommunityGoal, NumTimesComplimentedSomeone, and the life counter it would feed are
  not modelled - the port keeps no community goals and no such counter.

### Verified

* 133 cards over 40 zoo lives (seeds 1-40, zoo bought, zoo family only): every card is
  dismiss-only (`choice` null), titled from the four-title pool, at age 18 or later, with all stat
  deltas zero, and its table is a16_compliments-enc.
* All three frames appear (44 called, 44 told, 45 think), and both return-compliment forms (63
  called, 70 told), with the body's second paragraph naming the same keeper.
* The keeper's compliment is a row open to the keeper's gender, and the gender read off the
  return line ("She called me..." / "He told me that I'm...") agrees with the pronoun in the
  frame that carries one.
* The journal is one entry holding both lines: the mirror of what the hero said, then the keeper's
  return line.
* A hero with no zoo draws no card at all (control run, seed 3).

## 327. The agent's feedback card

Actors can hire an agent (325's neighbour code), and the adult game has exactly one card where
that agent talks back: a dismiss-only compliment. It is not a wheel family - the relationship
list builds it - so it has no visible push roll; what it does have is a readable body, a
relationship band and a second compliment the agent pays the hero back. This section ports
ScenarioAgentCompliment.

### The native card

* Class ScenarioAgentCompliment: `.ctor` 0x73f38629f4, RefreshScenario 0x73f3862a20,
  DismissSelected 0x73f3863418. Fields `+0x170` `_agent` and `+0x178` `_narrative`. The
  constructor passes 0 to Scenario::.ctor, so the card is not undoable, and writes only the agent
  field - unlike the employee card it never touches a colour scheme.
* It is a feedback-style card: RefreshScenario sets `+0x132` and `+0x133` (collapse any
  open lists on dismiss), so it carries no buttons at all. DismissSelected logs `_narrative`
  through the same designer-line path as 325 and 326.
* Only two callers construct it - LifeInterface::RelationshipItemArrayForAgent and
  BluePrintCompliment::GetNextScenario - and neither draws for it; RefreshScenario and
  DismissSelected have no callers at all in the binary, which is what a base-class virtual
  dispatch looks like.
* RefreshScenario, in order:
  1. year cache sync against the agent's `+0x144` field (one card per agent per year);
  2. a GetRandomNumber(0, 95) draw whose result is thrown away - it exists to advance the stream;
  3. the magnitude: `w20` is 80..99 when the agent's WillGiveHeroTimeOfDay() says yes,
     otherwise 10..39, and `w24 = min(w20, 100)`;
  4. the compliment: DataHub::GetRandomComplimentForGender over the AGENT's EffectiveGender from
     a16_compliments-enc (Compliment, Gender - 138 rows, 107 of them open to both genders);
  5. the title, picked uniformly: #10079 "A joy to be around", #42929 "There's that smile",
     #22091 "Good natured";
  6. one of three (body, journal) frames on GetRandomNumber(0, 3):
     #47950 "You called your agent, {0}, {1}." with #23675 "I called my agent, {0}, {1}.";
     #49496 "You told your agent, {0}, that {1} {2}." with #25260 "I told my agent, {0}, that {1} {2}.";
     #49495 "You told your agent, {0}, that you think {1} {2}." over the same #25260. The {1}
     pronouns are PronounStringForType(8) - he's/she's;
  7. a word-boundary bar graph: #69489 "{0} Appreciation" off PronounStringForType(6) with the value
     w24 loaded into it;
  8. an ignored line when w20 is 14 or below and GetRandomNumber(0, 100) comes out above the
     agent's `+0x330` field: #68842 "{0}\n\n{1} ignored you." with PronounStringForType(5);
  9. the relationship band, applied only on the years the card is new: w20 of 91+ moves the agent's
     relationship slot (vslot `+0x508`) by 5, 81-90 by 4, 41-80 by 3, 21-40 by 2, 11-20 by 1,
     and 10 or below by none;
  10. the return compliment, gated on the same WillGiveHeroTimeOfDay answer: c2 =
      DataHub::GetRandomComplimentForGender over the HERO's gender, then GetRandomNumber(0, 2) -
      zero gives #69883 "{0} called me {1}.", one gives #70323 "{0} told me that I'm {1}.", and both
      replace the journal line the body frame chose.
* The table is a16_compliments-enc; its Gender column reads "male", "female" or blank, and the
  blank rows belong to everybody.
* One dead arm, and it matters for a port: the tick-three arm of the GetRandomNumber(0, 2) at
  step 10 cannot be reached, because GetRandomNumber is System.Random.Next and Next(min, max) never
  returns max (REPORT.en.md 23.4). That arm would have built a six-title card - #16377 "Cordial
  business", #32611 "Oh Stop! No, you!", #18853 "Enough love to go around", #11718 "Are you just
  saying that?", #30537 "Much appreciated", #11307 "An agent of love" - and stamped the hero's
  stat slot (vslot `+0x408`) by +2. The formats #69888 and #70338 are consumed only by it. It
  is dead code in 3.25.1 and is not implemented here.
* Step 11, a counter: `life[0x3ac] += 1` after the card. What the field it increments belongs to
  is unrecovered, so the port does not write it.

### The port

* `Sim::agentComplimentYear` (src/sim.cpp) runs on the actor family's turns: the native card is
  pushed by the relationship list, and the port has no such list, so `Sim::actorYear` offers the
  card before its own. Its own stream is `agentCompRng_`, so it cannot shift the actor
  family's sampling.
* The hero has to be an actor with an agent: `h.actorAgent` is set by the actor family's hire card.
* The agent's gender is not stored by the hire card, but the name it drew came from
  a16_casino-casino-celebrity-name-enc, which carries a Gender column: the card reads the gender
  back by name, and only falls back to a coin when the name is not in the table (a fallback name).
* The three frames, the three titles, the two journal forms, the ignored line, the return
  compliment and the gender filters are transcribed. The band moves
  `h.actorAgentOpinion` - the port's stand-in for the agent's relationship slot - by the same amounts,
  clamped at 100.

### Ceilings

* The card's frequency is a coin, not a copied roll: nothing in the binary pushes the card with a
  GetRandomNumber, so there is no rate to transcribe. The port uses 0.35 per actor-family turn
  that finds an agent.
* WillGiveHeroTimeOfDay is modelled as GetRandomNumber(0, 100) below the agent's opinion, its style
  being unrecovered; the `+0x330` field the ignored line compares against is the same field the port treats
  as that opinion, so the two readings of it are one number here.
* The bar graph has no meaning outside the card's own UI: the value is computed and dropped, the
  label literal is not printed.
* There is no year cache and no cooldown in the port: one card per year is trivially true when a
  year can hold only one card.
* The opinion change is not visible to the scripted run, so the bands are only checkable by reading
  this section's arithmetic beside the code.
* The dead third arm of the return-compliment roll (and its six titles, both formats and the hero
  stat stamp) is not implemented.
* `life[0x3ac]` is not incremented, its owner being unrecovered.

### Verified

* 22 cards over 80 acting lives (seeds 1-80, actor hero): every card is dismiss-only
  (`choice` null), titled from the three-title pool, at age 18 or later, with all stat deltas zero,
  and its table is a16_compliments-enc. Recorded rows: the compliment the body pays the agent.
* The three frames all appear (8 called, 7 told, 7 think), and the parenthesis-split sentence
  matches exactly one frame.
* The agent's name is a celebrity-name row, and its Gender agrees with the pronoun in the body -
  "he's" for a male row, "she's" for a female one.
* 12 of the 22 cards pay the hero back: "He called me a stud.", "He told me that I'm a god." -
  with the returning compliment a row of the same table open to the hero's gender.
* 1 card ignores the hero: the appended paragraph starts with the agent's pronoun.
* A hero who never acts draws no card at all (control run, seed 26).

## 326. The walk's animal encounter

The animals table has been sitting on disk unused since the vampire hunt (306) turned out to
draw its own pool: a16_animals-enc is the DataAnimal set behind the one animal card the game
pushes at random. The walk activity rolls for it, and the card is where the hero can be chased,
mauled and killed by an alligator. This section ports ScenarioEncounterAnimal.

### The native card

* The table is a16_animals-enc: Animal, Danger Score, Aggression Score, Skittishness Score,
  Attack String, Rabid Score, Continent, Vampire Essence Gain - 72 rows. DataHub::LoadAnimalSet
  (0x26d0cc4) fills it, and DataHub::GetRandomAnimalForContinent (0x28151cc) filters it by the
  hero's country continent and returns one uniformly.
* Class ScenarioEncounterAnimal: `.ctor` 0x372303c, RefreshScenario 0x3723060,
  ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x37233b8, ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x37241dc. Fields
  `+0x16a` `_happenedOnWalk` (the constructor sets it) and `+0x170` `_animal`.
* Title #18740 "Encounter". Body #70590 "{0}, you encounter {1}.\n\nWhat will you do?" with
  #46721 "While on your walk" and the animal's name through AddIndefiniteArticleToString.
* Choices in stored order: #36406 "Run for my life", #36124 "Retreat slowly", #44143 "Try to
  rescue it", #33638 "Pet it". The handler dispatches on the lowercased label (Contains "run",
  "retreat", "rescue", "pet"), not on the index.
* Run: an animal with Aggression 4 or more rolls GetRandomNumber(0,2) and chases on a zero;
  anything else is evaded (#24097 "I encountered {0} and ran for my life. I evaded it."). A
  chase logs #24096 "I encountered {0} and ran for my life but it chased me!".
* Retreat: GetRandomNumber(0,30)+1 against Aggression - inside it the animal chases (#24101
  "I encountered {0} and tried to retreat but it chased me!"), outside it the hero gets away
  (#24106 "I encountered {0} but retreated carefully.").
* Rescue and pet share one lane. Both need Danger 2 or more and Aggression 2 or more before the
  attempts are offered. The first roll is GetRandomNumber(0,20)+1 against 5-Skittishness: under
  it succeeds, and the success line is #24105 "I encountered {0} and {1} it." with {1} #66340
  "successfully rescued" or #59500 "gently caressed". A success also writes #49867
  "You {0} the {1}!", pays SimPerson::ImpactKarma(hero, 3) and fires the rescue achievements.
  Over it, GetRandomNumber(0,8)+1 against Aggression decides whether the failure is only
  embarrassing (#24104 "I encountered {0} and tried unsuccessfully to {1} it.") or the animal
  answers (#24102 "I encountered {0} and tried to {1} it.").
* The answer is the attack: #69707 "{0} The {1} {2} me!" with the row's own Attack String column
  and the hero's death through DeathManager::UpdateWithKillerAnimal (0x2b16ecc) and
  ScenarioDeathHero (0x3700fd0), described afterwards by #9457 "{pronoun} died after being
  {attack} by {animal}.".
* Rabies rides the attack: GetRandomNumber(0,15)+1 under the row's Rabid Score contracts the
  disease (skipped for a vampire or a hero who already carries it), through
  SimHero::ContractDiseaseTypeAndShouldBeDiagnosedImmediately (0x2a846c4) and the
  ScenarioDiseaseContract card.
* The push is the walk's ninth outcome: ScenarioWalk::ChoiceSelectedAtIndex (0x239d9fc) rolls
  GetRandomNumber(0,24/32/40) depending on the walk, and case 9 builds the card when the hero
  is 18 or over, has not seen it three times, has an animal for his continent and is not in
  prison. The other animal cards (outdoor ride, car drive, actor challenge, hustle) can never be
  random-pushed: their base eligibility is false and only this class and the zoo pregnancy card
  override it.

### The port

`Sim::animalEncounterYear` (src/sim.cpp) is its own family, gated on an adult hero who is not
in prison, with its own RNG (`animalRng_`) and tickets 1. The port has no walk activity, so the
card arrives as an annual family rather than out of the walk's roll (shortcut); the continent
filter, the four lanes and every roll and comparison are the native ones. The kill is handed to
`checkDeath` as an `AnimalAttack` cause with the row's Attack String in the sentence, which is
the shape the other card-owned deaths use.

### Ceilings

* The card's trigger is a family coin of 1 in 20 rather than the walk's ninth outcome, because
  the port has no walk activity; the native per-walk probability was not computed either (the
  roll's upper bound varies by walk).
* The "#69707" attack line keeps only its tail: the "

" prefix the {0} argument carries was not
  recovered, so the log line starts at "The {1} {2} me!".
* The pet-and-rescue gate's native jump destination (when Danger or Aggression is under 2) was
  not recovered; the port writes the plain unsuccessful line there (#24104) instead of whatever
  the game does.
* The achievement manager is not modelled, so the rescue achievements and "acKilledByHippo" fire
  nowhere.
* The hippopotamus special case (a String::Equals against #60315 that completes its own
  achievement) is not reproduced.
* #49867's crazy branch puts #11716 "Are you freaking crazy" where the verb goes, which reads
  oddly in a sentence; it is what the literal and the argument do, and the port keeps it.
* Which subset of the rescue achievements a given success fires was not decoded, so none do.
* The walk's own narrative lines around the card (and the three-presented limit) are not
  modelled: the port's card can fire more than three times in a life, four years apart.

### Verified (test_animal_encounter.py, US male)

    card:          "While on your walk, you encounter a swan.\n\nWhat will you do?", title
                   "Encounter", four labels, residue empty
    the row:       the animal named in the body is an a16_animals-enc row whose Continent cell
                   lists the hero's own continent (or says "all 7 continents"), and the event's
                   row is that row
    lanes:         "Run for my life", "Retreat slowly", "Try to rescue it", "Pet it"
    escapes:       "I evaded it." and "but retreated carefully." both appear in the sweeps, and
                   the chase lines appear too
    hands-on:      a rescue and a pet success each write "and successfully rescued it." /
                   "and gently caressed it.", the card appends "You ... the <animal>!", and the
                   year's karma delta is +3
    kill:          a chase ends in the animal's own Attack String (" The swan bit me!") and the
                   hero dies with the AnimalAttack cause
    cooldown:      two cards in one life are at least four years apart
    minor:         no card at 17
