## 325. The workplace discipline card

The coworker family (113, 114) gave the hero a supervisor and eight incident cards, and the
supervisor card (117) gave him a team-building day, but the card the incident cards exist to
produce - the supervisor calling the hero in over an allegation, then warning or firing him -
was still missing. This section ports ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineSupervisor.

### The native card

* Class ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineSupervisor: `.ctor` 0x2992cac, RefreshScenario 0x299c290,
  ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x299c6ac.
* Title #47160 "Workplace Discipline".
* Body #50694 "Your {0}, {1}, has called you into {2} office to discuss allegations that you
  {3}." wrapped by #68658 "{0}\n\nHow will you react?". {3} is the allegation the pushing
  incident card recorded, {1} the coworker's name and {2} the supervisor's possessive pronoun.
* The eight incident cards that push it, with the seriousness each feeds the decision:
  an untrue rumour #66088 "started an untrue rumor about your {0}, {1}" (2), an insult
  #55436 "called your {0}, {1}, {2}" (2; the {2} is DataInsult's own Insult column, filtered by
  the hero's gender and the vampire flag), a hookup advance #62015 "made a sexual advance on
  your {0}, {1}" (4), a gift #67236 "tried to give your {0}, {1}, {2}" (1; the {2} is
  DataGift::GetNameWithArticle over a16_gifts-enc), and four cards
  that share #54544 "attacked your {0}, {1}" (4). Their shared gate is a workplace and a
  supervisor, a coworker who is not the hero's current lover, and GetRandomNumber(0,2)==0.
* Choices in stored order: #11553 "Apologize for my actions", #17416 "Defend my actions",
  #26846 "Insult {0}", #44151 "Try to seduce {0} so {0} forgets". The handler dispatches on
  the lowercased label (Contains "apologize", "defend", "insult", "seduce").
* Every reaction adds its seriousness to SimWorkplace+0x24 first. Apologize: severity -5 and
  #68956 "{0}\nI apologized for my actions.". Defend: severity +5 and #69053
  "{0}\nI defended my actions to {1}.". Insult: supervisor -6, Life+0x3a8 (the insulted
  counter) incremented, one of three insult sentences (#47966/#49529/#49527 - details under
  the ceilings) and a plain follow-up card titled one of #39989 "Stay classy", #40899 "Take
  that", #41445 "That's right" or #48825 "You heard me". The other lanes push their own plain
  follow-up card, titled one of #46403 "What happened now?", #15516 "Chewed out", #40840 "Tail
  between your legs", #16200 "Consequences" or #32904 "Oooh someone's in trouble". Seduce,
  success: ScenarioSupervisorSeduceSuccess is pushed and the
  decision is skipped. Seduce, rejected: #50762 "Your {0}, {1}, rejected your attempt to
  seduce {2}!", #68978 "{0}\nI attempted to seduce {1} but failed.", supervisor -5,
  ImpactWorkplacePerformance(-4) and severity +20.
* The decision, all of it in ChoiceSelectedAtIndex: the seriousness picks a multiplier for
  the supervisor's strictness (SimCoworker+0x244; 0.25, 0.5, 1.1 and about 204 for
  seriousness 1, 2, 3 and 5; seriousness 4 carries no strictness term), then
  score = severity + 0.5 * (strictness * multiplier + (100 - relationship strength)), with
  the strength from SimPerson::GetTotalHeroRelationshipStrength (0x2c46f14). The follow-up
  pass showed that getter sums no family graph at all: it reads the one float field
  SimPerson+0x118 (clamped 0-100), adding 50 only while the AuraRing perk is enabled and the
  person is not the hero's current lover, and returning a flat 150 when the hero is. Over 85 with strength under
  95 terminates, over 85 with 95 or better warns, at or below 70 warns, and in between
  terminates only when (100 - strength) beats GetRandomNumber(0,200).
* The warning lane: a supervisor whose professionalism (SimCoworker+0x240) is below a 0-25
  draw while the relationship is above 80 gives the lenient #70336 "{0} told you not to
  worry about it.". Otherwise a row of a16_supervisor-warnings-enc (31 rows, "<supervisor>"
  and "<he/she>" tokens) is appended and the journal is #69156 "{row}\nI received a
  warning.". No repeat-offence counter exists anywhere in the class.
* Before a termination the card files a reaction line drawn with GetRandomNumber(0,5): #70292
  "{0} shook {1} head and sighed.", #70509 "{0} {1} you!", #69859 "{0} asked what's wrong
  with you!", #70341 "{0} told you to collect your belongings and get out of {1} sight!" and
  #69884 "{0} called security to escort you out of the building!".
* Termination: ScenarioJobTermination(8) in a job - body #48756 "You have been {0} from your
  position as {1} for {2} for disciplinary issues.", journal #25739, reason row "Disciplinary
  Issues" #17783 - or ScenarioMilitaryTermination(8) in the military, whose title is
  "Dishonorable Discharge" and whose body is #48660 "You have been dishonorably discharged
  from the {0}.".

### The port

Sim::workplaceDisciplineYear (src/sim.cpp) is a wheel family named "workplace-discipline"
that sits beside the supervisor family, draws from its own stream (discRng_) and needs a
job or military service, age 18, no prison and a four-year gap. Because the port has none of
the eight incident cards, the family draws the allegation itself: the five reasons above,
with the gift and the insult filling their third placeholder from a16_gifts-enc and
insultToken(). It renders the recovered sentence and the four labels, adds the seriousness to
a trouble-points field, applies the reaction's severity and relationship move, then runs the
recovered decision and writes either the warning row (with the table and row named) or the
termination, prefixed by one of the reaction lines. Each supervisor's strictness,
professionalism, coolness and starting relationship are drawn on his first discipline card
the way PersonGenerator::GenerateRandomCoworkerInCompanyAndHeroCareerAndInPlaceAndIsSupervisor
(0x3382940) draws them: professionalism 0 to 20 on one draw in three and 0 to 100 otherwise,
strictness 0 to 100, coolness 0 to 100 (re-rolled to 0 to 20 half the time when the
professionalism came out under 20), and the relationship from
SetRandomHeroRelationshipStrength(0, 11, 20 or 40 or 50) tiered on that coolness - under 30
gives 20 to 30, up to 70 gives 40 to 50, above 70 gives 50 to 60.

### Ceilings, all deliberate

* The supervisor's personality is created here rather than by a workplace refresh, because the
  port has no SimWorkplace coworker array to generate him into: the first discipline card
  draws strictness, professionalism, coolness and the starting relationship exactly as
  PersonGenerator does (below). The decision reads them like the native one.
* A successful seduction queues the morning-after card the port already has (REPORT 123)
  instead of ScenarioSupervisorSeduceSuccess' own text, and the rejected-seduction lane's
  ImpactWorkplacePerformance(-4) has no port model.
* Insulting the supervisor still writes no journal line. The follow-up recovery found the aim:
  the lane picks one of three sentences uniformly - #47966 "You called your {0}, {1}, {2}."
  with journal #69007 "{0}\nI called {1} {2}.", #49529 "You told your {0}, {1}, that {2}
  {3}." and #49527 "You told your {0}, {1}, that you think {2} {3}." - and then a plain
  follow-up card titled one of #39989 "Stay classy", #40899 "Take that", #41445 "That's
  right" or #48825 "You heard me". The argument chains of the two "told" variants were not
  recovered, so the port writes neither the line nor the follow-up card.
* The HR discipline card (ScenarioWorkplaceDisciplineHR, 0x298d34c) is not ported. Its own
  body was not recovered, but its arithmetic was: it adds its seriousness to the same
  trouble-points field and then fires the job or military termination when
  int(strictness * multiplier + troublePoints * (10 in the military, else 5)) reaches 26 and
  GetRandomNumber(0,200) comes in under that score. Because the supervisor card now keeps the
  same trouble-points field, a ported HR card would inherit the accumulator as it stands.
* Trouble points are written but never read by the port's own decision, which is the native
  supervisor arithmetic; in the game they are read only by that HR card.
* The termination's reaction line is drawn among four of the five native lines: the middle
  one, #70509 "{0} {1} you!", needs a random-verb pool the recovery could not reach.
* The warning table's rows with slash alternatives ("<lenient/forgiving/...>") are skipped
  rather than printed with their slashes, since the family has no pool walker.
* The termination card's own buttons and the two follow-up cards are folded into the same
  year: the warning-or-firing decision resolves here and the job is cleared here.
* The reaction journal lines keep only the literal's tail: #68956 and #69053 open with a {0}
  the native code fills, and that prefix is not plumbed.
* #44151 dumps "Try to seduce {0} so {0} forgets" with the same placeholder twice while the
  native code formats two arguments (the object pronoun and then the subject pronoun). The
  port prints "Try to seduce him so he forgets", the shape the two arguments imply; a strict
  single-index Format would print "him so him forgets".

1 FAIL). The failure was test-side and was fixed here without a code change: a hero whose

## 324. The casino's complimenting gambler

The complaint card (322) got a punter with a grievance; the positive twin - a punter telling the hero the
floor is wonderful - shipped with the same expansion and was still missing. This section ports
ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplimentGame and, in passing, closes two fidelity gaps in 322.

### The native card

* Class ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplimentGame: `.ctor` 0x3572578 (tail-calls Scenario::.ctor(false),
  so no dismiss button), RefreshScenario 0x3571344, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x3571cf8,
  ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 0x3572134. Fields: 0x170 the assembled narrative, 0x178 the casino,
  0x180 the gambler.
* SimCasino::IncrementAge queues it at 0x2aacf04 (eligibility call), 0x2aacf08 (skip when not eligible)
  and 0x2aacf24 (constructor). The push draws no RNG at all: every casino card in that chain is gated by
  its ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush override and the first eligible one wins the year.
* Title #16100 "Compliment". The exterior title is never written, so it keeps the class default.
* Body = Concat(sentence, #46 "\n\n", the parsed row, #146 "\n\nWhat will you do?"), where the sentence
  is #50268 "Your casino's " + the gambler's relationship word + #5282 ", " + the full name + #5672
  ", is complimenting your casino for having " + the possessive + #1953 " favorite game, " + the game
  name run through CapitalizeAllMajorWordsInString + #6312 ".". The row comes from
  DataHub::GetRandomCasinoGamblerGameRoomComplimentForHappiness (0x26c89bc) over
  a16_casino-gambler-game-room-compliment-enc (String, Min Gambler Happiness, Max Gambler Happiness),
  banded by the punter's happiness; the parser is handed the gambler as its person and the class registers
  no bracket dictionary, so the row's own <he/she> tokens resolve against that punter only.
* RefreshScenario also stores the default journal line: #25215 "I thanked my casino's gambler, " + the
  name + #5547 ", for " + the possessive + #1659 " compliment about my casino.".
* Choices, in stored order: #41215 "Thank " + object pronoun, #21649 "Give " + object pronoun + #3411
  " some free games", #26366 "Ignore " + object pronoun. The handler dispatches on the lowercased label
  (Contains "thank" #66726, "games" #59394, "ignore" #60762).
* Effects. Thank: addiction -1, then the casino's negative vtable slot at -1 and its positive slot at +1,
  and the default journal line stands. Give: addiction +2, the same two slots at -2 and +2, and the line
  is extended with #341 "\nI gave my casino's gambler, " + name + #5857 ", some free games after " + the
  subject pronoun + #1660 " complimented my casino.". Ignore: the line is extended with #351
  "\nI ignored my casino's gambler, " + name + #5350 ", after " + the subject pronoun + #1660, and
  SimCasino::ImpactPopularity(-2) is applied. Every branch ends by logging the narrative through
  LifeLog::Log and refreshing the UI; nothing else is written - no money, no follow-up scenario, no table
  snippet lookup.
* Gates: a casino is owned, the gambler list is not empty, a favourite-game pre-check passes (hard AND,
  the predicate is the complaint card's shape: a punter's favourite game that the casino does not install),
  hero age 18 or over, not in prison, and Life::YearsSinceScenario of this class is greater than 4.
* Draw order inside the card: the gambler, the favourite game, then the compliment row. The choice handler
  and the push site draw nothing.

### The port

Sim::casinoComplimentYear (src/fam/casino.cpp) is a wheel family named "casino-compliment" whose ready
gate is casino ownership, sitting beside "casino-complaint" and drawing from the same casino card stream
(casinoCardRng_), so this card cannot shift any other family's sequence. It keeps the punter, the game and
the row in per-card state that is cleared on entry (one card, one punter - without the clear the previous
card's punter leaked into the next), renders the recovered sentence and row, offers the three native
labels with the recovered pronouns, applies the two slot moves and the addiction change, and writes the
same three journal shapes. The five-year cooldown is a value on the Hero (casinoComplimentAge) rather than
a native scenario clock. Sim::pickBandRow (src/sim.cpp) was added for it: the native band table is filtered
first and one row drawn, where the older pickWindow retried three times and could fall out of band.

The same edit set closes two gaps in the complaint card: its body now carries the mood row from
a16_casino-casino-game-room-complaint-enc banded by the floor's happiness (before it printed the sentence
only, dropping what the native Concat appends), and its two short labels now carry the punter's pronoun
plus, for a ban, the #2104 " from my casino" tail, so a ban reads "Ban her from my casino" as the native
label builds it rather than the punter's name.

Ceilings, all deliberate:

* The two casino vtable slots the native code moves (+0x738 and +0x508) are still unidentified, so the
  port pairs one with the floor's popularity and the other with its gambler happiness, and the complaint
  card's refusal-crazy band (gambler craziness) is approximated by that happiness value, as in 322.
* The native picks a random punter and a favourite game the casino installs from live game objects; the
  port has no gambler entities, so the name and game come from the same resolve tokens the complaint card
  uses.
* The native queues at most one casino card a year and the first eligible one wins; the port lets each
  family draw its own coin, so both casino cards can land in the same year.
* SimCasino::IncrementAge's own yearly books (319) run first, so the card always quotes a casino that has
  already aged that year.
* The card never moves money natively, so neither does the port; a hero who is skint still gets it.
* CapitalizeAllMajorWordsInString is reproduced with a small local helper (src/fam/casino.cpp), and
  <a/b/c> alternatives inside a row are drawn from the casino card stream rather than a card-local RNG.

### Corrections to 322

* The complaint card's body carries the mood row as well; the earlier section described the sentence only.
* The complaint buttons carry the punter's pronoun (#12770 "Ban " / #26366 "Ignore "), and a ban appends
  #2104 " from my casino"; the earlier section said the labels append the gambler's name.

2 FAIL). Both failures are test-side and were fixed here without a code change: the new
family's wheel ticket moved the first "Wish them well" branch of the lover-leaves card

## 323. The car's condition, the repair card and the scrap push

Every other vehicle in this port is a purchase lane (car, boat, aircraft) with no state behind it: the hero pays and the money is gone. The native game keeps a real car object, runs a breakage check on it every age-up and hands the hero a repair card when something falls off, so this section gives the port its first structured car and ports ScenarioCarRepair and the car scrap push.

The check lives in SimHero::IncrementAge (0x2b12b1c, called from 0x2a6c5f4). It reads the model's Reliability Score and turns it into a ceiling: 100 for a score of 1 down to 5 for a score of 5, so a score of 1 is the most breakable car and 5 the least. It draws A = GetRandomNumber(0, ceiling) and B = GetRandomNumber(0, 20), and the car needs work when Condition + B < A. A car with work outstanding queues ScenarioCarRepair; a car whose condition is gone queues the *ScrapPush lane instead, and the repair card is not offered.

The part is picked from a16_car-parts-enc (0x2804e4c) by appending each row's Break Commonness Score to a candidate list and drawing one entry, so a part with a score of 5 comes up five times as often as one with a score of 1. The row carries the part's name, its Base Cost and the Broken Terms the card quotes. The price (0x2804f88) is part.BaseCost * (model.Cost / 30000) once the model costs 30000 or more, times a multiplier M this port has not recovered (M = 1 here, the only ceiling that changes a number).

The card is ScenarioCarRepair (ctor 0x3557134, Refresh 0x3559384, Choice 0x3559924). Its title is the car itself, Format(#70426 '{0} {1}', make, model); its body is #50813 'Your {0}car has {1}.' with the make and model in {0} (plus the word #66160 'stolen ' when the car has been stolen, a state this port does not model) and the part's Broken Terms in {1}, wrapped by #68715 "{0}\n\nWhat will you do?". Two rows sit above the buttons: #35747 'Repair' and #45558 'Vehicle Condition'. The buttons are #35752 'Repair it', #45180 'Use the Golden Wrench' and #24668 'I might fix it later'; the handler dispatches on the lowercased label (Contains "use" and Contains "later"), which is why the Golden Wrench lane can be left out without moving the other two.

Repairing charges the row's price through AdjustBankBalanceByAmount(-cost) (0x3559fec) and writes exactly one piece of state: the car's ActiveRepair is cleared. It does not move the condition, does not restamp AgeAtLastRepair and does not touch the scrap flag, and it logs #70735 '{0}I repaired the {1} on my {2}.'. Declining charges nothing, leaves ActiveRepair set (so the card comes back next year) and logs #69029 '{0}\nI decided not to repair it.'. When the balance will not cover the row the native game opens ScenarioInsufficientFinances (0x37c6e98) instead of charging, with #67050 'to repair your {0}' as its item.

The scrap push (0x355a730) is the end of the line: #50259 'Your car will no longer start and is beyond repair.', a row pair #10954 'Age' / #69718 '{0} Years', the single button #38269 'Scrap it' and the log #24329 'I had to scrap my {0} {1}.'. It pays nothing - the car is gone and no money changes hands.

The port keeps the car on the Hero rather than in a SimCar array. carMake/carModel/carCondition were already there for the racing lane, so this section adds ownsCar, carCost (the model's Cost, the price scale), carReliability, carNeedsRepair, carPart, carBrokenTerms, carRepairCost, carYearAtLastRepair and carYearsOwned. Sim::ensureCarFields draws make/model/cost/reliability out of a16_car-models-enc once; Sim::carRepairYear runs the check, picks the part, prices it and renders one of the two cards. The family sits in the wheel with three tickets and its own carRng_ stream, so the roll cannot shift another family's sequence. The harness grew three keys for it: "car" gives the hero a car, "carCondition" and "carReliability" seed the two numbers the roll reads.

The Golden Wrench button is an in-app purchase this port does not carry, so a car the hero cannot afford shows one lane only ("I might fix it later") instead of the native two, and the insufficient-funds card is folded into that: the port never opens a repair card it cannot pay for. Three further ceilings: the condition drifts down by one on a quarter of quiet years (the native accidents and race damage that move it are not ported); the damage roll and the part pick happen once per break rather than the native per-check; and a car is scrapped when its condition reaches 0, which no ported lane can cause on its own, so the scrap card is reached through the "carCondition" fixture.

Verified (test_car_repair.py, seed 7, US male, cash 50000):

    repair card:  age 16   title 'Mazda CX-3'   $500   condition 50
    charge:      500 exactly, stopping both lives at the card's year
    decline:     'I decided not to repair it.'  nothing charged
    broke hero:  3 cards, every one offering only 'I might fix it later'
    scrap card:  age 16   'I had to scrap my Mazda CX-3.'   money unchanged, never twice
    no car:      no repair card and no scrap card on seeds 1..5

## 322. The casino's complaining gambler

The casino had an economy (319), a bankruptcy (320) and a zoo (321) but no card about a punter with a
grievance, even though the native game ships one with three buttons. This section ports
ScenarioCasinoAgeUpGamblerComplaintGame.

### The native card

* Title #16066 "Complaint" (exterior title #15240 "Casino").
* Body: concatenated literals, not a format template — #50268 "Your casino's " + the gambler's
  relationship word + #5282 ", " + the name + #5667 ", is complaining that your casino doesn't have "
  + the possessive + #1953 " favorite game, " + the game + "."
* Body, second half (added in 324): Concat also appends #46, the parsed row of
  a16_casino-casino-game-room-complaint-enc banded by the floor's gambler happiness, and #146
  "\n\nWhat will you do?".
* Choices: #12770 "Ban ", #11554 "Apologize for the inconvenience", #26366 "Ignore ". The two short
  labels end in a space because the native card appends the punter's pronoun, and a ban appends
  #2104 " from my casino" as well (corrected in 324).
* Effects: a ban costs the house two popularity points and reports what the gambler did, drawn from
  a16_casino-banned-gambler-snippet-enc banded by gambler craziness (Snippet, Log Version, Min/Max
  Gambler Craziness); apologising raises the floor's addiction by two points; ignoring costs two
  popularity points. The card consumes no other state.
* Eligibility: hero age 18 or over, not in prison, a casino owned, at least two years since the last
  one (0x3564f24's ladder).

### The port

Sim::casinoComplaintYear (src/fam/casino.cpp) is a wheel family named "casino-complaint" whose ready
gate is the casino's ownership, with its own stream (casinoCardRng_, REPORT.en.md 322) so the card
cannot move another family's draws for the seed. On firing it renders the recovered body, offers the
three native labels, appends the banned-gambler snippet for a ban and pushes its Log Version as a log
line.

Ceilings, all deliberate:

* The relationship word's ladder is unrecovered. Five rank words exist in the literal table
  (Beginner #13333, Amateur #11239, Novice #32248, Regular #35559, High Roller #22919) and the port
  already models five gambler styles (319), so style N is called rank word N. The words are native, the
  pairing is the port's.
* Gambler craziness is not tracked, so the banned-gambler snippet is banded by the floor's happiness
  instead.
* The card's fire rate is the port's (one in ten eligible years); the native card is queued by the
  scenario eligibility ladder, whose own rate is not recovered.
* The gambler's name comes from the existing <casino-gambler> token, which draws from the main stream,
  so a firing card moves later draws; the card's own choices do not.
* The popularity and addiction effects are wired to the port's hero fields but the script harness
  exposes neither, so the test pins the text and the labels rather than the numbers.

### Verified

tools/test_casino_complaint.py, casino seeded solvent so the bankruptcy card cannot close the floor
first:

* the card fires on a solvent casino, body matches the recovered concatenation (tier, name, "is
  complaining that your casino doesn't have", possessive, "favorite game", game), and the choice is
  one of the three native labels;
* a forced ban appends one snippet paragraph and at most one, that snippet is a row of the
  banned-gambler table, and the event carries no stat deltas;
* forced apologize and forced ignore render the two-button bodies without a snippet;
* a hero without a casino never sees the card, and a casino closed by the bankruptcy card never draws
  one afterwards.

## 321. The zoo's books and the federal inspector

Section 320 modelled a casino that drowns. The zoo has the same shape and, unlike the casino, it
does not close on a timer: the inspector warns first, and the hero can buy the park another year.
This section adds the zoo's pot, its losing-year counter and the warning card.

### The counter

SimZoo+0x148 is NumYearsZooHasNegativeBankBalance. The annual pass adds the year's profit to
BankBalance (SimZoo+0x28) and resets the counter when the pot is no longer negative (the single
store at 0x2b599b0, the reset at 0x2b599a8). At three consecutive losing years the pass compares
(0x2b5a0bc) and queues ScenarioZooAgeUpBankrupt (ctor 0x29a3370, Refresh 0x29a337c, Choice
0x29a3780) - and, unlike the casino, it does not reset the counter, so the warning returns every
year the books stay red.

### The warning card

* ExteriorTitle #50857 "Zoo", Title #12796 "Bankrupt", no dismiss button.
* Body #41980: "The federal inspector is informing you that your zoo has accrued too much debt to
  keep it operational."
* Affordable branch: body += #137 ("\n\nThey said if you don't do something about it right now,
  the government will confiscate your zoo.\n\nWhat will you do?"), choices #27219 "Invest more
  money" and #28743 "Let it go".
* Unaffordable branch: one choice #32432 "OK". Body = Concat(#41980, #46 "\n\n", the inspector's
  pronoun He #22743 or She #38849, #3283 " said because you don't have the funds in your bank
  account to bring it out of debt, ", #60155 "he's" or #65541 "she's", #2351 " immediately
  confiscating your zoo."). The recovered order reads awkwardly; the literals are transcribed, not
  paraphrased.

"Let it go" and the single OK both run ShutDownZoo (0x2b623f4): the park leaves the live life for
SimPast.ZooList, with no log line and no hero money (the pot was never hero money). "Invest more
money" spawns ScenarioZooAgeUpBankruptInvest (ctor 0x29a3b40): title #27203 "Invest", body #27214
"Invest in your zoo today!", an amount input bounded by the shortfall plus one and the hero's
capital, and its action debits the wallet into the zoo pot and the park's total investment, then
chains body #50400 "Your investment kept your zoo afloat for at least another year!". The narrative
is Concat(#24498 "I invested ", the amount, #3761 " to save my zoo.").

### The port

* Hero gains zooBank, zooNegativeYears, zooLedgerYear and zooBankruptQueued (game.h); pending kind
  25 is the inspector's card (sim.h).
* Sim::zooRunYear runs from Sim::ageUpYear on the hero's own tick beside the casino pass, guarded so
  it cannot run twice for one age, and settles the year against the pot. Three losing years queue the
  card, one request at a time.
* Sim::zooBankruptYear renders both branches, and the invest lane charges exactly the shortfall and
  renders the native follow-up line in the same card.
* The harness key zooBank seeds the pot, exactly like casinoBank in section 320.
* Section 65's money handling moved: the zoo function no longer charges upkeep straight to the
  wallet or credits the gate take, because the books now own both numbers.

Ceiling: the native profit formula is not recovered, so the pass calls the difference between the
port's own gate take (ticket * (animals + attractions) * 900) and its upkeep (2500 per animal, 5000
per attraction) the year's profit. Those two numbers were already this port's model of the park.

### Verified

tools/test_zoo_bankrupt.py, with the pot seeded through zooBank:

* a debt of a billion: one single-button card, body exactly the recovered concatenation above, no
  stat deltas, the park closed and no zoo card after it, and the card never arrives twice;
* the wallet matches a life with a far smaller debt, because closing charges nothing and the depth
  of the debt never reaches the wallet;
* an affordable debt: the two-button body exactly as above, the harness default "Let it go", and no
  zoo card afterwards;
* the investment lane (forced through the padding recipe): body ends with the native follow-up, the
  log reads "I invested $901,000 to save my zoo.", the park keeps drawing zoo cards afterwards, and
  the hero ends poorer than the life that let the zoo go;
* a debt the books can clear (five thousand) never calls the inspector in, over six seeds.

The full 109-test suite passed on the binary these notes describe
(62b33fd3f1bd67d34bf47bdd8bb55067cebce38f699f6ddb93e9fe13cc94b955).

### Ceilings

* The profit formula is the port's pair of numbers, not the native arithmetic.
* The native amount input cannot be typed in a script: the port invests exactly the shortfall, and
  the native follow-up card is folded into the same card instead of being chained.
* The native pass re-queues the warning every losing year; the port keeps one request open, so a
  second drain cannot show it twice.
* The recovered unaffordable sentence is literal-by-literal and reads awkwardly; it is not smoothed.
* Shutting the zoo down clears the port's park fields; the native move to SimPast.ZooList (and what
  the past list keeps) is not modelled.
* In "only" harness mode "ages" is the hero's age cap (the section 318 note).

## 320. The casino's bankruptcy: six losing years and a card that closes the house

Section 319 gave the casino a pot (BankBalance, SimCasino+0x28) and a yearly pass that moves it. A
house that bleeds money never closed: the pot simply went further negative. This section adds the
native counter and the card that ends it.

### The timer

SimCasino::IncrementAge tests the pot at 0x2aac7d4. While it is negative an int counter at
SimCasino+0x88 is incremented (store 0x2aac7e0, compare 0x2aac7e4); when the counter reaches 6
(0x2aac7ec) the pass calls CancelAllCasinoScenarios (0x2aac7f0) and queues
ScenarioCasinoAgeUpBankrupt (ctor 0x2aac80c), then resets the counter. The counter is not reset
when the card is queued, so any later losing year starts the climb again - in practice the casino
is gone by then.

Port side: Hero::casinoBankruptYears, incremented at the tail of Sim::casinoRunYear
(src/fam/casino.cpp) while casinoBank < 0, and at six it queues kPendingCasinoBankrupt and resets.
The pass itself draws no RNG, so the casino stream order from section 319 is unchanged.

### The card

* ExteriorTitle #15240 "Casino", Title #12796 "Bankrupt".
* Body #50267: "Your casino has been bankrupt for 5 years.\n\nYou were forced to close it for
  good." The literal says five years while the code fires on the sixth consecutive negative year;
  the port keeps both facts as they are.
* No dismiss button; the only choice is #32661 "Ok" (Refresh 0x3564dbc, handler 0x3564f50).

The handler (0x3564f50) calls ShutDownCasino (0x2ab3e10), logs, and refreshes the interface. It
writes no hero money, no hero stat, no room, amenity or zone state - the strb at 0x73f39fef78 is an
il2cpp class-init guard. ShutDownCasino moves the casino out of the live life, which the port models
by clearing ownsCasino, the pot, the rooms, games, amenities and the gambler bookkeeping.

### The zoo is not a mirror

SimZoo::IncrementAge (0x2b592bc) keeps the same sort of counter (SimZoo+0x148, threshold 3) but the
card it queues, ScenarioZooAgeUpBankrupt (ctor 0x29a3370), is a warning: body #41980, choices
#27219 "Invest more money" and #28743 "Let it go", where investing spawns
ScenarioZooAgeUpBankruptInvest with the shortfall in +0x180 and an amount input bounded by the
hero's capital. That chain is a later unit, not this one.

### Verified

With the pot seeded at -1,000,000,000 through the harness key casinoBank (a pot that can never
recover in the years a test can afford to run):

* the card lands at age 23 with the sixth losing year, body and choice exactly as above, and no
  stat deltas;
* capping the life at age 22 shows no card;
* after the closing card no Casino Ledger appears, and no life sees the card twice;
* the hero's money is identical to a control run with a solvent pot (2,940,000 on seed 7 - the
  missing 60,000 is the tuition of section 317, which both lives pay), because closing the casino
  charges nothing;
* a pot left at zero closes the house on seeds 2, 3 and 4 at age 23 and never closes it on seeds 1,
  5 and 6: the default house is not always losing, so the card is a consequence of the books, not
  of the harness.

tools/test_casino_bankrupt.py covers all of it; the full 108-test suite passed on the same binary
(bee47b9df9a7467de1df08952fa7eceee0c4515b6b0f76bae4fc0d30779adde3) that these sections describe.

### Ceilings

* The consumer order of the review card and the bankruptcy card in the same year is unrecovered;
  the port drains pending cards in queue order.
* The card frequency is the native counter, but the port's pass runs on the hero age-up only, so a
  year that draws no casino card can still close the house - native does the same, the card just
  arrives on the next pending drain.
* The five-year wording against the six-year threshold is native behaviour, not a port typo.
* Clearing the rooms and amenities approximates ShutDownCasino, whose exact field set was not
  walked; the pot and the hero wallet are the parts the tests pin.
* In "only" harness mode "ages" is the hero's age cap (see section 318's harness note), which is why
  the boundary test uses 22 and 23.

## 319. The casino's books: a silent yearly pass and the Casino Ledger card

Every other casino card in the port was a menu: it drew a few state values and printed a
sentence. The economy behind the casino was never modelled — buying a house paid for nothing,
and the yearly age-up ran no books at all. This section adds the pass and the card that reports
it.

### The pass

`SimCasino::IncrementAge` (vaddr 0x2aac1cc) runs once per hero age-up, whatever cards the year
draws, and it is silent: no LifeLog, no hero stat, no hero money. The port calls the same pass
from `Sim::casinoRunYear` (`src/fam/casino.cpp`), hooked into `Sim::ageUpYear` beside the
student-loan pass, and guarded so it cannot run twice for one age.

Draws happen in this order, and the order matters because a casino has its own stream:

1. per act: no draw in `IncrementAge` itself (0x2aac568);
2. per room: `SimCasinoGameRoom::SimulateAgeUpGames` (0x2abb0f8), four draws per installed
   unit — RNG(5,10), the room popularity band, the casino type band, then RNG(0,100) for the
   house-win roll — and two more per room afterwards;
3. per amenity: no draw (0x2aac63c);
4. `GetWagersPlaced` (0x2aad560): exactly one RNG(20,70), then a punter loop with no draw;
5. `GetGameRoomRevenue`: no draw;
6. `GetEntertainmentRevenue`: per act RNG(20,61) then RNG(60,101);
7. `GetAnnualAmenitiesRevenue`: per amenity the popularity band, then the type-4/5 band;
8. expenses and the tax rate: no draw;
9. the scenario eligibility ladder for the year's cards.

### Rooms

Per installed unit the game counts bets like this: `w21 = RNG(5,10)`, plus RNG(30,70) at room
popularity above 80, RNG(10,50) at 40–80 and RNG(5,30) at 40 or below, plus a type band —
RNG(0,10) at casino type 1, RNG(10,15) at 2, RNG(15,20) at 3, RNG(20,25) at 4, RNG(25,30) at 5.
The stake is `MinBetAmount * multiplier * w21` with multipliers 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.25 and 2.0 for
those types — no draw picks the multiplier. The house keeps the unit's wager when
`HouseWinRate >= RNG(0,100)`. Afterwards the room draws RNG(1,3) twice: once for a signed
popularity move inside 0..100, once to drift the house win rate.

A room's capacity is `BaseUnitCapacity + 5 * (type - 1)` (0x2abb4fc), its yearly cost is the
cost-of-living-adjusted `CostPerUnit * units` (0x2abb914), and a room's popularity is its own
0..100 float, not the casino's.

### Punters, amenities, expenses, tax

The punter side is one RNG(20,70) and then a deterministic walk over the gambler list, so a
punter's stake is a function of the floor's stats.

An amenity scores `themeTerm + popBand + typeBand`: +200 when the amenity's Theme matches the
casino's, otherwise −50; plus RNG(50,100) at casino popularity 40 or below, RNG(100,150) at
40–80 and RNG(150,200) above; plus RNG(300,500) at type 5 or RNG(100,200) at type 4. The score is
a percentage: `revenue = score / 100 * 12 * MonthlyExpenses`. An amenity's yearly cost is simply
`12 * MonthlyExpenses`, and amenities carry no popularity of their own — their
BasePopularityImpact feeds the casino's.

`GetAnnualExpenses` (0x2aadef8) adds, in order: every amenity's 12 months, the celebrity's
Salary, the celebrity's extra expenses, every act's Salary, every room's adjusted cost per unit
times units, and finally the casino's own 12 months of `GetMonthlyExpenses`. That last one
(0x2ab2d5c) cost-of-living adjusts the structure row's `Base Monthly Cost` with a floor of 100
and rounds to 100. Only the rooms and the monthly cost carry the cost-of-living ratio.

Then, in `IncrementAge` (0x2aac65c..0x2aac788):

```
payouts   = (roomWagers + gamblerWagers) - roomHouseWins - gamblerHouseWins
gross     = gamblingRevenue + entertainmentRevenue + amenityRevenue
taxable   = gross - expenses
taxes     = max(0, taxable * rate(taxable))
net       = gross - taxes - expenses + FirstYearGamblerProfits
bank     += net
```

`BankBalance` at SimCasino+0x28 is the **casino's** pot, not the hero's wallet: nothing in
`IncrementAge` credits `Hero.Money`. A casino that loses money pushes
`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpBankrupt`; the port does not model bankruptcy yet (see the ceilings).

The rate is `DataHub::GetTaxRateForUnadjustedIncomeInCountry`: the US ladder (10% to $9,325,
15% to $37,950, 25% to $91,900, 28% to $191,650, 33% to $416,700, 35% to $418,400, 39.6% above)
scaled by the country's Top Tax Rate against the US one. Measured: a $188,544 gross against
$134,000 expenses taxes at 25% of $54,544 = $13,636.

### The card

`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpAnnualReview` (refresh 0x3564230) is pushed every year its gate passes:
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` (0x3564d24) tests hero age 18 or over and not in prison, with
no RNG and no ownership check. Its exterior title is #15240 `Casino`, its title #15245
`Casino Ledger`, it has no dismiss button, its choice handler (0x73f39fed20) is a bare `ret`,
and its single choice is #32432 `OK`, so the card is pure reporting.

The body is the ledger feedback line plus #41701 `The annual report for your casino is now
available.` and the labelled rows — Wagers Placed, Payouts, Gambling Revenue, Performance
Revenue, Amenity Revenue, Taxes, Annual Expenses, Net Income — with the empty-house variant
#41702 `The annual report for your casino is now available.\n\nYour casino made no money.\n\nInstall
game rooms and amenities, or hire performers in order for your casino to be profitable.` in
place of the rows when no room, amenity, act or celebrity is installed. A bar labelled #34316
`Popularity` shows the casino's popularity.

The port renders that card with the same literals, the feedback window
`a16_casino-casino-ledger-feedback-enc` (Min Casino Popularity / Max Casino Popularity) and a
`My casino made {0} in revenue last year.` narrative line.

```
"only":"casino" seeds 1..24, ages 80:      26 Casino Ledger cards
seed 1, age 55:  wagers $42,531  payouts $15,987  gambling $26,544
                 amenity $162,000  taxes $13,636  expenses $134,000  net $40,908
tests: tools/test_casino_ledger.py green
```

### Ceilings

* How often the native casino card fires is not recovered: both the review card and the ordinary
  casino dumb-scenario card are queued in the same year and the consumer of that queue was not
  located. The port deals one casino card a year, so the ledger prints only in years where no
  other casino card claimed the year — measured above as roughly one a life.
* An act's salary and a celebrity's fee are runtime floats with no table column and no recovered
  producer, so the port prices neither: entertainment revenue and its share of the expenses stay
  at zero, and the act-side RNG(20,61)/RNG(60,101) pair is not drawn.
* The punter loop has no recovered expression; the port spreads the single RNG(20,70) over the
  punters by style, weights it by the room's popularity and lets HouseWinRate take its share.
* The cost-of-living ratio needs a reference country whose string is not recovered; the port uses
  the nominal amount with the native floor and rounding.
* Room popularity and house-win-rate drift: the sign draw is native, the drift magnitude toward
  the row's default is the port's.
* The port keeps a casino's rooms as installed at purchase time at `BaseUnitCapacity` units; the
  room-buying and upgrade cards (which change type and units) are not ported, so the type ladder
  is only ever used at the type the purchase row gave.
* Bankruptcy (`ScenarioCasinoAgeUpBankrupt`) is not implemented.

## 318. The mischief card: a friend, an activity, and a chance the police hear about it

`ScenarioCrimeDelinquencyPush` is the one delinquency card the played lives kept showing
(`{name} wants to get up to some mischief with you.`) and the port had no family for it. This
section recovers both halves — the push card (`RefreshScenario` 0x360eb10, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`
0x360ed74, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` 0x360f7ac) and the menu-side pull (`Ctor` 0x360bf3c,
`RefreshScenario` 0x360cabc, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x360cf28) — and wires the push into the port.
All addresses are 3.25.1 vaddrs.

**Who the friend is.** `GetAccomplice` 0x360e0d0 is deterministic: friends first (same place as the
hero, `SimPerson` +0xc0 outside a band, total hero relationship strength above a threshold, the
strongest kept), then the lover, then a sibling. The card formats that person into
`#70378 '{0} wants to get up to some mischief with you.\n\nWhat will you do?'` and offers
`#40427 'Sure, why not?'` / `#31851 "No, I'm not a troublemaker"`. The choice dispatches on
`ToLower(title)` containing `#66382 'sure'` or `#67261 'troublemaker'`.

**Refusing** is the whole payload of the polite branch: relationship -4, `ImpactDiscipline(+3)`,
`ImpactKarma(+3)`, and `#69215 '{0}\nI told {1} that I am no troublemaker.'` where `{0}` is a life
tag (one of `#39775 'Square alert'`, `#22120 'Goody two-shoes'`, `#29008 'Live a
little'`, `#31459 'Next time'`, `#40141 'Straight-laced lackey'`).

**Accepting** takes relationship +3, `ImpactDiscipline(-3)`, `ImpactKarma(-3)`, stamps the
accomplice's age field, logs `#69225 '{0}\nI told {1} that sounds great.'`, then draws one row from
`a16_delinquent-activities-enc` with
`DataHub::GetRandomDelinquentActivityForAgeAndHasAccomplice(age, hasAccomplice=1)`. The activity
text goes into `#47630 'You and {0} {1}.'` (duo) or `#49904 'You {0}.'` (solo) and the log form
`#69354 '{0}\n{1} and I {2}.'`. Life then keeps a mischief counter and a tag from the duo pool
`#26454 In deep together`, `#17481 Delinquent duo`, `#44049 Troublemaking`, `#30209 Mischief makers`,
`#33041 Our dirty secret`.

**Getting caught.** A row whose `Crime` cell is non-empty increments `Life.crimesAttempted` and
rolls `GetRandomNumber(0, chance[tier])` with the int table at 0xfc76cc = `[10, 7, 5, 4, 2]`
indexed by the row's `Charge Likeliness Score` tier; a row with no crime rolls a flat 20. A zero
means caught, and caught at 17 or older splices `GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType` — the port's own
`kPendingCrimeCharge` card, i.e. the 273 chain. Caught at 16 or under, with no criminal record in
the place of residence, splices `ScenarioRelationshipArgueInbound(arg2=8)` or a parent-punishment
variant instead.

**The port's card** (`Sim::mischiefYear`, own `mischiefRng_`) fires from the wheel with a 6% coin,
is gated on `age >= 8`, not in prison and `mischiefPresented < 3`, and requires the table. Both
branches are reachable because a forced choice bypasses the coin, exactly like the eye-exam and
sibling families. The accomplice comes from the existing `resolve("<friend>")` name pool, so the
identity gates of `GetAccomplice` are not modelled. The accept body is
`You and <name> <activity>.` and the refuse body keeps the native prompt shape.

Measured on the built binary (`tools/test_mischief.py`): seed 7, US male, cash 500, ages 40,
`choices[-1]*23 + [0]` → age 23 accept, friend `Mack D`, body `You and Mack D sold some pirated
copies of "Bohemian Rhapsody" at a local farmers market.`, karma and discipline -16 each; the same
padding with `[1]` → the prompt body and karma and discipline +16. Over 20 unforced lives the card
appeared 3 times in total, never more than once per life, youngest age 15. Seeds 1..40 with every
choice forced to `0` produce one catch: seed 27, age 34, `Criminal Mischief`, 2 years — the charge
card lands in the same year and names the table crime.

**The pull (menu card) is not ported.** `SimPlace` builds it from the Crime menu
`LifeInterface::GetCrimeList` 0x312a624, which shows a `#30205 'Mischief'` /
`#18805 Engage in some mischief` row at 8+. Accepting builds the accomplice array with up to five
entries (`DataHub::GetRandomStreetPersonAndMustBeInNeed`, `#10175 'A random {0}'`, then a
friend/child/lover/sibling pick), the prompt is `#50032 "You're thinking about possible accomplices
for your mischief.\n\nWho will you pick?"`, the dropdown label `#33826 'Pick your accomplice'` with
`#10673 'Act alone'` as its first row, and the single choice `#21491 'Get up to it'`. The commit
then re-rolls the crime chance on a second, different ladder (float table at 0xfc76b8 =
`[16, 12, 9, 7, 3]`, multiplied by wiliness: above 90 ×2, above 80 ×1.5, and halved below 5 or cut
to 0.3 below 10 attempted crimes). The port has no Crime menu and no accomplice selection, so none
of that is reachable and none of it was invented.

**Ceilings** (all of them visible in the code comments beside `Sim::mischiefYear`):

* No friend entities: the accomplice is always a generated name, so the relationship +3/-4, the
  `[p+0xc0]` bands and the "back out" gate of the pull are unmodelled.
* The `{0}` tag block of `#69225` / `#69215` has no home in the port, which models no life tags, so
  only the second half of each log line is rendered.
* `GetCrimeScenarioForCrimeType`'s own sentence length was not recovered; the port reuses the 273
  charge card and takes `crimeYears` from `{1, 1, 2, 3, 5}` by tier — a labelled shortcut.
* The caught-under-17 splice is unimplemented: neither target card exists in the port.
* The pull card, the juvenile branch, `Crime::get_Mischief`/`Scenario::PushBack`, and whoever queues
  the push (zero direct callers; the push catalogue is reflection-dispatched) stay unrecovered.
* The 6% coin is the port's own: no push rate was recovered. It is drawn on `mischiefRng_` so no
  other family's sequence moves for a given seed.

**Harness note.** A forced step skips that year's priority chain, so a padding length found in an
unforced run lands on a different card. Both test branches search the padding for the first step
whose `table` is `registry:ScenarioCrimeDelinquencyPush`.

## 317. The tuition screen and the student loan

An accepted university application hands the hero a card the port did not have:
`ScenarioSchoolFund` (`ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` 0x73f2a5b090). This section recovers it, the
four funding lanes it offers, and the `SimLoan` that one of those lanes creates. All addresses
are 3.25.1 vaddrs.

**The card.** Body `#23261 'How will you pay for your {0} program?'` over the five labels
`#20614 'Free public university'`, `#11616 'Apply for a student loan'`, `#11615 'Apply for a
scholarship'`, `#12168 'Ask my {0} to pay'`, `#33501 'Pay with cash'`. The dispatcher lowercases
the clicked label and tests substrings in a fixed order — `#59266 'free'`, `#66302 'student
loan'`, `#54429 'ask'`, `#65004 'scholarship'`, `#55533 'cash'` — then falls through to the
enrolment for any other label. The `{0}` in the body is the college row's `School`, taken from
`a16_colleges-enc` (row 0 is `Undergraduate`, `Years` 4, `Tuition` 15000).

**No money moves at the screen except on the cash lane.**

```
free         log #24117  'I enrolled in university for free thanks to {0} public education system.'
             body #47726 'You are now enrolled in {0}.'
loan         log #25337  'I took out a student loan to pay for my {0} tuition.'
             body #49557 'You took out a student loan to pay for your {0} tuition.'
             rejects #30702 criminal record / #50191 generic, #30701 age
scholarship  log #25614  'I was awarded a scholarship to {0}.'
             body #50189 'Your application for a scholarship to {0} has been awarded!'
             rejects #30700 / #50190
ask-parent   log #30902 accept / #30936 refuse over #64443 'refused' / #56645 "couldn't afford"
             / #55456 "can't afford", body #50558 accept / #50625 refuse
cash         no body and no log recovered
```

The free lane exists only where the country pays for college. `a16_countries-enc` gained two
fields in the port for this: `<FreeCollege>k__BackingField` (28 of the 102 countries set it —
Argentina, Australia, Austria, Bolivia, Brazil, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Egypt, Finland,
France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iran, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nicaragua and the rest) and
`<Adjectival>k__BackingField`, which fills `{0}` in the free-lane log.

**The loan.** `AddAnotherYearOfTuitionToStudentLoan` 0x73f300cd14 grows the principal by one
annual tuition for every college year, `BeginStudentLoanPayback` 0x73f300cc4c starts the payback
once the hero leaves college (log `#24386 'I have to start paying back my student loan for
{0}.'`), and `MakeAnnualPayment` 0x73f2fc2f2c takes twelve monthly instalments of the annuity
each year — `AdjustBankBalanceByAmount` with no floor, so the balance can go negative — with
`#24196 'I fully paid off my student loan for {0}.'` on the last one. `SimLoan.TermsForLoanType(1)`
is 5% over ten years with no down payment, so a 60,000 principal (four years at 15,000) costs
about 7,640 a year and clears on the eighth payment.

**What the port does.** `Sim::universityFundYear` (`_re/port/src/sim.cpp`) shows the lanes it
models — free when the country pays, then loan, scholarship and cash — and takes the cheapest
one the hero can get: free, else scholarship at 96 grades, else its own cash, else the loan. The
card is queued by the accepted application (`kPendingUniversityFund`), so it lands on the
application's own year; its answer is what enrols the hero (`universityStage` 1) or refuses him
(2) and it owns the `'I started college.'` line the application card used to carry. The loan is
four `Hero::StudentLoan` fields plus `Sim::studentLoanLines`, which adds the year's tuition, starts
the payback, and takes the annuity out of the bank balance.

**Verified.** `_re/tools/test_university_fund.py` pins every lane: the free lane in Germany
(label, body, `German public education system` log, no debt), the loan lane's wording and its
`start` line at 23, a `payoff` line eight payments later, the cash lane's exact
`Tuition * Years` deduction (the year's own money is the one the card moves), the scholarship's
awarded and rejected bodies, the broke path (`ScenarioInsufficientFinances` over
`'You don't have enough money to pay your {0} tuition.'`, nothing charged, no college start), and
one card per accepted life and none for a refused hero over ten seeds. `_re/tools/test_university.py`
moved its `'I started college.'` assertion to the new card.

**Ceilings, all marked in the source.**

* The native ability score behind the scholarship decision was not recovered; the port's own
  `schoolGrades` stands in, and the two parent-money tiers of that lane are dropped because the
  game reads `SimPerson.Att_money` (+0xbc), a field the port has no model for.
* The ask-parent lane is not offered at all: `WillingnessToFundSchoolScore` (Life +0xb8/+0xa8) was
  not recovered, so its accept and refuse conditions are unknown.
* A refused lane ends the application where the native card rebuilds itself and asks again.
* The two loan rejections are unreachable in the port: it has no criminal-record flag and the card
  only exists at 18/19, below the age-50 refusal.
* The cash lane's body and log were not recovered; the port leaves the body empty rather than invent
  one.
* `ScenarioSchoolFund`'s own `ExteriorTitle` was not recovered; the port keeps the education header.

**Harness note.** `--script` `choices[]` entries now accept `-1` as "let the card answer itself".
A test that wants to force one late card pads the earlier ones with `-1` instead of guessing their
answers, so the life up to that card is the unforced one — the tuition screen's odd lanes (a refused
scholarship, an unaffordable cash payment) are only reachable this way.

## 316. Twenty-six leisure tables: eighteen live, five unportable, three dead

The unreferenced-table list had grown to 37 names, and a name in that list says nothing about
whether the game uses the table. This section answers the question per table for the leisure
cluster by reading the loaders rather than the names: every `Load*Set` here is a lazy init
called **only** from its own DataHub getter (`UnityEngine.Resources::Load` 0x5579af0 on a Unity
TextAsset, not file IO), so the chain loader -> `DataHub+offset` field -> getter -> BL caller is
mechanical and can be walked to a real consumer. All addresses are 3.25.1 vaddrs.

The split for the 26 tables examined:

```
live, card the port lacks   18
non-portable (OS / sprites)  5
dead (no caller at all)      3
```

**The three dead ones are dead, not merely unwired.**

* `a16_dirty-talk-enc` (68 rows, 4316 B) has **no path literal at all** and no `Load*`/`Get*`
  symbol in the 140,207-entry index; `_dirtyTalkSet` (DataHub+0x380) is never populated.
* `a16_clubupdateufldumb-enc` (LIT#52185): `LoadDataClubUpdateUFLDumbScenarioSet` (0x288d130) is
  called only from `GetDataClubUpdateUFLDumbScenarioSet` (0x288dcf4), which has **zero** BL
  callers.
* `a16_black-market-auction-categories-enc` (LIT#52086, 7 rows): `LoadBlackMarketAuctionCategorySet`
  (0x2770ddc) has zero BL callers and `_blackMarketAuctionCategorySet` (DataHub+0xe80) is never
  read. Its row class stores the category as `Int32` while the CSV column is text, so the table
  would not even parse if it were loaded.

**Three near-duplicate pairs are orphans.** The shipped table set carries both a truncated and a
full form of the same name, and only one of each pair has a path literal:

| literal in metadata | rows | shipped twin | rows | literal for the twin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a16_casino-casino-ledger-feedback-enc` (LIT#52156) | 17 | `a16_casino-ledger-feedback-enc` | 2 | none |
| `a16_casino-casino-game-room-complaint-enc` (LIT#52153) | 17 | `a16_casino-game-room-complaint-enc` | 2 | none |
| `a16_casino-celebrity-demand-enc` (LIT#52166) | 22 | `a16_casion-celebrity-demand-enc` | 4 | none |

The port already reads the loaded form in all three cases (`src/fam/casino.cpp`, the ledger at the
"books" lane, the complaint at the gambler lane, the demand pool at the celebrity lane), so this is
a note about three more filenames that will stay unreferenced by design, not a port bug.

**The eighteen live tables belong to eighteen cards the port does not have.** Grouped by the
subsystem the consumer lives in, with the getter and the consumer's own address:

```

            youtube-channels  GetRandomYouTubeChannel 0x282f0c0      ScenarioFriendYouTube::RefreshScenario
            biographies       GetRandomBiographyForGender 0x28742a8  ScenarioFameBook::RefreshScenario
            compliments       GetRandomComplimentForGender 0x2808edc 83 Scenario*/FightClub sites

            wealthy-persons   GetRandomWealthyPerson 0x280c4c0       17 Scenario*SellOffer classes

            special-talent-filler GetSpecialTalentFiller 0x2872570   SimWorld::IncrementAgeAndSuppressLog
world       animals           GetRandomAnimalForContinent 0x28151cc  8 verified sites, see below
            ghosts            GetRandomGhostForCountryCode 0x282c3d0 SimGhost::set_Att_activeness
            body-parts        GetRandomBodyPart 0x2890c14/0x2890c70/0x2890f2c  DataHub injury/death getters
```

Two of the earlier notes are corrected here: the game-room-complaint set is `DataHub+0x160`, not
`+0x148`, and `crashout-celebrity-friend-string` is consumed by
`ScenarioFameCrashoutCelebrityFriend::.ctor+0x9c` (0x373960c), not by the crashout card's
`RefreshScenario`, so its line is chosen when the follow-up object is built, not when the card is
drawn.

Every getter picks a row with `GameReference::GetRandomNumber(0, count)` (0x2e112a8): `w0` is
zero, `w1` is the ArrayList count, and the helper locks `System.Threading.Monitor` before a
virtual dispatch through `klass+0x198`. Whether that bound is inclusive is **not** provable from
the dump (the target is not statically resolvable), which matters for the four-row and
seventeen-row tables where one row is a 6% slice and not for the others.

**The five that cannot be ported are not a gap.** `notification-heirlooms` (LIT#57162),
`notification-voices` (LIT#57163) and `local-notification-v1-text` (LIT#52527) feed
