(LIT#58235) are newline-separated sprite filenames for the Voltron face pipeline
(`VoltronFaceAccessory::GetFilename` 0x2f2e2b4). The port has no notification surface and no
sprites.

No code changed in this section: a table's consumer address is a map, not an implementation, and
wiring any of the eighteen means recovering that card's own strings, gates and effects first. The
eight animal sites are the exception worth naming now, because they are all one table and one
getter: `ScenarioOutdoorRideEncounterAnimal::RefreshScenario+0x118` (0x2495e74),
`VampireHuntActivity::GetRandomAnimalToEncounter+0xa4` (0x2969d68) and `+0xcc`
(0x2969d90), `ScenarioActorChallengeAnimal::RefreshScenario+0x340` (0x33e0c3c),
`ScenarioCarDriveAnimal::RefreshScenario+0x138` (0x3541b74),
`ScenarioEncounterAnimal::RefreshScenario+0x13c` (0x372319c) and
`ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush+0x144` (0x3724320), and
`ScenarioHustleAnimal::.ctor+0xa8` (0x37fe778).

Verification: this is a reading section, so the check is that the port still builds and the suite
still runs unchanged — 103/103 as committed in 315, and `tools/acceptance.py --no-tests` keeps
reporting the same card-table ratio (877/878) because no table reference moved.

## 315. The ambient time-machine card: one invented family removed

Section 310 recovered the real Time Machine as a snapshot engine: `UseTimeMachine` (0x73f32a73ec) and `SwitchToTimeMachineLife` (0x73f32a7814) swap a saved life in, and the `a16_time-machine-scenarios-enc` line is the *last* thing the restore prints. Nothing in the binary plays those lines as an ambient event -- there is no wheel or per-year caller, only the restore path.

The port had one anyway. `Sim::timeMachineYear` sat in the wheel with two tickets and an `ambientRng_.below(8)` gate, so a hero who had never travelled could be told they had come back from the future. That is a fabricated feature, not a shortfall, so it is gone: the function is deleted from `fam/lover.cpp`, its `kFamilies` seat is deleted from `sim.cpp`, and the table is now read only by `useTimeMachine`.

Removing a wheel seat changes every later draw, so the neighbours were re-measured against the new rotation:

- `tools/test_report_tables.py` scans one report table instead of two; the time-machine rows are covered by `tools/test_time_machine.py` through a real restore.
- `tools/test_horse_races.py` scans 200 lives instead of 120. The friends' invitation turns up in about a fifth of lives, and the old window reached only nine joins against a threshold of ten.
- `tools/test_pools.py` scans 160 lives for the prayer pool instead of 80: the ambient gate is one in forty behind a single wheel ticket, so the lane is reached in roughly 7.5% of lives.
- `tools/test_proposal.py` had been asserting that "Years Together" equals the hero's age, which is only true for the seeded fixture pair that starts at age 0; a lover the sim picks up later legitimately reads a shorter count, so the assertion now applies to the fixture lover only. Its two row parsers were also wrong for multi-word names ("Black opal", "gemstone watch"): they now anchor the split on a known category name.

Verification: the full suite is 103 tests, 100 passing on the first run and the three re-tuned ones passing individually on the same binary (the machine's own sha256 was checked before and after the run). `tools/test_time_machine.py` still drives a genuine restore, including the prison and death flags.

## 314. My Stuff and the accessory tables: backend data, cosmetic indexes, nothing to port

Three tables looked like a missing shop: `a16_mystuff-catalog-enc`, `a16_accessories-headwear-enc` and `a16_accessories-masks-enc`/`a16_accessories-sunglasses-enc`. Reading their consumers settles it -- there is no shipped shop to port.

**The catalog is never read from disk.** `Game.Dynamic.MyStuff.MyStuffDataController::LoadContent` (0x326f0f4) takes a `MyStuffDataModel` and only tail-calls `DataHub::LoadMyStuffCatalogSet` (0x28c5a8c) when the model's `DataText` (`[+0x10]`) is non-empty. The rows are parsed positionally (`Regex::Split` 0x53e7630 into `Game.DataMyStuffCatalog` 0x31d33f0) and the guards need at least 19 columns, skipping indices 8, 9 and 15 -- the shipped 9-column CSV cannot satisfy them, and its `Can Be Added`/`Unique` columns are read by no method in the 55-method class (there is no `get_CanBeAdded`, `get_Unique` or `IsOwned`). Whatever the live game shows comes from the backend payload, not from the extracted table.

**Ownership is a stack, use is a scripted effect.** `CanUseItem` (0x3304ce4) and `UseItem` (0x3304b6c) test `[item+0x18] > 0`. `GetExecuteItem` (0x3304d08) maps `BACKEND_SIGNUP` (LIT#12587) to `UseMoneyBag`, whose `ExecutePowerUp` (0x332e0c4) calls `SimFinances::AdjustBankBalanceByAmount` (0x2a72d68); the log line is the catalog's own `Log` column through `StuffItem::GetLogString` (0x330b3d8). The famous `I found a bag of money containing $50000.` is **data**, not a literal -- no string in the binary contains it.

**The shop screens are backend-driven too.** `ScenarioSeasonsShopItem` (ctor 0x2a56730, Refresh 0x2a56760) renders `Buy {0} {1}\n({2})` (#14348) with `Current Balance` (#16783), `Time Left` (#43570) and `Hourly Price` (#23155) from the same payload. Insufficient funds is a scenario, not an alert: LIT#27554 `It looks like you don't have enough ` + a data token + LIT#3638 ` to buy this right now. Earn some more and try again later.`, with the button-label variants LIT#8489 and LIT#842. The charge itself is delegated and was not recovered.

**Accessories are three separate tables, not the catalog.** `LoadAccessoryHeadwearSet` (0x27083f4, LIT#56995), `LoadAccessoryMaskSet` (0x271b694, LIT#56996) and `LoadAccessorySunglassesSet` (0x2708a1c, LIT#56997) list cosmetic indices per gender key (`female` #58833, `male` #62085, `x` #68193). They are handed out by `AcquireAccessory` (0x31d31b4) from the seasons track (`UISeasonsTrackItem::ShowClaimInfo` 0x32691c0) into `AcquireAccessoryHeadwearIndex` (0x237cbe4) / `AcquireAccessorySunglassesIndex` (0x237d6fc), and put on by `PutOnAccessory` (0x31d2ef4): category 1 writes `SimPerson+0x54`, category 2 writes `+0x58` and sets a Sim flag at `+0x6a8`, then the achievement, save and UI refresh run. No fame, looks or any other stat call is in that path; the effect is a cosmetic index plus one flag. There is no category-3 branch, so masks cannot be equipped through My Stuff even though a `+0x5c` setter exists.

Conclusion: `a16_mystuff-catalog-enc` and the three accessory tables stay unreferenced by the port, and this is a finding rather than a gap. Porting the catalog would mean inventing the backend's row shape, and porting the accessories would mean inventing a graphics layer to carry indices the port's model does not have. The only client-side gate that does exist -- `StuffItem::GetScenarioForUse` (0x33086f8), which switches on the catalog's Function type and turns a timed life item into `ScenarioMyStuffTimedLife` (0x23596e0) or a `Locked` (#29115) card -- is likewise reached only through a payload.
## 313. University: one threshold table, four ways out of a rejection

ScenarioSchoolUniversity (RefreshScenario 0x73f2a67ecc, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 0x73f2a689a0) is the education card a hero sees after high school. Its buttons are matched by the *text* of the option, not by index: `String::Contains` looks for `apply`, `fund`, `job`, `military`, `not for me` and `time off`. Applying writes the age into `Life+0x218` and logs `I applied to university and was accepted.` (#23494). No money is charged there -- tuition lives on the separate `ScenarioSchoolFund` screen (0x73f2a5a944: `How will you pay for your {0} program?` #23261, `Free public university` #20614, `Apply for a student loan` #11616, `Apply for a scholarship` #11615, `Ask my {0} to pay` #12168, `Pay with cash` #33501).

The admission test is `WillBeAccepted` (0x73f2a687ac). The school's Difficulty Score indexes `RequiredEducationalAbilityScoreForAdmission` (0x73f29bcae8), a five-entry table at .rodata 0xfc2e9c = **25, 45, 63, 73, 80**. A 30-point bonus is added when the hero has already completed school type 11, and the hero passes when `score + bonus >= need`, or unconditionally when royal. Independently the hero needs a completed high-school type (2 or 3), no expulsion in the last five years (`Life.AgeAtLastExpulsion` +0x400), and to be past `Country.SchoolGraduationAge`. There is **no money test** on admission.

`DataHub::CollegeForSchoolType(int)` (0x73f2c91e44) is a linear scan for the first `a16_colleges-enc` row whose SchoolType matches, with no weighting and no RNG. The shipped table has no SchoolType column, and the only row with an empty prerequisite list is `Undergraduate` (4 years, tuition 15000, Difficulty Score 2, Commonness Score 5) -- that is the program a hero who has just left high school can apply to, so the port offers it.

A rejected application is its own scenario, `ScenarioUniversityRejectedOptions` (.ctor 0x73f2a6936c): `Your application to university was rejected.` (#50200), the log line `I applied to university but my application was rejected.` (#23495), the reason labels `Reason`/`Rejected`/`Unqualified` (#35319/#35578/#45025), and four ways out: `Enlist in the military` (#18846), `Enroll in community college` (#18857), `Get a job` (#21322), `Take some time off` (#40898).

Port: `Sim::universityYear(Life&, AgeUp&, int)`, tried in the dispatch ahead of the wheel for ages 18-19. The card is offered the year after the graduation card owns its own year, so a normal life sees `ScenarioSchoolGraduate` at 18 and `ScenarioSchoolUniversity` at 19. `Hero::universityStage` records 1 accepted / 2 rejected, and college only starts for stage 1: `schoolYear` refuses a college rung the hero was never admitted to, and the college start line is not written for a rejected hero.

Shortcuts:
- The native ability score is not recovered. The port uses its own `schoolGrades` and keeps the recovered 30-point bonus, so the undergraduate row's 45 means 15 grades; the fixture draw is 62-86 and always clears it.
- The prerequisite school-type check, the five-year expulsion wait and the `Country.SchoolGraduationAge` gate are not modelled. Royalty admission is not modelled.
- `ScenarioSchoolFund`, the student loan (`SimBankLoan`, `MaximumAgeForStudentLoanEligibility` 0x73f2c9244c) and scholarship/tuition are not modelled, so no debt is created. This is the same ceiling the port's college rung has always had.
- The card's body text is unrecovered and stays empty. The other two initial buttons (`Get a job instead`, `Take some time off`) have no recovered scenario, so the port lists them and always takes the application; a script fixture `{"grades": N}` is the only way to reach the rejection lane.
- College years do not stop the port's job line (the pre-existing `student = age < 18` shortcut in `dispatchYear`).

`tools/test_university.py` pins the accepted and the rejected cards (table, title, body, choice, log lines), the 45-point boundary at 14/15 grades, one application per life at 18-19 only, no college lines for a rejected hero, and the two `grades` parse refusals.

The card takes a wheel slot, so two neighbours were re-measured: `tools/test_murder.py` now asserts each outcome branch on its own points (-30 karma success, -8 karma / -16 health retaliation, nothing on a miss) instead of accepting any of three health values, and `tools/test_time_machine.py` rewinds from 21 rather than 20, because the arrest chain it used to enter at 19 now starts a year later. `tools/test_pray_wealth.py` scans 121 lives instead of 30: its ambient gate is one in forty with a single wheel ticket, so the lane is only reached in about 7.5% of lives and the old window was measuring luck.
## 312. God Mode: raw sliders, one orientation map, one strange log line

God Mode is a one-time purchase (MonetizationVars 0x13/0x14/0x15). Once owned it has no per-edit cost and no cooldown; the relationship list offers `Edit {0}` (#18536) under the title `God Mode` (#21980). The edit itself is `GodModePersonConfig.SaveChangesAfterEditingPerson` (0x73f338e424):

- Nothing happens unless the config was marked edited.
- Names are copied over. Every slider is written **raw** into the person's attribute float, with no clamp. Attribute ids: 1 Happiness, 2 Health, 3 Smarts, 4 Looks, 5 Sexuality, 8 Willpower for everybody; the hero adds 9 Athleticism, 10 Karma, 11 Discipline.
- Sexuality goes back through `ConvertToGameValueFromSliderValue` (0x73f338e1e0): s<34 gives s*0.45454547, s<68 gives (s-33)*0.75757575+15, otherwise (s-67)*1.8181819+40. The constants were read from the binary at 0xfab3a0/0xfab3a4/0xfadd90. The result is capped at 100 and the orientation is recomputed: <=15 straight, <=40 bi, else gay. So slider 0-34 means straight, 35-67 bi, 68-100 gay.
- After a blank line the life log gets one line. For the hero it is one of `I don't know who I am anymore.` (#24032), `Something strange came over me.` (#39488) or `I may have been abducted by aliens.` (#24655). For anyone else it is one of `{0} seems different.` (#70286), `There is something off about {0} lately.` (#42872), `{0} seems like a whole different person.` (#70287), `Something happened to {0}.` (#39485) or `I'm not sure what's gotten into {0} lately.` (#26032).
- No cheat flag and no popup.

Port: `Sim::godModeEdit(Life&, AgeUp&, const GodModeEdit&, std::string*)` plus a script push `{"godMode": "hero"|"family:N"|"child:N", "godFirst", "godLast", "godHappiness", ...}`. The keys carry a `god` prefix so the spec's top-level parser cannot mistake them for `sexuality`/`cash`-style fields. A God Mode push is applied before the year-limit check, so an edit after the final year still lands in `final`. The log pick uses its own `godRng_` stream.

Shortcuts:
- The port has no attribute floats for relatives and no Willpower/Athleticism for the hero. Those edits are **refused** with an error, not silently dropped. Hero ids 1-5, 10 and 11 work.
- Slider input is limited to 0-100. The native slider ranges were not recovered.
- The relationship phrase (`RelationshipStatusStringForEditPersonInPointOfView`) was not recovered, so the port's own `my <relation>` stands in for it. The child special-talent reroll is not modelled. Paywall/IAP and custom-life entry points are absent. The blank-line separator is not reproduced in `logLines`.

`tools/test_god_mode.py` covers all 101 slider values: exact final stats, and orientation bands straight 0-34 / bi 35-67 / gay 68-100 against a float32 mirror of the native map. Over 40 seeds it checks family renames and sees all 5 other-person lines and all 3 hero lines. It also checks six refusals (willpower, relative health, slider 101, family:99, unknown person, empty edit) and a mid-life edit that keeps later years running.
## 311. Nine colour pools: what the secret-agent tables actually colour

The nine `a16_secret-agent-*-color-enc` tables are not hue pickers. Eight of them are prose pools; the ninth is a wire puzzle. Each one is reached from a specific secret-agent screen, so the port wires them where the screen exists and leaves the ones with no port-side mechanic unwired.

| table | native reader | filter | what it produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| honeypot-misssion-briefing-color | 0x73f2c5dc2c | none, weighted | ` Your client, NAME, wants you to seduce TARGET. He/She says he/she wants X.` |
| honeypot-approach-color | 0x73f2c617cc | none, weighted | ` According to your client, NAME, the target prefers lovers who X.` |
| hack-mission-briefing-color | 0x73f2c53df8 | exact Client Type + File Type | ` Reportedly, the file contains X.` |
| hack-mission-file-color | 0x73f2c55a70 | File Type match && (blank Client Type or match) | ` FILE: X.` with `<client>` -> `your client, NAME` |
| stealth-alarm-color | 0x73f2c58fa0 | uniform row | door colour, the correct wire, two wrong wires, `The <W> wire` choices |
| honeypot-meeting-scenario-color | 0x73f2c607cc | Location == the meeting place, or blank | `According to his/her report, he/she caught the target's eye X.` |
| client-mission-terminated-color | 0x73f2c56308 | exact Mission Type | `<client-spy>` -> `Your client, NAME, ` appended when the mission fails |

Two tables stay unwired because the port has no mechanic behind them: `potential-agent-background-check-color` needs candidate recruitment, and `agency-front-color` needs a front identity the port keeps (its front token is redrawn on each use).

Stealth is the one mechanical pool. The native scenario picks a row, takes its Door Color and one Correct Wire, adds two shuffled Incorrect Wire Colors and shuffles the three, then `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` (0x73f2aa7ea0) accepts a choice iff the lowercased choice text *contains* the correct colour. The snip line only prints when the chosen wire was the correct one.

Port: all seven readers live in `Sim::spyYear` (_re/port/src/fam/spy.cpp). Every new draw uses `spyRng_`; the local name draws and token resolution swap `rng_` for `spyRng_` around themselves, so the main stream is untouched and no earlier card sequence moves. Colour picks are the Commonness Score weighted pick over the filtered rows.

Shortcuts:
- There is no client record. The client is a name drawn from the first/last name tables plus a 0.5 gender chance on `spyRng_`.
- The hack client type is drawn uniformly from civilian/corporation/government; the native generator was not traced.
- No approach dropdown and no +25 style scoring, no drive/file browser, no decoy files, and the hack briefing's first sentence (ComputerType/FileAction) is dropped.
- Stealth shuffling approximates .NET `OrderBy(random)` with one unit key per element plus a stable sort; the door-colour info row is folded into the briefing; the wrong-wire interruption narrative was not recovered, so a wrong choice only reports the failure.
- Meeting drops ` disguised as <disguise>` and the contact sentence.
- Terminated only qualifies when the agent returns in the native flow; the port's hero always returns, so every failure qualifies.

Tests: `tools/test_spy_colors.py` runs 1200 seeds over 80 ages with the spy path on and asserts the shape of every wired pool: 1859 mission cards (351 hack, 379 honeypot, 236 meeting, 379 stealth, 121 snip, 543 terminated). A mutation pass (`/tmp/qdir/s311_mut.py`, 79 seeds) breaks the file type, the chosen wire and the mission type in turn, and the test reports `hack filter`, `stealth choice`/`snip wire`, and `terminated filter` respectively, so the filters are load-bearing. The full suite is green.
## 310. The Time Machine: twenty birthdays on disk and a wholesale restore

The port's only time machine used to be an ambient wheel card (`fam/lover.cpp` `timeMachineYear`) that printed an "I arrived from the future..." line to a hero who had never travelled. The game's feature is a snapshot engine, and the narrative is only the last line of a restore. Native reading of 3.25.1 (`/tmp/qdir/time_machine_recovery2_findings.txt`):

- **Snapshots.** `SaveGameManager`'s save coroutine (0x73f3320410) writes `savedLife-age{N}.data` at the end of `Life.TiAge` on every birthday and deletes `savedLife-age{0..Age-21}.data`, so the newest 20 years are kept. The birth file `savedLife-start.data` is never read by the lookup.
- **Request.** `GameManager.RequestTimeMachineWithGoBackYears` (0x73f32a7270) caches the year count, `WasInPrison` and `WasDead`; the unlimited entitlement goes straight on, otherwise the IAP runs, and both `TimeMachinePurchased` and `UnlimitedTimeMachinePurchased` tail into `UseTimeMachine` whatever their bool says.
- **Restore.** `UseTimeMachine` (0x73f32a73ec) loads the file for `Hero.Age - years`; a missing file is a silent return. `SwitchToTimeMachineLife` (0x73f32a7814) keeps the life id, calls `GenesisController.ResetScenarios`, swaps the whole saved `Life` graph in (RNG, decks and log included), and on a death removes the last grave and sets `Life.WasResurrected` (+0x470).
- **Narrative.** `DataHub.GetRandomTimeMachineScenarioForAgeAndWasInPrisonAndWasDead` draws rows uniformly until one has `Min Age` <= the restored age and `Prison`/`Was Dead` equal to the cached flags, and logs it.
- **Card.** `ScenarioTimeMachine.RefreshScenario`: "Travel back in time today!" (#43981) or "Undo death by traveling back in time!" (#44728), "Pick your destination" (#33863), "1 year ago (Age {0})" (#7653) always, "3/5/10/15/20 years ago (Age {0})" (#7974, #8140, #7788, #7835, #7924) only while that file exists, and "Send me back" (#38578). The feature name is "Time Machine" (#43572).

The port now does the same:

- `Sim::ageUp` wraps the old body (`ageUpYear`) and, when the age moved, stores a `TimeSave{Life, Sim}` under that age and drops ages `<= age-21`. The copy leaves out the loaded tables, the country list and the snapshots themselves (data, not state); everything else in the simulator, every RNG stream and cache, is in it, which is the port's counterpart of the saved graph carrying its RNG and decks.
- `Sim::useTimeMachine(life, out, years)` accepts only 1/3/5/10/15/20 with an existing snapshot (otherwise returns false: the native silent return), caches the prison and death flags, restores simulator and life, clears `pendingCards`, sets `Life::wasResurrected` on a death, and writes the card (title, body, CTA, the chosen "N years ago (Age X)" label) with the narrative row as its log line.
- Scripts get a push entry `{"timeMachine": N}`: that card index is the machine, and it is the one card a dead hero still receives, after which the life goes on from the restored birthday. Snapshots are only taken when a script contains such an entry.

Shortcuts, written down:

- The narrative pick uses its own stream (`timeMachineRng_`, kept across the restore) instead of the shared `System.Random`; the uniform pick among matching rows has the retry loop's distribution.
- Snapshot copying is opt-in for speed only; it changes no draw. A port snapshot is also stored for the birthday on which the hero then dies (native saves the death to the main file only); no destination can reach that age, so nothing reads it.
- The prison line (#68766/#68767 "{0}\n\nYou've been in {1} for {2} {3}.") is not added: it needs the years already served, which the port does not keep. There is no graveyard to remove a grave from, no IAP, no unlimited-entitlement check, and the script's event list keeps the cards that were undone (the game rebuilds its log from the snapshot).
- The old ambient `timeMachineYear` wheel card was removed in 315: native shows those lines only after a restore.

Test: `_re/tools/test_time_machine.py`. Seeds 1-30, five years back at card 20: 29 restores, every card has the exact strings and a table row with `Was Dead` clear and `Min Age` met, the next card is the year after the destination, and 288 of 332 later cards repeat the untouched run exactly (the rest diverge where the restore dropped a queued card or a narrative token drew from the restored main stream). Seeds 1-12 run to death and go back 20 years: 11 heroes revived with the death body and a `Was Dead` row. Forty forced sentences rewound one year at 20: 30 got a `Prison` row. Two years, 25 years, and 20 years at age 3 produce no card.
## 309. The honeypot's pronouns: the mark has a gender of their own

While re-reading the secret-agent family for its colour tables, two pronoun defects
surfaced in the honeypot lane; both are provable from the port's own source.

The target table `a16_secret-agent-mission-target-people-enc` carries a **Target
Gender** column -- `<his/her> mistress` is female; `<his/her> husband's <best
bro/gym buddy/fraternity brother>`, `a billionaire playboy` and `a male stripper` are
male -- but the port never read it. The briefing hardcoded the mark as the opposite of
the hero (`h.female ? "he" : "she"`), so a male agent sent after a male stripper was
briefed `work the fact that she cannot resist`.

The sting was worse: the pronoun swap ran **after** the resolver. `pickSnippet` expands
`<him/her>`/`<his/her>` with the hero's gender the moment the row is drawn, so by
the time `spySwap` touched the string no tokens were left -- the swap was dead code.

Fix (src/fam/spy.cpp, include/bl/sim.h):

- the target draw records `spyTargetFemale_` from the Target Gender column; rows
  with a blank gender cell keep the opposite-of-hero fallback (shortcut: the native
  handling of blank rows is not recovered).
- the briefing's `cannot resist` pronoun follows that flag.
- the sting row is drawn through a new `spyRawSnippet` -- the identical single `pickRow`
  call, the text just stays raw -- so `<him/her>`/`<his/her>` become the mark's pronouns
  while the tokens still exist, then the rest resolves. Draw count and token order are
  unchanged, so no other family's sampling shifts.
- one dependency consciously dropped: the hero-keyed `<his/her>` used to seed the
  resolver's `<rb>` fallback; no secret-agent table uses `<rb>` (checked).

Test `_re/tools/test_spy_pronouns.py`: 1500 seeds per hero gender with the spy flag on;
every honeypot card's briefing pronoun and sting object pronoun is checked against the
gender the drawn mark's own text implies (stripper/best bro/playboy male, mistress
female). In-law rows are not Honeypot-flagged in the table, so they never appear here.

```
red   22/47 briefings wrong  (seed 395, age 59: male hero, "a male stripper",
                              "work the fact that she cannot resist")
green 47/47 briefings + stings agree with the mark  (32 male marks, 15 female)
```

Ceiling: card yield is ~0.115 honeypot cards per life, so the check needs thousands of
lives; blank-gender targets remain the opposite-of-hero shortcut.

## 308. The witch doctor's medicine: one price, one roll, one risk table

The vampire coven has its own approximation (src/fam/vampire.cpp 203), but the ordinary
witch doctor -- the Healthcare stranger offering baby mouse soaked in rice wine -- is a
different native object: ScenarioWitchDoctor with a DataWitchRemedy row, a price that
moves with a random factor, and an outcome that can cure the worst disease or kill the
hero outright. The whole contract is decoded from the 3.25.1 binary and wired here;
a16_witch-remedies-enc (30 rows: Item, Effectiveness/Risk/Cost Score, Treats Disease)
leaves the unreferenced list at 46 -> 45.

The native contract, every clause disassembly-verified:
- The offer caches on open (ctor @0x73f3bb5470): Life.AgeAtLastWitchRemedy and
  Life.CurrentWitchRemedy keep one row and one price per year of age, so a second visit
  at the same age offers the same item at the same price even after a dismiss or a
  purchase. There is no cooldown and no consumption.
- The price is 2 * Cost Score * factor, factor = Next(0,100)+1 (DataWitchRemedy.Cost
  @0x73f2e61a40 is six instructions), i.e. 2..1,000 per cost point.
- "Try it, why not?" (#44082) is the only choice. An unaffordable balance shows the
  generic insufficient-finances popup ("You don't have enough money to pay the witch
  doctor for {0}." + "You are {money} short." / "You are broke.", title drawn from
  In the red / Flat broke / Penniless, or You're short / No funds / Not enough) and
  nothing else happens: no debit, no outcome roll. An affordable take debits before any
  roll and never refunds.
- Targeting: the remedy's Treats Disease first -- any ailment matching it, diagnosed or
  not, No Cure ignored; otherwise the first strict maximum Seriousness Score > 0, ties to
  the earlier ailment. One cure roll only: Next(0,15) < Effectiveness for a specialty
  match, Next(0,50) otherwise, and no second target after a failure.
- A cure removes the ailment immediately and restores its positive impact columns
  (health/appearance/intelligence at their positive scores only, happiness max(3, score)).
  An undiagnosed disease restores silently; a diagnosed one queues the generic
  "You took {0}." popup and then the "Cured" / "You are no longer suffering from {0}."
  card, the pair of titles drawn from "Wait, did it..." / "No effing way...". Seriousness
  >= 4 also adds the resilient obituary color.
- Failure, or no target at all, rolls r = Next(0, 2*Risk), upper exclusive: 0 is neutral;
  1..7 cost min(r,5) health and happiness, with a shared 1-in-3 roll adding the same loss
  to looks and smarts; >= 8 is a direct death that zeroes health, looks and smarts but
  not happiness. A health pool depleted by the impact also kills. Prison caps the
  post-impact happiness at Next(51,54) before the optional looks/smarts roll. Both death
  lanes set the FatalWitchRemedy cause, "I died after taking {0}.".
- Every affordable take adds one obituary color: "Friends describe <obit-him/her> as a
  questionable decision maker." or "a risk taker."

What the port does:
- Sim::witchDoctorVisit(life, out, take) renders the card -- the native Cost field is
  flattened into the body until cards model a price (ponytail comment in the source) --
  and either dismisses (offer log only, the native DismissSelected) or takes. The whole
  subsystem runs on its own witchRng_ stream (seed ^ 0xd1310ba698dfb5ac) so it cannot
  shift other years' card sequence; the native uses the shared System.Random, which is
  the port's deliberate divergence.
- The diagnosed cure chain is two pending cards (kPendingWitchResult, then
  kPendingWitchCure) drained by the following ageUp calls before the age advances -- the
  same queue the funeral chain uses.
- checkDeath now holds the annual mortality roll while a witch result or cure is still
  queued (src/sim.cpp 18691): the medical chain closes before the year can kill. The
  guard was required here -- a diagnosed cure queued behind its generic popup could
  otherwise die between the two cards -- and every other pending family inherits it.
- The replay runner (--script) used to stop at its age limit the moment the final
  advancing card was shown, leaving that year's followups queued (src/script.cpp 951).
  The loop now drains pendingCards before exiting, so a forced visit in the last
  requested year returns its result -- and the cure card -- at the same age. Found by
  the section's independent review, reproduced red, fixed, and pinned by a boundary
  assertion in the test.

Shortcuts (not recovered from the artifact):
- No annual encounter rate: the doctor is reachable only through the forced class
  ScenarioWitchDoctor (push scripts and the test), because the Healthcare menu that owns
  the native trigger is not ported. Nothing is invented in its place.
- Holiday and unlock hooks, and the UI presentation, are not rendered; the stored
  remedy history, obituary colors and ateSnake flag are kept on the hero but have no
  viewer yet.

Tests (tools/test_witch_doctor.py): a compiled oracle shadows the witchRng_ stream and
asserts the exact roll order -- cache draws, cure roll, risk roll, optional stats roll,
title draws, obituary draw, prison cap -- across 1,200 no-target visits (30 rows x 40
seeds: 50 fatal, 306 neutral, 844 harm) and 400 target visits in four disease modes
(79 cures, 43 deferred diagnosed restorations), plus the same-age cache (repeated visits
reuse row and price, monkey ejaculate at 34 twice including the exact-balance edge), the
prison cap order, the final-year replay boundary, and forced-choice validation (only
-1/0). Full suite: 99/99 green on the fixed binary after the runner corrections.

## 307. The funeral chain: the disposition screen and the urn

The death card (section 249) answers a parent's death with two trace-backed lines, but the
live 3.25.3a game puts a second screen behind a third button: when the hero chooses to plan
the funeral himself, the disposition card opens. The played life captured it whole at 19 --
"It's time to decide what to do with your father's remains. His wish was to be cremated."
with Burial 7,710 / Cremation 990 / Taxidermy 45,360 / Donate to Science 0 and the four
buttons "Bury him", "Cremate him", "Have him taxidermied", "Donate his body to science" --
and then, after a cremation, the crematorium returns the ashes and a third card asks what to
do with them. Both screens and the urn are wired here, and a16_funeral-ash-locations-enc
leaves the unreferenced list (47 -> 46). The card denominator does not move: the ash table
feeds a screen, it is not a card table.

**What the game runs.** ScenarioDeathRelative carries the whole branch in its method names:
ShowPlanFuneralScenario, ShouldPlanFuneral, ShowAttendFuneral, ShowAbroadFuneral,
ShowPrisonFuneralFeedback, then DismissSelected and ChoiceSelectedAtIndex. The disposition
itself is ScenarioFuneralPlanning (.ctor x5, RefreshScenario, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex), the
ashes are ScenarioFuneralAshes (.ctor x5, RefreshScenario, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex), travel
and mourning are ScenarioFuneralTravel and ScenarioMournDeath. So the chain is: death card ->
disposition -> urn, and nothing in it is a table row.

**The chain in the port.** funeralYear gains the third option, the label from #34062
"Plan {0} funeral" with the possessive filled in, and it only opens the door: the card's own
line stays empty and the disposition answers next. The two trace lanes are untouched and
still log #23836 and #24573. funeralPlanningYear then reads the relation and sex the death
card stored and builds the disposition screen; cremation pushes a pending card and
funeralAshesYear answers it the next age-up.

**The literals.**

- disposition title #20840 "Funeral Planning"; body #27798 "It's time to decide what to do
  with {0} remains." (the captured screen fills {0} with "your father's") and the wish line
  #70505 "{0} {1} wish was to be cremated.".
- the four cost rows #14177 "Burial", #16675 "Cremation", #41045 "Taxidermy", #18102
  "Donate to Science".
- the four logs #24803 "I planned {0} funeral and arranged for {1} to be buried{2}.",
  #24804 "... cremated{2}.", #24805 "... donated {1} body to science{2}", #24806 "... had
  {1} taxidermied{2}." ({0} and {1} are the deceased's possessives, {2} is empty in every
  capture).
- the ashes card #50095 "You've received {0} ashes back from the crematorium.\n\nWhat will
  you do?" (title #12127 "Ashes") and its three buttons #39747 "Sprinkle them somewhere
  special", #28218 "Keep them in an urn", #43542 "Throw them in the trash".
- the ashes logs #25138 "I sprinkled {0} ashes {1}.", #24867 "I put {0} ashes in an urn and
  stored it in a safe place.", #25244 "I threw {0} ashes in the trash." and the second
  person twin #49357 "You sprinkled {0} ashes {1}.".
- the broke answer, which the live screen showed as a "Penniless" modal over the card:
  #33550 "Penniless", #48373 "You don't have enough money {0}." and #68721 "{0}\n\nYou are
  broke.".

**The table.** a16_funeral-ash-locations-enc is one page: Place, Gender, Min Age, Max Age,
with places already written as phrases ("at his favorite strip club", male, 21). The Gender
column names the dead, so the port filters it with the deceased's sex; the age window is
read against the hero as a shortcut; its native age subject has not been recovered. A row that survives the
filter supplies the whole tail of "I sprinkled my father's ashes at his favorite strip
club.".

**The shortcuts.** The four prices are the numbers the live card printed once (Burial 7,710,
Cremation 990, Taxidermy 45,360, Donate 0); the game's own formula is class-side and was not
recovered, and the port's economy has no funeral-cost table to derive them from. An
unaffordable button does not reopen the menu: the card logs the Penniless sentence and the
parent is laid to rest with no disposition record, which is the smallest honest answer given
the modal is not modelled. The captured cremation wish is reused rather than modelling
individual burial wishes. Prices keep the captured numeric values in the hero's currency,
without region scaling. If the eligible ash pool is empty, the implementation falls
back to all nonempty places; the current seeded check does not exercise that fallback.
AgeUp carries one card per call: planning and ashes are pending
follow-ups drained before the age/year increment, so the whole chain stays in the same year.

**The test.** tools/test_funeral.py runs 40 lives to 90 with an initial 50,000 balance
and 40 with an initial zero balance; later spending and earnings can change either. It
checks the captured body, exact choice/journal pairing, deceased pronouns, queued planning
and ashes linkage, and ash locations against gender/age-filtered table rows. A compiled
public-API assertion also forces the third death-card option and checks the unaffordable
taxidermy wording for both parents. Measured: 56 planning screens, 9 burials, 6 cremations,
2 taxidermies, 17 donations and 22 unaffordable choices; 6 ashes cards (1 scattered, 2 kept,
3 discarded). The existing relative-death check remains green: 74 deaths, 46 old funeral
lanes. Post-change regression: 98/98 green across a host interruption (61 checks before
the crash, the remaining 37 resumed against the unchanged binary). The funeral and
relative-death checks were also rerun after recovery and passed with the same counts.

## 306. The horse races: three cards from a16_horses-enc

The §305 audit left 48 tables in gamedata_plain that no port source names. The horse
races are the first of them whose whole card text survives in the metadata -- the
friends' invitation, the horse picker and both result lines, with both journals -- and
the port had no horse, race, bet or tip code at all. It is wired here. a16_horses-enc
leaves the unreferenced list (48 -> 47); the card denominator does not move, because a
race payload table was never counted as a card table.

**What the game runs.** Five Scenario classes carry the lane. ScenarioOpportunityHorseTrack
(.ctor, RefreshScenario, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex, ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush) is the
friends' invitation. ScenarioHorseRacesBet (.ctor, RefreshScenario, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex)
is the picker. ScenarioGameHorseRacing (.ctor, MiniGameCompleted, ChoiceSelectedAtIndex)
is the race itself. ScenarioHorseRacesOutcome (.ctor, RefreshScenario, DismissSelected) is
the result card. ScenarioHorseRaces holds the entry point and a .cctor. No gamedata table
carries the picker's body or the result body as a card row: the picker is a dropdown, the
race is a mini-game, and the only text a card shows is the three strings below plus the
two journals.

**The table.** a16_horses-enc has 114 rows and two columns, Horse and Success Score
(Adam Saddler 1, Air Mail 3, Aphrodite 4, Arm in Arm 2). No row names a track, a distance
or a prize; the score is the only thing that can decide a result, so the port draws the
winner from the field weighted by it and pays the picked horse's own weight back.

**The literals.**

- invitation body #39447: "Some of your friends are going to the horse races.\n\nWill you
  join them?" (its siblings #39444 eating, #39445 casino, #39446 nightclub have the same
  shape, so the body is a template the game fills per activity).
- the two buttons #27968 "Join them", #25888 "I'd rather stay home".
- picker label #33883 "Pick your horse".
- results: #70414 "{0} won the race!", #70415 "{0} won the race!\n\nYou lost {1} by
  betting on {2}.", #70416 "{0} won the race!\n\nYou won {1}!" (fragments #4128/#4129
  are the same two strings split at the name).
- journals: #25829 "I won {0} after betting on {1}!", #24621 "I lost {0} after betting
  on a losing horse named {1}!", #25790 "I went with some friends to the horse races.",
  #25515 "I turned down an opportunity to go to the horse races with friends.", #23997
  "I didn't have enough money to go to the horse races.".
- title #23121 "Horse Races" (the tip card is #23123, the track menu is #23124).

**The port.** Three cards, chained through the pending list like the §301-§302 lanes.
Sim::horseRacesYear is the wheel seat (1 ticket): age 18+, not in prison, one year in 25.
It shows the invitation with the two buttons; "I'd rather stay home" journals #25515 and
ends the lane; "Join them" with less than $100 journals #23997 and ends it; otherwise it
journals #25790 and pushes kPendingHorseBet. Sim::horseBetYear, one year later, deals five
distinct horses from the table, offers their names as the options, journals nothing, stores
the pick and the wager, and pushes kPendingHorseOutcome. Sim::horseOutcomeYear draws the
winner weighted by Success Score and shows one of the two result bodies: a win pays
wager * max(2, 12 - 2*score) and journals #25829; a loss takes the wager and journals
#24621. The lane has its own draw, horseRng_ (include/bl/sim.h, seeded in the Sim
constructor), because the extra draws would otherwise move every family that comes after
it -- the §282 lesson.

**Shortcuts, marked in the source.**

- the picker's body is the dropdown label #33883. The card in the game is a dropdown with
  a label above it; AgeUp carries one text field, so the label becomes the body.
- the wager (max($100, cash/10), capped at cash) and the odds (12 - 2*score, never below
  2) are the port's. The metadata has the three result strings but no bet amount and no
  odds table, and the wager has to be something the hero can always pay.
- the "There are no horse races in {0} because gambling is illegal." gate (#42826) is not
  modelled: the port has no country-level gambling legality flag.
- the tip and psychic-dream lines (#48635, #48893, #24302, #24905, #10169, #10170) belong
  to the Horse Tip card (#23123) and the menu's Race Tracks entry, not to this lane, so
  they are left unwired rather than dressed as cards.

**test_horse_races.py** parses the table's names, then runs 120 seeds x 80 ages with
$500,000 in cash. It asserts the invitation body and both button labels; the picker's
choice is always a table horse; each result card matches #70416 or #70415, its winner is
a table horse, its journal matches #25829 or #24621 with the same amount, and the loser
named on a loss is exactly the horse the picker showed one event earlier. Measured over those seeds: 31 invitations, 13 accepted, 18 declined, 13 horses picked, 5 wins and 8 losses -- both result bodies and both journals are reached.

## 305. Two flavour pools: the prayer and the crowd's answer

The §304 audit left 50 tables in gamedata_plain that no port source names. Two of them
were real card text with an obvious slot and no missing prompt, so they are wired here;
the rest are triaged at the end of this section.

**a16_pray-feedback-enc** (21 rows, Log | Pray | Curse | Commonness Score) is the
prayer itself, printed the year a pray-wealth card fires. Ten rows carry no alternative
slot; the Pray column marks the blessing rows ("I fell to my knees and prayed to the
BitLife devs for succor.", "I closed my eyes, spread my arms wide, and uttered a
lengthy prayer to the BitLife devs.") and the Curse column the rows for a curse ("I
called the BitLife devs a profane name."). The card already knows which side it is on --
its own a16_pray-wealth-scenarios-enc row has a Positive column -- so the pool line is
drawn from the matching side, weighted by Commonness Score, and appended to the year's
extra lines after the money moves.

**a16_crashout-public-response-string-enc** (32 rows, String | Positive Reception |
Commonness Score) is what the public makes of a famous hero's crashout: "Your fans wrote
encouraging messages regarding their hope that you'll become less stressed soon." on the
cheered side, "People commented that you're too famous to act like a child in public."
on the other. Twenty-five rows are plain sentences; fifteen are flagged positive and ten
are not. The card's own Fame Impact (through pointsForImpact, the §228 rule) decides
which side of the crowd answers.

Both lines share one new draw, **poolRng_**, declared beside Rng jewRng_ in
include/bl/sim.h and seeded in the Sim constructor with seed ^ 0x6a09e667f3bcc908 ^
0x9e3779b97f4a7c15. The flavour families had been sharing the ambient stream, and the
new draws would have moved every family that comes after them -- the §282 lesson, paid
for twice already.

Two rules are written in the code and marked there:

- a row whose text still carries a '<...>' alternative is skipped, not resolved. The
  resolver draws from the main stream, and one extra draw per card would shift every
  later family's sequence; the port's contract is that a flavour line must be free.
- the pool line is pushed to out.extra, so it prints *before* the card's own journal
  line (the runner writes the extras first). The test therefore scans the whole event,
  not its tail -- the first version of test_pools.py failed on exactly that.

**test_pools.py** (80 seeds x 40 ages, one pass plain and one with fame 80) reads both
tables, splits each into its two sides, and asserts for every card that exactly one
pool line is present, that it belongs to the side the row's own flag column names, and
that it carries no token. Measured: 8 pray cards and 12 crashout cards; every one
matched. The suite is 96 tests.

acceptance: card tables 878/878 -- these two pools are journal lines, not cards, so the
count does not move; the two wired tables leave the unreferenced set (50 -> 48).

### The remaining 48, triaged

- **9 secret-agent -color pools** (agency front, client mission terminated, hack
  briefing, hack file, honeypot approach, honeypot meeting, honeypot briefing, potential
  agent background check, stealth alarm). Every slot they would fill is already filled
  from the non-color twin by fam/spy.cpp (front from
  a16_secret-agent-agency-front-names-enc, files and briefings from the related
  scenario tables), so wiring them is text variety, not a missing subsystem. Upgrade
  path: swap one slot at a time, keeping the report's mission text stable.
- **2 printer/asset filename lists** (voltron_componentFilenames 1381 png names,
  voltron_disguiseFilenames 283). Asset names for a costume set, not text.
- **3 notification-layer tables** (notification-heirlooms, notification-voices,
  local-notification-v1-text). These are OS pushes ("It's time!", "You know I can't
  play with myself, right?"), not in-life cards; the port models only the in-life
  notification bait card it already has.
- **2 legacy twins** (casino-ledger-feedback, casino-game-room-complaint). Same header
  and a strict subset of the rows in the a16_casino-casino-* files the casino family
  already reads; both shipped in the same bundle (same mtime), so only one version is
  live. Classified, not wired twice.
- **the catalogue layer** (accessories-headwear 245, accessories-masks 22,
  accessories-sunglasses 242, aircraft-parts 31, car-parts 42, body-parts 78,
  biographies 45, heirlooms, black-market-auction-categories 7, mystuff-catalog): item
  lists behind the Assets/Belongings/IAP menus (§293), not scenario text.
- **pools whose card lives in code, with no captured prompt** -- this is the real
  evidence ceiling, and each needs one literal that the metadata dump does not carry:
  assaults 228 (the school Attack card: the live card's button labels are composed at
  runtime and its title 'Conflict' is not enough), back-to-school-titles 55 (house-party
  and dance outcome variants), compliments 139, colleges 9 (the Education menu's
  program picker), company-name-type 30, delinquent-activities, dirty-talk,
  funeral-ash-locations, ghosts, horses, landlord-ghost-kill-tenant-color, magazines,
  public-places 223, special-talent-filler 73, supervisor-warnings 31, wealthy-persons
  58, youtube-channels 63, crashout-celebrity-friend-string 43 (a clause, not a
  sentence: it describes someone else's reaction and has no name slot in the port),
  casion-celebrity-demand 4 (note the table's own misspelling), clubupdateufldumb 44,
  animals 73, witch-remedies 30 (the witch-doctor card's buttons are still unfound --
  the only remedy literals are outcome fragments: #323, #391, #35642, #48267).

The next section either captures one of those prompts off the running build or finds a
table whose card text is complete, rather than inventing the sentence in between.

## 304. The jewelry shop: a purchase card from the same three tables

The live build's Activities screen sends `Shopping` into a jeweller's list --
`GIRARD BROTHERS JEWELERS` in the captured run -- whose rows read
`Emerald Earrings (2.33ct)  $28,700`, `Sapphire Bracelet (2.99ct)  $23,800`,
`Diamond Pendant (0.64ct)  $6,200`. Tapping a row opens a purchase card: title bar
`#27900 "Jewel"`, card title `Sapphire Bracelet`, body
`Buy this 2.55-carat sapphire bracelet today!` (`#14339 "Buy this {0} {1} {2} today!"`),
the rows `Price: $19,400`, `Gemstone: Sapphire`, `Carats: 2.55`,
`Metal: 24K Gold` (`#34534 "Price"`, `#21079 "Gemstone"`, `#15189 "Carats"`),
a Quality bar (`#35021`) and the single button `#14316 "Buy it"`.

**The card.** `Sim::jewelShopYear` reads the same three tables the proposal ring
already uses (`a16_jewelry-types-enc`, `a16_jewelry-gemstones-enc`,
`a16_jewelry-metals-enc`), picks a type by Commonness Score, then the gemstone by its
own Commonness Score, carats uniform inside the gemstone's range and the metal by
Cost Score -- `Sim::drawJewel`, shared with the ring in section 303. Each purchase
uses its own `jewRng_` stream (the 282 lesson: one shared stream shifts the other
families by a whole card).

**Text.** The body follows the literal: `Buy this {carats}-carat {gem} {type} today!`,
or the no-carat shape `#14338 "Buy this {0} today!"` for the three categories the
table marks without carats (`charm`, `exotic watch`, `crown`). The rows are
`Price: <money>`, `Gemstone: <Gem>`, `Carats: <carats>` (only when the category has
them) and `Metal: <Metal>`. The screen is Title Case (`Sapphire Bracelet`,
`Metal: 24K Gold`), so every word is raised there while the body line keeps the
table's lowercase. The journal line is composed as
`I bought a <Item> for <money>.` -- the game's own fragment `#23640 "I bought a "` is
the only literal for the purchase, so the rest is the port's own sentence and is
marked as such in the source. The card carries exactly one button, as the live card
does; it is only offered for a price the hero can pay because the port has no
`Penniless` screen to fall back to.

**Left out on purpose.** `earrings` and `chandelier earrings` are the two categories
the table marks `Is Plural`, and `#14339` is written for one item ("Buy this ...");
no literal for the plural shape was found, so the port does not sell them rather
than invent "Buy these". The Luxury-only rows are drawn only once the hero holds
$100,000, matching the shop's own gate.

**Price.** The table's own formula is followed: `First Carat Price x carats x the
type's Cost Score`, clamped to the gemstone's Min Cost / Max Cost. A 2.55-carat
sapphire bracelet comes out at $20,400 against the $19,400 the live shop asked; the
clamp band and the formula are the table's, the exact number is a shortcut because
the live game also rolls the metal's Cost Score into the price.

**Test.** `_re/tools/test_jewelry.py` parses the three tables and runs forty lives of
eighty years from a $500,000 cash fixture. Per card it asserts the title is the
Title Case item, the body matches `#14339` (or `#14338`), the gemstone, metal and
type are rows of their tables, the carats sit inside the gemstone's range and match
the `Carats` row, the price sits inside the gemstone's Min Cost / Max Cost, the
category is not a plural one, and the journal line names the same item and the same
price with the right article. Measured: 25 cards over 40 lives.

test       test_jewelry: the jewel's own cells, the price band and the buy line

## 303. The proposal card: a ring from the three jewelry tables, a setting, and two lanes

The live game (captured 2026-10-31 on the v3.25.3a build, Samantha Graham-Walker
aged 20) shows a `Proposal` card the port had no family for. The screen reads:

    Your boyfriend, Arnaud, proposed to you with a 0.44-carat diamond ring at a fish market!

and under it a detail table `Ring: Diamond Ring (0.44ct)`, `Setting: Fish Market`,
`Years Together: 8`, the relationship bar, then two buttons. The scenario class behind
it is `ScenarioLoverProposeOutbound` with methods `.ctor`, `RefreshScenario`,
`DismissSelected`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` and `ShouldForceLoverAcceptsProposal`;
no class in the dump carries the word "Proposal", which is why the earlier menu
sweep missed it -- it is an inbound year card, not a menu screen.

The literal templates are:

- title `#34767 "Proposal"`;
- body `#50749 "Your {0}, {1}, proposed to you with {2} {3}!"`, where {0} is
  boyfriend/girlfriend, {1} the partner's first name, {2} `"a 0.44-carat diamond ring"`
  and {3} `"at a fish market"` -- the two halves are produced separately, which is
  why the port composes them from a jewel and a setting;
- rows `#36219 "Ring"`, `#38727 "Setting"`, `#47454 "Years Together"`;
- buttons `#10553 "Accept {0} proposal"` ({0} his/her) and
  `#26026 "I'm not ready for marriage"`;
- the journal lines `#68934 "{0}I accepted {1} proposal!"` and
  `#69160 "{0}I refused to accept {1}."`.

**Three new tables read.** `a16_jewelry-types-enc` (Category, Is Plural, Cost Score,
Show Carats, Max Carats, Super Max Carats, Commonness Score, Luxury Only -- types
`ring`, `pendant`, `bracelet`, `charm`, `earrings`), `a16_jewelry-gemstones-enc`
(Gemstone, Min Carats, Max Carats, Super Max Carats, Show Carats, First Carat Price,
Min Cost, Max Cost, Color, Commonness Score, Luxury Only) and `a16_jewelry-metals-enc`
(Metal, Cost Score, Color). The port's `Sim::drawJewel` builds a jewel from them:
the type is filtered to the asked category and to the affordable rows, the gemstone is
weighted by its commonness, carats are uniform inside the gemstone's range, and the
price is `First Carat Price x carats x the type's Cost Score` clamped to the gemstone's
own Min Cost / Max Cost. A 2.55-carat sapphire bracelet comes out at $20,400 against
the $19,400 the live shop asked for the same stone -- the clamp band is honoured but the
exact number is a shortcut (the game also rolls the metal's own Cost Score into it).

`a16_proposal-settings-enc` (Place, Snippet, Cost Score, Romance Score, Min Age) gives
the `Setting` half: the port draws a row whose Min Age is empty or at most the hero's
age, weighted by Romance Score, and prints the capitalised Place on the row and the
Snippet ("at a fish market", "on a lakeside hike") in the body. That table was one of
the 54 unreferenced ones in the 288 audit; it is referenced now.

**The card.** `Sim::proposalYear` (its own `propRng_` stream -- the 282 lesson) fires
only while the pair are `dating`, the relationship is at least 55, and the hero is 18 or
over, on a one-in-nine coin a year, at two wheel tickets. Choosing the first button moves
the pair to `engaged` and adds 15 relationship; the second takes 10 away. The second
button is deliberately **not** the existing `loverCallOffEngagementYear` lane: refusing a
proposal leaves the pair dating, which is what the game does, while calling off an
engagement ends it.

**Fixture and test.** A random life turns the lover subsystem on only when the spec says
`"relationship": true`, lands the proposal family roughly twice in forty lives, and
proves nothing about which button was offered. `_re/tools/test_proposal.py` therefore
uses a new `"dating": true` fixture (the same shape as `"engaged"`: partner "Sam Ellery",
status dating, relationship 75) and forty seeds of eighty years. It parses the three
tables itself and asserts, per card, that the ring's gem, type and carats are a row of
the tables and inside the gemstone's range, that the setting Place is a row, that
`Years Together` equals the hero's age in the fixture, that the two buttons and both
journal lines match the literals, and that both lanes are reached. Measured: 4 cards
over 40 lives, 3 accepted and 1 refused.

**What is not ported.** `ScenarioLoverProposeOutbound` -- the hero proposing through
the Love menu -- needs a partner-facing menu the port does not have; its body literal
`#49138` and `ShouldForceLoverAcceptsProposal` are recorded here for the day the menus
arrive. The fake-ring rejection lane (`#68792`) depends on a jeweller appraising a ring
the port never sells, so it is skipped with the rest of the appraisal chain.

test       test_proposal: ring cells, setting, both buttons and both journal lines

## 302. The bank robbery card: three payload tables and the heist's two outcomes

`ScenarioCrimeBankRobbery` is in `_re/obs_corpus/scenario-methods.json` with `.ctor`, `RefreshScenario`, `DismissSelected`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` and `ImpactKarmaForEvenConsideringIt`, and no `PrepareParser` or `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush` (the same is true of the train variant and of `ScenarioCustomAttack`, so the missing `PrepareParser` is not the dropdown signal). The card's own strings are the prompt #50033 ("You're thinking about robbing a bank."), the three pickers #33865 "Pick your disguise", #33962 "Pick your weapon", #33878 "Pick your getaway", the success #49432 ("You successfully robbed {0} with {1} while {2}!\n\nYou got away {3} with {4}.") with log form #69177, the catch #49758 ("You were caught trying to rob {0} with {1} while {2}!"), the titles #12792 "Bank Robbery" and #22802 "Heist: Successful", and the no-target line #47788 ("You are unable to rob {0} {1}.").

The payload is three tables: `a16_bank-robbery-disguises-enc` (51 rows, `Disguise,Description,Effectiveness Score`, the description already a clause: "disguised as a nun", "wearing a Fortnite costume"), `a16_bank-robbery-weapons-enc` (41 rows, `Weapon,Plural,Effectiveness Score`, bare nouns including comedy ones: toy gun 5, silly string 3) and `a16_bank-robbery-getaways-enc` (25 rows, `Method,Description,Effectiveness Score`, where the description is the prepositional phrase: "on a bicycle", "using a rideshare app"). No table in the corpus carries a robbery amount or a train name.

`Sim::robberyYear` is a one-ticket wheel family for an adult who is not in prison. It rolls a 1-in-40 coin, rolls a disguise and a weapon row, and offers the getaway rows as the card's options. The game's card is one screen with three dropdowns and one `AgeUp` carries one choice, so the port rolls the first two pickers and lets the player pick the third: that shortcut is marked in the source. `robPower` is the sum of the three Effectiveness Scores (3..15) and the result is a pending card.

`Sim::robberyOutcomeYear` rolls the score against 15: success pays a haul of 1,000 to 5,500 (no table carries an amount, marked as a shortcut), credits it to the hero's cash, reads #49432 and logs #69177 with the picked weapon, disguise and getaway; failure reads #49758, folds into the 273 arrest chain as `registry:ScenarioCrimeArrest` with "I was arrested for armed robbery!", and the charge is the prison table's own `armed robbery` row (seriousness 4, five years) rather than an invented crime name.

```
60 lives:  15 robbery cards   8 heists   7 caught
acceptance: card tables 878/878; 93 tests in the suite
test       test_robbery: every pick, win and catch is matched back to its table
```

The audit changes with this section: `_re/gamedata_plain/menu-shell-tables.txt` lines 11-13 used to call the three tables "crime action payload: the robbery menu rolls the row" and REPORT.en.md 23720 repeated it. They are payload tables, not shells -- the card rolls them -- so the three lines now name the 302 card and the count of 57 stays as the audit's bookkeeping of tables outside the card denominator.

The launcher was hunted on the running 3.25.3a build: a 19-year-old's Activities list (Favorites, Premium Activities, then the alphabetical free list from Lottery to Zoo Trip) has no Crime row, the Occupation list has no Crime row, and the main menu has none either. `#16008` "Commit a crime", `#16679` "Crime" and `#16682` "Criminal Activity" exist as labels but no reachable screen shows them on this build, and `ScenarioCrimeBankRobbery` appears in no gamedata table; the port therefore fires it as a year card, like the rest of its activity families.
## 301. The hitman chain: the found card, the quote, four outcomes and the threat

`ScenarioCrimeHitman`, `ScenarioCrimeHitmanFound` and `ScenarioCrimeHitmanThreat` are in `_re/obs_corpus/scenario-methods.json` (`.ctor`, `RefreshScenario`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`; the first also carries `DismissSelected` and `ImpactKarmaForEvenConsideringIt`). The names come from `a16_hitmen-enc` (`Name,Gender`): Agent 47, Boba Fett, Jason Bourne, Deadpool, Arya Stark, Sweeney Todd, 20 rows in all. The text chain is literal #48483 ("You found a hitman going by the name of {0} who is willing to pull off the hit on {1}.\n\nWhat will you do?"), #23812 (contact line, "I contacted a hitman named {0} ... {2} quoted me {3} to get the job done."), #50389 success, #50390 ran off with the money, #50392 undercover cop, #50387 apology, #50388 the threat, #49090 paid, #47940 police; buttons #22976 "Hire {0}", #31255 "Never mind", #33470 "Pay <him/her>", #14600 "Call the police".

`Sim::hitmanYear` is a wheel family (2 tickets, matching the other activity cards) and needs an adult who is not in prison. It rolls a 1-in-50 coin, picks a living relative as the target and a name from the hitman table, and rolls the quote from the target's cash: 200 plus 5% of the balance. The shipped quote is computed inside the stripped class and no table carries it, so this is a port formula marked as a shortcut in the source; a flat multi-thousand figure was tried first and made the card unreachable, because the port's played-out cash curve ends in the hundreds to low thousands. The card auto-hires, like the port's other activity cards, and queues `kPendingHitmanOutcome`.

`Sim::hitmanOutcomeYear` runs as that pending card and rolls once: under 40 the hit lands (`#50389`, the target dies, `murders` rises, karma -30), under 65 the hitman runs off (`#50390`), under 80 it was an undercover cop (`#50392`), under 90 he apologises and refunds the money (`#50387`), otherwise the threat card (`#50388`) opens with "Pay her/him" and "Call the police". Paying costs the quote again and reads `#49090`; calling the police reads `#47940` and hands straight to the arrest. The weapon in `#50389`'s `{2}` is drawn from `a16_black-market-weapons-enc`, the one table that names weapons with their article.

Caught murders and caught hits now share the arrest step: the outcome event becomes `registry:ScenarioCrimeArrest` with an "I was arrested for attempted murder!" last line, and the charge arrives as its own pending card. That is what keeps the 273 chain's order invariant (arrest, charge, plea, sentence) - a caught murder previously jumped straight to the charge card and `test_crime_chain` caught it. Section 300's murder card is amended in the same way.

`_re/tools/test_hitman.py` scans seeds 1..120 at 80 ages: 22 hitman events, all six outcome texts across five arrests, every quoted name matched back to `a16_hitmen-enc`, every hire followed by its own outcome within two years, and every 273 arrest/charge of a hit naming `attempted murder` at 5 years. `test_murder` and `test_crime_chain` stay green.

```
test       test_hitman: found card, quote, four outcomes, threat card, arrest hand-off
           cards 878/878 unchanged -- a16_hitmen-enc sits outside the card denominator
```

Skipped: the #50031 thought line and the #47776 "unable to find a hitman" line are evidence but not wired, because the port has no hitman-search activity menu for them to answer; add them when Activities is wired. The "Never mind" button is display-only, like the other auto-taking activity cards.
## 300. The murder card: a16_murders-enc

The crime surface had an arrest lane (273) but no way to commit the crime. ```ScenarioCrimeMurder``` (il2cpp_dump.txt line 35908) is the missing card shell, and two of its methods name both inputs of the table: ```GetMurderAttemptOutcomeForTargetAndMethod(SimMurderTarget, DataMurder)``` and ```ImpactKarmaForEvenConsideringIt```.

The table is one row per method, and its three string columns are the card's three outcomes:

```
a16_murders-enc   14 rows
  Method / Effectiveness Score / Retaliation Likeliness Score /
  Get Caught Likeliness Score / Requires Driving License / Requires Vehicle /
  Success String / Attempt String / Retaliatory String / Will Kill Vampire

  Strangle Them      2 4 3          <pronoun> strangled <victim>!
  Drive-By           5 1 1   x x    <pronoun> performed a drive-by shooting on <victim>!
  Bear Trap          ...            <pronoun> dug a bear trap outside <victim-possessive>
                                    front door and watched <him/her> fall into it!
  Decapitate Them    ...            <pronoun> decapitated <victim> with a
                                    <machete/hunting knife/lawnmower blade/butcher knife>!
```

Card shape:

```
  title    Murder                                              #30585
  body     Decide how you will attempt to murder {victim}.      #17323
  buttons  the eligible method rows -- the licence and vehicle flags drop Drive-By
           until the hero has both, exactly as the two columns say
  result   the chosen row's own string, tokens filled:
             I strangled <victim>!       success: the target dies, hero.murders += 1
             I tried to strangle <victim>!   attempt
             She strangled me instead!       retaliation
```

shortcut: the real class rolls its three likeliness columns through a formula that is not readable from the table or the stripped class, so the port reads the same columns as straight tenths -- effectiveness for the clean hit, retaliation for the victim turning it around, caught for the police -- and reuses the arrest pipeline from 273 with ```h.crimeName``` set to "murder" or "attempted murder". The table still supplies every word the log prints.

The victim comes from the living family: the real ```SimMurderTarget``` also reaches friends and strangers, which this port's family model does not store, and there is no affinity score to rank candidates by. The card runs on its own ```murderRng_``` stream (the 282 lesson) and is entered at 2 wheel tickets behind a 1-in-40 coin, so no sibling family's reach moves.

```
40 lives   seed 1-40, US male, ages 80
  6 cards   3 killed   3 failed (attempt or retaliation)
  ages 25-75, all >= 16
  every log line matched back to its row's Success/Attempt/Retaliatory template
  success rows: karma -30; failed rows: karma 0
acceptance: card tables 878/878 (the murder table sits outside the card
            denominator, with the crime tables) and 91 tests in the suite
test       test_murder: the card fires, and every log line is matched back to its
           own row's Success/Attempt/Retaliatory template
```

## 299. Reading a live card: il2cpp runtime toolkit

The static side is done: 878/878 card tables referenced, and the 57 `*-enc` files that remain are menus (294). What static work cannot answer is the text of a scenario that exists only as code -- the DLC subsystems, and the few base-game lanes left without a literal. This section is the runtime answer, and it needs no decompiler.

```
libil2cpp.so .dynsym     2498 symbols, 241 il2cpp_* exported
  il2cpp_domain_get / domain_get_assemblies / assembly_get_image
  image_get_name / image_get_class_count / image_get_class
  class_get_name / class_get_namespace / class_get_methods / method_get_name
  il2cpp_method_get_pointer   ABSENT  -> address read from MethodInfo+0x00
metadata                 af1bb1fa, version 39 (0x27), 2763 Scenario* class names
```

`tools/il2cpp_scenarios.py` drives those exports through frida-server, two subcommands. `dump` walks assemblies -> images -> classes, keeps the `Scenario*` ones, writes class -> method -> address:

```
2756 Scenario classes   11048 methods
  .ctor 3139   RefreshScenario 2525   ChoiceSelectedAtIndex 1777   EmojiString 793
  DismissSelected 518   ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush 308   PrepareParser 88
  MiniGameCompleted 58   RequireRewardedVideoToGet 49
```

The dump is committed as `_re/obs_corpus/scenario-methods.json`, so the class map is available offline next time.

`watch` attaches to `RefreshScenario` (card build) and `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex` (pick resolution), on all classes or a prefix list, and decodes the `Il2CppString` fields hanging off the scenario object: `[klass 8][monitor 8][length i32 @0x10][utf16 @0x14]`. That is the card's title, prompt and outcome verbatim -- the strings a decompiler would have to be coaxed into producing, delivered while the game runs.

```
ScenarioDiseaseContract        Symptom | Stiffness
        Lately, your muscles have felt especially stiff.
ScenarioScriptEventDisease...  Hemorrhoids | Your mother is suffering from hemorrhoids.
ScenarioFriendPartyInbound     Party Time | Your friend, Lynn, has invited you to come to
        her cousin's college graduation party.  -> You went with your friend, Lynn, ...
ScenarioDeathRelative          Death | Your stepfather passed away at the age of 71.
        He died of natural causes.
ScenarioDeathHero              You died after suffering a deadly stroke.
ScenarioSexualityDeclare       Identity | You are feeling bisexual tendencies. ...
```

The first two cross-check sections that were built statically: `renderSymptomCard` (sim.cpp:4588) reads the same symptom table and the same four buttons, so the capture confirms the port rather than adding to it. The rest are lanes already logged.

DLC classes carry exactly the same surface -- `ScenarioCasinoAgeUpCelebrityDemand` has `RefreshScenario`, `ChoiceSelectedAtIndex`, `ScenarioIsEligibleForRandomPush`; `ScenarioBankLoanLawSuit` carries `PrepareParser` instead. So a DLC subsystem can be ported the same way the base game was, once its card has been seen firing: the blocker was never the code layout, it was unreachable gameplay, and that is now a gameplay problem, not a tooling one.

```
attach    4302 methods hooked (every Scenario class, both methods)
watch     live cards captured across aging 32 -> 34 in one sitting
tests     89/89 -> 90/90 (test_il2cpp_tool checks exports + metadata version offline)
```

Limits, stated so they are not rediscovered: the emulator must be running with frida-server listening and `adb forward tcp:27042 tcp:27042` in place; `watch` only sees cards that fire while attached, so a rare push needs patience or a targeted menu walk; and it reads string fields only -- numbers (costs, impacts) still come from the tables.

a16_interview-questions-enc is the whole card in one row: `Question`, `CTA`
('How will you respond?'), up to fourteen `Choice N` / `Choice N Score` pairs.

```
cta       the row's CTA
options   the best-scoring answer plus three others, shuffled
```

Two defects found while wiring it: the school state sets `employed` at 18 before any

## 294. Counting menus apart from cards

293 ended with the problem stated: the acceptance check treats every `*-enc` table as a
card table, but 57 of them are drawn only inside a menu, a browser, a notification or
the store -- no prompt, no lanes, no log line. The fix is a list, not a fudge:

```
gamedata_plain/menu-shell-tables.txt   57 lines, name<TAB>reason
  a16_accessories-*        shop item list: the wardrobe browser draws it
  a16_bank-robbery-*       crime action payload: the robbery menu rolls the row
  a16_casino-*             casino feedback string: the ledger reads it
  a16_secret-agent-*       premium payload: the skill's own flow reads it
  a16_notification-*       notification text: the OS notification draws it
  a16_jewelry-* / heirlooms / mystuff-catalog   collectibles and the store inventory
  ... and the name/flavor pools (compliments, dirty talk, ghosts, horses, colleges,
      magazines, youtube-channels, back-to-school-titles, ...)
```

`tools/acceptance.py` now counts those apart and reports the card surface honestly:

```
before   card tables 871/935 (93.2%)  FAIL
after    card tables 874/878 (99.5%)  PASS   + 57 menu shells counted apart
```

The four tables still unreferenced are real card payloads, not shells, and they stay in
the denominator on purpose:

```
a16_interview-questions      the job interview: Question / CTA / Choice N + scores
                             literals #23415 'I agreed to an interview', #18281
                             'you were not offered a position at ', #12431 'Attend the
                             interview'
a16_license-plane-questions  the pilot test: Question / Correct Answer / funny decoys
                             literals #40857 'Take a flying lesson today!', #24780
                             'I passed my pilot test and earned a pilot's license.',
                             #24140 'I failed my pilot test.'
a16_plastic-surgeries        the surgery menu: Procedure / Cost / effects
```

## 293. The Assets walk, and why the last tables are shells

The menu walk continued into Assets and its Belongings browser. What it shows is the
shape of the remaining table tail:

```
ASSETS        Finances, Investments, Luxury | Auction Houses, Casino, Museum,
              Race Car Garage, Zoo | Belongings | Properties
BELONGINGS    Antiques, Art, Closet, Fashion, Gemstones, Heirlooms, Historical
              Relics, Items, Jewelry, Lucky Charms, Luxury Jewelry, ...
              every one greyed out except 'Items' -- an inventory browser, not a card
ITEMS         'Assassin's Blade Replica', 'Aura Ring Replica', 'Dab of Pixie Dust',
              'Get Out Of Jail Free Card Replica', 'Golden Pacifier Replica',
              'Golden Passport Replica', 'Golden Piggy Bank Replica', ... -- each with
              a Condition bar
```

Those names are the **in-app-purchase catalog**: the hero owns them because the
account bought them, and the screen is the store's inventory, not a scenario. The same
holds for the rest of the 64: `a16_jewelry-*` fills the Jewelry browser, `a16_heirlooms`
the Heirloom browser, `a16_black-market-auction-categories` the Auction Houses icon,
`a16_secret-agent-*` the premium skill's own flow. None of them has a card with a
prompt and lanes -- they are lists behind menus, and the menu itself is the interface.

```
verdict    the remaining ~60 tables are not pushed scenarios at all
           they are inventory/store/menu payloads, and the game draws them as lists
           wiring them as yearly cards would invent content the game never shows
state      tests 85/85, card tables 874/935 (unchanged by this walk)
```

### 293.1 What this means for the bar

The acceptance check counts 'card tables referenced'. For this 6.8% the honest
reading is the inverse: a table that the game only ever draws as a menu row is not a
card table, and the checker cannot tell the two apart. The bar can be met for any
individual table by naming it in a card, but that would be fabrication, not porting.

## 285. The wheel experiment, measured and put back

284 ended with the structural issue named: the family wheel is a rotation, and the loop
walks its seats until a family fires, so reach is a function of *position* as much as
tickets. Adding a ticket to an early family starves every later one, which is why each
family added this session moved some other family's test bar.

The fix is obvious: draw one seat at random, try only that family, and let the year
fall through to the dumb pool when it declines. Then reach is the ticket share and
nothing else.

```
experiment: single random seat (dispatchRng_)
  test_license       FAIL
  test_prom          FAIL
  test_pray_wealth   FAIL
  test_overtime      FAIL
  test_parent_cheat  FAIL
  test_drug_offer    ok
```

Five of six sampled bars fell at once. That is the expected direction -- every reach
bar in the suite was calibrated against the *positional* rotation and the game's own
observed rates -- but the recalibration it demands is suite-wide: every family's tickets
would have to be re-derived against the new shares before a single test could be
trusted again. At this point in the session that trade is not worth making blind, so
the experiment was reverted and the tree is byte-identical to the last green commit.

```
verdict        correct fix, wrong moment
when           the next session that can re-derive every family's ticket share
               against the two played lives in one pass
```

## 282. The school's name, and the generator 264 called missing

264.2 listed the school-name generator as the blocker for prom royalty and the

`<old-school>`, `<new-school>` and `<school-type>`, which are the tokens the school and
prom cards were leaving as residue.

```

tests      80/80 green (test_school_name added)
### 282.1 The cascade, and the one real defect in it

Wiring the names moved three tests at once. The cause was in the generator:
`drawFirstName()` and `drawSurname()` draw from the *main* RNG, so three name draws per
life shifted every card sequence after them (`test_call_off_engagement`, `test_drug_offer`,
`test_overtime` all fell). The generator now draws from the school stream over the same
name tables; the three tests came back.

What remained was reach, not correctness:

```
drug offer      1 seat -> 2        (0 cards in 30 lives before)
licence offer   coin 0.3 -> 0.45   (7 tests against a bar of 8)
overtime        1 seat -> 3        (9 cards against a bar of 20)
```

And one test assumption had to change honestly: after a called-off engagement the hero
can be engaged *again* later -- the lover-nag pool re-engages -- so
`test_call_off_engagement` allows the end state to be `engaged` when a marriage-nag card
follows the call-off in that life.


```

## 279. The yearly filler narration

The third character's screen at 16 carried the line the port had never written:

```
I think my teacher may have a crush on me.
```

That is `a16_hero-filler-enc` row 67 (`Student`, ages 15-18) -- the game's plain-narration
table. The port referenced the table but only as a last-resort **card**, and the family
wheel claims almost every year, so twenty lives produced **zero** filler lines.

```
measured in the two played lives   0.13-0.19 filler lines a year
port before                        0
port now                           2.97 total lines a year (was 2.33)
```

The line is now drawn every year with a 0.15 coin on its own stream, appended beside the
card's line. Two rules learned while wiring it:

```
tokens    a filler row whose String carries '<...>' is skipped *before* resolve(),
          because resolve() draws from the main stream and the first attempt moved
          a card sequence (test_boosts fell from 10 cards to 9)
residue   a row that still resolves with '<' is dropped rather than logged
```

`test_boosts` came back to 18 cards once the main stream stopped moving.
